{{Recipe}}

'''Bolinhos de Mandioca com Mel''' (Cassava Fritters with Honey) is a sweet [[Cookbook:snacks|snack]] made from grated [[Cookbook:cassava|cassava]], shaped into small [[Cookbook:cake|cakes]] and fried until golden. The fritters are traditionally served warm and drizzled with [[Cookbook:honey|honey]]. This dish is commonly associated with the [[Cookbook:Cuisines|cuisine]] of '''Cape Verde''', an island country in West Africa, where cassava is an important staple crop. Similar cassava-based fritters are also prepared in other African countries, including '''Angola''', '''Mozambique''', and '''Guinea-Bissau'''. The fritters are typically cooked by deep-frying the cassava mixture until crisp on the outside and soft on the inside, then serving them with honey as a dessert or snack.

== Ingredients ==

* 500 g cassava (mandioca), peeled and grated
* 2 [[Cookbook:eggs|eggs]]
* 3 tbsp [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:vanilla|vanilla]] extract
* ½ tsp ground [[Cookbook:cinnamon|cinnamon]]
* ¼ tsp salt
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|Vegetable oil]], for frying
* 4 tbsp honey, for serving

== Procedure ==

Place the grated cassava in a large bowl.

Add the eggs, sugar, vanilla extract, cinnamon, and salt.

Mix thoroughly until a uniform batter forms.

Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.

Scoop small portions of the mixture and carefully place them into the hot oil.

Fry until golden brown on all sides, about 3–4 minutes.

Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Arrange the fritters on a serving plate.

Drizzle generously with honey before serving.

== Serving ==
Serve warm as:

* A dessert
* An afternoon snack
* A breakfast treat with tea or coffee

== Variations ==

* Add grated coconut to the batter.
* Replace honey with maple syrup or fruit syrup.
* Sprinkle with powdered sugar before serving.

== Notes ==

* Fresh cassava should be used for the best texture.
* Ensure cassava is properly peeled and prepared before cooking.
* The fritters may also be baked instead of fried.

== See also ==

* Cassava Bread
* Fritters
* Honey Cake

title: Cookbook:Brown Rice with Other Starches and Vegetables (Pandora's Feast)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Vegan recipes
| Servings = 1
| Time = 25–45 minutes
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Rice|Rice]]

'''Pandora's feast''' is a complete vegan meal that can be served several times a week due to the ease with which it can be modified.  The meal is easy to prepare in a [[Cookbook:Rice Cooker|rice cooker]].

==Ingredients==

=== Base ===
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] uncooked [[Cookbook:Rice|brown rice]]
*2 cups water

=== Additions ===
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soaked]] and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiled]] [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black]], [[Cookbook:Pinto Bean|pinto]], [[Cookbook:Kidney Bean|kidney]] or other [[Cookbook:Bean|beans]]
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]] [[Cookbook:Potato|potato]]
*1 cup cubed [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potato]]
*1 cup cubed [[Cookbook:Squash|squash]]
*1 clove [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]]
*1 cup cubed [[Cookbook:Beet|beet]]
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Kale|kale]]

=== Serving ===
*[[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]], hemp oil, flaxseed oil, or other nutritious [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
*[[Cookbook:Nutritional Yeast|Nutritional yeast]]
*[[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|Soy sauce]]
*Black [[Cookbook:Sesame Seed|sesame seeds]]

==Procedure==

#Add the brown rice and water to a [[Cookbook:Rice Cooker|rice cooker]].
#Drain, rinse, and add the beans to the rice cooker.
#If using, add the garlic to the cooker.
#If using, add the sweet potato, squash, beet, or potato.
#If using a fuzzy logic (i.e. programmable) cooker, set the cooker to the brown rice setting and turn it on. If using an on/off cooker, simply turn it on.
#In about 20–40 minutes, your cooker should finish cooking the rice. When finished, open the lid, add the kale, close the lid, and wait about another minute or two.
#Open and serve. Top with oil, yeast, soy sauce and/or sesame seeds, to taste.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you have "Thai sweet black rice" or "Chinese forbidden black rice", replace about 10% of your brown rice with this, and your finished product will be a lovely purple and will have a different taste.
* The beans must be either pre-soaked for at least 8 hours and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiled]] briskly for 20 minutes (preferred) or from a can. It is important to soak and pre-cook dried beans. Dried kidney beans will cause nausea, vomiting and diarrhea unless they have been boiled briskly for at least 20 minutes to destroy the very indigestible phytohaemagglutinin that they contain (the slow cooker will not do and can even make things worse). They will then need another 60–90 minutes at a slow [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] to be tender. Tinned kidney beans are quite safe and do not need pre-cooking, as their preparation involves sufficient heat to destroy the toxin.)
* The cubed vegetables should be 1[[Cookbook:cm|cm]] x 1cm for optimal cooking.

text:
{{Recipe summary

{{recipe}}
== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] minced meat (approximately 60% [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] + 40% [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]]) 
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste 
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]] 
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]]
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] water
== Procedure ==
# Salt the meat, and mix well with spices and water.
# Cover, and let stand in the refrigerator for 1–2 days. This is the most important and tricky part of the recipe, as the goal is to allow the meat to [[Cookbook:Fermentation|ferment]]. 
# Form mixture into oblong rissoles (skinless sausages) by passing through a grinder with a funnel at the end.
# Grill sausages on medium-high heat. Do not flip more than once when grilling—flipping multiple times will produce a dry instead of juicy product.
# Serve hot with your choice of sides. They are best with golden French fries and cold beer. 

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If the minced meat is very lean, modify the ratio to 75% pork + 25% beef—otherwise the kepabcheta will be dry. The target fat content should be about 30% fat, like a US style burger.
* Kebapche does not contain [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], which is found in the related dish called Kyufte.
* When the meat is well fermented, the cooked product looks puffed (compare to a Walmart burger, which shrinks when cooked).

text:
{{recipesummary

| Image = [[File:Brigadeiro.jpg|300px]]

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Brazil|Brazilian Cuisine]]

'''Brigadeiro''' is a simple Brazilian chocolate fudge candy created in the 1920s. It is named after Brazilian airman  Eduardo Gomes (''brigadeiro'' being his rank in the Air Force). It's commonly served with soda, coffee or milk.
== Ingredients ==

* 1 can (395 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) of [[Cookbook:Sweetened Condensed Milk|sweetened condensed milk]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] of [[cookbook:butter|butter]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]]s of [[Cookbook:Cocoa powder|cocoa powder]]
* 1 box (482 g) of [[Cookbook:Sprinkles|chocolate sprinkles]] 

== Procedure ==

# In a heavy [[cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]], combine the milk, cocoa powder, and butter. Stir to dissolve the chocolate.
# Put over low heat and stir constantly to avoid formation of lumps.
# Continue stirring for 10–12 minutes, or until you are able to see the bottom of the pot for one second when you scratch it side-to-side with the spoon. The more you cook, the harder the resulting candy will be—it may vary from liquid fudge to hard candy.
# Allow mixture to cool.
# Butter your hands, and roll the mixture into small balls (around 2 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] in diameter). Alternatively, you can use two metal spoons to shape the candies. Roll them in the chocolate sprinkles.  

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Should you accidentally get hard candy, fill the pot with water and leave to rest—the candy will dissolve completely and the pot will be easy to clean.
* You can substitute 100 g of baking chocolate for the cocoa powder. If you want a lighter candy, use powdered chocolate (such as Nestlé Quick). You can also put [[cookbook:raisin|raisin]]s or [[Cookbook:Nut|nut]]s in the center of the candy. You can decorate with powdered [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] instead, or cocoa powder.
* Brazilian brigadeiros also have gourmet varieties. Some references are available in specialized houses in Brazil: [http://www.mariabrigadeiro.com.br Maria Brigadeiro] and [http://www.brigadeirissimo.com.br Brigadeiríssimo] and [http://www.BrigadeiroGourmet.com Brigadeiro Gourmet]

title: Cookbook:Bruschetta
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Italian recipes|servings=depends on loaf size|time=10 minutes|difficulty=1}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine_of_Italy|Cuisine of Italy]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian_cuisine|Vegetarian cuisine]]

This article describes general preparation procedures for the popular Italian appetizer (or ''antipasto'') '''Bruschetta''' (plural ''bruschette''), slices of toasted or grilled bread rubbed with garlic, drizzled with olive oil, and seasoned with salt and pepper.<ref name=Field>{{cite book |last=Field |first=Carol |title=Italy in Small Bites |publisher=William Morrow and Company, Inc. |location=New York, New York |date=1993 |page=77 }}</ref> This basic preparation is frequently topped with combinations of flavorful seasonal ingredients. It is a dish coming from the Southern Italian culinary tradition, though variants exist throughout Italy. It is commonly mispronounced in America as "bru-shetta", but should be pronounced with a hard K sound, "bru-sketta."

There are many types of ''bruschetta'', some involving special roasted and/or hard bread which may require a different preparation than the one below. 

The recipe below is a meeting point between Northern and Southern Italy, using an Italian or French baguette-style loaf. You can adapt this recipe to as many servings as you need. As a guideline, you can serve 1 or 2 ''bruschette'' per person.

== Ingredients ==

=== Base ===
* 1 loaf of Italian or French [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]], sliced ½ inch (1.25 cm) thick on the bias
* ½ head [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* Kosher salt or sea [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* Freshly-ground black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* Extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive oil|olive oil]]
* Toppings of your choice (see examples below)

=== Toppings ===

* Chopped [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] with [[Cookbook:Arugula|arugula]] or [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]]
* Cooked white [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]] (topped, if you like, with sautéed kale)
* Sautéed [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]] (preferably wild varieties)
* Minced [[Cookbook:Anchovy|anchovies]] flavored with wine [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] and herbs
* Thinly-sliced [[Cookbook:Pancetta|pancetta]] crisped under the [[Cookbook:Broiler|broiler]]
* Pugliese-style chopped mixture of summer vegetables (red [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]], [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]], flat-leaf [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]], and [[Cookbook:Red pepper flakes|red pepper flakes]])

==Procedure==
#Toast the bread slices in a toaster oven, under a broiler, or on a grill, until they turn golden.
#Immediately rub the bread with the cut side of the garlic. Sprinkle with salt and black pepper, and drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil.
#Serve warm topped with whatever combinations of seasonal ingredients you choose.<ref name=Field></ref>

title: Cookbook:Bryndzové Halušky (Slovak Dumplings with Cheese)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Dumpling recipes
| Servings = 2–3
| Image = [[File:Bryndzové halušky so slaninou.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Bryndzové halušky''' is a Slovak [[Cookbook:Dumpling|dumpling]] dish. The ingredient that makes this national dish of Slovakia a favorite is the sheep's milk cheese, which has a slightly sharper taste than the non-flavored goat cheese spread available at many US grocery stores. The most abundant ingredient is the raw potato, which comprises most of the dough that creates the halušky and is a major staple in the Slovak diet.

==Ingredients==
* 750 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], peeled and finely [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] (optional)
* 250 g [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]] (''hladkej múky'')
* 250 g [[Cookbook:Bryndza|''bryndze'' cheese]], cut into very small pieces
* 100 g [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]] (''údenej slaniny''), cooked and cut into small pieces

==Procedure==

# Combine the grated potatoes with with the flour and salt to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Shape the dough into small cylindrical pieces less than 3 cm in size.
# Transfer the dumplings to a pot of [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] salted water. When the dumplings rise to the top of the boiling water, remove one to make sure they are thoroughly cooked.
# Remove the dumplings from the pot with a slotted spoon, and transfer to a warmed plate.
# Immediately after dumplings are placed on the plate, scatter the cheese over top, and let the cheese melt over the dumplings. Mix if desired.
# Sprinkle the crispy bacon bits on top of the cheese.
# Serve piping hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If in a hurry, try replacing the from-scratch halusky with store-bought potato gnocchi.
* If unable to find ''bryndze'', you can substitute crumbled goat cheese or one of several types of crumbled feta. Some feta are stronger-flavored, which is preferable here.

title: Cookbook:Buchteln (Austrian Sweet Buns)
text:
__NOTOC__{{recipesummary|Dessert recipes|15–20|Prep: 1 hr</br>Cooking: 30 min|difficulty=2| Image = [[File:Buchteln on plate.jpg|300px]]}}{{recipe}} Cuisine of Austria

Originally, '''Buchteln''' (singular: Buchtel) were a Bohemian sweet dish. However, in the course of time they have become part of the traditional Austrian Cuisine.

This dough is [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]-based. In order to get nice, fluffy dough, the right combination of [[Cookbook:flour|flour]], [[Cookbook:milk|milk]] and [[Cookbook:yeast|yeast]] is needed. Additionally, as a yeasted dough, this recipe is somewhat time consuming. This is indispensable as the dough needs to rise, and this takes some time.      

The joy for cooking and baking should be in the foreground in today’s hectic society. So, take your time and try this traditional Austrian sweet dish.

# [[cookbook:Scalding|Scald]] milk by bringing it to at least {{convert|180|F|C}}, then let it cool.
# Put the yeast in a small bowl and add some lukewarm milk to it. Add 1 teaspoon of sugar. Let it rest for a moment, as yeast in general needs some time to ferment.
# When ready, add the yeast mixture to the bowl with the flour. Put the remaining sugar into the bowl. Make sure the mixture has reached at least room temperature, then mix in the eggs and a pinch of salt. Finally, add ground lemon peel.
# [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] it until you get nice, smooth [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. 
# Use a cloth to cover the bowl. Let it rest until the dough has risen significantly.
# In the meantime, thoroughly oil or butter a [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]], preferably of about 5 to 10 cm height.
# When ready, take the dough and put it on a clean, floured surface. [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] the dough to 1 cm thickness. Divide it so that you get equal squares of about 4 x 4 square centimeters each.

# Place the buns side-by-side in the greased pan. Cover them with a cloth once more, and let them rest for 20 minutes.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the buns in a preheated [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] until they are golden brown.

{{recipe}}

'''Christmas pudding''' is a traditional British dish served at Christmas time. British people in different regions may call this dish by different names. Traditional Christmas pudding can be served with coated butter, or sauce, or even cream. Moreover, it can be cooked nearly 6 weeks before Christmas. British people keep the pudding in a greaseproof paper stored in a cool place. The longer it is being cooked, the brighter it will be. As a rule the pudding must consist of 13 ingredients; however, British cuisine of those old times was really different and today we present a new recipe of Christmas pudding that is common in the modern British society. It is very easy and will take you nearly 45 minutes to prepare this dish.

}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Bubur ketan hitam''' is a dish of black glutinous rice pudding with coconut milk.

==Ingredients==
===Porridge===
* 250 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]] black glutinous [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Liter|litres]] water
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pandan|pandan]] leaves
* 250 grams coconut sugar or [[Cookbook:Palm Sugar|palm sugar]], microwaved for couple minutes to dissolve easily
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

===Coconut milk sauce=== 
* 350 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] thick [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] salt
* 2 pandan leaves

==Procedure==
===Porridge=== 
# Soak black glutinous rice in water overnight.
# Drain the rice. Cook with water and pandan leaves until soft and thick.
# Add coconut sugar and salt, and continue cooking until the sugar is dissolved and the water is absorbed.

===Coconut milk sauce===
# Cook thick coconut milk with salt and pandan for a few minutes.
# Serve the black rice pudding in a bowl, and pour coconut milk sauce on top.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Additional toppings might be added, such as sliced baked [[Cookbook:Banana|banana]], brown sugar powder, or [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] powder.

==Ingredients==

title: Cookbook:Bua Loi (Rice Balls in Sweet Coconut Milk)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Thai recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

'''''Bua loi''''' is a traditional Thai rice flour dessert. It is often prepared for religious or ritual ceremonies, but it can also be eaten as an everyday dish. Bua loi are often brightly colored with various ingredients (see notes).

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] sweet glutinous [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|rice flour]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Steaming|steamed]] and mashed [[Cookbook:Taro Root|taro]] root
* ¼ cup water
* [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|Coconut milk]]

== Procedure ==
# Combine rice flour, mashed taro, and water to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Shape the dough into small balls, using additional rice flour to prevent sticking.
# Bring a large pot of water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Add the dough balls to the boiling water. They will initially sink but will gradually float to the surface as they cook.
# Remove the cooked bua loi from the pot, and drain the water.
# Transfer the bua loi to a dish, and serve with coconut milk. This dish is best served hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you want to make your bua loi more colorful, you can add [[Cookbook:Pumpkin|pumpkin]] (yellow) or [[Cookbook:Pandan|pandan]] (green).

title: Cookbook:Brown Butter Toffee Chocolate Chip Cookies
text:
__NOTOC__{{recipesummary
| category = Recipes for dessert
| servings = 9–10
| difficulty = 4
| time = 49 hours
}}{{recipe}}

'''Brown butter toffee chocolate chip cookies''' are flavorful [[Cookbook:Cookie|cookies]], and it takes 48 hours for the dough to develop the flavors. This recipe is adapted from the YouTube channel Tasty.<ref>https://google.miraheze.org/wiki/YouTube_Wiki:2-Minute_Vs._2-Hour_Vs._2-Day_Cookie_%E2%80%A2_Tasty</ref>

== Ingredients ==
=== Toffee ===

* ¾ stick (90 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (140 g / 5 oz) lightly packed light [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] kosher [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* Water, as needed

=== Cookie dough ===

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (2 sticks / 250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 9 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) unsalted butter
* 4 ice cubes
* ¾ cup (160 g / 5.5 oz) white [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
* 1½ cups (270 g / 9.5 oz) packed light brown sugar
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Coffee|espresso powder]]
* 2 teaspoons kosher salt
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (100 g) standard [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract
* 2½ cups (350 g / 12.5 oz) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 6 oz (170 g) dark [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]] (50–70% cacao), [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* Flaky sea salt, for sprinkling

== Procedure ==

# Line a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] with baking [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment]].
# Melt the butter, sugar and salt in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over medium heat. Add water if necessary to keep fat from separating. Continue to cook until the temperature is 150°C (302°F) and when dropped in water it forms brittle threads.
# Pour the toffee onto the prepared baking pan. Freeze until ready to use, about 30 minutes.
# Meanwhile, line another baking sheet with parchment.
# Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook until it turns dark brown. Remove from the heat.
# Add an ice cube to the butter and let it melt. Repeat with remaining ice cubes.
# Combine the sugars, espresso powder, salt, and baking soda in a large bowl.
# Pour the brown butter into the sugar mixture and [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] until combined.
# Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
# [[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] in the flour until combined.
# Remove the toffee from the freezer and break into chunks. Put into a zippable bag and break into bits using a [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]].
# Add the toffee and chocolate to the dough and fold in.
# Scoop the dough onto the baking sheet and let it chill for 48 hours for flavors to develop.
# When ready to bake, preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 163°C (325°F). Line 2 [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheets]] with baking parchment.
# Arrange the cookies on the baking sheets, leaving at least 2 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] (5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) of space between each other.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 18–20 minutes until golden brown.
# Take the cookies out of the oven and sprinkle with a little sea salt before leaving them to cool.

title: Cookbook:Buckwheat Crêpes
text:
__NOTOC__ {{Recipe summary | Name = Buckwheat pancake
(Galette de blé noir) | Category = Pancake recipes | Yield = 12 pancakes | Servings = | Difficulty = 2 | Image = [[File:Galette de sarrasin complète bretonne.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} '''Buckwheat crêpes''' are a type of savory crêpe from Upper Brittany made with [[Cookbook:Buckwheat|buckwheat]] flour. They are locally known as "'''galettes de blé noir'''" or "'''galettes de sarrasin'''" and are traditionally eaten on Fridays. Nowadays, these are cooked at home, served in crêperies, and can be a typical takeaway dish. In all cases, they are served stuffed with fillings like ham, egg, cheese, sausage, etc. == Ingredients == * 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Buckwheat|buckwheat]] flour * 1 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]] (optional; see note) * [[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]] for cooking * Fillings as desired == Procedure == === Batter === # [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] together the flour and salt in a [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]]. # Whisk in the egg and half the water to make a [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]]. # Cover the batter with a cloth, and let it rest for 1 hour at room temperature. # Gradually whisk in the remaining water as needed to get the correct consistency. It needs to be thin enough to flow and coat the pan, but not so watery that the pancake will not bind during cooking. You may not need to add all the water. === Cooking === # Prepare your desired fillings in advance. Anything that requires more than 1 minute to cook (e.g. onions, mushrooms, meat, etc.) should be pre-cooked. # Heat a large flat [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] (about 30 cm in diameter) over medium heat. # When the pan is hot, grease it with a dab of butter (start with about a [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]]), and spread so it melts and coats the pan. The batter may set quickly, so you may need to adjust the volume of butter used for the first few pancakes. # Ladle enough batter into the pan so that you get a large pancake no more than 3 mm thick after spreading it out. # Let the pancake cook until it is dry on the top surface and lightly golden on the bottom. Use a spatula to flip it to the other side. # If you will not be filling the pancake immediately, cook until golden on the other side, then remove and set aside (see notes). If you will be filling the pancake, arrange the ingredients in the center, leaving several centimeters/inches bare all around the filling. Once cooked on the bottom, fold four edges of the pancake into the center to enclose the filling and make a square. Remove and serve hot. # Continue cooking until the rest of the batter is used up. == Notes, tips, and variations == * There is a debate on whether you should include egg in the batter. It seems to act as a stabilizer depending on the quality of the flour used. * If you fully fold the ''galette'' (see image), you can flip it one more time after filling without the risk of the filling escaping. This gives you a little extra time to heat or cook the filling if needed.[[File:Galette_de_Haute_Bretagne.jpg|thumb|Fully folded ''galette'']] * If you choose to pre-cook or buy the pancakes before filling, you should warm them in a pan before filling. To do so, simply butter a skillet over medium heat, place the pancake flat in the pan, and fill/fold as described above. Make sure everything gets well-heated. title: Cookbook:Bánh Mì
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Sandwich recipes
| Yield = 1 sandwich
| Difficulty = 1
| Image = [[File:Banh Mi, Eden Center.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Vietnam|Vietnamese Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|Sandwiches]]

'''''{{lang|vi|Bánh mì}}''''' means 'bread' in [[Vietnamese]], and it often refers to a type of Vietnamese [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|sandwich]]. It may have started as a 'kitchen sink' recipe in [[w:Vietnam|Vietnam]], where various leftovers would be tossed into a [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|sandwich]] to finish them up (like a [[Cookbook:Po' Boy|po' boy]]). {{lang|vi|Bánh mì}} is now sought after by many for its unique and delicious flavours.  There are many different types of ''bánh mì'' sandwiches, ranging from chunked BBQ grilled [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]], sliced pork pâté, and shredded grilled [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], to grilled and smoked [[Cookbook:Seafood|fish]], sardine, meatball, Chinese-style [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]], and tripe.

Choices of bread are also quite varied. It is customary to use a toasted French [[Cookbook:Baguette|baguette]] or French bread, because of the textures these breads provide: Bánh mì tastes best when the outer crust of the bread is firm but not overly hard, and the inner part of the bread is fluffy and light like a yeast roll, that is, one which is not overly dense or spongy. The reason for this is that the crust's firmness provides a barrier for the moisture of the sandwich, and the lightness of the inner bread does not overwhelm the flavors of the sandwich, which would otherwise make the sandwich taste overly 'bready'. Still, no sandwich tastes better than the flavor of the bread, so make sure the bread is fresh and flavorful (preferably one from a bakery). Using a store-bought bread yields unpredictable results as they tend to taste overly processed or they taste like the plastic or paper bag in which they are kept. 

== Ingredients ==
Many different ingredients may be used to make bánh mì. Put in as many as you wish in your sandwich—each is different.

=== Core ingredients ===

* 1 loaf baguette-style [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]]
* [[Cookbook:Julienne|Julienned]] [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]
* Julienned [[Cookbook:Daikon|daikon]] radish
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* Water
* Coconut [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] or white vinegar
* [[Cookbook:Sugar|Sugar]]

=== Standard bánh mì fillings ===
* [[Cookbook:Cilantro|Cilantro (coriander)]] leaves and stems
* Super-thin [[Cookbook:Jalapeño|jalapeño]] [[Cookbook:Slicing|slices]]
* Fresh sliced [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]]

=== Protein fillings ===
* BBQ [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
* BBQ [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]
* Sliced pork pâté
* Sliced pork meatloaf
* Sliced [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]]
* BBQ [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]]
* [[Cookbook:Meatballs|Meatballs]]
* Sliced Chinese/Thai/Vietnamese-style [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]] (waxy kind)
* [[Cookbook:Sardine|Sardines]]
* [[Cookbook:Tripe|Tripe]]
* [[Cookbook:Smoked Salmon|Smoked salmon]]
* Grilled or [[Cookbook:Frying|fried]] whitefish
* [[cookbook:Textured Vegetable Protein|Textured vegetable protein]] (wheat gluten, [[Cookbook:seitan|seitan]], sueyu, suegai - vegetarian fish fillets)
* Seasoned [[cookbook:tofu|tofu]]

=== Optional additional fillings ===
* Sliced [[Cookbook:Turnip|turnip]]
* Sliced [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onion]]s
* Sliced, patted dry [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* Sprigs of [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]]
* Sprigs of [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]]
* Shredded [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]]
* [[Cookbook:Sprout|Sprout]] mix
* [[Cookbook:Lettuce|Lettuce]]

=== Sauces for sandwich ===
* [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Japan|Japanese]] [[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayonnaise]] (Kewpie Mayo - squeeze bottle with a baby on front)
* Mayso ([[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayo]] and [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]])
* Maysocha (mayo, soy sauce, and [[Cookbook:Sriracha|sriracha]] chili sauce)
* Maycha (mayo and sriracha)
* Hot Mom (mayo, Lao Gan Ma Chinese hot sauce)
* Any of the above with [[Cookbook:Lime|lime]] or [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] juice and [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* [[Cookbook:Barbecue Sauce|BBQ sauce]] and mayo

== Procedure ==

=== Pickling the vegetables ===

# Lightly sprinkle the julienned carrot and radish with salt. Let rest 5 min, then rinse with cold water.
# Mix equal parts of water, vinegar with sugar. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], cool, and pour over vegetables.
# Store this mixture in a container in the refrigerator for at least a day before using.

=== Sandwich assembly ===

# [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] a length of baguette lengthwise. Form a trench in each half by either removing the excess bread or compressing it. These depressions are where you will put the filling.
# Toast the bread if desired.
# Spread a layer of desired sauce(s) on each half of the bread.
# Fill the sandwich with any of the desired fillings listed above.
# Serve.

| Image = [[Image:Gimchi.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Korea|Korean Cuisine]]

'''Kimchi''' (김치), also spelled '''kimchee''' or '''gimchi''', is a Korean dish of pickled [[Cookbook:Vegetable|vegetables]], usually [[Cookbook:cabbage|napa cabbage]] or Korean radish and is commonly served as a [[Cookbook:Side dishes|side dish]]. It is usually fermented in a brine of [[Cookbook:Anchovy|anchovy]] sauce, [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Green onion|green onion]], and [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chilli pepper]]. There are countless varieties—at least as many as there are households. The following is a standard recipe for ''baechoo kimchi'' (napa-cabbage kimchi), a common variety and often the first kind of kimchi that jumps to mind for non-Koreans. 

==Ingredients==
*1 head [[Cookbook:Cabbage|napa cabbage]] (baechu, Chinese cabbage, wombok)
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] sea salt (or any coarse salt)
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tbsp|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tsp|tsp]] minced [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Gochugaru|gochugaru]] (Korean chile flakes)
*2 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*¼ cup [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|aekjeot]] (Korean fish sauce)
*½ [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], thinly [[Cookbook:Julienne|julienned]]
*¼ Korean [[Cookbook:Radish|radish]] (muwoo), thinly julienned
*4 [[Cookbook:Green onion|green onions]], cut into 3-cm pieces

==Procedure==
#Quarter the napa cabbage, wash, and drain.
#Combine coarse sea salt and water.
#Put cabbages in salted water and take out one at a time to get salt down.
#Add cabbages to a container. Pour salted water over top, and set aside for at least 6–8 hours (overnight is great). The cabbage should be soft enough to bend.
#Wash cabbages and drain well.
#Combine gochugaru, salt, sugar, jeot gal (Korean fish sauce), minced garlic, and minced ginger.
#Mix the onion, carrot, radish, and green onion into the chilli powder mixture.
#Take one cabbage, and stuff the above mixture between every layer.
#Try to fold the cabbage in half. With 2 outer leaves, wrap the whole thing securely.
#Put cabbages in an airtight container, and let it sit at room temperature overnight.
#Refrigerate for 2–3 days at minimum. After a few days, you will notice some liquid. This is totally normal and a sign that the kimchi is ripening. 
#Enjoy your kimchi!
==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Korean radishes are large (about ½ to 1 kilogram). Japanese (daikon) radishes or a larger quantity of small European radishes could substitute.
*The brine can be varied to include many other ingredients. Be creative.
*The aekjeot can be replaced with moderate amounts of saeujeot (Korean salted tiny shrimp), raw butterfish, or raw oysters. Seafood can also be left out entirely, although an appropriate amount of salt needs to be added in place of missing jeot gal. Alternative flavors can include Asian pears or tangerines.

title: Cookbook:Butter Tart
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert| Yield = 24 tarts|time=70 minutes|difficulty=2}}
__NOTOC__
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:North American cuisines|North American Cuisines]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Canada|Canadian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Ontario|Cuisine of Ontario]] | [[Cookbook:Desserts| Desserts]]

'''Butter tarts (tartes au sucre)''' are an extremely common dessert in Canada. Many versions are made; some are gooey while some are not, and different nuts, fruits, and other fillings can be used. Similar tarts can be found in the culinary traditions of [[Cookbook:Scottish cuisine|Scotland]] and [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|France]].

== Ingredients ==

=== Dough ===

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Shortening|shortening]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
* ¾ cup boiling water
* 3 ½ cups [[Cookbook:Pastry Flour|pastry flour]] or 3 cups [[Cookbook:Flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

=== Filling ===

* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1 ½ cups [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Corn Syrup|corn syrup]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Currant|currants]] or [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of salt
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Vanilla Extract|vanilla extract]]

== Procedure ==

=== Dough ===

# [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] the shortening, butter, and hot water together until creamy. 
# While still warm, sift in the flour, baking powder, and salt. Mix gently until a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] forms. Try not to [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] it while forming it into a large ball. 
# Separate the dough into two equal portions and chill 20 to 40 minutes.
# Divide the dough into two dozen equal balls. [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] each ball into a flat disc.

=== Tarts ===

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (175˚C).
# Beat the eggs well. Add sugar, syrup, and melted butter and beat again.
# Add the currants, walnuts, vinegar, salt, and vanilla extract and mix vigorously.
# Put a small amount of cornmeal into small [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|tartlet pans]], or count out 24 cupcake papers.
# Fit the flat circles of pie crust into the pans, or fit them into cupcake papers and insert them into the pans.
# Fill the shells ⅔ full with the prepared filling.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] until the pastry is light brown (about 20 minutes).
# Remove from the oven and let cool.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* For runnier tarts, cook for 15 to 17 minutes. You can also adjust the filling ingredients to 1 cup of corn syrup and 1 cup of brown sugar.
* Try replacing the currants with [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]], or omit entirely.
* Try replacing the walnuts with [[Cookbook:Pecan|pecans]], or omit entirely.
* Try drizzling 4 oz (120 g) melted [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]] over the cooked tarts.
* This recipe (both the tarts and the pie crust) is a century-old recipe from rural North Western Ontario.
* If the top of the tart hasn't frothed while baking and formed a cream coloured crunchy top it means there was too much time between when you beat the mixture and when it started baking. If you have to do multiple batches in the oven with the same mixture, be sure to keep the batter cool and keep stirring it to make sure the second batch has the traditional crispy top.

== Links ==

* Recipe source: http://www.boutell.com/vegetarian/butter-tarts.html

title: Cookbook:Cabbage Rolls in Yogurt Sauce (Sarmi)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Cabbage recipes
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[File:Sarmi.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Sarmi''' is a [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Bulgaria|Bulgarian]] dish of stuffed [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]] leaves, which shows significant [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Greece|Greek]] influences. For a gathering you may wish to consider presenting these somewhat 'white' rolls side-by-side with a dish of cabbage rolls in tomato sauce (see [[Cookbook:Cabbage Rolls in Tomato Sauce (Holubtsi)|Cabbage Rolls in Tomato Sauce (Holubtsi)]]).

==Ingredients==
*500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (about 1 ⅛ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) minced (ground) [[Cookbook:Veal|veal]] or [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]]
*300 g (about ¾ lb) minced (ground) [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
*1 bunch of [[Cookbook:Spring Onion|spring onions]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] uncooked [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]]
*[[Cookbook:Parsley|Parsley]]
*[[Cookbook:Mint|Mint]]
*[[Cookbook:Paprika|Paprika]] (optional)
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
*30–40 [[Cookbook:Grape|grape]] or [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]] leaves (depending on the size, a substantially smaller number of leaves may be needed)
*100 g [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or ½ cup [[Cookbook:Sunflower Oil|sunflower oil]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the vine or cabbage leaves in salted water until they look cooked and are just bendable enough to roll. Drain and allow to cool during the following steps.
#Lightly [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] the finely chopped onions in a small amount of oil, and stir in a teaspoon or more of paprika. 
#Add the meat, rice, pepper, mint, and finely chopped parsley, then cook until the meat looks almost done.
#Add ¾ cup of water, bring to a boil, then immediately cover and reduce heat to a bare minimum for 10 minutes, until the water is absorbed by the rice. Uncover and fluff as needed with a small spatula or spoon. Allow to cool to handling temperature.
#Put 1 teaspoon of the meat mixture on each leaf and make into a rolled, fully enclosed, package, similar to a small egg roll. A bit more filling can be used if you are using large cabbage leaves, but try to make all the rolls somewhat uniform in size.
#Arrange the rolls in a saucepan, add 1½ cups of warm water, cover, and simmer gently over low heat.
#In the meantime, mix the yogurt with a bit of paprika for color (or omit if you wish to keep the dish somewhat white in color), and other spices as you desire.
#When rolls are done, allow to cool a bit, gently transfer to a dish, and add the yogurt mixture to coat. 
#Serve with vegetables of your choice. Enjoy!

title: Cookbook:Burrito
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Tex-Mex recipes
| Image = [[File:Papa chevos burrito.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Cuisine of Mexico]]

A '''burrito''' is a flour [[Cookbook:Tortilla|tortilla]] filled with some filling. Generally, the filling includes meat such as [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]], [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], or [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], but also often includes beans and/or rice. Vegetarian burritos are also common.

==Ingredients==

===Base===
* Large [[Cookbook:Flour Tortilla|flour tortilla]]
* [[Cookbook:Bean|Beans]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Rice|Rice]] (optional)

===Possible fillings===
{{div col|3}}
* [[cookbook:Pork|Pork]]
* Ground or shredded [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]]
* Ground or shredded [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]
* Flaked [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]]
* [[Cookbook:Shrimp|Shrimp]]
* [[Cookbook:Chorizo|Chorizo]]
* Refried beans
* Seasoning (e.g. [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]], [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]], [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]], [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chili]]s, etc.)
* Picadillo
* [[Cookbook:Tomato|Tomatoes]]
* Black [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]]
* [[Cookbook:Lettuce|Lettuce]]
* [[Cookbook:Cilantro|Cilantro]]
* [[Cookbook:Avocado|Avocado]]
* [[Cookbook:Onion|Onion]], raw or sautéed
* [[Cookbook:Garlic|Garlic]], raw or sautéed
* [[Cookbook:Mushroom|Mushrooms]]
* Chiles
* Shredded cheese
* Sour cream
* [[Cookbook:Salsa|Salsa]]
* [[Cookbook:Guacamole|Guacamole]]
{{div col end}}

==Procedure==

===Beans===
#If using dried beans, wash them and examine them for any rocks, then soak overnight in plenty of water. Discard the soak water before cooking—your pot plants will love it!
#Cook the beans until soft:
#*If using a stove-top method, [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] them in lots of water until they are very soft. You'll need to cook the beans a very long time on very low heat. You may add salt or black pepper to the water. You may add onion halves or a [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]] bone, which you can remove at the end. Changing the water from time to time will reduce the risk of [[w:Flatulence|gas]]. Expect the cooking to take at least 3 hours, if not 6 or more.
#*If using a [[Cookbook:Pressure Cooking|pressure cooker]], place the beans and some flavoring (typically [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]) in enough water to cover all the beans fully, and bring to pressure.  Keep the pressure for about 20 minutes, turn off the heat, and let the pressure fall naturally (about 15 minutes).
#If desired, smash the beans, perhaps with a potato masher.
# Season with spices as desired.
=== Meat ===
#Get a large wide pot or tall-sided [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]].
#Add any uncooked meats to the pan and fry, stirring to ensure it browns all over. If using a ground (minced) meat, break it up as it cooks. Drain any excess grease.
#Add spices and other flavorings as necessary.

===Rice===
#If using rice, rinse rice well until the water runs clear.
#Add 2 cups of water per 1 cup of rice, bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes.
#Set aside with the lid secured for at least 5 minutes before use.

===Assembly===
# Soften the tortillas by heating them up. Use a small amount of oil to prevent sticking if heating in a pan that isn't non-stick. If heating them in an [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]], cover with [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminium foil]] to protect the tortillas from moisture loss.
# Position a tortilla flat on a suitable surface such as a kitchen counter top.
# Place your desired fillings on the tortilla in any order, leaving a border of at least a couple inches all around.
# Fold the bottom flap up. A small flap will allow the fillings to escape from the finished burrito.
# Bring the side up and over your filling. Tucking the edge of the tortilla under your filling is an excellent extra step.
# Create a small fold with the remaining side of the tortilla. This is the ''key'' to maintaining burrito integrity. Failure is a given if you do not follow this step! The small, diagonal flap is an extra "lock" for the bottom flap of the tortilla—without it, the weight of the filling has the power to force the bottom flap right out of itself.
# Bring the remaining tortilla flap over the filling.
# Eat with confidence, though the fillings may be very hot.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* 12-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] tortillas are suggested. If you can find bigger tortillas, use them!
* When using beans alone, you might want to add up to 20% home-[[Cookbook:Rendering|rendered]] [[Cookbook:Lard|lard]] (lard substitutions are obvious, but will lack flavor).
* Common ingredients in Mexican burritos include fried pork (carnitas), marinated grilled steak (carne asada), marinated grilled chicken (pollo asado), stewed pork (al pastor), pork in green chile sauce (chile verde), fried [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]], beef [[Cookbook:Tongue|tongue]] (lengua), beef [[Cookbook:Brain|brains]] (cabeza), [[Cookbook:Goat|goat]] meat (birria), [[Cookbook:Tripe|tripe]] (tripas), and ''chicharrones'' (fried pork rinds, stewed).
* The Mission burrito generally combines whole beans (sometimes refried beans), Mexican rice, traditional Mexican meats (sometimes ground beef), with optional grated cheese, sour cream, guacamole, sliced jalapenos, salsa fresca/salsa cruda, and sometimes shredded lettuce.
* A smothered ("wet") burrito is generally a Mission burrito with enchilada sauce, either "red" or "green", poured over it, with grated cheese topping it. it is meant to be eaten with a knife and fork, not held in the hand as other burritos can be.

title: Cookbook:Buttermilk Fried Chicken with Pan Gravy
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Chicken recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Southern cuisine|Southern cuisine (USA)]] | [[Cookbook:Fried Chicken|Fried Chicken]] 

'''Fried chicken''' is a Southern main meal in the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|USA]], served often at "Sunday dinner" ("dinner" being the midday meal for many Southerners) or church "suppers" ("supper" being the term for the evening meal). Recipes are legion; every family has one handed down. 

== Ingredients ==

=== Chicken ===
*1 whole [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard powder]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|cayenne powder]]
*2 tsp cracked [[Cookbook:Pepper|black peppercorns]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
*1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
*[[Cookbook:Flour|Flour]] seasoned with herbs and spices (e.g. pepper, cayenne, salt, ground coriander, cinnamon, thyme, oregano)
*Oil (e.g. peanut or corn oil)

=== Gravy ===
* [[Cookbook:Oil|Oil]]
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] (or [[Cookbook:Green onion|shallots]]), [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Garlic|clove of garlic]]
* 3–4 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 3 cups [[Cookbook:Stock|chicken stock]] (or 2 cups stock + 1 cup [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]])
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

== Procedure ==

=== Chicken ===
# Cut the chicken into 8–10 pieces.
# Combine the buttermilk and spices, and [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] the chicken pieces for 4 hours in the mixture.
# Take each chicken piece out of the marinade and allow it to drip dry for a few seconds. Then, dredge it in seasoned flour. An easy way to dredge involves putting flour and seasonings in a small plastic bag, dropping the piece in, and shaking.
# Let the pieces rest (separately; do not stack) for about 10 minutes. Then dredge them again. The first dredging absorbs the buttermilk marinade. The second dredging gives a seasoned flour outer coat.
# Heat the oil in a deep, wide pan. When oil is smoking hot, drop chicken pieces into the pan, and be careful to not overcrowd (pieces should not touch; fry in multiple batches). After 3 or 4 minutes, turn the chicken, and reduce the heat. Let the chicken fry for 20–25 minutes, turning the pieces every few minutes. When the chicken is a deep golden-brown, and the juices run clear, it's done. The chicken will continue to cook after being removed from the pan, so err on the side of "just about done".
# Drain the chicken on [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|absorbent paper]] or cloth. If you are not serving the chicken immediately, place it in a lightly-warmed [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]], uncovered, separately (not stacked).

===Gravy===
# Pour off the accumulated oil from the pan, reserving 3–4 tablespoons and all the flour and chicken residue. Keeping the pan on medium flame, add the chopped onion and garlic. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] for a few minutes. Whisk in 3–4 tablespoons of flour, and keep stirring until the mixture becomes light to medium brown. Do not burn.
# [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] in 3 cups of chicken stock. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] over low heat, covered, for 15 minutes. Salt and pepper to taste.
# Serve chicken with [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] and some green vegetables. Spoon gravy over rice and chicken.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The spice mix isn't fixed. You can use more or less as desired.

'''Butter tea''', known as ''Po Cha'', is a traditional drink of the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Tibet|Tibetans]] and is also consumed in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Bhutan|Bhutan]]. Butter tea is an indispensable part of Tibetan life. Before work, a Tibetan will down several bowlfuls of this tangy beverage, and it is always served to guests. Since butter is the main ingredient, butter tea is a very warming drink and a good antidote to the cold, so it is especially suited to high altitudes. 

According to the Tibetan custom, butter tea is drunk in separate sips, and after each sip the host refills the bowl to the brim. Thus the guest never drains his bowl yet it is constantly topped up. If the visitor does not wish to drink, the best thing to do is leave the tea untouched until the time comes to leave and then drain the bowl. In this way etiquette is observed and the host will not be offended.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] regular [[Cookbook:Tea Leaf|black tea leaves]] (preferably [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Nepal|Nepalese]] or [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]])
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] whole [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] (or 1½ cup [[Cookbook:Half and Half|half-and-half]] + 1½ cup water)
* 2 tablespoons unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

== Procedure == 
# Boil tea with milk for 2–10 minutes, depending upon the strength of tea desired
# Strain into tea cups. 
# Add butter and salt. Stir thoroughly, ideally by carefully using a blender, and serve.

'''Cachapas''' are traditionally made with fresh corn, and are a summer favorite, but this easy recipe uses canned cream corn, pancake mix, and whatever cheese you have on hand. Try this simple appetizer for a taste of Venezuela whenever you like.

== Procedure ==
# Blend all the ingredients together in a [[cookbook:blender|blender]]. The mix should become thick and heavy. If not, add more corn.

title: Cookbook:Börek (Turkish Filled Pastries)
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Recipes for pastries
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Turkey|Cuisine of Turkey]]

'''Börek''' is a general term in Turkish cuisine that applies to a family of [[Cookbook:Pastry|pastries]] with about fifty different members.  They have in common the fact that they are all pastry layers of some type enclosing a filling. There are two basic methods; one consists of rolling out very thin sheets of dough, called [[w:en:yufka|yufka]] in Turkish and [[w:en:phyllo|phyllo]] in Greek. The other main type of börek, called ''[[w:en:nemse börek|nemse börek]]'' in Turkish, uses a dough very similar to ''[[Cookbook:Puff pastry|pâte feuilletée]]'', in which the dough is layered with butter, folded, and rolled out several times.<ref>Algar, Ayla Esen (1985) ''The Complete Book of Turkish Cooking'' {{#isbn:0-710-30334-3}}</ref>

The following recipe describes the procedure required to prepare triangle-shaped börek from commercially produced phyllo. Links to recipes for fillings are listed at the end of the recipe.

==Ingredients==

=== Fillings ===
*[[Cookbook:Cheese Filling for Peynirli Börek|Peynirli börek]] (white cheese filling)
*Kıymalı börek (minced meat filling)
*Tavuklu börek (chicken filling)
*Ispanaklı börek (spinach filling)

=== Assembly ===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] prepared filling (see above)
* 1 box yufka/[[Cookbook:Phyllo Dough|phyllo]] pastry sheets<ref>Available from Turkish, Greek, Armenian and Middle-Eastern grocers, among others, as well as some supermarkets.</ref>
* Melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or high-quality [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]<ref>e.g. peanut, hazelnut, walnut, almond, grapeseed. Avoid anything with a greasy taste such as corn oil.</ref>
[[Image:Wrapping börek.jpg|thumbnail|right|250px|Assembling börek triangles]]
==Procedure==
#Remove the phyllo sheets from the container. Unfold carefully so as not to break them. Lay them flat and cover with a clean, damp tea towel to prevent them from drying out—this is important.
# Working quickly, cut the phyllo into lengthwise thirds (step 1 in the diagram). Lay one of these out and cover the other two with the damp tea towel.
# Brush the strip of phyllo with the melted butter. Place a heaped [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoonful]] of filling on one end of the strip (step 2 in the diagram).
#Fold the right lower corner upward over the filling to form a triangle (step 3 in the diagram).
#Now fold the right upper corner over to the left (step 4 in the diagram).
#Continue folding in this manner until you reach the end of the strip.
#Trim of any excess dough and seal the edges by rubbing a damp finger over the dough and pressing the edge of the triangle where the strip ends.
#[[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] in oil at 340°F until golden brown or [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] at 350°F for 15 minutes.<ref>Prewrapped, uncooked börek freezes well. To cook, bake at 325ºF for 30 minutes.  Do not deep-fry frozen foods.  Splattering oil can cause burns and fires.  You may sautée them in a covered pan 2 or 3 at a time.  Hold the cover in front of your face as you place each börek in the pan.</ref>

title: Cookbook:Buttermilk Biscuits
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Biscuit recipes| Yield = 12 ea. 3-inch biscuits|servings=6|time=40 minutes|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}}

'''Buttermilk Biscuits''' are a variety of [[Cookbook:Biscuits|biscuits]] using cultured buttermilk as the primary liquid.  Other biscuits use milk, or a combination of milk and cream, or powdered milk and water as the liquid.  Since buttermilk is an acidic ingredient, typically an increased amount of baking soda is used, and baking powder is reduced or eliminated.  This recipe is for one variety of Southern-style (U.S.) hand-rolled biscuits, which are formed in the hands as opposed to being rolled and cut, but the shaping style is optional.  These biscuits are incredibly light and fluffy.

==Ingredients==

==Procedure==

#Move oven rack to highest position, and preheat to 450 °F.
# Grease the bottom of a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|cookie sheet]] with shortening or butter.

=== Dough ===
# Mix sifted self-rising flour, soda, salt, and sugar (if using) in a bowl.
# Using a [[Cookbook:Pastry Blender|pastry blender]] or [[Cookbook:Fork|fork]], [[Cookbook:Mixing#Cutting|cut in]] shortening until evenly distributed, with no flakes of shortening bigger than a green pea remaining. It will look like [[Cookbook:Cornmeal|cornmeal]] but coarser.
# Using a large spoon, [[Cookbook:Folding|fold]] in ½ cup buttermilk, then another ½ cup to moisten the flour evenly. [[Cookbook:Mixing#Stirring|Stir]] only long enough to moisten the mixture sufficiently. If dry flour remains after a few stirs, add the remaining 2 Tbsp buttermilk.
# Let mixture rest and rise 3–5 minutes. The mixture should be quite moist, but not pourable. If the mixture seems too dry, add more buttermilk.

=== Shaping ===
# Pour ½ cup all-purpose flour in a plate.
# Assuming you are right-handed, grab a teaspoon or so of the all-purpose flour in your left hand, and make sure your inner palm is mostly covered.
# With your right hand, using a soup spoon, scoop about 3 Tbsp of the biscuit mixture in your left hand.
# Working over the flour plate, Grab some flour with your right hand and sprinkle on top of the scoop of biscuit mixture. The wet mixture will not stick to your hands if enough flour is used.
# Begin gently tossing the biscuit back and forth between your floured hands until the outside of the biscuit is coated lightly with flour. The excess flour will fall off your hands back into the plate.
# Gently shape the dough into a fairly smooth ball, place on the greased biscuit sheet with sides touching, and press to flatten slightly to about 1-inch high.
# Grab a little more flour and continue with the next biscuit.

=== Baking ===
# Delicately but generously [[Cookbook:Brushing|brush]] the biscuits with melted butter.
# Bake in the preheated [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] for 12–16 minutes, depending on the biscuit size, until tops and bottoms are nicely browned.
# Serve immediately with softened butter. See notes section for additional ideas.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

=== Ingredient notes ===

* If cultured buttermilk is not available, similar results can be obtained by mixing 2 Tbsp lemon juice with enough [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] to make 1 cup, and letting it stand 10 minutes.
* [[Cookbook:Lard|Lard]] or [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] may be used instead of shortening.
* If self-rising flour is not available, substitute all-purpose flour and add baking powder and salt.  An alternative is to add baking soda and [[Cookbook:Cream of Tartar|cream of tartar]]. If desired, use only baking soda as leavening. This is acceptable since the buttermilk is acidic.
* [[Cookbook:Cream|Cream]] may be substituted for ¼ cup of the buttermilk.
* Use all-purpose flour for rolling to avoid tasting the leavening in self-rising flour.
* The preferred flour is Southern "biscuit" flour, a soft wheat flour with a protein content of 2 g per ¼ cup.  Non-Southern flours, at 3 g protein per ¼ cup, are acceptable.
* For a traditional Southern topping, mix equal parts softened butter and [[Cookbook:Molasses|molasses]].

=== Procedural notes ===
* If your hands become sticky when rolling biscuits, wash and dry your hands and use more flour.
* Biscuits do not need to be [[Cookbook:Kneading|kneaded]]. In fact, if you knead the biscuits, you will likely incorporate too much flour to get a high, fluffy biscuit.
* If using a convection oven with the fan on, the oven rack may be in the center position.
* Do not skip the resting step, as the flour needs a brief period to accept the moisture.
* The sugar and salt may be dissolved into the buttermilk if desired. The sugar may be omitted altogether.
* If you are unsure if a biscuit is done, use an instant read [[Cookbook:Thermometer|thermometer]] and remove when internal temperature reaches 205–210 °F.
* Butter the baked biscuits immediately so the butter melts. Always used softened or melted butter as refrigerated butter is too hard and will tear the biscuit.
* Low-protein flours require less buttermilk than higher protein flours. You will have to adjust the liquid in the recipe according to the protein content of the flour, the type of fat used (butter is part liquid), the humidity of the flour, and the desired texture of the final biscuit. In general, the mixture you roll should be quite moist, but not pourable.

* If the dough isn't moist enough to stick to your unfloured hands, the dough mixture isn't moist enough for this style of biscuit. The biscuits will taste fine, but will not be as fluffy.
* Instead of brushing the butter on the biscuits before baking, you can pour the butter slowly over each biscuit, letting the excess drip between the biscuits. Use your fingers to evenly coat each biscuit top with butter.
* Thin biscuits can be made with the same recipe, except you will use less buttermilk and [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll out]] ½ inch thick on a floured board. Cut with a floured [[Cookbook:Cookie Cutter|biscuit cutter]].
* To save time, spread out all the biscuit mixture onto the pan using a spatula, and with floured hands, pat the "cake" to an even 1-inch height. Bake as usual.

=== Alternative dough mixing procedure ===

# Mix dry ingredients in a large bowl. Make a well in the center.
# Put all the shortening in the center of the flour. Add ¾ cup buttermilk, and using one hand, cream the buttermilk and shortening until mostly smooth.
# Gradually pull in flour from the sides, until the appropriate the flour has been incorporated. Add more buttermilk and flour as needed.
# Shape dough by hand or roll out on floured surface and cut with biscuit cutter, dipping cutter in all-purpose flour when cutting each biscuit.

== Warnings ==
* Biscuits are best consumed immediately. However, left-over biscuits can be heated or toasted. Buttering immediately helps for a better-tasting left-over biscuit.
* Do not use bread flour (protein content 4 g per ¼ cup) as the biscuits will not be light and fluffy.

This recipe is loosely derived from the animated television show ''Chowder''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Burple Nurples (food) |url=https://chowder.fandom.com/wiki/Burple_Nurples_(food) |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=Chowder Fan Club |language=en}}</ref>. == Ingredients ==
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
*2 sticks [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]

title: Cookbook:Béarnaise Sauce
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Sauce recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sauces|Sauces]]

'''Béarnaise sauce''' is an egg-yolk and butter emulsion in the [[Cookbook:Hollandaise|Hollandaise]] family of sauces. 

== Ingredients ==
* 30 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]]) tarragon [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 30 ml (2 tablespoons) [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]] [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] or dry white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg yolk|egg yolks]]
* 75–100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (⅓–½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] / 3–4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] (warm but not hot)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|Cayenne pepper]] to taste
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] freshly-chopped [[Cookbook:Tarragon|tarragon]]
* 1 tablespoon freshly-chopped [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]

== Procedure ==

# Put the vinegars, shallot, and herbs in a small [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]; [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until reduced to 1 tablespoon. This is the flavorful glaze. Strain and set aside to cool.
# Add the egg yolks and [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] until the ribbon stage with a balloon whisk.
# Place the bowl over a pan of hot water (a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double boiler]]) and continue whisking. Gradually add the melted butter, whisking until the sauce thickens and all the butter has been added.
# Season and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Do not use dried tarragon; if you cannot find fresh tarragon, use a sprig from the vinegar bottle.
* To find the right temperature to [[Cookbook:Emulsification|emulsify]] the egg mixture and the butter, the bowl should be just hot enough so that you can still touch it. If you cannot hold the bowl it is too hot. Be forewarned that this trick may not always work depending on a multitude of conditions.

==References==
* Julia Child (1961), ''Mastering the Art of French Cooking'', Alfred A. Knopf

title: Cookbook:Burmese Pork Curry
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Curry recipes|servings=4|time=2 hours|difficulty=2}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Burma|Cuisine of Burma]] | [[Cookbook:Meat|Meat]] | [[Cookbook:Curry|Curry]]

'''Burmese pork curry''' is a light, flavoursome pork dish.

== Ingredients ==

* 8 dried red [[Cookbook:Chiles|chillis]]
* 2.5 [[Cookbook:cm|cm]] fresh root [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], crushed
* [[Cookbook:Lemongrass|Lemongrass]] stalks, finely [[Cookbook:chopping|chopped]]
* 15 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]] (1 [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tbsp]]) fresh [[Cookbook:Galangal|galangal]], chopped
* 15 ml (1 tbsp) [[Cookbook:Shrimp paste|shrimp paste]]
* 30 ml (2 tbsp) fine [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 675 [[Cookbook:gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] into chunks
* 600 ml (2½ [[Cookbook:cup|cup]]) water
* 10 ml (2 [[Cookbook:teaspoon|tsp]]) ground [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]]
* 5 ml (1 tsp) dark [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* 200 [[Cookbook:gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Green Bean|French (green) beans]]
* 5 ml (1 tsp) brown sugar
* 45 ml (3 tbsp) [[Cookbook:Tamarind|tamarind]] juice or 5 ml (1 tsp) tamarind pulp concentrate
* 15 ml (1 tbsp) [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallots]], finely chopped
* 15 ml (1 tbsp) [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|fish sauce]]
* Fresh red chillis, to [[Cookbook:garnish|garnish]]

== Procedure ==

# Soak the dried chilli in warm water for 20 minutes.
# Crush the ginger, chilli, lemongrass, and galangal in a [[Cookbook:mortar and pestle|mortar and pestle]] until they form a coarse paste.
# Add the shrimp paste and fine sugar, and continue grinding to a dark grainy paste.
# Place the pork in a [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] or large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] over medium heat, and [[Cookbook:Mixing#Stirring|stir]] in the curry paste until the meat is well coated.
# Cook the pork over a low heat, stirring occasionally, until the meat changes colour and [[Cookbook:rendering|renders]] some of its fat, and the curry has started to release its aroma.
# Stir in the turmeric, water, and soy sauce, then [[Cookbook:simmer|simmer]] gently, uncovered, for 40 minutes until the meat is tender.
# [[Cookbook:steaming|Steam]] the beans separately for about 10 minutes.
# Stir the sugar, tamarind, garlic, shallots, and fish sauce into the meat until the sugar and tamarind are dissolved.
# [[Cookbook:garnish|Garnish]] with the fresh chillis and steamed beans, and serve immediately.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The pork can have some of its fat trimmed, but should have some remaining to [[Cookbook:Rendering|render]] into the sauce as it cooks.
* Instead of galangal, additional root ginger can be used.

'''Béchamel''' or '''French white sauce''' (French: ''Sauce Béchamel'') is a white rich [[Cookbook:Sauces|sauce]], used as a basic sauce for many dishes.<ref>{{cite book|title=Mrs. Beeton's Book of Household Management|last=Beeton|first=Isabella|author-link=|isbn=|publisher=|date=1907|location=|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Mrs._Beeton%27s_Book_of_Household_Management/Chapter_X|page=220}}</ref>

* 700 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1¼ pints) of [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] (or white [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]])

* 1 small [[Cookbook:Bouquet Garni|bouquet-garni]] ([[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]])

# Put the milk into a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] and place on the [[Cookbook:Cooktop|hob]]. Add the onion or shallot, the bouquet garni, peppercorns, mace, and bay leaf, and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].

'''Béchamel''' is one of the five "mother [[Cookbook:Sauces|sauces]]" in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|French cuisine]]. As a basic white sauce, it can be used as the base of many other sauces.

==Ingredients==
* 50 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 50 g (¼ cup) white wheat [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] (type 405)
* 1000 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (4½ cups) whole [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] (>3% milk fat)
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]

*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

==Procedure==

#In a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], melt the butter over medium-low heat. Whisk in the flour to make a [[Cookbook:Roux|roux]].
#Cook the roux over gentle heat for 3–5 minutes, but do not brown. This cooking is necessary to remove the floury taste.
#In a separate pot, begin heating the milk. Peel the onion, but do not cut it.
#Add the onion and bay leaf into the pot with the milk. Keep stirring until milk is heated to 80°C. Do not let the milk adhere and cook to pot bottom.
#Remove onion and bay leaf.
#Gradually whisk the heated milk into cooked roux. Add salt and pepper to taste.
#Stir and cook for 15 minutes until thickened. No lumps should be present.

title: Cookbook:Cachupa (Cape Verdean Corn Stew)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Stew recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Cachupa''' is a popular dish eaten throughout West Africa. It requires a lot of time to prepare.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] [[Cookbook:Corned Beef|corned beef]] brisket, cut into cubes
* 1½ pound [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] pork, cut into big chunks
* 3 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] apple cider or white [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 2 fresh [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] powdered smoked paprika
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] or to taste
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]] or to taste
* 3 tablespoons crushed [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] feijao Pedro beans (rock [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]])
* 3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 2 medium-size [[Cookbook:Onions|onions]], neatly [[Cookbook:Chop|chopped]]
* 2 large beef bouillon cubes
* 3 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* About 18 cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]<nowiki/>y
* 2 cups dry yellow [[Cookbook:Hominy|hominy]], well-rinsed
*1 cup cranberry [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]]
* 1¼ cup large white [[Cookbook:Fava Bean|fava beans]]
* 1 medium size [[Cookbook:Cassava|madioca or yuca]]
* 4 cups [[Cookbook:Collard Greens|collard greens]] or [[Cookbook:Kale|kale]], rinsed and chopped
* 2 pounds [[Cookbook:Chorizo|chourico]] or linguica [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]], rinsed and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] into rounds

== Procedure ==

# Season the corned beef and salt pork the night before with vinegar, bay leaves, smoked paprika, salt, black pepper, and 2 tablespoons crushed garlic. Let the meat [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] in the refrigerator overnight.
# [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|Soak]] the beans overnight as well.
# In a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], heat the olive oil over medium heat and add the neatly chopped onions and the remaining tablespoon of garlic. Transfer the bay leaves from the seasoned meat to the saucepan. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] the onions until fragrant.
# Add the marinated meat to the saucepan and let brown for about 10 minutes (5 minutes for each side). Remove the meat from the saucepan and set aside.
#Add the tomato paste and some of the crushed bouillon cubes to the saucepan. [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] until smooth. 
#Add the meat back to the saucepan, then cover with water. Cover the pot and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
#Stir in the hominy, bring to a boil, and reduce the heat to low. Cover and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 1 hour. Make sure there is enough water in the saucepan, and check on the hominy about every 20 minutes to give it a stir.
#Remove the meat from the saucepan and shred it by lightly dragging a fork against it. This step is optional but can help break up some of the pieces of meat to make more space in the saucepan for the remaining ingredients.
#Add the meat back to the saucepan, stir it again and add the cranberry beans, fava beans, yuca, and greens. If the ingredients seem too bulky, add about half of the greens at first and let it cook for about 5 minutes, then add the remaining ones. Let everything cook for about 50 minutes.
#Add the chourico, and let cook for about 20 minutes.
#Stir and taste the cachupa, then adjust the seasoning as desired. Leave it to simmer for another 10–15 minutes.
#Remove from the heat, and let the cachupa rest, covered, for 20 minutes.
#Enjoy with any complimentary or favourite side dish of your choice.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* When preparing this meal, it is advisable to have a kettle of boiling water at hand throughout the cooking process so more water can be added at any stage when needed—do not use cold water.
* You can also use white hominy instead of yellow; it all depends on your preference, although most people prefer to use the yellow hominy.

title: Cookbook:Bánh Chưng
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
|Category   = Vietnamese recipes
|Servings   = 10–15
|Time       = 18 hours
|Difficulty = 3
|Image      = [[Image:Nguyen lieu banh chung.jpg|300px]]
}}{{recipe}}

'''Bánh chưng''' (literally "steamed cake") is a traditional Vietnamese dish made from glutinous rice, mung beans and pork,<ref>{{Cite web |last=pasgo.vn |title=Sự tích bánh chưng bánh dày:Nguồn gốc ý nghĩa sâu xa của bánh truyền thống |trans-title=The story of Chung cake and Day cake: The origin and profound meaning of traditional cakes |url=https://pasgo.vn/blog/su-tich-banh-trung-banh-day-nguon-goc-y-nghia-sau-xa-cua-banh-truyen-thong-hoamkt-124-5655 |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=pasgo.vn |language=Vietnamese}}</ref> all wrapped in ''lá dong'' (''Stachyphrynium placentarium'') and tied tightly with strings. It is traditionally eaten during Lunar New Year ({{w|Tết|''Tết''}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bánh Chưng biểu tượng văn hoá trong ngày Tết cổ truyền Việt |trans-title=Bánh Chưng – A Cultural Symbol of Vietnam’s Traditional Lunar New Year (Tết) |url=https://banhbaominh.com/banh-chung-bieu-tuong-van-hoa-trong-ngay-tet/#:~:text=%C4%91%E1%BB%83%20g%C3%B3i%20b%C3%A1nh.-,Chu%E1%BA%A9n%20b%E1%BB%8B%20nguy%C3%AAn%20li%E1%BB%87u,ti%E1%BA%BFng%20ho%E1%BA%B7c%20%C4%91%E1%BB%83%20qua%20%C4%91%C3%AAm. |access-date=3 February 2026 |website=banhbaominh |language=vi}}</ref>

Bánh chưng is often eaten with pickled onions (dưa hành), pickled vegetables in fish sauce (dưa món), or dipped in sugar for a sweet treat. It can also be sliced, pan fried until golden, and served with sugar or sweet chili sauce.

== Ingredients ==
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Mung Bean|mung beans]], washed and soaked in water for 4 hours, or better overnight
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] belly (both lean pork and pork fat), cut in large cubes
* 2½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2½ tsp freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Black pepper|black pepper]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] fried [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 3 shallots, [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|fish sauce]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] banana leaves (fresh or thawed)
* 5½ cups sticky [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]], washed and soaked in water overnight

== Procedure ==
# Place the mung beans in a pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil.
# Reduce to a simmer, and cook for about 20 minutes until the beans are soft and easily mashable.
# Mash the beans into a paste. Season to taste with 1 tsp salt, fried shallots, 1 tsp pepper and vegetable oil.
# Season the meat with ½ tsp salt and 1½ tsp pepper, and combine with the shallots and fish sauce. Mix well and let it marinate for a few hours.
# Spread about 1 cup of mashed mung bean onto plastic wrap, add a few pieces of lean pork and pork fat, and shape it into a round or squared piece.
# Tear the banana leaves into very large pieces(around 18–20 inches).
# Season the soaked rice with a pinch of salt.
# Lay out two sheets of partially overlapping banana leaves on a flat surface. Place 1 cup of sticky rice at the center of the leaves. Place the fillings on top of the rice and then cover it up with another cup of sticky rice. Fold the leaves and wrap it up tightly like a present.
# To prevent water penetrating into the cake during the boiling process, it is important to wrap up the cake a second time. For the inner layer, make sure that the darker side of the banana leaf faces the rice so that it can tint the cake with a nice subtle green color later on. However, for the outer layer, the darker side of the banana leaf should face outside to give it a beautiful green package.
# After wrapping, tie the cake tightly with twines.
# Arrange the cakes tightly in a large stockpot and fill with water. Bring the stockpot to a boil and let it simmer for about 6 to 8 hours until the cakes feel plump and the rice is congealed.
# To serve, untie and unwrap the cakes, and cut into pieces with a thread or dental floss.
