* [[Cookbook:Vinegar|Vinegar]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]

== Procedure ==

# Use a knife to remove the cauliflower's green leaves.
# Submerge the cauliflower head in water with vinegar. Soak for 5 minutes to 1 hour. Drain the cauliflower and dry well.
# Use a [[Cookbook:Grater|grater]] with medium-sized holes to grate the cauliflower into rice-like bits. 
# Heat 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] vegetable oil in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]]. Add the riced cauliflower, and stir continuously for 3 minutes over low heat. This gives the cauliflower rice a texture similar to regular rice and helps to lessen the amount of water in it.
# Add a dash of salt and some white pepper, then cover and cook for 1 minute.
# Remove from the heat, season, and use as desired.

title: Cookbook:Chapati Za Maji (Tanzanian Pancakes)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Pancake recipes
| Time = Prep: 10 minutes</br>Cooking: 20 minutes</br>Total: 30 minutes
| Difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Chapati za maji''' (literally "water bread/pancakes") are thin Tanzanian [[Cookbook:Pancake|pancakes]] very similar to [[Cookbook:Crêpe|crêpes]].

== Ingredients ==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] 
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]] 
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]] 
* ⅓ cup white [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] 
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Rapeseed Oil|Canola oil]]

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowls]]
* [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]]
* [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|Frying pan]]
* [[Cookbook:Stovetop|Stovetop]]
* [[Cookbook:Spatula|Spatula]]

== Procedure ==

=== Batter ===

# Combine the milk, eggs, and water.
# Combine the flour, sugar, and salt.
# Gradually whisk the wet mixture into the dry mixture until you get a thin [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]] similar to [[Cookbook:Crêpe|crêpe]] batter. If it feels too thick, add some additional water.
# Cover the batter and let rest for 30–60 minutes.

=== Cooking ===

# Preheat a frying pan over medium heat.
# Grease the pan with a small amount of canola oil, swirling the pan to coat the entire surface.
# Scoop or pour a small amount of batter into the pan. Immediately tilt the pan in all directions to coat the whole surface with a thin film of batter.
# Cook the pancake for about 1 minute. Then, carefully raise the edge with a spatula, flip it over, and cook for another minute. The pancake should be faintly browned on both sides.
# Remove the pancake and set aside.
# Repeat the greasing and frying process until all the batter is used up.
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You can sprinkle the pancakes with [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] and [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] and roll them up to eat them.

title: Cookbook:Chadian Gilled Fish
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Fish recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Chadian grilled fish''' is a popular dish in Chad known for its simplicity and flavorful taste. Fresh fish is marinated with local spices, then grilled to perfection, resulting in a delicious and aromatic meal. It is often served with a side of rice or millet for a complete and satisfying experience.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* Freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]], to taste
* 2 whole fresh [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] (such as [[Cookbook:Tilapia|tilapia]] or [[Cookbook:Catfish|catfish]]), cleaned and scaled
* [[Cookbook:Lemon|Lemon]] wedges, for serving

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Grill|Grill]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* Basting [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]]
* [[Cookbook:Tongs|Tongs]] or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
* [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|Aluminum foil]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|Paper towels]]

== Procedure ==

# Preheat your grill or barbecue to medium-high heat.
# In a mixing bowl, combine the vegetable oil, paprika, ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to form a smooth [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinade]].
# Pat dry the fish with paper towels and place them on a plate or tray. Using a basting brush, generously coat both sides of the fish with the marinade. Make sure to cover the fish thoroughly for maximum flavor.
# If desired, you can let the fish marinate in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes to allow the flavors to penetrate. However, this step is optional, and you can proceed directly to grilling if you're short on time.
# Once the grill is heated, lightly oil the grates to prevent sticking. You use a folded paper towel soaked in vegetable oil and held with tongs to do so.
# Carefully place the marinated fish on the grill and close the lid. Cook for about 4–5 minutes per side, depending on the thickness of the fish, or until the flesh is opaque and easily flakes with a fork. While grilling, you can [[Cookbook:Basting|baste]] the fish with any remaining marinade using a basting brush for added flavor and moisture.
# Once the fish is cooked through and nicely charred, remove from the grill using tongs or a spatula. Be careful not to break the delicate flesh.
# Serve hot with lemon wedges on the side for squeezing over the fish. It pairs well with a side of rice or millet and can be accompanied by a fresh salad or steamed vegetables.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Cooking times may vary depending on the size and thickness of the fish, as well as the heat of your grill. Adjust accordingly to ensure the fish is cooked to your desired doneness.
* If desired, you can place the fish on a sheet of aluminum foil on the grill to prevent direct contact with the grates and facilitate easier flipping.

title: Cookbook:Chadian Salad
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Salad recipes
| Difficulty = 1
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Chadian salad''' is a colorful and flavorful [[Cookbook:Salad|salad]] that combines fresh vegetables with a zesty dressing. It is a healthy and refreshing dish, perfect for hot summer days or as a side dish to accompany grilled meats or fish.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]], diced
* 1 red [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]] (any color), diced
* 1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]], juiced
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] or [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]] leaves, chopped (optional, for garnish)

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* Mixing bowl
* [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] or fork
* [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|Plastic wrap]]

== Procedure ==

# Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, red onion, and carrot in a mixing bowl.
# In a separate small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper to make a dressing. Adjust the seasoning according to your taste.
# Pour the dressing over the vegetables in the mixing bowl. Gently [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|toss]] the salad to ensure all the vegetables are coated with the dressing.
# Cover the mixing bowl with plastic wrap or a lid and let the salad marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. This allows the flavors to blend together and enhances the taste.
# Remove the salad from the refrigerator. Give it a final toss to mix the flavors, and transfer it to a serving dish. If desired, sprinkle chopped parsley or mint leaves on top as a [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]].
# Enjoy as a standalone dish or as a side salad alongside grilled meats, fish, or other main courses.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Feel free to customize the salad by adding or substituting vegetables according to your preference and availability. You can also add a touch of heat by including chopped chili peppers or a sprinkle of paprika.

[[Category:Chadian recipes]]

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

title: Cookbook:Chakalaka (South African Vegetable Stew)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Name = Chakalaka
| Category = Stew recipes
| Servings = 4–6
| Time = 30–40 minutes
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[File:Chakalaka.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Chakalaka''' is a spicy South African vegetable relish made from beans, peppers, carrots, and tomatoes. It is often served as a side dish with bread, pap (maize porridge), or meat. Chakalaka is versatile and can be customized with various vegetables and spices depending on regional or personal preference.
== Ingredients ==

*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]], or as needed
*3 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Curry Powder|curry powder,]] or to taste
*1 teaspoon [[Cookbook: Chile Powder|chile powder]]
*2 small Thai green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]], chopped
*3 medium [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], diced
*3 medium [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], diced
*2 medium green [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]], diced
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*1 cube vegetable [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|bouillon]], crumbled
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] and ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]] to taste

== Equipment ==

* Large [[Cookbook: Saucepan|saucepan]] or [[Cookbook: Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]]
* [[Cookbook: Cooking Spoon|Cooking Spoon]]
* [[Cookbook:Cooktop|Stove]] or Cooking gas

==Procedure==

# Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onions and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] for 2–3 minutes until softened.
# Stir in the curry powder, chile powder, and chopped chile peppers. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
# Add the chopped tomatoes, grated carrots, and diced bell peppers. Stir well.
# Add the crumbled bouillon cube and water. Cover and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 10–15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
# Stir in the baked beans and cook for an additional 3–5 minutes, uncovered, until the mixture thickens.
# Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Chakalaka can be made ahead of time and tastes even better the next day.
* Grated [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]] or [[Cookbook:Green Bean|green beans]] can be added for extra variety.
* It can be served hot or cold, depending on preference.

'''Carrot cookies''' are soft cookies with an orange-flavored icing.  They get their golden color from pureed carrots, but they taste like oranges instead of carrots.  

This recipe is adapted from the "Golden Carrot Cookies" recipe in Betty Crocker's ''Cooky Book''.

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixer#Stand mixer|Stand mixer]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|Baking sheet]]

== Procedure ==

=== Make the cookies ===
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|400 °F (205°C, gas mark 6—moderately hot)]]. Line baking sheets with parchment baking paper, or lightly grease the pans with shortening.
# Put the butter in a large mixing bowl, and [[Cookbook:Beat|beat]] it with an electric mixer for about 30 seconds. Alternatively, beat it with a wooden spoon until soft.
# Beat in the sugar, scraping the bowl as needed.
# Beat in the eggs, vanilla extract, and orange extract.
# Stir in the carrots, then the flour, salt, and baking powder.
# Stir in the coconut.
# Drop the cookie dough by rounded teaspoonfuls on the prepared baking sheets. Space them out, as they will spread somewhat while baking.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the preheated oven for 8–10 minutes, until they are golden in color and no imprint remains when you gently touch them.
# Cool slightly on the pan, then remove from the pan and cool completely.

=== Make the icing ===

# Using an electric mixer or a wooden spoon, beat together the butter and powdered sugar.
# Stir in the orange juice, zest, and extract to make a smooth, soft buttercream icing.
# Spread gently on the tops of cooled cookies. If the icing is too stiff, the cookies will break when you try to frost them—thin it by adding a small spoonful of water, or warm it slightly to make it softer.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you want a solid, uniform color for the cookies, then the carrots should be pureed (smooth like baby food). If you want visible streaks of orange, then shred the carrots on a grater.
* You can use [[Cookbook:Gluten-Free Flour|gluten-free flour substitutes]]. Avoid high-gluten bread flours.
* You can replace up to half the sugar with a sugar substitute.
* This recipe can be halved or doubled easily.
* The dough is soft enough to pipe through a large pastry bag, which may be faster than scooping when making larger batches.
* Store at room temperature or in the refrigerator for a few days.

'''Cherry brownies''' are a rich [[Cookbook:Brownies|brownie]] with no frosting, a fudge-like base, and a [[Cookbook:Cheesecake|cheesecake]]-like top, filled with maraschino cherries and chocolate chips.

== Ingredients ==

=== Base ===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (100 g) [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (2.4 [[Cookbook:Deciliter|dl]]) white granulated [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (0.6 dl) [[Cookbook:Cocoa|cocoa]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (1.8 dl) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

=== Topping ===
* 4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] (110 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) softened [[cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (0.6 dl) [[Cookbook:Maraschino Cherry|maraschino cherry]] syrup
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (0.6 dl) [[cookbook:icing sugar|icing sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (1.2 dl) semi-sweet [[cookbook:Chocolate chip|chocolate chips]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (1.2 dl) [[cookbook:Cherry|maraschino cherries]]

== Procedure ==

=== Base ===
# Melt margarine in a [[cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]] over medium-low heat, then mix in the cocoa.
# Add the sugar, salt, and eggs. Mix well and then [[cookbook:fold|fold]] in the flour.
# Spread in a greased 9 x 9-inch (22 x 22 cm) [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake pan]] and set aside.

=== Topping ===
# [[cookbook:Beat|Beat]] the cream cheese, cherry syrup and icing sugar together in a bowl until creamy.
# Add the egg to the mixture and blend well.
# Mix in the chocolate chips and cherries.
# Pour the second mixture over top the base.

=== Baking ===
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 350 °F/175 °C for 30–40 minutes, until a [[Cookbook:Toothpick|toothpick]] poked through the centre comes out moist (but not wet with batter).
#  Let cool and cut into 36 squares.

== Notes, tips and variations ==

* Cool for at least 10 minutes before cutting and eating or you will have hot broken brownies.

#Mix the milk and oil together in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] until a white foam appears.

#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 375°F (190°C).
#Mix the eggs, cheese, salt, and pepper into the dough. The dough will become sticky and wet. If the dough is too wet, add more flour and cheese in order to make firmer balls (instead of cookies).

| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sauces|Sauces]]

'''Cheese sauce''' is a variation of [[Cookbook:Béchamel Sauce|Béchamel Sauce]].

== Ingredients ==
* 2½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 1½ tablespoons [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Heavy Cream|heavy whipping cream]] or ½ cup whole [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]], hot
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar cheese]]
* ⅓ cup grated [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella cheese]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] (optional)
* 1½–2 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinches]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

== Procedure ==
# Melt the butter in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Add the flour and [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] together over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, to make a white [[Cookbook:Roux|roux]]. Do not allow to brown. Remove from heat and allow to cool nearly to room temperature.
# Gradually add hot heavy whipping cream to the roux, whisking to combine. This will also work with a hot roux and room temperature heavy cream or milk.
# Add the salt, cheese, and mustard, then heat till just [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmering]] and cheese has melted.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* If desired, you may bring the sauce to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]; once the cheese sauce has come to a boil, lower the heat to low and very slowly simmer for about 45 minutes. Stir it every so often to avoid sticking to the bottom (a whisk is appropriate here). 
* Do not allow the sauce to brown. 
* The longer the sauce is simmered, the smoother it becomes due to the cooking and swelling of the starch grains.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Tex-Mex cuisine|Tex-Mex Cuisine]]

This '''cheese enchilada''' recipe was handed down from the grandmother and mother of the original contributor.  

==Ingredients==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:flour|flour]]
* 3 tbsp [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chili powder]]
* 3 tbsp [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:water|water]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] (680 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) grated [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar cheese]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* ~20 corn [[Cookbook:tortilla|tortillas]]

==Procedure==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (175°C).
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] chili powder and flour in oil in a 10–12-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (25–30 cm) skillet until emulsified. Add water, bring to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]], and then stir for ~5 minutes until slightly thickened. Turn down heat to low.
# Soak one tortilla in the chili gravy until softened (20–30 seconds). Remove tortilla from gravy, place flat on a plate, and add ~1 tbsp cheese and ~1 tbsp onion to center of the tortilla. Roll it up, and place with edges facing down in a 9 x 12-inch (23 x 30 cm) baking pan. Repeat this until you have used all the tortillas. If you get low on the gravy at the end, stir in ⅛–¼ cup of water.
# Cover the enchiladas with the remaining cheese, onions, and chili gravy.
# Bake in oven for about 5 minutes—longer will toughen the cheese.
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* These freeze well, but defrost completely before reheating.
* In Tex-Mex cuisine, these are often served with [[Cookbook:Mexican Rice|Mexican rice]], pinto beans, and guacamole salad.

title: Cookbook:Cheese Dumplings
text:
__NOTOC__{{recipesummary
| category = Dumpling recipes
| servings = 4–6
| time = Prep: 15 minutes</br>Cooking: 12 minutes
| difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Austria|Austrian Cuisine]]

'''Cheese dumplings''' (''kaspressknödel'') are a typical Austrian dish, originally eaten by farmers throughout Austria. Bread, potatoes, and flour were used for the dough. In addition eggs, butter, left-over meats, bacon, or fruits from the garden were used to fill them. Tyroleans, south Tyroleans, and Bavarians all claim that cheese dumplings come from their respective regions. Today cheese dumplings are served and eaten throughout Austria, and they are a favourite at ski huts.

As well as using left-overs, another advantage of cheese dumplings is that they are easy to prepare. Not many ingredients are needed and these can be varied. Cheese dumplings can be served in a soup, with sauerkraut, or with a salad.

When making these dumplings, the kind of cheese used is of particular importance. It should be a strong cheese with a lot of flavour. In Austria they are predominately made using either Pinzgauer beer cheese or grey cheese from Tirol. You can experiment with whichever cheese you like.

==Ingredients==
*250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (8.8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 1¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) white crustless bread, finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (8.5 fl oz / 1 cup) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
*2–3 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*250 g (8.8 oz / 2½ cups) grated [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (e.g. Pinzgauer beer cheese, Tyrolean grey cheese )  
*50 g (1.8 oz) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], thinly-sliced
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] each of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]], [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], and [[Cookbook:Caraway|caraway seeds]]
*[[Cookbook:Flour|Flour]]

== Procedure==

# Mix the eggs with the milk.
# Soak the white bread in the egg mixture. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] and then let it rest.
# Brown the onions with the butter in a pan.
# Add the cooked onions, salt, pepper, parsley, caraway seeds, and grated cheese to the white bread. Add the flour and let the mixture rest for a further 10 minutes.
# Form dumplings that are approximately the size of a golf ball, then press them flat (about 2–3 cm / 0.8–1.2 inch thick). Forming them is easiest when your hands are slightly wet.
# Heat some butter or oil in a pan, and put in the pressed cheese dumplings. Cook them on one side and then the other until golden brown.
# Place the dumplings on a [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]] to absorb the excess fat.
# Serve the dumplings in a beef broth, with sauerkraut or a green salad. Enjoy!

title: Cookbook:Chereh Tamba (Gambian Groundnut Stew)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Stew recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Chereh tamba''', also known as Gambian groundnut stew, is a flavorful and hearty [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]] that showcases the use of groundnuts (peanuts) as a key ingredient. It is a traditional Gambian recipe that highlights the rich flavors of the region. Chereh tamba is a popular main course that is often served with rice or couscous, providing a satisfying and nourishing meal.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Groundnut|groundnuts]] (peanuts)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 2 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 4 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]], diced
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]] (optional, for added spiciness)
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut into pieces
* Water or [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]] for cooking
* Salt
* Pepper

==Equipment==
* Large pot with a lid
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* Measuring spoons
* Cooking spoon or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
* [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|Baking sheet]]
* [[Cookbook:Food Processor|Food processor]] or [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]]

==Procedure==

# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 180°C (350°F).
# Spread the groundnuts evenly on a baking sheet. [[Cookbook:Roasting|Roast]] the groundnuts in the preheated oven for about 10–15 minutes, or until they are golden brown and fragrant.
# Remove the roasted groundnuts from the oven and allow them to cool. 
# Once cooled, transfer the roasted groundnuts to a food processor or blender and grind them into a smooth paste. Set aside.
# In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and minced garlic. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until they become soft and translucent.
# Add the diced tomatoes, diced bell pepper, ground ginger, ground paprika, and ground cayenne pepper (if using) to the pot. Stir well to combine.
# Mix in the tomato paste and the groundnut paste, ensuring that they are evenly incorporated into the mixture.
# Add the chicken pieces to the pot and stir to coat them with the sauce. Pour enough water or broth into the pot to cover the chicken and create a stew-like consistency. Bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], then reduce the heat to low and cover the pot with a lid.
# Allow the chereh tamba to [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 30–40 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
# Taste the chereh tamba and adjust the seasoning with salt, pepper, and additional spices if desired.
# Serve hot with rice or couscous.

text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary

| Servings = 4
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}

This is a recipe for a '''chicken madras'''. It is a popular curry in the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|UK]].

==Ingredients==

*4 [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breasts, [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*2 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*4 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
*1 jar of [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato puree]], mixed with an equal volume of water 
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] of ground [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]]
*3 teaspoons of [[Cookbook:Garam masala|garam masala]]
*1 teaspoon of ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
*1 teaspoon of ground [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]]
*8 [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]] pods
*½ teaspoon of ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
*½ teaspoon of ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
*Juice of ½ [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]

=== Garnish ===

* Fresh [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]]
* 1 pinch of garam masala
* Freshly-chopped [[Cookbook:Cilantro|coriander leaves]]

==Procedure==
# Heat a large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] or [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over medium heat, and add a liberal amount of cooking oil. When at temperature add the chopped onions. Cook the onions for a couple of minutes until they start to brown slightly.
# Add the minced garlic, cayenne pepper, and garam masala. Stir for 2 to 3 minutes.
# Add the ground cumin, ground turmeric, ground ginger, and ground coriander. Stir in for about 30 seconds.
# Add the diced chicken. Cook, stirring, until the chicken is cooked through.
# Add the diluted tomato puree and the seeds from the 8 cardamom pods. Stir, then lower the heat and place a lid on the saucepan.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] for 30 minutes stirring occasionally. If the sauce starts to stick to the pan add some water.
# Remove the lid and squeeze the juice of half a lemon into the pan along with a pinch of salt. Stir and let simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes.
# Serve with garnishes.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Other meats can be substituted for the chicken.
* This dish currently has a heat level of a hot masala. To bring the heat up to about a madras level, add approx ½ teaspoon of [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chili powder]] when adding the cayenne pepper.

This '''chicken cabbage salad''' is a very easy way to make a tasty cabbage [[Cookbook:Salad|salad]]. It works well as both a side salad or a main dish. 

== Ingredients ==
* 1 head [[cookbook:cabbage|cabbage]]
* 1 bunch of [[cookbook:cilantro|cilantro]]
* 1 bunch of [[cookbook:green onion|green onion]]s
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[cookbook:Almond|slivered almonds]], toasted
* ½ cup [[cookbook:Sunflower Seeds|sunflower seeds]]
* 2 packages of [[Cookbook:Instant Noodles|instant ramen noodles]] (Oriental/soy sauce flavor)
* 2 cooked [[cookbook:chicken|chicken]] breasts
* ½ cup of [[cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable]] or [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola]] oil

* [[cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[cookbook:pepper|Pepper]] to taste
* [[cookbook:sugar|Sugar]] to taste
== Procedure ==
# [[cookbook:Chop|Chop]] the cabbage, cilantro leaves, and green onion until it is at an even consistency among the three. Mix together.
# Add the almonds and sunflower seeds.
# Break up the ramen noodles and place in the salad.
# Mix oil, rice vinegar, and flavoring. This is now your dressing.
# Pour dressing over salad, and add salt and pepper to taste
# Leave salad to sit and absorb flavor for an hour for best taste.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Vegetarian chicken patties can be used to replace the chicken breasts
* Cooked and cooled ramen noodles can be used for those who don't like crunchy noodles in their salad.
* Try browning the noodles a nuts in a little butter, let them cool, and sprinkle on salad.

text:
{{Recipe summary

| Servings = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

This is a classically-inspired steak recipe, with influences from both [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American]] and [[Cookbook:European cuisines|European cuisine]].

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (16 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 550 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Beef#Loin|sirloin steaks]]
* [[cookbook:Montreal Steak Seasoning|Montreal steak seasoning]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] Cabernet Sauvignon [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Vinegar|balsamic vinegar]]
* 8–10 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], minced
* ⅓ large white [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], diced
* 4 cloves [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallots]], diced
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

==Procedure==
# Preheat a medium-sized [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over medium-low heat and preheat the [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]] to high.
# Add the onions to the pan, and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until light yellow.
# Add the shallots and garlic to the pan and sauté for a few minutes more. Make sure all ingredients are lightly crisped.
# Pour in about ⅓ of the wine and ⅓ of the vinegar. Let this [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] and reduce over lower heat for about 5–10 minutes.
# Place the steaks on the [[Cookbook:Barbecue|barbecue]], seasoning with the Montreal steak spice.
# Add the rest of the wine and vinegar and season by sprinkling some fresh black pepper on top. Boil off until you no longer smell the alcohol coming from the steaming wine.
# Flip the steaks. You want them to be soft on the inside (cooked rare) yet quite charred on the outside, to get that charcoal flavor.
# Once the sauce has gone down to about ⅓ of its original volume, take off heat.
# Remove steaks from grill and take inside.
# Place the steaks on your plates, cover with the sauce and serve!

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You may wish to serve this flavourful dish with a side that compliments its strong flavors such as [[Cookbook:Asparagus|asparagus]], new [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], or roasted [[Cookbook:Brussels Sprout|Brussels sprouts]].

title: Cookbook:Chicken and Andouille Sausage Gumbo
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Stew recipes|servings=12|time=3–4 hours|difficulty=3|
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:North American cuisines|North American Cuisines]]

'''Chicken and andouille sausage gumbo''' is a soup or[[Cookbook:Stews | stew]] which is is prepared using[[Cookbook:Roux | roux]].

== Ingredients ==
* about 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] (1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breasts
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola oil]]
* 1 cup (240 g) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Bell pepper|bell peppers]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] into ¼-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] pieces
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], chopped into ¼-inch pieces
* 4 stalks of [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]], chopped into ¼-inch pieces
* [[Cookbook:Chicken Stock|Chicken stock]] or equivalent
* about ½ lb (¼ kg) Andouille [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]] or other spicy sausage
* [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper |Cayenne pepper]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Salt |Salt]] to taste

== Procedure ==
# Brown outside of chicken breasts in small amount of oil then set aside.
# Make a [[Cookbook:Roux|roux]] from the flour in a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]].
# Add peppers, onions, and celery to roux. Cook until softened.
# Slowly stir in water, and bring to a simmer.
# Cut up browned chicken breasts, add to gumbo, and cook until done.
# Slice up sausage and add ½ hour after the chicken.
# Season to taste with cayenne and salt.
# Serve in a bowl with a little rice and green onions on top.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*Hot sauce can be added to taste.
*[[Cookbook:Filé|Filé]] may be added to thicken individual servings as served.
*Home-made chicken stock is preferable to store-bought.
*Gumbo will be better if left over night and eaten the next day.

title: Cookbook:Chicken and Corn Empanadas
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for pastries|servings=6|time=2 hours|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:South American cuisines|South American cuisines]] | [[Cookbook:Caribbean cuisines|Caribbean cuisine]]

'''''Empanadas''''', which come from the Spanish word for "bread," are baked or fried turnovers made from bread, pastry, phyllo, or even pizza dough.

==Ingredients==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Onion|Oso sweet onions]]
* 1 diced red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (hot) [[Cookbook:Red pepper flakes|crushed red pepper]] (optional)
* 1½ cup frozen [[Cookbook:Corn|corn kernels]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
* 3 cups (1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]]) [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] cooked [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] shredded Monterey Jack [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]
* [[Cookbook:Kosher|Kosher]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] and [[Cookbook:Pepper|fresh ground black pepper]] to taste
* 2 packages (28 ounces) frozen [[Cookbook:Rolls|crescent rolls]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]], lightly [[Cookbook:Beat|beaten]] with 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Water|water]] 

==Procedure==

# In large [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]], heat oil and lightly brown onions.
# Add pepper, crushed red peppers, corn, and oregano. Cook 5 minutes over moderate heat or until liquid has mostly cooked away.
# Remove from heat; stir in chicken and cheese, season to taste and chill.
# Unroll crescent dough into two perforated squares.
# Place one square over second square.
# Roll out with a little flour to form a single large rectangular sheet.
# Cut out four circles about 5 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] in diameter.
# Repeat with remaining package of rolls.
# Refrigerate circles on waxed paper until firm, about 30 minutes.
# Spoon ¼ cup filling into center of each circle, leaving a 1-inch border.
# Brush edges with egg mixture.
# Fold over to seal, stretching dough slightly.
# Press edges together while pushing out any air pockets.
# Seal by crimping with the tines of a fork.
# Brush top with egg wash. Prick with fork.
# Arrange empanadas on buttered and floured [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]].
# Refrigerate until ready to bake, up to two days ahead of time.
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven_temperatures|400°F]].
# [[Cookbook:Bake|Bake]] 25 to 30 minutes or until puffy and brown and filling in bubbling hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Use rotisserie-roasted chicken.
* Oso sweet onions are the winter sweet onion from Chile, in season from January to March. They have record-high sugar content, crisp texture, and mild flavor. Vidalias would be a reasonable onion substitute if Oso Sweet onions cannot be found.
* You can use this as a base to experiment with any filling or combination you desire.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Barbecue Sauce
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Sauce recipes
| Yield = 6 tablespoons (90 mL)|servings=2|time=5 minutes|difficulty=1
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sauce|Sauce]]

This '''chicken barbecue sauce''' is a [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]] based sauce used as marinade or barbecue sauce for grilled [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] parts such as wings, drumsticks or breasts. It also works very well for vegetarian (e.g., wheat- and soy-based) meat alternatives. It was invented by Johan Zandin from Gothenburg, Sweden and mixes 9 different ingredients from Europe, Asia and North America.

==Ingredients==
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (30 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) [[Cookbook:Peanut Oil|peanut oil]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (5 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) walnut oil
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (30 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) mild [[Cookbook:Chili Paste|chili sauce]] (the kind just slightly hotter than ketchup)
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (5 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]] (see below for vegetarian alternative)
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (5 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) [[Cookbook:Teriyaki|teriyaki]] marinade
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] (10 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) tandoori powder
*2 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]] ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|white pepper]]
*2 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]] [[Cookbook:Salt|herbal salt]]
*1 small, dried, crunched piri-piri [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile pepper]]

==Procedure==
#Mix everything together in a small [[Cookbook:Mixing bowl|mixing bowl]].
#Use a brush to apply a thick layer of the sauce to your favorite chicken parts or vegetarian alternative.
#[[Cookbook:Barbecue|Barbecue]] chicken over fire, charcoal or in the oven.
==Notes, tips and variations==
*The sauce can also be used as a [[Cookbook:Marinade|marinade]]: Soak the chicken parts in it, for half an hour to a few hours.
*Any remaining sauce can be applied with the brush during the cooking.
*In case of allergies or problems to find some ingredient, most ingredients can be replaced by similar alternatives:
**Peanut oil → [[Cookbook:Sunflower Oil|sunflower oil]], [[Cookbook:Corn Oil|corn oil]] or any other neutral oil
**Walnut oil → [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame oil]]
**Mild chili sauce → [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]] or [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato purée]]
**Worcestershire sauce → HP sauce
**Teriyaki marinade → [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
**Herbal salt → plain salt
**Piri-piri → any other hot [[Cookbook:Chili pepper|chili pepper]]

==Warnings==
*Make sure that any sauce that has been in contact with raw chicken gets properly heated. So do not apply more sauce just before taking the chicken from the heat or use the sauce uncooked after you have dipped the brush in it.
*Note that Worcestershire sauce usually is non-vegetarian, since at least the original recipe contains [[Cookbook:Anchovy|anchovies]]. (See above for alternative.)

This dish is a spicy '''chicken black-eyed pea stew''' or [[Cookbook:Curry|curry]]. It is a meal on its own.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] of dry [[Cookbook:Black-eyed Pea|black-eyed peas]] (or about 2 cups canned)
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]] or [[Cookbook:Schmaltz|chicken fat]]
* 2 medium (~2 cups) [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] white or red [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (~2 cups) chopped [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]]
* 1 stalk (~½–1 cup) chopped [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]] including the leaves
* 6 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1–2 tbsp minced [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]], preferably freshly-crushed peppercorns
* 1 cup uncooked long-grained [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]], preferably brown rice
* 2 cups chicken [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]], canned tomato liquid, water, or vegetable stock
* 2 cups canned [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] (crushed or diced), or 1 pound diced fresh tomatoes.
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] bone-in [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] meat (e.g. two chicken legs)
* 2 medium to hot [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]] (optional)
* 2 tsp [[Cookbook:Curry Powder|curry powder]] stirred into the juice of ½ [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]

== Procedure ==

# If using dry black-eyed peas, wash them, then cook for 20 minutes or until [[Cookbook:Al dente|al dente]]. When done, drain.
# Meanwhile, [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] onions, carrots, and celery in oil for 5 minutes.
# Add garlic, ginger, salt, and pepper, and sauté for 2 more minutes.
# Stir rice into vegetable mix.
# Add stock and tomatoes, then bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Add the cooked black-eyed peas.
# Add meat, cook a further 5 minutes, turn heat to low, and let [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 30–40 minutes. The stew is ready when the rice is soft.
# Add chili peppers and curry-lemon paste, then cook for 10 more minutes. Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* This dish works well as a vegetarian dish. Just omit the chicken, and increase the amount of black-eye peas by 50%.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Cockaigne
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Chicken recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

This technique is used for cooking chicken using a 'poaching' technique, where the chicken is cooked from the outside over time using medium to low heat. If the directions are followed exactly, the chicken will be cooked to a safe temperature, ready to use in any recipe.

== Ingredients ==
* [[Cookbook:Chicken#Breast|Chicken breasts]] (preferably boneless and skinless)
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]] or [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Black pepper]]

== Procedure ==

# Flatten the chicken breasts to an even thickness using a nonporous [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]], jar, mallet, or other flat clean object. This step is important—this way there are no high points in parts of the breast, and it will cook evenly.
# Season or [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] the breasts as desired. If no seasoning is desired, or if you're after a neutral chicken taste, use a sprinkle of salt and pepper.
# Place a [[Cookbook:Sauté Pan|sauté pan]] over medium-high heat, and coat the bottom evenly with a layer of olive oil or butter.
# Turn the heat down to medium, place the breasts in the pan, and cook on one side for 1 minute.
# Turn the heat down to simmer (not low), flip the breasts over to the uncooked side, and cover the pan. Let the chicken sit on that same burner for 10 minutes as it reduces in temperature over time. It is important NOT to open the lid, as the trapped heat will be needed to finish cooking the chicken.
# After 10 minutes, if you're using a gas range, turn the pilot off. If an electric range, take the chicken off of the range, shut the burner off, and put it on the counter. In either case, let it sit for an additional 10 minutes, as it is still cooking. Again, do not open the lid.
# Open the lid and check the chicken to make sure it isn't pink in the middle. If using an instant-read [[Cookbook:Thermometer|thermometer]], the center of the chicken should at least be 165 °F.
# If the chicken is not cooked after sitting, or if the lid is opened, return to the range, flip the breasts over, and continue cooking covered on medium heat until the safe temperature is reached.

text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Chicken recipes
| Servings = 10
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (5–6 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) fat [[Cookbook:Chicken|hen]]
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] (about the size of a lemon or smaller)
* 1 small green [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]], chopped small
* 1 stick [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] (¼ lb), if needed
* 2 lb uncooked long grain white [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] (not instant rice)
* ¼ lb [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|Black pepper]]

== Procedure ==
# Put chicken in heavy aluminum pot and cover with hot water. Be sure there is enough water so that there will be at least 6 cups of broth after cooking chicken. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], then reduce heat, cover, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until chicken is very tender (an hour or more).
# While the chicken is cooking, put 4 cups of rice into a bowl, cover with cold water, and let soak.
# When chicken is very tender, remove pot from stove and let cool until the chicken can be handled.
# Take chicken from pot, and pull meat from bones in large pieces; do not cut it up. Discard any fat-heavy skin.
# Pour broth from pot into a bowl. If chicken was very fat and broth is very fatty, pour off about 1 cup of fat from broth.
# Wash pot, then put bacon in pot and cook slowly until bacon is crisp.
# Take bacon from pot and drain; leave bacon grease in pot.
# Put in chopped onion, green pepper and brown slightly.
# Add 6 cups chicken broth to pot, and season to taste with salt and pepper (at least a tablespoon of each—use a heavy hand since rice will absorb salt).
# Increase heat, bring broth to a boil, and put chicken in pot.
# Drain rice and put rice in pot.
# Add a stick of butter and mix well. Reduce heat, cover with lid, and simmer very slowly for about an hour. To avoid gooey rice, avoid stirring.
# When rice is tender and has absorbed the liquids, remove from stove. Serve hot. You can crumble bacon for a topping, according to taste.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Chicken bog can be kept in refrigerator or frozen and later reheated.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Bog III
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Chicken recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
* 1 whole [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 2 stalks [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]], washed and snapped in halves or quarters (leaves and all)

* 2 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], halved or quartered

* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] poultry seasoning
* 1 tablespoon dried [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] flakes
* 2 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]], to taste
* 1 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (3–3½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]]) whole [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]
* [[Cookbook:Water|Water]]
* 2 ½ cups long-grain [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large soup pot, kettle, or deep-sided heavy casserole with top, combine onion, celery, carrots, poultry seasoning, parsley flakes, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
# Rinse the chicken and place on top of the other ingredients in the pot. Add enough water to cover the chicken and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], uncovered, over medium-high heat.
# Reduce heat, cover, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 1 hour, or until juices run clear when the chicken is pricked with a fork.
# Remove chicken to a platter to cool. [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] broth from pot (you should have about 8 cups; if you have more, set aside for another use).
# Return 8 cups broth to the pot and bring to a boil over high heat. Pour in rice and return to a boil. Adjust heat to lowest possible setting, stir and cover.
# Cook 20 minutes, stirring occasionally and keeping an eye on the pot to be sure it does not cook dry. Add more of the broth if necessary.
# While the rice is cooking, skin and remove chicken meat from the bones; discard bones and skin. Cut meat into bite-sized pieces and set aside.
# When the rice is cooked, add the boneless chicken and butter. Stir together carefully, taste to correct seasoning and serve. Or, keep pot covered over low heat until ready to serve.

== Nutrition ==
Per serving (with 2 teaspoons butter per serving): 60 calories, 2 grams protein, 4 grams fat, 6 grams carbohydrates, 10 milligrams cholesterol, 43 milligrams sodium, 60 percent calories from fat.

title: Cookbook:Chibwabwa (Zambian Pumpkin Leaves with Groundnut Sauce)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = Vegetable recipes
| cuisine = Zambian
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Chibwabwa''' is a classic Zambian dish that features tender pumpkin leaves in a flavorful groundnut sauce. Also known as pumpkin leaves with peanut sauce, this dish is a delightful combination of nutritious greens and a rich, nutty sauce.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pepper|hot pepper]] (optional, for heat), chopped
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] fresh [[Cookbook:Pumpkin|pumpkin leaves]], chopped
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Peanut|peanuts]], [[Cookbook:Roasting|roasted]] and ground into a smooth paste
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* Large [[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|pot]]
* [[Cookbook:Blender|Blender]] or [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* [[Cookbook:Wooden Spoon|Wooden spoon]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onions are soft and translucent.
# Add the diced tomato and chopped hot pepper (if using) to the pot. Cook until the tomato is soft and tender.
# In a blender or food processor, blend the roasted peanuts until they form a smooth paste. You may need to add a little water to achieve the desired consistency.
# Add the peanut paste to the pot with the cooked vegetables. Stir well to combine.
# Pour in the water and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
# Add the chopped pumpkin leaves to the pot. Stir to incorporate the leaves into the groundnut sauce.
# Let [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pumpkin leaves are cooked and tender.
# Taste the sauce and season with salt according to your preference.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Chibwabwa is traditionally served with nshima, a thick maize meal porridge that complements the flavors of the dish.
* You can add other vegetables like [[Cookbook:Okra|okra]] or [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]] to the dish for added taste and nutrition.
* For extra creaminess, you can blend some of the cooked pumpkin leaves with the groundnut sauce before serving.

== Nutrition ==
* Pumpkin leaves are rich in vitamins A and C, iron, and calcium.
* Peanuts provide protein, fats, and various other nutrients.

title: Cookbook:Chicken and Dumplings
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Stew recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Stew|Stew]] | [[Cookbook:Chicken|Chicken]]

'''Chicken and dumplings''' is a traditional American comfort food.

==Ingredients==

===Stew===
* Approximately 2 [[Cookbook:liter|liters]] (2 [[Cookbook:quart|quarts]]) [[Cookbook:Chicken Stock|chicken stock]]
* Approximately 1 [[Cookbook:kilogram|kilogram]] (2 [[Cookbook:pound|pounds]]) cooked boneless [[Cookbook:chicken|chicken]] meat, cut into bite-sized pieces
* 1 [[Cookbook:carrot|carrot]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] into rounds
* 1 [[Cookbook:celery|celery]] rib or ¼ [[Cookbook:celeriac|celeriac]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:bay leaf|bay leaf]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], chopped
* 1 [[Cookbook:teaspoon|teaspoon]] dried [[Cookbook:thyme|thyme]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], [[Cookbook:pepper|pepper]], and [[Cookbook:Liquid Seasoning|liquid seasoning]] to taste

===Dumplings===
* 150 [[Cookbook:gram|grams]] (1¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|U.S. cups]]) [[Cookbook:Wheat Flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1½ teaspoons [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* ½ teaspoon salt
* 20 grams (1½ [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tablespoons]]) [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|solid fat]] (such as [[Cookbook:Shortening|vegetable shortening]], [[Cookbook:lard|lard]] or [[Cookbook:butter|butter]])
* 150 [[Cookbook:milliliter|milliliters]] (5 [[Cookbook:Fluid Ounce|U.S. fluid ounces]]) [[Cookbook:milk|milk]]

==Procedure==
# Combine all the stew ingredients in a large pot and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Reduce heat and allow to [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] while you make the dumplings.
# For the dumplings, mix the dry ingredients together and [[Cookbook:Mixing#Cutting|cut in]] the shortening until the mixture is coarse and grainy.
# Add milk and mix just until combined into a dough.
# Drop dough by spoonfuls onto the stew.
# Simmer 5 minutes with the lid off and 15–20 minutes longer with the lid on.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* You can buy chicken stock in cans or jars if you don't want to make it by hand.
* The stew portion of the recipe is very flexible. You can use whatever vegetables and flavorings you like and have on hand.
* To make it [[Cookbook:kosher|kosher]], use vegetable shortening or [[Cookbook:schmaltz|schmaltz]] for the dumplings, and replace the milk with any [[Cookbook:Vegan Substitutions#Dairy|plant milk]].

title: Cookbook:Chili (Vegan)
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Stew recipes
| Servings = 8
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Tex-Mex cuisine|Tex-Mex cuisine]]

'''Vegan chili''' is [[Cookbook:Chili con Carne|chili]] that uses no animal or meat products in its creation. Many variations of a vegetarian based chili have been created using meat substitutes, tofu and even vegetables. The most popular vegan chilis use beans as the main weight of the dish, but others use tofu, eggplant, butternut squash or zucchini.  

This is a kind of chili that needs no meat (and uses no ersatz meat). Many variations are possible; the recipe is very flexible. The molasses gives this chili a somewhat Louisiana flavor.

==Ingredients==
* 2 cans (30 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) red [[Cookbook:Kidney Bean|kidney bean]]s
* 1 can (15 oz) [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black bean]]s
* 1 can (15 oz) [[Cookbook:Navy Bean|navy bean]]s
* 1 can [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]] kernels
* 1 can (6 oz) [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 1 medium [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] (canned diced tomato works too)
* 2 fresh [[Cookbook:Jalapeño|jalapeño]]s (or your favorite [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chili pepper]] works too; more if you like it really hot)
* 1 green [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]], chopped
* 1 red or yellow bell pepper, chopped
* 2 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]s, chopped
* 4 medium cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], chopped or crushed
* 10 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]] [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chili powder]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (optional)
* pinch of [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
* 10 ml [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] (or any other kind of vegetable oil)
* 50 ml [[Cookbook:Molasses|molasses]]
* [[Cookbook:Chili Garlic Sauce|Chili garlic sauce]] (optional)

==Procedure==

# In a large pot, heat the olive oil with a few drops of water. When the water starts sizzling, add the onions and garlic. Stir until the onions are soft (optionally until they are slightly brown).
# Add the chili peppers and fry for a few more seconds. Add the tomato paste and tomato, and the chili powder, salt, and oregano. Stir a few times then let [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]].
# Rinse the beans well and add them to the simmering vegetables. Drain the corn and add to the chili. Add the molasses.
# Taste the chili; if it needs more seasoning, add it now (perhaps with the exception of salt, as people can add this at the table). It is probably better not to add more jalapeños at this point, but if the chili is not spicy enough, some chili sauce or chili garlic sauce can be added.
# Let the pot simmer, covered, for at least 30 minutes—longer will distribute the flavor better. If the chili is too thick, add a little water; if it's too thin, uncover the pot to let water evaporate.
# Add the bell peppers, stir, and simmer for a minute or two (peppers should stay crunchy). 
# Serve with [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]]; Keeps well, perhaps even better the second day.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You may add 2 cups of vegetable broth along with the tomatoes before bringing to a boil.

{{Recipe summary

| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Meat Recipes|Meat]]

'''Chicken Parmesan''' is a classic Italian dish, which is wonderful served over [[cookbook:pasta|pasta]] or on a [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|sandwich]]. This is a fairly simple recipe made mostly with ingredients already on hand.

==Ingredients==
* 6 [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken breast halves]], flattened to ½-inch thickness
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Flour|all purpose flour]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1½ cups Italian seasoned [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|bread crumbs]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] [[cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]], divided
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]], freshly-ground if possible
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
* 1 jar (16 oz) [[Cookbook:Spaghetti Sauce|spaghetti sauce]] (or make it fresh)
* 1 package [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] [[cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella cheese]]

==Procedure==
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (175°C).
# Mix the breadcrumbs, salt, black pepper, and half the Parmesan cheese in a [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]].
# [[cookbook:Beat|Beat]] the eggs in a small bowl.
# On the [[Cookbook:Cooktop|stove]], heat olive oil in a large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] over medium-high heat
# Take each chicken breast and dip it into the flour, then into the eggs, then into the breadcrumb mixture. Make sure to coat it thoroughly.
# [[cookbook:Pan fry|Pan fry]] the chicken breasts lightly in the olive oil until brown on both sides. You do not need to cook them through, just [[cookbook:brown|brown]] them. Once brown, the breadcrumbs should stick to the outside.
# Pour half a jar of pasta sauce into a shallow [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]], then lay the chicken out in the pan. Pour the rest of the sauce on top.
# Sprinkle the remaining grated Parmesan cheese over the chicken.
# Place the dish in the oven and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for 30 minutes at 350°F (175°C).
# Remove and add a slice of mozzarella cheese to each chicken breast.
# Return to the oven for 10 more minutes to melt the mozzarella.
# Serve with [[cookbook:pasta|pasta]].

title: Cookbook:Chicken Parmigiana
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Chicken recipes|servings=2|time=30 minutes|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|US Cuisine]]

'''Chicken parmigiana''' is a popular [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]]-[[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American]] dish served in a variety of ways. The same basic recipe works for a number of dishes. The components usually consists of a breaded, tenderized piece of [[Cookbook:Meat|meat]] (or slice of [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]]), a simple [[Cookbook:Marinara Sauce|marinara sauce]], and [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (usually [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella]]). A thicker [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]], such as linguini, a toasted loaf of Italian [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]], and a light red wine such as Chianti complement this dish well.

This recipe is typical of the parmigiana recipes from New York and New Jersey.

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breasts
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 teaspoon of [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]]
* ½ a teaspoon of dried [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
* ¼ teaspoon of dried [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]]
* ¼ teaspoon of finely-crushed [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* ½ a [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] of all-purpose [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ½ a cup of [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato puree]]
* ¼ cup of [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]
* ½ a cup of [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola oil]] (see below if you wish to use [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]])
* ½ a cup of shredded [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella cheese]]
* ¼ a cup of grated [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|parmigiano cheese]]

==Procedure==
#In a heavy [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] (preferably cast iron), heat the oil on medium heat.
#While the oil is heating, use a tenderizing mallet (or the ball of your hand) to pound the chicken breasts to about ½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick. This step is important to ensure the chicken is tender and more importantly to ensure the chicken cooks thoroughly.
# Season the chicken breasts with salt and garlic powder.
# [[Cookbook:Dredging|Dredge]] the breasts in flour and shake off any excess.
# Place both breasts in the heated oil for 3 minutes, then flip and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for an additional 2 minutes.
# Remove the breasts and place on a rack or [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]].
# Preheat a [[Cookbook:Broiler|broiler]].
# In a large oven-safe [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], heat the tomato puree and chicken stock until it begins to [[Cookbook:Simmer|simmer]].
# Add the oregano, basil, and pepper to saucepan and mix
# Place cooked chicken breasts in pan and flip a number of times to coat with sauce.
# Add mozzarella and parmigiana cheese to the tops of the breasts.
# Broil for 30–60 seconds. It will burn very quickly, so check it frequently.
# Remove from oven and serve.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Use thin-sliced chicken cutlets (available at most supermarkets) to avoid the BIG mess and time of pounding.
* If [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]] is to be served with this meal, it should be timed so that the parmigiana is done right when the pasta is. The pasta should be removed directly from the pot and placed into the pan. The remaining sauce can then be used with the pasta.
* This recipe works best with breasts that come from slightly older chickens (such as broiler or fryer chickens). These chickens have a stronger taste but are generally tougher.  The tenderizing step takes care of the toughness of the older birds though.
* If you do not live in area where fresh tomatoes are grown, canned tomatoes are usually superior to the low-cost ones you will find in the supermarket.

* For [[Cookbook:Veal|veal]] parmigiana, follow the same steps except do not tenderize.  Veal is already tender enough.  The veal can also be cooked for 2 minutes on each side.
* Omit the tenderizing step for [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]] parmigiana.
* If you want to use fresh garlic instead of powder, add it to the sauce instead of adding it to the chicken breast.
* You can also try using other types of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]] [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheeses]] such as [[Cookbook:Provolone Cheese|provolone cheese]] or [[Cookbook:Fontina Cheese|fontina cheese]] to add more of a "tasty kick" compared to a mild cheese like mozzarella 
* You may wish to use [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]. When frying with olive oil, be sure to use a cheap solvent-extracted grade! The fancy grades can not tolerate heat. They have [[Cookbook:Smoke Point|smoke points]] as low as 200°F (93°C), making for both a fire hazard and a source of smoke. Save the cold-pressed extra-virgin olive oil for a [[Cookbook:Salad|salad]].

title: Cookbook:Chicken-fried Steak
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Beef recipes|servings=2|time=20 minutes|difficulty=2
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Texas cuisine|Texas cuisine]]

'''Chicken Fried Steak''' is a hearty food dish in the southern USA. The dish is commonly served with mashed potatoes smothered in chicken fried steak gravy. 

It is, simply, a cut of steak (usually cheap round steak) pounded until tender, breaded like you would bread chicken, and fried in oil. Milk, salt, flour and pepper are added to the grease drippings and used to make a thick gravy, which is generously poured over the steak and, usually, mashed potatoes. Many people think the gravy makes the steak!

==Ingredients==
*[[cookbook:Flour|White flour]] as needed plus 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[cookbook:pepper|freshly-ground black pepper]]
*1 tbsp kosher [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*2 [[cookbook:egg|egg]]s, beaten
*1 cup whole [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]], combined with ¼ cup heavy [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
*3 ea. beef steaks, ½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick
*3 tbsp bacon drippings, divided
*2 tbsp smoked paprika
*⅓ cup chicken [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]

==Procedure==

#Pour 2 tbsp drippings into a 12-inch cast-iron [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]]. Preheat the pan over medium high heat. Wet hand, drip 1 drop of water in pan to test the heat. If it sizzles, it's hot enough.
#Trim each steak.
#Beat eggs with seasonings, then dip steaks into eggs.
#Thoroughly [[Cookbook:Dredging|dredge]] steak in flour on both sides.
#When the pan is hot enough, put steaks in pan in a triangle formation. Fry until golden brown, about 4 minutes per side.
#Remove steak(s) from pan and place in a 200°F [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]].
#Pour remaining drippings into pan and lower heat to medium. Add flour and cook, whisking, until light blonde color is achieved.
#Add chicken broth to pan, and whisk to [[Cookbook:Deglazing|deglaze]] pan. Add cream mixture and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Reduce heat to low and cook until gravy coats back of spoon. Don't let the gravy get too thick.
#Drizzle gravy over steaks and serve.

title: Cookbook:Chilaquiles
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Mexican recipes
| Servings = 1
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}

The following recipe is quite common in most of Mexico as a breakfast item, due to the addition of eggs, but is also eaten throughout the day including during dinner time. The additional recipe for a ''salsa de chile de árbol'' will be used as the primary sauce.

== Ingredients ==

=== Salsa de chile de árbol ===
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Tomatillo|tomatillos]], dehusked
* 4–6 dried ''[[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]] de árbol'', roasted
* 1 clove [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* ½ cup water
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste

=== Chilaquiles ===
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]] (enough to cover the tortillas to deep-fry them)
* 2 day-old corn tortillas, cut into strips then squares
* 1 standard [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
* ¼ white onion, [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]

* Crumbled or shredded [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]

== Procedure ==

=== Salsa de chile de árbol ===
# [[Cookbook:Roasting|Roast]] the tomatillos by wrapping them in heavy duty [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminum foil]] and placing them on a ''comal'' (cast iron [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]]) over your stovetop (this does not need to be done in the oven; it never is in Mexico). 
# After roasting the tomatillos for approximately 15 to 20 minutes, pull them off the heat and reserve.
# Roast the dried chilies and garlic directly on the ''comal''. Caution: the dried chilies will roast in less than a minute while the garlic will take longer.
# Combine the roasted tomatillos, chilies, garlic, water, salt, and pepper in a blender. Liquefy the mixture thoroughly for a few minutes to ensure that the sauce is smooth and consistent with no large pieces left floating around. You will probably end up with more salsa than you need for this recipe. Use it as a condiment for any other of your favorite Mexican dishes!

=== Chilaquiles ===
# Heat enough vegetable oil in a frying pan to deep fry the tortillas. It should be hot enough so that when you drop the pieces of tortillas into it they immediately begin to fry at a rapid pace.
# Allow the tortillas to fry until they become a chestnut brown, just not too dark or burnt. At this point, drain most of the oil out of the pan leaving only enough to fry the rest of the ingredients.
# Crack the egg into the fried tortillas and scramble it, folding the fried tortilla strips into the egg. At this point season this mixture with salt and pepper if desired. Take this mixture out of the pan and let it rest on a plate while you continue with the rest of the dish.
# Add some of the oil that was taken out of the pan earlier back into it and heat it up again. To this add the diced onion, and allow it to soften for a few minutes. Add the ''salsa de chile de árbol'' to the oil and onions and sauté it for a minute or two. Add a little bit of water to dilute it if it becomes too thick.
# Finally, return the fried tortilla and egg mixture to the onion and chili sauce in the pan and allow it cook only for about a minute, enough time to allow the tortillas to soak up some of the sauce.  Before plating it, add the cheese and enjoy!
==Notes, tips, and variations==

* In Mexico, very rarely is this dish made with tortilla chips but rather day-old tortillas that have stiffened. If you don't have day-old tortillas you can leave out fresh tortillas until they are stiff to get the right texture.
* The chiles are very hot; adjust to taste.
* For the cheese, you can use anything that melts well such as [[Cookbook:Monterey Jack Cheese|Monterey Jack]] or [[Cookbook:Manchego Cheese|Manchego]]
* The recipe for the chili sauce used in this recipe is of course a red sauce. If you prefer a green sauce, simply substitute the ''chiles de árbol'' with fresh jalapeño chilies that you can also roast in the same way. After you have roasted the chilies on the ''comal'' and thoroughly burnt the skins, place the chilies in a plastic bag with a small amount of water so as to allow them to steam. After about 5 minutes, remove the jalapeños from the bag and simply rub the skin off of them. Continue to make the sauce as indicated above.
* This dish can be made with strips of chicken in addition to or as a replacement for the egg. In Mexico chilaquiles are often served throughout the day and as such the addition of chicken strips will complement it as a dinner item. Using all the same ingredients just add some warmed and shredded chicken meat during the last step before you add the cheese.  Oftentimes, my mother would add a little bit of Mexican cream (somewhat like sour cream but more akin to creme fraiche) over the top of the chilaquiles right before we enjoyed them on our serving plate as a way to tone down the spicy heat of the dish.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Tikka
text:
__NOTOC__{{recipesummary|category=Chicken recipes|servings=4|time=30 minutes|difficulty=2|Image=[[Image:Chicken Tikka with some salad.jpg|300px|The cooked Chicken Tikka]]}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Meat_Recipes|Meat recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine_of_India|Cuisine of India]]

'''Chicken tikka''' is a chicken dish originating in the Punjab region of the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian Subcontinent]] made by baking [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] which has been [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinated]] in [[Cookbook:Spices and herbs|spices]] and [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yoghurt]]. It should not be confused with [[Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala|Chicken Tikka Masala]] (of which it is an ingredient). It is traditionally cooked on [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewers]] in a [[Cookbook:Tandoor|tandoor]] and is usually boneless. It is tasty when served with yellow rice and a spicy salad.

==Ingredients==
*675 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (1.5 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) skinless and boneless [[Cookbook:Chicken#Breast|chicken breast]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] into cubes
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] seed oil (see notes)
*50 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]] (2 [[Cookbook:Fluid Ounce|fl oz]]) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
*150 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]] (5 [[Cookbook:Fluid Ounce|fl oz]]) natural [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yoghurt]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]] (coriander leaves)
*4 large cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], finely [[Cookbook:Chop|chopped]]
*1–4 chopped fresh red [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chillis]] (depending on strength of the chillis and the desired strength of the marinade)
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Garam Masala|garam masala]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]] powder
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (use rock salt for best results)

==Procedure==
#Add all of the ingredients except the chicken to a non-metallic [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]], and mix well.
#Add the chicken and mix until fully coated.
#Ideally, the chicken should now be left in a refrigerator to [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] for at least 24 hours. It may not be safe to leave chicken which has previously been frozen for longer than 24 hours, but fresh chicken should be left to marinate for 48 hours for best results. If you do not wish to leave the chicken to marinate, simply continue to the next step.
#For best results, place on skewers and cook in a [[Cookbook:Tandoor|tandoor]] or ceramic pot oven. The chicken can also be cooked on skewers under a medium [[Cookbook:Grilling|grill]] for 5–8 minutes on each side or barbecued (cooking times depend on the temperature of the barbecue). Always ensure the chicken is cooked throughout before serving. It should come apart easily when pressed down with the side of a fork.
#Serve with [[Cookbook:Naan|naan]], with [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] or use in a [[Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala|Chicken Tikka Masala]].

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Mustard seed oil is considered unfit for human consumption in many parts of the world and is therefore not readily available. A poor alternative can be made by crackling 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] of [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] seeds in approximately 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbs]] of very hot [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]. Allow to cool then use in place of mustard seed oil.
*It is possible to make a tikka with almost any meat, the most commonly used other than chicken being [[Cookbook:Lamb|lamb]] and [[Cookbook:Mutton|mutton]].
*Tikka can be served either as main meal or as an appetiser.
*Powdered or dried ingredients can be substituted for fresh, but at the expense of taste.
*Some people prefer to make tikka with meat on-the-bone for improved flavour.

==Bibliography==
*  ''Curry Club Tandoori and Tikka Dishes'', Piatkus, London — {{ISBN|0749912839}} (1993)		
* ''India: Food & Cooking'', New Holland, London — {{ISBN|978-1845376192}} (2007)

title: Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
| category = Chicken recipes
| servings = 4
| time = 1 hour
| difficulty = 3
| Image = [[Image:Chicken Tikka Masala Curry.png|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Meat_Recipes|Meat recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]]

'''Chicken tikka masala''' is a dish based on chunks of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]]-style roasted chicken ([[Cookbook:Chicken Tikka|Chicken Tikka]]) cooked in a [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]] [[Cookbook:Curry|curry]] sauce, originating in India. There is no standard recipe for chicken tikka masala; a survey found that, of 48 different recipes, the only common ingredient was chicken.<ref>{{cite web |author= BBC E-Cyclopedia | url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/special_report/1999/02/99/e-cyclopedia/1285804.stm | title=Chicken tikka masala: Spice and easy does it |accessdate=28 September 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070716024029/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/special_report/1999/02/99/e-cyclopedia/1285804.stm |archive-date=16 July 2007}}</ref> The sauce usually includes tomato and either [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]] or [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut cream]] and various spices.

==Ingredients==
*675 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (1.5 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) cooked [[Cookbook:Chicken Tikka|Chicken Tikka]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] seed oil (see notes)
*4 large cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*200 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], finely chopped (optional)
*1 tin (28 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) plum [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], chopped
*1–4 chopped fresh green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]] (depending on strength of the chiles and the desired strength of the sauce)
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] chopped fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]] (coriander leaves)
*50 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]] (4 [[Cookbook:Fluid Ounce|fl oz]]) single [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] malt [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] or tamarind extract
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] curry paste
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbs]]<nowiki/>p [[Cookbook:Tandoori masala|tandoori masala paste]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbs]]<nowiki/>p [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbs]]<nowiki/>p [[Cookbook:Garam Masala|garam masala]]

==Procedure==
#Heat the oil in a [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] or large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]].
#Add the garlic and onions and [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|stir-fry]] until browned.
#Add the curry pastes and mix well, adding a little water or yogurt.
#Add the cooked chicken tikka, and [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|stir-fry]] for two minutes to heat through.
#Add the tomatoes, vinegar, tomato paste, and chilies and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for five minutes. Add more extra water if needed.
#Add the cream, garam masala, and chopped cilantro and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for a few times.
#Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with [[Cookbook:Naan|Naan]], [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] coloured yellow with [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]], [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] [[Cookbook:Bahjis|bahjis]] and/or a glass of white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]].

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*[[w:Mustard oil|Mustard seed oil]] is considered inappropriate for human consumption in many parts of the world and is therefore not always available. A poor alternative can be made by crackling ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] of [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] seeds in approximately 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] of very hot [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]. Allow to cool, then use in place of mustard seed oil.
*Powdered or concentrated ingredients can be substituted for fresh ones but at the amount of taste.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Riggies
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Chicken recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|Cuisine of the United States]]

'''Chicken Riggies''' (recipe by P.A. Johnson) is a Utica, NY classic. It is well known throughout the greater Mohawk Valley and once a year there is a festival in honor of this dish called Riggiefest, held to benefit the YWCA of the Mohawk Valley. Here is a recipe based from a Mohawk Valley native:  http://miocibo.com/2008/12/21/chicken-riggies/.

==Ingredients==
* 1 stick [[cookbook:margarine|margarine]] (not butter), melted
* 1 [[cookbook:onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 2–5 cloves [[cookbook:garlic|garlic]], minced
* 1 jar (20 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) sweet peppers, sliced and seeded
* 3 sliced hot cherry peppers (jarred ones with oil)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] grated [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]] 
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] boneless [[cookbook:chicken|chicken]] breast, [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]]
* 1 can [[cookbook:Chicken Broth|chicken broth]]
* 1 can (15 oz) [[Cookbook:Tomato Sauce|tomato sauce]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pint|pint]] [[cookbook:cream|cream]]
* 1 small can sliced black [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]]
* 1–1½ lb rigatoni [[cookbook:pasta|pasta]], cooked

==Procedure==
# [[cookbook:Sauté|Sauté]] onion, peppers, and garlic in the margarine slowly over low/medium heat until the onions are clear.
# Add the Parmesan, chicken breast, chicken stock, tomato sauce, cream, and olives. [[Cookbook:Simmer|Simmer]] for about an hour.
# Serve over the cooked pasta.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* It is important to use jarred peppers—the flavor of fresh peppers completely changes the recipe.
