'''Chocolate fudge''' is a traditional, rich [[Cookbook:Confections|candy]], especially around the holidays in the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|United States]].

==Ingredients==

* 2 ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (550 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 1.2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) white granulated [[cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ½ cup (125 g / 4.4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[cookbook:Margarine|margarine]] or [[cookbook:butter|butter]]
* ⅔ cup (160 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 5.4 oz) [[cookbook:Evaporated milk|evaporated milk]]
* 1 jar (7 oz / 200 g) [[Cookbook:Marshmallow Creme|marshmallow creme]]
* 2 cups (160 g / 5.6 oz) semi sweet [[cookbook:chocolate chips|chocolate chips]]
* ¾ cup (75 g / 2.6 oz) chopped [[cookbook:walnuts|walnuts]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]]

==Procedure==

# Line a {{convert|9|in|cm|adj=on}} square or {{convert|13|by|9|in|cm|adj=on}} pan with [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|foil]] so that foil extends over sides of pan; butter foil.
#In large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], combine sugar, margarine, and evaporated milk. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over medium heat, stirring constantly.
# After 5 minutes of constant stirring, remove saucepan from heat.
# Add marshmallow creme and chocolate chips; blend until smooth. Stir in walnuts and vanilla.
# Pour into buttered, foil-lined pan. Cool to room temperature.
# Score fudge into 36–48 squares. Refrigerate until firm.
# Remove fudge from pan by lifting foil; remove foil from sides of fudge. Using large knife, cut through scored lines. Store in refrigerator.

'''Chocolate sour-cream icing''' is an [[Cookbook:Icing|icing or frosting]] with a bit of tang to take the edge off the sugar overload. It can be icing or frosting depending on what you want.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Chocolate Chips|chocolate chips]]

title: Cookbook:Chocolate Chip Cookies (Gluten-Free)
text:
__NOTOC__ {{recipesummary | Category = Cookie recipes | Yield = 30 cookies | Servings = | Time = Prep: ~10 minutes
Baking: ~25 minutes | Rating = 2 | Energy = | Image = [[Image:Gluten-free chocolate chip cookies.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Desserts|Desserts]] These '''gluten-free chocolate chip cookies''' use [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|sweet rice flour]], also known as glutinous rice flour. Don't be fooled by the name; there's no gluten in glutinous rice flour (or any rice flour, for that matter). This flour, like most [[Cookbook:Gluten-Free|gluten-free]] flours, is easy to find if an Asian grocery can be located. It can also be found in many boutique grocery stores, such as Trader Joe's or Whole Foods. Other gluten-free flours may be substituted, but be prepared to adjust the amount of flour needed to compensate for variations in starchiness. It should go without saying, for any household coping with celiac disease, that it is imperative to make sure all your ingredients, work surfaces, and utensils are free of gluten contamination. Special care should be taken with compound ingredients such as baking powder; make sure its ingredients list does not include gluten-containing items such as modified food starch. The cookies are pictured to the right with various additions to the dough. Experimenting is encouraged, but please be careful choosing additions. Some of the cookies pictured have oats added, which introduce trace amounts of gluten and are '''not''' safe for celiacs. ==Ingredients== *½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (1 stick / 120 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] *½ cup (120 ml) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] *½ cup (120 ml) [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]] *2 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Eggs|eggs]] *½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]] *1¼ cup (300 ml / 1 cup + 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]]) [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|sweet rice flour]] *1 tsp [[Cookbook:Xanthan gum|xanthan gum]] *¾ tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]] *½ tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]] *[[Cookbook:Chocolate chip|Chocolate chips]] (as many as you like) ==Equipment== *Large [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]] *[[Cookbook:Mixer|Stand mixer]] and bowl (or a [[Cookbook:Mixer|hand-held mixer]] and a medium mixing bowl) *Wooden spoon *[[Cookbook:Cookie Sheet|Cookie sheet]] *Non-stick [[cookbook:silicone baking sheet liner|silicone baking sheet liner]] (Silpat, etc.) ==Procedure== [[Image:Gluten-free chocolate chip cookie dough.jpg|thumb|The finished dough (with various additions), ready for baking]] #Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). #Mix the sweet rice flour, xanthan gum, baking powder and baking soda in a large mixing bowl. #In a smaller mixing bowl or stand mixer, [[Cookbook:Creaming|cream]] the butter, sugar, and brown sugar. Add the eggs and vanilla and continue mixing. #Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix thoroughly with a wooden spoon. Don't worry about over-mixing; since there is no gluten in the flour, there is no danger of overworking it. #[[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] in the chocolate chips. #Line [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|cookie sheet]] with silicone mat and spoon on balls of dough, about 1½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] (4 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) in diameter. #Put cookie dough in the fridge for 30–40 minutes or into the freezer for 10–20 minutes. #Bake until golden brown. ==Notes, tips, and variations== * These will likely take longer to bake than gluten-containing cookies—perhaps about 25 minutes. Baking time will depend on the flour you use, since the protein content of the flour will determine the rate of browning from the Maillard reaction. * The silicone baking sheet liner is important, as these cookies tend to stick to the pan more than most. If you don't have one, [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]] might also work. title: Cookbook:Chokladboll (Swedish Chocolate Balls)
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Cookie recipes|yield=24 balls|time=20 minutes|difficulty=1|image=[[Image:Chokladbollar.jpg|300px]]|energy=207Calories/866 kJ}}
{{nutritionsummary|1 ball (47 g)|24|207|94|10.4 g|7.5 g|20 mg|92 mg|26.2 g|1.0 g|12.9 g|2.2 g|3%|2%|3%|4%}}

A '''chokladboll''' (literally meaning ''chocolate ball'') is a traditional [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Sweden|Swedish]] pastry often eaten with [[Cookbook:Coffee|coffee]] during [[w:Fika_(coffee_break)|fika]]. They are quick and easy to prepare, since they require no baking and only a few, common ingredients.

== Ingredients ==
* 3 ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 1.1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) [[Cookbook:Oats|quick oats]]
* 1 ¼ cups (275 g / 9.7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Tbsp|Tbsp]] (75 g / 2.6 oz) [[Cookbook:Cocoa|cocoa]]
* 1 Tbsp (15 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 14 g / 0.49 oz) [[Cookbook:Vanilla Sugar|vanilla sugar]] OR 1 tsp (5 ml / 0.17 oz) [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract, added with the coffee
* ⅔ cup (160 g / 5.6 oz) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]], softened
* 6 Tbsp (90 ml / 3 oz) cold [[Cookbook:Coffee|coffee]]
* Flaked [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] or [[Cookbook:Pearl Sugar|pearl sugar]]

== Procedure ==
# Mix oats, sugar, vanilla sugar, and cocoa in a large bowl.
# Using your hands or a [[Cookbook:Potato Masher|potato masher]], incorporate the butter into the dry ingredients until the dough has an even consistency.
# Add the coffee and mix until incorporated.
# Fill a small bowl with flaked coconut or pearl sugar.
# With your hands, roll the dough into 1-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (3 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) diameter balls.
# Roll each ball in the coconut or pearl sugar and place on a tray.
# Chill chocolate balls for at least one hour before serving.

title: Cookbook:Chocolate Chip Pancakes I
text:
__NOTOC__{{recipesummary
| category = Pancake recipes
| difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] 
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (½ stick) unsalted [[cookbook:butter|butter]] 
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 8.5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) non-skim [[cookbook:milk|milk]] 
* 1¼ cups (170 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 6 oz) [[cookbook:flour|flour]] 
* 1 tablespoon granulated [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]] 
* 4 teaspoons [[cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]] 
* ¾ teaspoon [[cookbook:salt|salt]] 
* 2 ea. (100 g) [[cookbook:egg|egg]]s 
* 6 oz (170 g) semisweet [[cookbook:chocolate chips|chocolate chips]], or less to taste
* [[cookbook:Butter|Butter]], for cooking

== Procedure ==
#Combine the butter and milk in a small [[cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]].
#Place over low heat just until warm and the butter is melted. Let cool slightly.
#In a bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt; mix well.
#In a large bowl, [[cookbook:whisk|whisk]] the eggs with a fork. [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] in the milk mixture. 
#Add the dry ingredients and mix just until barely blended.
#Add the chocolate chips and mix.
#Heat a [[cookbook:griddle|griddle]] or large [[cookbook:skillet|skillet]] over medium heat.
#Add about 1 teaspoon of butter and melt until bubbly.
#Ladle 3 tablespoons of batter for each pancake onto the hot surface and cook until bubbly on the top and golden brown on the bottom.
#Flip and cook until golden brown on the other side, about 30 seconds more.
#Repeat until all the batter is used.
#Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Use bleached instead of unbleached flour to make a more tender pancake.
* If using salted butter, reduce salt to ¼ teaspoon.
* You can substitute 1 tablespoon of lemon juice (or vinegar) in milk for the buttermilk.
* Pancake batter should pour, not glug! On the other hand, runny batter makes thin, oddly shaped pancakes that frequently collide on the griddle. Stir in a touch more flour into thin batter. For batter that's too thick, whisk in water, a teaspoon at a time.
* The temperature of the pan or griddle is important: too hot and the pancakes are dark and raw; too cool and they're blond and hard. For tender, golden brown pancakes, heat the pan or griddle on low while you make the batter. Then increase the heat to medium and generously brush the pan or griddle with oil. It's ready when the oil starts to shimmer and, in any skillet or griddle other than non-stick, sends out tendrils that resemble an octopus or spider. But if the pan starts to smoke, set it down off the burner until the smoking subsides and the oil cools a bit.

You've heard of Reese's Peanut Butter Cups, and you've heard of peanut butter toast. Why not combine them!?

==Ingredients==

* 1 slice of [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]]
* 2–4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]], smooth or crunchy
* 1–2 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] [[Cookbook:Chocolate Chips|chocolate chips]]

==Procedure==

# [[cookbook:toast|Toast]] the bread on both sides in a [[Cookbook:Oven|toaster oven]], using the broiler setting.
# Smear the peanut butter on the bread.
# Sprinkle chocolate chips lightly (or heavily, if you want!) over the peanut butter.
# Put the toast back under the broiler for about 20 seconds to melt the chocolate.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Some people like to spread the chocolate chips, after softening under the broiler.
* One variation is to spread marshmallow fluff over the peanut butter, replace the chocolate chips with a Nestles' crunch bar, use 2 toasts, and make it a sandwich.
* Instead of heating the chocolate under the broiler, add cold chocolate chips (from the refrigerator) for a nice temperature contrast.
* According to taste, use milk, dark, semisweet, or white chocolate chips.

title: Cookbook:Chocolate-Jalapeno Truffles
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Confection recipes|yield=36|time=1 hour|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Mexican cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Native American cuisine|Native American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

==Ingredients==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Coffee|instant coffee powder]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 10 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] best-quality semisweet [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]], in small pieces or chips
* 10 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (1¼ sticks) best-quality unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], cold and cut into small pieces
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Jalapeño|jalapeños]], roasted, peeled, seeded, and finely [[Cookbook:Chop|chopped]] (wear rubber gloves)
* ½ cup unsweetened [[Cookbook:Cocoa Powder|cocoa powder]], [[Cookbook:Sift|sift]] onto a plate

==Procedure==

# In a metal 1-[[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] mixing bowl, dissolve coffee in water.
# Add the chocolate and set on top of a pan of gently [[Cookbook:Simmer|simmering]] water.
# When the chocolate has softened completely but is not hot, remove from heat and stir until smooth.
# [[Cookbook:Beat|Beat]] in the cold butter a small piece at a time, adding a new piece as soon as the previous one is almost absorbed.
# Beat with a [[Cookbook:Mixer|hand-held electric mixer]] until creamy, about 10 minutes.
# Continue beating for a few minutes to cool. This can also be done in a stand mixer, fitted with the whip attachment.
# Add half of the jalapeños and taste. Add more jalapeño to your taste; remember that the heat will intensify with time. Try for a balance of sweet and heat.
# Scrape into a small, deep container, press a piece of plastic wrap on the surface, and chill overnight, until completely firm.
# Scoop out small balls and roll in the cocoa powder.
# Keep refrigerated until ready to serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Roll the balls in finely chopped pistachios, almonds, or macadamia nuts.

title: Cookbook:Chocolate-coated Marshmallow Treats (Flødeboller)
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Confection recipes
| Difficulty = 4
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Flødeboller''' are a Danish chocolate-coated [[Cookbook:Marshmallow|marshmallow]] treats. You can use flat, round shortbread (or other) biscuits instead, or even sponge circles instead of the marzipan biscuits.

== Ingredients ==

=== Marzipan biscuits ===
* 100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|icing sugar]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (60 g) pasteurized [[Cookbook:Egg White|egg whites]]
* 300 g [[Cookbook:Marzipan|marzipan]] (pure)

=== Vanilla filling ===
* 250 g white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 75 g water
* 110 g [[Cookbook:Glucose|glucose syrup]]
* 4 ea. (140 g) pasteurized egg whites
* 15 g sugar
* ½ [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] pod/bean
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] icing sugar
* Concentrated or dry flavoring (optional)

=== Chocolate coating ===
* 500 g dark (58–64%) [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]]

== Procedure ==

=== Marzipan biscuits ===
# Mix icing sugar and egg whites in a bowl
# Mix the egg-sugar mixture into the marzipan in several stages until the dough is uniform.
# Use a [[Cookbook:Pastry Bag|pastry bag]] to make flat, round biscuits, approximately 5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] in diameter.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in oven at 190°C until golden (approximately 10 min).
# Cool to ambient temperature.

=== Filling ===
# Mix 250 g of sugar, the water and glucose syrup in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and heat to exactly 117°C.
# Meanwhile, [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] the egg whites lightly with 15 g of sugar.
# Gradually pour the hot sugar mixture directly into the egg whites, while still beating.
# [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] the egg white mixture until very stiff.
# Split open vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds, mix these with the icing sugar. Add this to the egg white mixture along with any flavoring, and stir slowly until uniform in appearance. Avoid deflating the meringue.
# Use a pastry bag to pipe 5 cm tall meringue tops on the marzipan biscuits. Make sure the foam adheres to the biscuit, otherwise it will fall off while coating.
# Leave at room temperature or put in refrigerator while preparing chocolate coating.

=== Chocolate coating ===
# Finely chop the chocolate.
# Melt half the chocolate carefully in a bain-marie (or a pot floating in water in a bigger pot). Aim for 48–50°C.
# Put the other half of the chocolate into a bowl (make sure it is big enough for the entire cake can be submerged in chocolate). Add ⅔ of the melted chocolate, and let the two melt together WITHOUT HEATING! Only add more melted chocolate if the lumps do not melt away. The temperature must not exceed 34°C. This will keep the chocolate shiny and crunchy.
# Dip the meringue tops into the chocolate. Make sure all the meringue is covered. The biscuit is up to you.
# Sprinkle or roll in desiccated coconut, then leave to set. Do not reheat the chocolate if it starts to set, use instead some of the warm melted chocolate.

title: Cookbook:Chocolate Chip Cookies I
text:
__NOTOC__ {{recipesummary | Category = Recipes for dessert | Yield = 56 cookies | Servings = 10 | Time = Prep: 20 minutes
Cooking: 12 minutes
Total: 32 minutes | Rating = | Energy = | Image = [[Image:Chocolate chip cookies.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|Cuisine of the United States]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] ==Ingredients== *2 sticks (½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] / 225 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], softened *¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (180 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated white sugar]] *¾ cup (180 ml) packed [[Cookbook:Brown_Sugar|brown sugar]] *¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla_Extract|vanilla extract]] *2 standard (100 g) [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] *2 ¼ cups (600 ml / 290 g) [[Cookbook:Flour|all-purpose flour]] *1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Baking_Soda|baking soda]] *1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] *1 teaspoon dry ground [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] or [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]] peel (optional) *2 cups (480 ml / 12 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Chocolate_chip|semi-sweet chocolate morsels / chips]] *5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (150 g) chopped [[Cookbook:Nuts and Seeds|nuts]], such as groundnuts (optional) ==Procedure== #Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to {{#invoke:temperature|f|375}} ({{#invoke:temperature|c|210}}), or {{#invoke:temperature|f|350}} ({{#invoke:temperature|c|195}}) if you want chewy cookies. #[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar in a large mixer bowl. #Add eggs one at a time, [[Cookbook:Beating|beating]] until fully incorporated. #Add vanilla extract and beat in. #In a small bowl, [[Cookbook:Sifting|sift]] together the dry ingredients (except chocolate and nuts). Add to the wet mixture in two parts and [[Cookbook:Folding|fold]] until combined. If you beat this too long, you may get some [[Cookbook:Gluten|gluten]] formation which will change the cookie texture. #Stir in chocolate morsels (chips), and nuts if using. #Drop dough by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheets]]. There should be enough fat in the cookie dough to prevent sticking, but using [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]] or [[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] pans may help if you find this not to be the case. #[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the preheated oven for 10–12 minutes or until golden brown (cooking times may vary). Let stand for about 1 minute and remove from hot baking sheet to cool on a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|wire rack]]. ==Notes, tips, and variations== === Ingredients === * Use cake flour instead of [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose]], replace granulated sugar with brown sugar and use butter instead of margarine. Using cake flour and brown sugar allows you to use butter without fear of your cookies becoming puddles (which is the only reason to use margarine in the first place). * Use some vegetable shortening in place of butter/margarine to reduce "spread" (cookies will be thicker). * Add some vegetable oil (no more than 1/5 of total fat) in place of butter/margarine to increase spread, resulting in thinner cookies. * Using chocolate with a cocoa content greater than 65% will result in a significantly different taste than the "traditional" recipe. In general, if you find the raw chocolate to be too bitter or not enjoyable to eat, you may not like them in the cookies (no matter the quality). * Adding a few shakes of ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] with the dry ingredients also gives more flavor. * If you want to use regular flour as well as butter, the trick is to increase the amount of flour to 3+ cups, which should result in a fairly stiff dough that will not spread out very much. This trick even works with whole wheat flour. * The proportion of granulated to brown sugar may be adjusted to suit taste. More brown sugar will result in chewier cookies. More white sugar will result in crisper cookies. * Adding a greater quantity of vanilla extract (between ½ and ¾ of a teaspoon, rather than ¼) gives the cookie a more pronounced flavor. * If vanilla extract is not readily available, substitute two teaspoons of vanilla sugar for granulated sugar. * Add a small amount of oatmeal to give cookies more flavor and mouth-feel. === Method === * Some people also recommend chilling dough before baking, though this is usually not necessary. Chilling dough may help to reduce spread, resulting in thicker cookies. * Use an ungreased, non-stick baking sheet instead of a greased sheet to help reduce spread, for thicker cookies. Conversely, grease your sheet if you like thinner (crispier) cookies. *The quality of the flavoring ingredients makes a great difference in the outcome. Using top-quality butter, chocolate, and vanilla will produce a superior cookie. *Using chopped bar chocolate instead of pre-formed chips will result in a more rustic texture -- just make sure the pieces are small enough to eat comfortably. *Do not stack hot cookies otherwise they will bend out of shape and not cool as quickly. Use a cooling rack instead for the best results. * For a stronger nut flavor, toast the nuts. Spread them evenly on a baking pan and set them in the 350°F oven for ten minutes. Take them out and let them cool before adding them to the dough. *If you like a soft and squishy middle in your cookie, take them out one minute sooner for a nice soft middle. == Ingredients ==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 170°C fan/convection.

Cooking: 5 minutes per skillet | difficulty = 2 }}{{Recipe}} == Ingredients == * 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (140 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 4.9 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose bleached flour]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] * ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]] * ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]] * ¾ cup (185 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 6.3 oz) [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]] * ¼ cup (60 ml / 2 oz) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] * 1 standard (50 g) [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted * 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]] * [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]] for brushing [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]] * 8 tablespoons miniature [[Cookbook:Chocolate Chips|chocolate chips]] == Procedure == # Heat a large non-stick [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] or griddle over low heat while preparing ingredients. # Mix flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, and baking soda in medium bowl. # [[Cookbook:Microwave Oven|Microwave]] buttermilk and milk in a 2-[[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] glass measuring cup until room temperature (20 to 30 seconds). # [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] in egg, butter, and vanilla. # Add wet ingredients to dry ingredients and whisk until just mixed. # Return [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]] to measuring cup, stirring in a teaspoon or two of [[Cookbook:Water|water]], if necessary, to make a thick but pourable batter. # Increase heat to medium and generously brush skillet or griddle with oil. # When oil starts to spider, but before it starts to smoke, pour in batter, about ¼ cup at a time, to make pancakes. Work in batches, if necessary, to avoid overcrowding. # Sprinkle 1 tablespoon miniature chocolate chips on uncooked side of each pancake as it cooks. # When pancake bottoms are golden brown and tops start to bubble (2 to 3 minutes), flip pancakes. # Cook until pancakes are golden brown on remaining side. # Repeat, brushing skillet or griddle with oil. # Serve hot. title: Cookbook:Chocolate Scotcheroos
text:
__NOTOC__ {{recipe summary | category = Recipes for dessert | Yield = 36 bar cookies | servings = | Time = Active: 30 minutes | difficulty = 2 | image = [[File:XXX Chocolate Scotcheroos (6564988783).jpg |300px]] | energy = 160 calories each
(~5,800 for the whole pan) | note = }} {{recipe}} '''Chocolate scotcheroos''' are a peanut butter cereal bar with a chocolate topping. They are similar to Rice Krispie Treats, except that they contain peanut butter instead of marshmallows. They are cooked on the stovetop instead of being baked in the oven. == Ingredients == {| class="wikitable" style="background: none;color:inherit;" !Ingredient !Volume !Weight |- |[[Cookbook:Corn Syrup|Corn syrup]] |1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] |300 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] |- |[[Cookbook:Sugar|White sugar]] |1 cup |200 g |- |[[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|Peanut butter]] |1 cup |275 g |- |Puffed rice [[Cookbook:Breakfast Cereal|cereal]], such as Kellogg's Rice Krispies |6 cups |175 g |- |[[Cookbook:Chocolate chips|Chocolate chips]] |1 cup |175 g |- |[[Cookbook:Butterscotch|Butterscotch]]-flavored chips |1 cup |175 g |} == Equipment == * 9 x 13 x 2 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (33 x 23 x 5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]] or [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]] * 3 [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] or larger [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] * [[Cookbook:Mixer|Mixing spoon]], such as a wooden spoon * [[Cookbook:Wax Paper|Wax paper]], [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]], or [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|baking paper]] (optional) * [[Cookbook:Spatula|Spatula]], for spreading the chocolate topping == Procedure == # Spray the baking pan with cooking spray, or butter it lightly. Set aside. # Put the corn syrup and sugar in the saucepan. Cook over medium heat until the sugar is dissolved and the mixture begins to bubble. Do not overcook, or the bars will be hard. If you are using a [[Cookbook:Candy Thermometer|candy thermometer]], aim for 235–240 °F (115 °C), which is the soft ball candy stage. Remove from the heat. # Add the peanut butter, and stir until the color is uniform. # Stir in the cereal. It may be easiest to stir in half the cereal at a time, instead of adding it all at once. # Scrape all of the warm cereal mixture into the baking pan. Gently press it into a flat layer. You can do this with back of the mixing spoon, or you can cover the cereal mixture with a sheet of wax paper and use your hands. Do not crush the cereal, or the bars will be too hard and dense. Set aside. # Place the chocolate and butterscotch chips in the saucepan (it is not necessary to wash it first), and put it back on the stove over medium heat. Stir to [[Cookbook:Melting chocolate|melt the chocolate]] and butterscotch chips together. As soon as the morsels have melted, spread the chocolate mixture over the top of the cereal mixture. # Cool the pan until the topping is firm. If you put it in the refrigerator, this step will take about an hour. # Cut the bars into 36 small pieces, approximately 1.5 x 1.5 inches (4 x 5 cm). Serve at room temperature. == Notes, tips, and variations == * Store at room temperature, tightly covered. They will keep for a week. * Any type or shape of pan can be used, as long as it can comfortably hold about 10 cups (2.5 liters) in volume. The warm cereal mixture can also be pressed into large [[Cookbook:Cookie Cutter|cookie cutters]] or other forms to make circles, hearts, or other simple shapes. * You can reduce the amount of white sugar to as low as 50% (though some will think this too far). The result will be a softer, chewier treat that will still taste very sweet. * You can use brown sugar instead of white. * You can use either ordinary or natural ("stirring type") peanut butter. * You can use a 60% chocolate bar instead of chocolate chips. * The chocolate and butterscotch-flavored chips can alternatively be [[Cookbook:Melting chocolate|melted]] in a microwave. * If you can't get butterscotch-flavored chips, then you can substitute peanut butter-flavored morsels. Semi-sweet chocolate chips are harder than either, so if you use only semi-sweet chocolate chips, consider melting a small spoonful of white vegetable shortening into the chocolate to soften the topping. * The topping can be decorated with colorful sprinkles or drizzled with a little bit of melted white chocolate, butterscotch chips, or peanut-flavored chips. * This dish is not suitable for people with peanut allergies, but it looks similar to non-peanut butter cereal bars. If you are taking these treats to share at a potluck or another group, consider decorating the top with peanuts or with a drizzle of melted peanut butter to make sure the peanut content is clear. * These bars are sturdy and travel well. They can be safely mailed during cold weather, but during warm weather, the chocolate topping will smear. * Compared to marshmallow-based rice crisp treats, this has more fat (from the peanut butter and the chocolate topping), more sugar, and about three times as many calories per pan. Consequently, it is normal to cut smaller pieces. [[Category:Recipes using white sugar]] [[Category:Recipes for dessert]] [[Category:Gluten-free recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using chocolate]] [[Category:Recipes using peanut butter]] [[Category:Recipes using corn syrup]] [[Category:Recipes using cereal]]

title: Cookbook:Chocolate Orbit Cake
text:
__notoc__ {{recipe summary | category = Cake recipes | Yield = 9-inch single layer cake | servings = 12 | time = Active: 20 minutes
Baking: 90 minutes
Chilling: 3 hours | difficulty = 2 | image = | Energy = 400 calories per serving | note = }} {{Recipe}} '''Chocolate orbit cake''' is a dense, flourless, gluten-free, nut-free, deeply chocolate dessert made with just four ingredients. The texture is somewhere in between a [[Cookbook:New York Cheesecake|New York cheesecake]] and cooled [[Cookbook:Chocolate ganache|chocolate ganache]]. The recipe was originally developed by American pastry chef and cookbook author David Lebovitz. This version of [https://www.davidlebovitz.com/shf-27-chocolat-1/ his original recipe] requires relatively few skills beyond stirring and following directions, and no special equipment. It is baked with a [[Cookbook:Bain-marie|''bain-marie'']] method. == Ingredients == {| class="wikitable" !Ingredient !Count !Volume !Weight |- |Unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] |almost 2 sticks |14 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] |200 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) |- |Chopped semi-sweet or bittersweet [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]] (60% to 70%) |– |1 ⅔[[Cookbook:Cup| cup]] |280 g (10 oz) |- |White granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] |– |1 cup |200 g |- |Whole [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] |5 ea. |– |– |} == Equipment == * Microwave-safe bowl, or a pan for [[Cookbook:Melting chocolate|melting chocolate]] and butter on the stove top * [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]] * [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] (or spoon or fork for stirring) * 9-inch round [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake pan]], at least 1.5 inches (4 cm) deep * [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|Parchment baking paper]] (or waxed paper) * Aluminum foil * An oven-proof pan that is big enough for a 9-inch pan to sit inside (e.g., a larger cake pan, casserole dish, or all-metal skillet) == Procedure == # Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|350 °F (175°C, gas mark 4—moderate)]]. # Line the bottom of the cake pan with a piece of parchment paper. Optionally, butter the sides of the cake pan. # [[Cookbook:Melting chocolate|Melt the butter and chocolate]] together until smooth and well-combined. The easiest way to do this is in the microwave: Put the chocolate and butter in a microwave-safe bowl or glass measuring pitcher and heat it for 30–60 seconds at a time, stirring each time, until it is nearly all melted. Let it sit for a few minutes so the residual heat will finish melting the chocolate, then give it a final stir. # Put the sugar and eggs in a large mixing bowl. Briefly whisk the sugar and eggs together. # Drizzle the melted chocolate mixture into the sugar–egg mixture, whisking until the batter is smooth in texture and uniform in appearance. The goal of whisking is to combine the ingredients thoroughly, but not to beat air into the cake batter. # Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan, then cover the cake pan with a piece of aluminum foil. # Place the foil-covered pan in a larger, oven-proof pan. Carefully pour very hot water (can be [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]]) into the larger pan, so that the foil-covered cake pan is sitting in a [[Cookbook:Bain-marie|hot water bath]] (called a ''bain marie'' in French). The water should be an inch (2.5 cm) deep, or approximately halfway up the side of the foil-covered cake pan. Don't pour the hot water on top of the foil or so high that it might get inside the cake pan. # Carefully put the whole bain-marie assembly in the preheated oven. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for about 75–90 minutes, until the cake is set and the surface is nearly dry. To test, remove the cake and its water bath from the oven, and remove the aluminum foil from the top. The surface will be pocked by little craters like an asteroid, which is the source of its name—don't worry, as they'll be covered before serving. The middle of the cake shouldn't jiggle when the cake pan is moved, and when you lightly touch the surface, your finger should come away nearly clean. If it needs just a few more minutes, it's okay to put the cake back in the oven without re-covering it. However, if you think it will need more than about 10 more minutes, re-cover it with the foil and put the whole water bath assembly back in the oven. # When it is done, remove the cake pan from the water bath and remove the foil. Cool the cake in the pan on the counter or a wire cooling rack until it is safe to cover it with plastic wrap and put it in the refrigerator. A large rubber band can help secure the plastic wrap, if needed. Chill the cake in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours (and up to overnight) until firmly set. # To serve, first let the cake warm up to room temperature for about 30 minutes. Slide a dull knife around the edge of the cake pan to loosen the sides. Flip the cake upside down onto a large plate or serving platter. Carefully peel the parchment paper off the cake. == Notes, tips, and variations == * This recipe is gluten-free, nut-free, flourless, and low in sodium. It is also high in total fats, saturated fats, and cholesterol, as well as being moderately high in added sugars. * This recipe can be scaled up or down somewhat. For an 8-inch round pan, scale the recipe down to use 4 eggs. For a 10-inch round, scale the recipe up to use 6 eggs. The baking time will need to be adjusted as a result (possibly by about 10 minutes). To serve a larger crowd, bake two cakes instead of trying to double the recipe. A half recipe could be baked in a [[Cookbook:Loaf Pan|loaf pan]], with a shorter baking time. * Use high-quality chocolate bars (or fèves), not chocolate chips or chocolate-flavored melting wafers, which may contain unwanted additives such as milk, whey, milkfat, vegetable oil, or palm oil. There are many brands of couverture chocolate that are popular with professional bakers, such as Valrhona, Callebaut, and Guittard; anything that you like to eat and is similar to these will work. * The recipe was designed to work with a bittersweet or semi-sweet chocolate (around 60% to 70% cacao solids)—do not use other varieties such as unsweetened baking chocolate or milk chocolate. You could try somewhat lighter or darker, depending on your preferences, but it should be a plain chocolate with simple ingredients (cacao beans, sugar, cocoa butter, vanilla, lecithin) that you like eating by itself. For example, Scharffen Berger Chocolate recommends their 62% semi-sweet chocolate for this recipe. * For a mocha variation, add 2 teaspoons of instant espresso powder to the sugar and egg mixture. * Optionally, decorate the top of the cake with lightly sweetened [[Cookbook:Whipped Cream|whipped cream]] or a sifting of [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|powdered sugar]] just before serving. The cake can also be served with a favorite flavored whipped cream (e.g., chocolate, mint, raspberry, or coffee), [[Cookbook:Crème Anglaise|crème anglaise]], or raspberry sauce. A dark chocolate ganache would probably be gilding the lily. * To cut the cake into neat slices, place a thin knife in very hot water until it is heated. Make one cut through the cake. Wipe the chocolate off the knife blade, and reheat the blade in hot water. Repeat this until the cake has been cut into 12 (or more) wedge-shaped slices. * It is possible to bake this cake in a [[Cookbook:Springform Pan|springform pan]]. However, that will require carefully wrapping the outside of the pan in large pieces of aluminum foil, to prevent any of the hot water in the ''bain marie'' from leaking into the cake. Using an ordinary cake pan reduces the risk of ending up with chocolate soup instead of chocolate cake. * This cake can be stored in the refrigerator, covered, for at least 3 days. For the best flavor, remove the cake from the refrigerator about 30 minutes before serving, so it can come to room temperature. {{DEFAULTSORT:{{PAGENAME}}}} [[Category:Recipes using dark chocolate]] [[Category:Recipes for cake]] [[Category:Recipes with metric units]] [[Category:Gluten-free recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using butter]] [[Category:Recipes using egg]] [[Category:Recipes using granulated sugar]]

title: Cookbook:Christmas Mince Pies (Meat-Free)
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Pie recipes

}}

{{recipe}}

This is the recipe for the fruity mince pies that we all know and eat at Christmas time. These typically do not contain minced beef, but they may not be completely vegetarian since fruit mince can sometimes contain [[Cookbook:Suet|suet]].

== Ingredients ==
* Shortcrust [[Cookbook:Pastry Dough|pastry dough]], either homemade or shop bought
* Fruit mince, either homemade or shop bought

title: Cookbook:Chuu Chee Fish
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Fish recipes|servings=4|time=1 hour|difficulty=3}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine_of_Thailand|Thai Cuisine]]

'''Chu Chee Fish''' is whole [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] in ''kaeng chuu chee curry'' [[Cookbook:Sauces|sauce]] with lime leaves. This very tasty distinctly [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Thailand|Thai]] fish dish is great as one of the main courses of a Thai banquet. It is also good on its own with [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]].

==Ingredients==
*650 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] whole [[cookbook:bream|bream]] or similar [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|metric cup]] vegetable [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]] (reserve 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] for [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|stir-frying]] curry paste)
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] of kaeng chu chee curry paste
*6 dried [[Cookbook:Kaffir Lime Leaf|Kaffir lime leaves]]
*1 metric cup [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] (warning: perhaps the metric 20 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]] one) [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|fish sauce]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*Fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]]
*1 fresh red [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile pepper]]

==Procedure==
#In a [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] or large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frypan]], over high heat, [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] fish using most of the vegetable oil, until golden on one side. It will take about 5 minutes.
#Lower heat and, using [[Cookbook:Tongs|tongs]], gently turn fish over.
#Turn up heat again and cook until golden. Using tongs again, lift fish gently onto a serving plate.
#In the wok, gently [[cookbook:stir-fry|stir-fry]] the curry-paste and lime leaves in remaining tablespoon of oil.
#Add coconut milk and fish sauce. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] for about 5 minutes.
#Add sugar and simmer for another 5 minutes.
#Taste to see if extra coconut milk, fish sauce, or sugar is required.
#Pour sauce over fish and [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]] with cilantro and chopped chili peppers.

==Warnings==
*Always wash your hands after handling chili peppers. Be especially careful not to touch your eyes, your kids, or pets.

==Ingredients==
*1 or so [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] of [[Cookbook:Duck|duck]] [[Cookbook:Fat|fat]]

==Procedure==
#In a [[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|pot]] large enough to in the end hold everything, melt the duck fat over medium heat.

title: Cookbook:Cioppino (Italian Seafood Stew)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Seafood recipes|servings=6–8|time=1 hour|difficulty=2
| Image = [[Image:Cioppino.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Seafood|Seafood]] | [[cookbook:Italian-American cuisine|Italian-American cuisine]]

'''Cioppino''' is a [[cookbook:fish|fish]] [[cookbook:stew|stew]] descended from the various regional fish soups and stews of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian cooking]]. It was developed by the fishermen who settled in the North Beach section of San Francisco. Originally it was made on the boats while out at sea and later became a staple as Italian restaurants proliferated in the city. The name comes from the Italian ''ciuppin'', a word which described the local fish stew in the regional dialect of the port city of Genoa.<ref>[http://www.nytimes.com/1988/04/24/travel/fare-of-the-country-cioppino-fish-stew-from-the-pacific.html?sec=travel&spon=&pagewanted=print Info on cioppino from the ''New York Times'']</ref> It's customary to serve cioppino with San Francisco sourdough bread. However, any bread with a thick, chewy crust will do.

The below recipe is based on one by Giada De Laurentiis.<ref>[http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/giada-de-laurentiis/cioppino-recipe2/index.html Cioppino recipe by Giada De Laurentiis]</ref> Be sure to review the [[Cookbook:Mussel|tips for cooking with mussels]].
==Ingredients==
*3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*1 large [[Cookbook:Fennel|fennel bulb]], thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*6 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] [[cookbook:onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*8 ounces of [[cookbook:celery|celery]], chopped
*3 large [[Cookbook:shallot|shallots]], chopped 
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*4 large [[cookbook:garlic|garlic]] cloves, finely chopped 
*¾ teaspoon dried crushed [[Cookbook:Red pepper flakes|red pepper flakes]], plus more to taste 
*6 ounces [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:tomato|tomatoes]] 
*1 ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] dry white [[Cookbook:wine|wine]] 
*5 cups water
*1 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]
*2 pounds [[Cookbook:crab|crabs]] (any type), cut into pieces
*2 pounds [[Cookbook:mussel|mussels]], scrubbed and debearded
*1 pound [[Cookbook:scallop|scallops]]
*1 ½ pounds [[Cookbook:Tilapia|tilapia]] (or other white, firm-fleshed [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]]), cut into 2-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] chunks
*2 loaves of [[cookbook:San Francisco Sourdough Bread|San Francisco sourdough bread]] or any other [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] with a chewy crust

==Procedure==
#Heat the oil in a very large pot over medium heat. 
#Add the fennel, onion, shallots, and salt and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until the onion is translucent. 
#Add the garlic and red pepper flakes, and sauté for 2 minutes.
#Stir in the tomato paste.
#Add tomatoes with their juices, wine, water, crabs, celery and bay leaf. Cover and bring to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]].
#Reduce the heat to medium-low. Simmer, covered, for about 30 minutes to allow the flavors to blend.
#Add the mussels to the cooking liquid. Cover and cook until the mussels begin to open.This should take about 5 minutes.
#Add the scallops and fish. Simmer gently until the fish and scallops are just cooked through and all the mussels are completely open, gently stirring occasionally. This should take about another 10 minutes.
#Check the soup for closed mussels and throw them out. Remove the bay leaf. 
#Season the soup to taste with more salt and red pepper flakes.

'''Cinnamon croûtons''' are a sweet variation on the classic salad [[Cookbook:Crouton|croûton]], which can be used to enhance a fruit salad. Alternately, these croûtons make a good addition to pumpkin, sweet potato, or carrot soups.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Breakfast Recipes|Breakfast Recipes]]

A tasty [[Cookbook:Muffin|muffin]] recipe with apple chunks and dried cranberries.

==Ingredients==
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (180 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) natural wheat bran
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (180 g) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (360 g) [[Cookbook:Flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
* ⅛ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]

* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (80 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]

* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 g) dried [[Cookbook:Cranberry|cranberries]]

==Procedure==
#Combine bran and milk into a [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]]. Let rest for 5 minutes.
#Combine flour, baking powder, cinnamon, salt, baking soda and nutmeg in another [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]].

#Spoon batter into greased [[Cookbook:Muffin Pan|muffin cups]].
#Fill muffin cups ¾ full. Bake at [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|400°F]] (200°C) for 15 to 20 minutes, or until tester comes out clean.

==Notes, tips and variations==
*For an optional topping, add 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] of granulated sugar and ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] of cinnamon to the batter when they are in the muffin cups.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Desserts|Desserts]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Mexican cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Tex-Mex cuisine|Tex-Mex cuisine]]

This is a very simple recipe for plain '''churros'''. Makes one plateful, suitable for about 4 people. It can easily be doubled or halved, but be warned that attempting to mix more than double this recipe at once is very hard work.

==Ingredients==
* 400 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (~3¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) [[Cookbook:Flour|plain flour]]
* 400 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (~1⅔ cups) boiling water
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|bicarbonate of soda]] (baking soda)

* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)

==Procedure==

#[[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] the flour, baking soda, and salt into a large mixing bowl.
#Add the boiling water gradually to the flour, mixing constantly until you get a very thick, smooth paste.
#Allow to stand for about an hour.
#Heat up a deep [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] of oil until it shimmers.
#Using an [[Cookbook:Pastry Bag|icing bag]], or a freezer bag with the corner cut out to give a hole about the size of your little finger, squeeze the paste into the pan. Use a pair of scissors to cut the sausage-shaped pieces off after about 10 cm.
#Fry the churros until golden brown and crunchy. If the pieces are too thick and are still raw in the middle, cut them in half lengthwise and fry again.
#Remove churros from oil, and drain on a rack or [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]].
#Serve dusted liberally with sugar or hot chocolate sauce (or both).

title: Cookbook:Cinnamon-braised Chicken (Kotopoulo Kapama)
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Chicken recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}

'''''Kotopoulo kapama''''' is a Greek dish of braised chicken flavored with cinnamon. This recipe is the Catsoulis family version, from the Greek island of Kythera.

==Ingredients== 

* [[Cookbook:Chicken|Chicken]] pieces (one per person)
* 2 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 4 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], finely chopped
* 1 tin [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], or 300 g of fresh tomatoes
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] stick
* 3 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]
* ½ tablespoon finely-[[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] fresh [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] red [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]] (shiraz)
* 3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]

* 1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], cut into thick slices
* 1 stick of [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]], cut into thin 3-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] strips
* Finely-chopped celery leaves
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
==Procedure==

# Heat oil in [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] and add onion. Stir gently until onion is well browned.
# Add chicken, bay leaves, and cinnamon, then thoroughly brown chicken on all sides. The objective is to get as much "stock" from the skin as possible as this adds to the flavour later on.
# Add tomatoes, garlic, wine, and water, and cook through. Add parsley, celery leaves, celery, carrot.
# Add enough water to cover the contents of the pot. Allow to cook slowly for at least 2 hours. It is important to cook over a low heat so that sauce does not catch. Stirring or agitation will only cause the vegetables and chicken pieces to break up.
# Serve with thin [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]]. Grate cheese generously over dish.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The fresher the ingredients, the better it will taste.
* It is important to get as much "stock" from the chicken as possible. This is the reason for leaving the skin and bone on, although too much skin will result in a fatty dish.
* The chicken should be browned for at least 10 minutes before the tomatoes are added.
* If wine is added, it should be a good wine. When wine is used in cooking, the alcohol boils off leaving only the taste of the wine, therefore a poor quality wine will do little for the flavour.
* Don't be overgenerous when adding ingredients, as an imbalance will shift the final result. In particular, strong sauces should only be used in small quantities.
* In addition, a small piece of pumpkin may be finely chopped and added to thicken the sauce. It will cook away completely but will enhance the flavour.

'''Chraime''' is a popular Sephardic Jewish fish and vegetable [[cookbook:casserole|casserole]] often eaten as the first course at Rosh Hashanah. It can also be eaten as an entrée, and is normally served with [[cookbook:challah|challah]].

==Ingredients==
*2 large baking [[cookbook:potato|potato]]es
*2 medium red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]]s, cored, seeded, and cut into ½-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick wedges
*5 [[cookbook:garlic|garlic]] cloves, peeled and smashed
*1 small [[Cookbook:Jalapeño|jalapeño]] or other hot [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chili pepper]], quartered and seeded
*[[cookbook:salt|Salt]], to taste
*1¼–1½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] of [[cookbook:Fish|white fish]] fillets (e.g. sole, [[Cookbook:Halibut|halibut]], or [[cookbook:cod|cod]])
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] sweet [[cookbook:paprika|paprika]]
*3 ripe [[cookbook:tomato|tomato]]es, coarsely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] chopped fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]] or [[cookbook:parsley|parsley]]
*1 cup [[cookbook:water|water]]
*⅓ cup [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*Coarse salt, to taste

==Procedure==
# In a large flame-proof casserole or [[Cookbook:Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]], set the potato slices on the bottom. Scatter the bell peppers, garlic, and jalapeño pepper on the potatoes. Sprinkle with salt.  Place the fish on top and sprinkle it with paprika and salt. Add the tomatoes and cilantro or parsley.
# Pour the water in at the edges. Sprinkle the top with oil and sprinkle generously with salt.
# Set the pan over high heat, cover, and bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Reduce the heat slightly and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 25–30 minutes or until the vegetables are tender and the fish is cooked through. Check the pan after 20 minutes; if there seems to be too much liquid, uncover the pan for the remaining cooking time.
# Serve hot or warm with [[Cookbook:Challah|challah]].

title: Cookbook:Christmas Ham
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Pork recipes
| Difficulty = 3
| Servings = 3–4
| Time = 8–11 hours
}}

{{nutritionsummary|1/3 of recipe (1.5 kg)|3|2908|1474|163.8 g|67.2 g|765 mg|3401 mg|53.2 g|2.1 g|12.9 g|305.2 g|47%|21%|14%|123%}}
{{recipe}} 

The ancient Romans, who sacrificed a pig to their god Saturn about the same time Christmas is celebrated nowadays, are probably the starters of a Christmas tradition still alive in some parts of the world. This is a recipe for a boneless, lightly salted Finnish-style ham, popular since about the 1940s, before which Finns used to eat several kinds of meats during Christmas.

This is often eaten with traditional Christmas cuisine, including [[cookbook:Potato|baked potato]]es, [[cookbook:Red Wine|red wine]], and potato, carrot, and rutabaga casseroles, as well as during the night or in the morning and in-between 'proper' meals with bread, mustard and milk. Ham goes well with almost anything. If you have been eating ham for several days with mustard, try chili for a change.
==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (7–10 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) [[cookbook:ham|ham]], lightly salted and boneless
* Prepared [[cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]
* [[cookbook:Breadcrumbs|Breadcrumbs]]

==Procedure==
# If ham is frozen, thaw it in its plastic package, for 3 days in the refrigerator for a 7kg ham, 5 days for a 10kg ham.
# Before putting the ham in the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]], take it out from the refrigerator and let come closer to room temperature. If you intend to put the ham in the oven in the evening, take it out during the early morning. The ham should be about 10 °C (50 °F)  when you put it in the oven.
# Use a wet [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]] to clean the ham a bit; then dry it.
#Place ham on [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking tray]] in oven, with some water on the tray. Or, if you have a large roasting bag, there is no need for water. Do not use only the oven rack, as nothing will catch all the liquid from the ham if the roasting bag fails, messing up your oven. However, you can put the ham on the rack if you put a baking tray beneath that to catch drips.  [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|Aluminum foil]] can be used on the baking tray to protect it. 
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 200 °C (390 °F) and let ham [[Cookbook:Roasting|roast]] in the oven for half an hour. You can skip this if you are not worried about the possible bacteria on the ham. 
# Turn temperature down, and cook at 100–125 °C (210–260 °F), for about 1 hour/kg (a 7 kg ham will take 7 hours or more) until a meat [[Cookbook:Thermometer|thermometer]] in the center of the ham reads 75–80 °C (158–176 °F). Traditional ham is ready at 80 °C but most take the ham out of the oven at 77 °C or so, when the ham has more water left in it and is considered tastier.
# After you take the ham out of the oven, wait a little while before removing the thermometer. It is recommended you do not pour the liquid from the bag or baking tray down the drain.
# Wait until ham is cool enough to handle, then glaze it all over with mustard and breadcrumbs. First remove the rind from the ham, then cover the ham with mustard, then with breadcrumbs. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in a 250 °C (480 °F) oven for 10 minutes.
# The ham is ready to eat when it has cooled down a bit. This makes about enough for 3 or 4 people for a week, but if you think you will not eat it all within a week, freeze the rest.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*A 10 kg ham is considered better-tasting as the pig has gotten bigger.
*The use of a meat thermometer is recommended because the actual temperature of an oven commonly varies from its setting; thus the ham can be severely under- or overcooked if you do not use a thermometer. The thermometer should be placed in the middle of the ham. Be careful that it does not touch the oven walls. You can test if the thermometer works properly before using it by dipping it in boiling water–it should show about 100 °C (212 °F).
*It is possible to salt a ham yourself if you buy ham from a farm or butcher or buy a pig in time to fatten it for Christmas. There are several methods available; here is one that is called ''tönkkösuolaus'': Dissolve 1.8 kg large crystal salt into 10 L water, and cool to 0 °C or slightly lower. Fully submerge a 10 kg ham in the brine, and let it brine at around 0 °C for 2 months, replacing the brine from time to time. During the last week you can keep ham in water only if you want it to be slightly less salty.
*Several people swear by sauna-cooked ham, in which case you will put the ham in a sauna instead of an oven (glazing still done in oven). It will take maybe 12–24 hours for a ham in a 100 °C sauna, and several days in a 80 °C sauna. Use a meat thermometer if you use a sauna to cook a ham and remember to have something beneath the ham collecting all the liquid. Often people also use a wood-burning stove to cook a ham, this method is hardest as you can not use a meat thermometer easily with one, so unless you have good instructions to the very oven you have (or have a spare ham just in case), this would not be recommended for first-time Christmas ham lovers.

text:
__NOTOC__ {{recipesummary | Category = Chickpea recipes | Time = soak: 12 hours
prep: 45 minutes | Rating = 2 | Difficulty = 3 | Image = [[Image:Chana masala.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|India]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Pakistan|Pakistan]] | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan]] '''Cholley''', also '''chole''', '''choley''', '''cholay''', '''white cholay''', '''chana''', '''channa''', or '''chana masala''', is a popular and versatile [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] and [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Pakistan|Pakistani]] chickpea dish. It is commonly cooked in Northern India (especially Punjab) and Pakistan for breakfast, but it is also regularly served at dinner parties, picnics, wedding receptions and other special events. Cholley features chickpeas, onions, tomatoes and spices; variations include additions such as [[Cookbook:Potato|potato]] (alu). This dish pairs well with a range of grain-based accompaniments including, [[Cookbook:Puri|puri]], [[Cookbook:Roti|roti]], [[Cookbook:Naan|naan]], [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] and [[Cookbook:Fried Wheat Bread Balls (Bhatoora)|bhatoora]]. ''See also: [[Cookbook:Chickpea Curry (Masaledaar chole)|Masaledaar chole]] (Chickpea Curry)'' ==Ingredients== * 250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] dried [[cookbook:chickpea|chickpea]]s * 500 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] [[cookbook:water|water]] for cooking * [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] (to taste) * 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[cookbook:oil|oil]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander seeds]] * 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin seeds]] (optional) * 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Nigella|nigella]] seeds (optional) * 1 [[cookbook:onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] * 1 clove [[cookbook:garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] * 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Garam Masala|garam masala]] * 2 medium [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] * 2 tsp [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] * Fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|coriander leaves]] (as a garnish) ==Procedure== #Wash the chickpeas, then [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soak]] overnight in water, allowing them to soften somewhat. Make sure that the chickpeas are well-immersed with at least a few inches of water above them, as they will expand significantly while soaking. #The next day, drain the water and place the chickpeas in a [[Cookbook:Pressure Cooking|pressure cooker]] or large cooking pot. Add the 500 ml fresh water and salt to taste, then cook until the chickpeas are tender (10 minutes at 15 psi in a pressure cooker; if using a regular pot, place the chickpeas in hot water to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], and then reduce to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 60–90 minutes). #Heat the oil in a thick-bottomed pan. Add the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and nigella seeds, cooking them briefly until they crackle. Quickly add the onions and garlic, reduce the heat to medium, and [[cookbook:sautéing|sauté]] until the onions are transparent. #Add garam masala, tomato, turmeric, and salt and cook for 1 minute. #Add the boiled chickpeas, reduce the heat, and allow the cholley to [[cookbook:simmering|simmer]] for around 15 minutes. Check that the gravy has thickened before removing from the heat. #Once done, place the cholley in a serving bowl, add your coriander garnish, and serve with [[cookbook:rice|rice]] or [[cookbook:bread|bread]]. == Notes, tips, and variations == * Try adding [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] flakes and [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]] to taste. == External links == * [http://showmethecurry.com/2007/12/10/chole-a-la-easy-garbanzo-beans-curry-how-to-video/ Chole a la Easy - Garbanzo Beans Curry How-to Video] [[Category:Indian recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Pakistani recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Vegan recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Recipes using chickpea]] [[Category:Boiled recipes]] [[Category:Gluten-free recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Low-GI recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Recipes with metric units]] [[Category:Recipes using coriander]] [[Category:Recipes using garam masala]] [[Category:Recipes using garlic]] [[Category:Recipes using whole cumin]]

'''Chupaquesos''' ("suck cheese") are a cheesy dish invented by Howard Tayler in his webcomic, Schlock Mercenary.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saturday 6 September 2003 |url=https://www.schlockmercenary.com/2003-09-06 |access-date=2023-04-25 |website=www.schlockmercenary.com |language=en}}</ref> The basic idea is to fry cheese until it reaches a rubbery consistency, then cover that rubbery layer with cheese and toppings, then fold it into a tube.  
==Ingredients==
*About 3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (85 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) shredded "shell" cheese (e.g. [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar]])
*About 1 oz (28 g) shredded "filler" cheese (e.g. [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|parmesan]], [[Cookbook:Monterey Jack Cheese|Monterey Jack]])
*Example toppings:
**[[Cookbook:Bacon|Bacon]]
**Chopped cold cuts
**Banana peppers
**[[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|Chili peppers]]
**Marinated [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]]
**Marinara sauce

==Procedure==
#In a medium-large [[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] or cast-iron [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]], sprinkle the "shell" cheese evenly. It will melt and bubble, and eventually form a layer of cheese.  
#Once the underside is orange or brown colored, flip it over.
#Sprinkle the filler cheese down the middle, and put whatever toppings you want down the middle.
#Fold the shell over, and let it cook long enough to melt the filler cheese if desired.
#Serve and eat right away.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* It's advisable to get the toppings ready in advance—it's a time-critical procedure once the cheese is flipped.

title: Cookbook:Christmas Cake
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
| category = Recipes for dessert
| Yield = 10-inch cake
| servings = 10
| time = About 4 days
| difficulty = 3
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

'''Christmas cake''' is a fruitcake traditionally served around Christmas in the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|United Kingdom]], especially after long walks, to be had with tea.

This is a traditional, somewhat extravagant recipe which is quite easy to make, but steeping the fruit should be done over a long time for best results. The resultant cakes should last in very good condition for several months if kept whole in air-tight tins.

Traditionally, the cake is made on the first Sunday of Advent and (once cooled) is 'fed' with alcohol (brandy or rum) every few days until just before Christmas, when it is iced.

==Ingredients==

=== Fruit ===
* 600 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Currant|currants]]
* 400 g [[Cookbook:Sultana|sultanas]]
* 400 g glacé [[Cookbook:Cherry|cherries]], quartered
* 200 g [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]]
* 100 g chopped candied peel
* 200 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]]
* 100 ml [[Cookbook:Brandy|brandy]]
* 50 ml [[Cookbook:Kirsch|kirsch]] (or [[Cookbook:Rum|rum]])

=== Cake ===
* 4 standard (100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 300 g lightly-salted soft [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]] (The "Stork" brand is traditional)
* 300 g dark [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 100 g [[Cookbook:Self-rising Flour|self-raising flour]]
* 200 g plain [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 100 g finely-chopped [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] ground [[Cookbook:Mixed Spice|mixed spice]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] black [[Cookbook:Treacle|treacle]]

==Procedure==

=== Fruit ===
# Place all the fruit in a large bowl and pour the spirits over the mixture.
# Cover the bowl in [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|foil]] and leave in a cool place.
# Mix and stir the fruit every day for at least three days; after a fortnight most of the alcohol will have soaked in and further soaking has no benefit.

=== Cake ===
# [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] together the sugar and margarine with the eggs.
# Add the almonds and black treacle, and mix further.
# [[Cookbook:Sieve|Sieve]] the flours and the mixed spice into the mixture, beating until a smooth mixture results. 
# Combine with the pre-prepared fruit (above) and place in a [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake tin]] lined with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|baking parchment]].
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at a low temperature (140°C / 275°F / Gas mark 1) for at least 4 hours. It may take up to 5 hours, depending on the oven.
# Once a knife comes out clean, remove from the oven and allow to cool fully.

title: Cookbook:Chow Mein
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
| Category = Chinese recipes
| Servings = 4–6
| Time = 1 hour
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[Image:Chow_mein_1_by_yuen.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of China|Chinese Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Noodle|Noodles]]

'''Chow mein''' is a generic Chinese term for a dish of stir-fried [[Cookbook:Noodle|noodles]], of which there are many varieties. Authentic chow mein is generally made of soft noodles, whereas chow mein in Westernized Chinese Cuisine may also be made from thin crispy noodles.

This version of chow mein is made with [[Cookbook:Seitan|seitan]] instead of the more traditional use of chicken, pork or shrimp, making this dish fit for vegans. Also, instead of using oyster sauce in the marinade, shiitake mushrooms are used to achieve a similar depth of flavour.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] mung [[Cookbook:Bean Sprout|bean sprouts]]
* 15 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] [[Cookbook:Seitan|seitan]]
* ½ pound dry wonton [[Cookbook:Noodle|noodles]]
* 2 medium stalks [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]]
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:Bok Choy|bok choy]] or [[Cookbook:Broccoli|broccoli]]
* ½ pound fresh [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]]
* 1 red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Red onion|red onion]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onion]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]] for frying, as needed
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] toasted [[Cookbook:Sesame Seed|sesame seeds]]

=== Marinade ===
* ¼ cup finely-chopped shiitake mushrooms
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame oil]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* Salt to taste
* Pepper, to taste
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]]

=== Sauce ===
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] water or low-sodium vegetable [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* 1 tablespoon soy sauce
* Salt to taste
* Pepper, to taste
* 1 tablespoon cornstarch
* 4 tablespoons water

==Procedure==

# 1–2 hours before cooking, rinse the mung bean sprouts so that they have time to drain thoroughly.
# Cut the seitan into thin strips. Add the marinade ingredients, adding the cornstarch last. [[Cookbook:Marinating|Marinate]] the seitan for 20 to 25 minutes.
# The following 3 steps can be completed while the seitan is marinating:
#* To prepare the sauce, in a small bowl dissolve the 1 tablespoon cornstarch with the 4 tablespoons water. [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] the water or vegetable broth with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, salt, pepper and cornstarch and water mixture and set aside.
#* Soften the noodles by placing them in boiling salted water. Plunge into cold water to stop the cooking process and drain thoroughly.
#* Wash all the vegetables as needed. Cut the celery and the bok choy into ½-inch pieces on the diagonal. If substituting broccoli for bok choy, peel the stalks until no more strings come out, and slice thinly on the diagonal. Wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp cloth and slice. Cut the red bell pepper in half, remove the seeds and cut into chunks. Peel and chop the onion. Dice the green onion.
# Heat a [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] or [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] over medium-high to high heat. Add 2 tablespoons oil. When the oil is hot, add the noodles. Fry in batches until golden. Remove the noodles from the pan.
# Heat 2 tablespoons oil. Add the onion and the seitan, keeping remaining marinade aside for later use. Let the seitan brown briefly, then stir-fry until the redness is gone and the seitan is nearly cooked through. Remove the cooked seitan and onion from the pan.
# Cook the rest of the vegetables separately, except for the green onion, seasoning each with a bit of salt while stir-frying if desired. When cooking the bok choy or broccoli, add ¼ cup of water and cover while cooking. Remove each of the vegetables from the pan when finished stir-frying. Add more oil as needed.
# Give the sauce a quick re-stir. Add all the ingredients back into the wok, making a "well" in the middle of the wok for the sauce. Add the sauce and any remaining marinade, stirring quickly to thicken. Mix everything together. Stir in the green onions. Pour the cooked vegetable and sauce mixture on top of the noodles. Garnish the chow mein with the toasted sesame seeds. Serve hot.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* For crispy chow mein noodles, add more oil than the recipe calls for and cook the noodles longer to dry them out.

text:
__NOTOC__

{{recipe}}

A classic '''apple pie''' is a double-crusted [[Cookbook:Pie|pie]] filled with sweetened and spiced apples. The exact spices vary by recipe, but cinnamon is traditional.

== Ingredients ==

=== '''Dough''' ===
* 12 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 8 ounces cold [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], cut into ½-inch pieces
* 5–7 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] applejack (apple [[Cookbook:Brandy|brandy]]) or hard [[Cookbook:Cider|cider]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] table [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 tbsp sugar

=== '''Filling''' ===
* 6 Honeycrisp [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]], peeled, cored, and cut into 12ths
* ½ cup granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]], divided
* ¼ tsp salt
* ¼ tsp freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Grains of Paradise|grains of paradise]]
* ¾ tsp freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] apple [[Cookbook:Jelly|jelly]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Apple Cider|apple cider]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Tapioca Starch|tapioca starch]] 
* 2 tsp freshly-squeezed [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]

== Procedure ==
#Combine dough ingredients to get a mealy dough. Split in half by weight, shape into 2 disks, and chill for 1 hour.
#[[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|Toss]] apples with ¼ cup sugar and place in a [[Cookbook:Colander|colander]] set over a large bowl. Let drain for 1 ½ hours.
#Transfer liquid from bowl into a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over medium high heat. Cook until reduced to 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]. Set aside.
#Toss apples with remaining filling ingredients. Set aside.
#[[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] both disks of crust into rough circles. Place one inside a 9 ½–10-inch [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|tart pan]] and attach.
#Add apples to the crust in a concentric circle, starting from the outside and working to the inside, making the center slightly taller than the outside. Pour any liquid in the bottom of the bowl over the apples.
#Top with the second sheet of dough, and seal the edges. [[Cookbook:Pie Crust Edges|Crimp the edges]] if desired, then snip 3 incisions in the center. [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] top with reduced apple liquid.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 425°F on the floor of the oven in a half sheet pan lined with parchment for 30 minutes. Transfer to the lower rack, and bake for another 20 minutes.
#Remove and cool for 4 hours. Serve.

title: Cookbook:Ciabatta
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Bread recipes|servings=4|time=18 minutes|difficulty=3|image=[[Image:Ciabatta cut.JPG|300px|A sliced Ciabatta]]}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Ciabatta''' is an Italian white [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] made with wheat flour and yeast. The loaf is somewhat elongated, broad and flattish and, like a slipper, should be and somewhat collapsed in the middle. Since the late 1990s it has been popular across Europe and in the United States, and is widely used as a sandwich bread.

Ciabatta was first produced in Liguria, although at least one type of ciabatta can be found in nearly every region of Italy nowadays. The ciabatta from the area encompassing Lake Como has a crisp crust, a somewhat soft, porous texture, and is light to the touch. The ciabatta found in Tuscany, Umbria, and Marche varies from bread that has a firm crust and dense crumb, to bread that has a crisper crust and more open texture. The more open-crumbed form, which is usual in the United States, is made from a very wet dough, often requiring machine-kneading, and a biga or sourdough starter. 

There are many variations of ciabatta. When made with whole wheat flour, it is known as ''ciabatta integrale''. In Rome, it is often seasoned with olive oil, salt, and marjoram. When milk is added to the dough, it becomes ''ciabatta al latte''.

A toasted sandwich made from small loaves of ciabatta is known as a panino (plural ''panini'').

== Ingredients ==
* 350 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Sifting|sifted]] wheat [[cookbook:flour|flour]]
* 280 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] lukewarm [[cookbook:water|water]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 38 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[cookbook:olive oil|olive oil]] (optional)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] active dry [[cookbook:yeast|yeast]]

== Procedure ==
# Dissolve salt and yeast in lukewarm water
# Add sifted wheat flour and olive oil into lukewarm water. Mix.
# After thoroughly being mixed and one is left with a dough that is of a uniform texture and consistency, cover and leave to rest in warm place for 45 minutes.
# Take out and begin to work the dough once more, stretching it and folding it over itself on all four corners; adding flour to surface to prevent its sticking. Cover and leave it to rest for about 30 minutes, during which time the dough will rise.
# Repeat this process, by stretching the dough and folding it over itself on all sides, allowing for air pockets to be formed (which will make the bread airy when it is baked). Cover and allow to rest for 30 minutes.
# Repeat the above process once more and leave the dough to settle for 30 minutes while covered.
# Take up dough and place on [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]], and cut the dough into equal parts to form into smaller, separate loaves (elongated).
# Place dough in pre-heated [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] at {{convert|430|F}} for 18 minutes.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Before closing oven, mist the bread dough with a spray bottle to ensure a crusty top.
* Some doughs used for making Ciabatta bread were left to ferment 18–24 hours before being worked; the batch of dough then being refreshed with the addition of water, [[cookbook:malt|malt]], and salt, after which it was again allowed to sit without agitation so that it could rise.

title: Cookbook:Cinnamon Rolls
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Recipes for pastries
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

Cinnamon buns are another name for cinnamon rolls. These sweet rolls are created with flour and sugar.

== Ingredients ==

=== Dough ===
* [[Cookbook:Milk|Milk]], warm
* Active dry [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]], room temperature
* 2½ [[Cookbook:Tbsp|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* [[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]], softened
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1 pinch [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

=== Assembly ===
* 16 tbsp (8 [[Cookbook:Oz|oz]]) butter, softened
* 1 cup sugar
* 2 tbsp ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]

== Procedure ==

==== Dough ====
# Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk. Stir in the sugar, and let it sit for 5 minutes to activate the yeast.
# Combine the egg, 2½ tbsp sugar, and softened butter until smooth. Mix in the milk mixture.
# Combine the flour and salt. Gradually stir this dry mixture into the wet mixture until it forms a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] the dough for at least 5 minutes until it is smooth, stretchy, and no longer sticky. If it is still sticky, add a little more flour. If it is too dry, add a little bit of warm water.
# Cover the dough in the bowl, and let rest for 5 minutes to make it more controllable because it becomes too soft and flexible to roll into the proper cylindrical shape.

==== Assembly ====
# Place the dough on a lightly floured surface, and roll it out into a flat rectangle. Lightly dust the dough if needed to prevent sticking.
# Spread the softened butter in a thin layer over the dough. Combine the sugar and cinnamon, and sprinkle it evenly over the butter.
# Roll up the dough rectangle like a mat so you get a cylindrical log.
# Cut the log into [[Cookbook:Slicing|slices]] a few inches thick. Arrange the slices cut-side up in a [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]].
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] at 350°F until it turns golden brown.
# Cool slightly and serve warm.
