title: Cookbook:Lemon Pickle I
text:
__NOTOC__ {{recipesummary | Category = Indian recipes | Time = Preparation: 20 minutes
Fermentation: 1 to 2 months | Yield = about 1 litre of pickle | Servings = | Rating = 3 | Image = [[Image:Lemon Pickle.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]] '''Lemon pickle''' is a traditional condiment used with [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] food. Many pickle recipes from India have oil to help preserve the pickle, but this recipe uses no oil. {{see also|Cookbook:Lemon Pickle II}} ==Ingredients== * 12 small or 6 large [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]] (thin skins preferred) * 1 large or 2 small lemons, [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|juiced]] * ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * ¼ cup red [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile]] powder * ½ cup [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] * 3 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] powder * 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Fenugreek|fenugreek]] seed * 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Mustard|black mustard]] seed * ¼ tsp [[Cookbook:Asafoetida|asafoetida]] powder (omit for [[Cookbook:Gluten-Free|gluten-free]] version) ==Procedure== === Preparation === # Wash the lemons and dry them well, leaving no water on the lemons. Trim off the stalk and any odd bits. # Cut the lemons in to small pieces about 2 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] (¾ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]) on each side, and place in a bowl. # Dry-roast the fenugreek, black mustard, and asafoetida together in a pan on a medium heat for about 5 minutes. Don't burn them! # Grind the roasted spices in a grinder or a [[Cookbook:Mortar and Pestle|mortar and pestle]]. # Add the ground spices, turmeric powder, salt, sugar and chili powder to the bowl and mix together well. # Pack the mixture into a 2 [[Cookbook:Liter|litre]] (2 [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]]) jar, or use a couple of smaller jars. Don't fill quite to the top—allow at least 1 cm space. === Fermentation === # Sit the jar where it will get the heat of the sun. Bring the jar inside in the evening, and put it back out in the morning. Do this for at least a month in summer, two months in winter. The warmth of the sun will help the pickle to ferment. ==Notes, tips and variations== * Don't worry about the amount of sugar in the recipe, because it will be fermented away over time. * Asafoetida powder generally has wheat flour added to it to help it flow well. You can omit this ingredient if you want to make it gluten-free. ==External links== * [http://indianfoodrocks.blogspot.com/2006/05/lemon-pickle-without-oil-picture.html Lemon Pickle without cooking], the inspiration for this recipe * [http://www.bharatviews.in/lemon-pickle-recipe/ Making Lemon Pickle Recipes] [[Category:Indian recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using lemon]] [[Category:Fermented recipes]] [[Category:Gluten-free recipes]] [[Category:Vegan recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using asafoetida]] [[Category:Recipes using sugar]] [[Category:Recipes using chile]] [[Category:Recipes using fenugreek seed]] [[Category:Recipes using mustard seed]]

title: Cookbook:Lemon Pickle II
text:
{{recipesummary | Category = Indian recipes | Time = Preparation: 20 minutes
Maturation: 1 month | Yield = about 1 pint of pickle | Image = [[Image:Lemon pickle star anise.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]] '''Lemon pickle''' is a traditional condiment used with [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] food. Many pickle recipes from India have oil to help preserve the pickle, but this recipe uses no oil. {{see also|Cookbook:Lemon Pickle I}} ==Ingredients== * 8 small or 4 large [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]] * ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * ¼–½ cup [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] * 4 small green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|yellow mustard]] seed * 1 tablespoon ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Fenugreek|fenugreek]] seed * ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] powder * 1–2 [[Cookbook:Star Anise|star anise]] pods ==Procedure== # Cut lemons into small pieces, and place in a bowl. # Cover with salt and set aside for at least 4 hours (24 is better). # Dry-roast the yellow mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, star anise, and chopped chilis in a pan over high heat, shaking constantly—don't burn them! # Strain the juice from the lemons into a small [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], add the turmeric, ginger and sugar, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 2–3 minutes until the sugar has dissolved. If there isn't enough juice, add 1–2 tablespoons water. # Add the spices and sugar mixture to the bowl of lemons, and mix together well. # Pack into a pint jar, pressing the pieces in if needed, to ensure that the liquid covers all the lemon pieces. # Set aside to mature for 1 month. ==Notes, tips and variations== * If you don't have fresh chilis, add some dried chilis or chili powder. The pickle in the photo has three whole dried chilis in it. title: Cookbook:Lemon Mille-feuille
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
| category = Recipes for pastries
| servings = 10
| time = 10–20 minutes
| difficulty = 3
| image = [[Image:Mille-feuille 01.jpg|300px|''Mikke feuille'']]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

'''Mille-feuille''' (literally "a thousand leaves/sheets") is a [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|French]] [[Cookbook:Pastry|pastry]] made of many [[Cookbook:Puff pastry|puff pastry]] layers. 

==Ingredients==
=== Pastry ===
*375 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (12 [[Cookbook:Oz|oz]]) ready-made [[Cookbook:Puff pastry|puff pastry]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]] , beaten
*2 level [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Icing sugar|icing sugar]] 

=== Lemon filling ===
*3 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]] yolks 
*1 whole egg
*75 g (4 Tbsp) [[Cookbook:Castor sugar|castor sugar]]
*275 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
*40 g (4 Tbsp) plain (all-purpose) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*3 large [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]s, zested and juiced

==Procedure==
===Pastry===
#Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C).
#Unroll the pastry on a lightly floured surface.
#Trim the pastry so that you are left with a rectangle approximately 23 x 25.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]].
#[[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] the larger piece of pastry to a 30 cm square, making sure you use a very even, gentle pressure on the [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]] so that you end up with nice even edges.
#Grease a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] and use the rolling pin to transfer the pastry to the baking sheet.
#Prick the surface of the pastry with a fork. [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] the pastry all over with the beaten egg.
#Place the baking sheet on a high shelf in the oven and bake for 12–15 minutes until crisp and golden.
#To get it extra crisp, heat the oven to its highest setting, sift 1 teaspoon of the icing sugar all over the pastry, and flash it under the grill.
#Remove from the grill and, using a sharp knife, cut the square into three equal strips.
#Turn the strips over, sift the rest of the icing sugar over them, and then flash them under the grill again.
#Cool on a wire rack, then store in a polythene box, each layer separated with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|greaseproof paper]].

===Lemon filling===
#Place the egg yolks and whole egg into a roomy bowl.
#Use an electric [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]] to [[Cookbook:Whipping|whip]] the eggs together with the castor sugar until the mixture is pale, thick and creamy (4–5 minutes). Add the milk as you mix.
#Sift the flour onto the mixture and whisk again until smooth.
#Add the lemon zest and juice.

===Assembly===

{{Recipe}}

==Ingredients==

==Procedure==
===Filling===
#Add all the filling ingredients to a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], bring to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], and whisk for a few minutes. When you can’t stir anymore it’s ready. 
#Keep the filling warm and covered while preparing the meringue.

#Combine the starches, baking powder, guar gum, lemon juice, and about half the water. [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] by hand until stiff peaks start to form.

Using a rubber [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]], touch flat side of spatula on meringue and pull away. Repeat over entire surface of meringue.

title: Cookbook:Lentil Burgers
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Yield = 4–8 burgers, depending on size
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[File:Lentil burger.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}

[http://www.foodista.com/recipe/KCHZXPP2/easy-lentil-burgers Originally posted to Foodista] by user dad1337. Foodista recipes are released under a [http://www.foodista.com/static/legal CC-BY license].

==Ingredients==
*1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] dried [[Cookbook:Lentil|lentils]], picked through
*3–4 cups water or [[Cookbook:Stock|vegetable stock]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Garlic Salt|garlic salt]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*1 medium to large [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*1 stalk [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]], finely diced
*2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
*4 tbsp dried [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
*1–2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
*2 whole [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*¼–1 cup plain or Italian [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|bread crumbs]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste

==Preparation==
#Place the lentils in a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and add water or stock so that it covers the lentils by at least 2 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] (check the cooking instructions for the type of lentil you are using, as some may require soaking before cooking).
#Cook for the approximate time as suggested by the lentil package (usually 30–45 minutes at a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]).
#Place the cooked lentils into a fine [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]] and allow to drain and cool.
#Sauté the carrot and celery in the butter and oil over medium heat until softened (about 10 minutes).
#Just before the carrot and celery are done, add the dried onion and parsley.
#Place the drained and cooled lentils in a large bowl, add the carrot mixture, and mash everything with a potato masher. Don't over-mash; it is fine to leave some of the lentils whole.
#Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
#Add the eggs and about ¼ cup bread crumbs, and stir to combine all the ingredients. Continue to add bread crumbs until you have a slightly moist but not wet mixture.
#Form mixture into patties. Place the formed patties onto a plate and layer with waxed paper in between. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
#To cook, it is best to use either a large [[Cookbook:Sauté Pan|sauté pan]] or a griddle on the [[Cookbook:Grilling|grill]]—these burgers don't do well on grill grates. Cook over medium to medium-high heat until warmed through and a nice crust has formed on the outside. Depending on the thickness of the burgers, this will take anywhere from 3–7 minutes per side.
#To serve, you can place on a bun with the usual accoutrements or go crazy with whatever you think will go (garlic aioli, roasted peppers, etc). You could also serve without the bun with grilled [[Cookbook:Pineapple|pineapple]], barbecue sauce, etc—the choices are endless.

'''Lemon drizzle cake''' is a simple butter [[Cookbook:Cake|cake]] flavored with lemon zest and juice, and topped with a lemony [[Cookbook:Frosting and Icing|icing]].
==Ingredients==

=== Cake ===
*280 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (9.9 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]/2¼ sticks) unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], plus extra for greasing

title: Cookbook:Liberian Chicken Gravy
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Chicken recipes
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[File:Chicken Gravy 02.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian chicken gravy''' is a delicious African [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]]. A lot of oil is required to cook most African stews, but when it comes to this dish, you don't need so much.

== Ingredients ==

* 3 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut into medium pieces
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* Ground red or black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] to taste
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] chicken [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|bouillon cube]]
* 2 medium-size [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], neatly [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 4 fresh [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 4 medium-size red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]]
* 5 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]] and [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 2 lb any type of dried [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] steak of your choice, cleaned
* Smoked [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]] (optional)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] powder
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]]
* 2 medium-size habanero [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]], neatly chopped
*1 pound large [[Cookbook:Shrimp|shrimp]], cleaned 

== Procedure ==

# In a medium-size [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] the chicken with salt, pepper, some chopped onions, and 1 tablespoon of the chicken bouillon. Let them cook until tender—the cooking time varies according to the chicken.
# Remove the chicken to a bowl, reserving the stock.
# In a blender, purée the tomatoes, red bell pepper, onions, garlic, basil, and parsley.
# Add ½ cup oil to a pot, then add the blended mixture followed by the tomato paste. Allow it to cook for about 15 minutes, stirring the pot frequently as the sauce simmers.f
# Add the reserved chicken broth, then the chicken, dried fish, smoked paprika, ginger powder, cayenne pepper, and habanero pepper. Let simmer for about 10 minutes.
# Add the shrimp and cook for about 5 minutes.
# Adjust the stew with water, broth, and/or bouillon cubes if needed.
# Enjoy with any complimentary dish of your choice.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* It is not compulsory to use fish when preparing this stew.
* You can use any variety of tomatoes such as canned tomatoes, fresh tomatoes, or Roma tomatoes.
* Use any range of vegetables such as [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], green [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]].
* You can also make use of extra spices such as [[Cookbook:Curry Powder|curry powder]], [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], and [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]] as desired.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Cassava Leaf Soup
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = African recipes
| difficulty = 3
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian cassava leaf soup''' is a delicious and hearty dish that is widely enjoyed in Liberia. Made with cassava leaves, meat, and an assortment of vegetables, this soup is a flavorful and nutritious meal that is perfect for gatherings and special occasions.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] [[Cookbook:Cassava|cassava leaves]], fresh or frozen
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:Meat|meat]] ([[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], or [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]]), cut into bite-sized pieces
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2–3 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 piece of [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]]
* 2–3 Scotch bonnet [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]], finely chopped
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* 4–5 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Chicken Broth|chicken broth]] or water
* 1 [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potato]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Plantain|plantain]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* [[Cookbook:Black pepper|Ground black pepper]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* Large pot
* Wooden spoon

== Procedure ==
# If using fresh cassava leaves, wash them thoroughly and remove any tough stems. If using frozen cassava leaves, thaw them according to the package instructions.
# In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and fragrant.
# Stir in the chopped Scotch bonnet peppers and cook for a few minutes to release the flavors.
# Add the meat to the pot and cook until it is browned on all sides.
# Pour in the chicken broth or water and bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Cover the pot and let the meat cook for about 20–25 minutes, or until it is tender.
# Add the diced sweet potato and sliced plantain to the pot. Let the soup simmer for another 10–15 minutes, or until the vegetables are cooked through.
# Stir in the cassava leaves and let the soup simmer for an additional 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
# Season the soup with salt and ground black pepper to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let the soup rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Cassava leaves can be found in African or international grocery stores. If unavailable, you can substitute with spinach or other leafy greens, but the taste will be different.
* The longer the cassava leaf soup cooks, the more flavorful it becomes. It is traditionally simmered for several hours to develop its rich taste.
* This soup is often served with rice or [[Cookbook:Fufu|fufu]], a starchy side dish made from cassava, plantains, or other ingredients.
* Cassava leaves are a good source of vitamins A and C, as well as calcium and iron.
* The meat and vegetables in the soup provide protein, vitamins, and minerals.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Fried Fish
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = African recipes
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian fried fish''' is a popular and delicious dish in Liberia. Made with fresh fish and a flavorful spice blend, this dish is crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, making it a delightful meal for seafood lovers.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] fresh [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] ([[Cookbook:Tilapia|tilapia]], snapper, or any firm white fish)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|ground black pepper]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Garlic powder|garlic powder]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Onion powder|onion powder]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|cayenne pepper]] (optional)
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]], for frying

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* Large bowl
* Deep [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] or pot
* [[Cookbook:Tongs|Tongs]] or slotted spoon
* [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|Paper towels]]

== Procedure ==
# Clean and gut the fish, removing any scales and innards. Rinse the fish thoroughly under cold running water and pat them dry with paper towels.
# In a large bowl, mix the all-purpose flour, salt, ground black pepper, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne pepper (if using).
# Pour the buttermilk into another bowl.
# Dip each fish into the buttermilk, allowing any excess to drip off, and then coat the fish with the seasoned flour mixture, pressing the flour onto the fish to adhere.
# Heat about 1 inch of vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or pot over medium-high heat. To test if the oil is hot enough, drop a small piece of bread into the oil; it should sizzle and turn golden brown.
# Carefully place the coated fish in the hot oil, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pan.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the fish for about 3–4 minutes per side, or until they are golden brown and cooked through. Use tongs or a slotted spoon to flip the fish during frying.
# Remove the fried fish from the oil and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil.
# Serve the fish hot, with your favorite side dishes like plantains, rice, or salad.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* You can adjust the level of spiciness by increasing or decreasing the amount of cayenne pepper in the seasoning mixture.
* For a gluten-free version, you can use [[Cookbook:Cornmeal|cornmeal]] or [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|rice flour]] instead of all-purpose flour.
* Make sure the oil is hot enough before frying to ensure that the fish comes out crispy and not greasy.
* Leftover fried fish can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. To reheat, place the fish in the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] at 350°F (175°C) for a few minutes until warmed through.
* Fish is a rich source of protein and essential omega-3 fatty acids.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Collard Greens Stew
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = African recipes
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian collard green stew''' is a hearty and flavorful dish that is a staple in Liberian cuisine. Made with tender collard greens and a rich tomato-based sauce, this stew is both nutritious and delicious. It can be served as a main course with rice or bread, and it's perfect for sharing with family and friends.

== Ingredients ==
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]], diced
* 1 green bell pepper, diced
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Paprika|ground paprika]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|ground cayenne pepper]] (optional, for heat)
* 1 bunch of fresh [[Cookbook:Collard Greens|collard greens]], washed and chopped
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Broth|vegetable broth]] (or water)

== Equipment ==
* Large pot
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and the garlic becomes fragrant.
# Stir in the diced tomato, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper. Cook for a few minutes until the vegetables are softened.
# Add the chopped collard greens to the pot and mix well with the sautéed vegetables.
# Season the stew with ground paprika, ground cayenne pepper (if using), and salt to taste. Stir to coat the collard greens and vegetables with the spices.
# Pour in the vegetable broth (or water) to the pot, ensuring that the collard greens are well covered.
# Cover the pot and let the [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]] simmer on low heat for about 30–40 minutes, or until the collard greens are tender and flavorful.
# Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed, adding more salt or spices according to your preference.
# Serve as a main dish with rice or bread, and enjoy.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* You can add other vegetables like [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]] or [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]] to the stew for extra flavor and nutrition.
* For a richer taste, you can add some [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]] to the stew during cooking.
* Leftover stew can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat before serving.

== Nutrition ==
* Collard greens are a good source of vitamins A, C, and K, as well as calcium and iron.
* The variety of vegetables in this stew provides a range of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Butter Rice
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = African recipes
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian butter rice''' is a flavorful and comforting dish that is a popular staple in Liberian cuisine. Made with aromatic ingredients and cooked in butter, this rice dish has a rich and delicious taste that pairs well with a variety of proteins and vegetables. It's a versatile side dish that can be served on its own or as an accompaniment to other Liberian dishes.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] long-grain [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 4 cups [[Cookbook:Broth|chicken broth]] (or vegetable broth)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay leaf|bay leaf]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* [[Cookbook:Black pepper|Black pepper]], to taste
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] or [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]], chopped (for garnish)

== Equipment ==
* Large pot with a lid
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]

== Procedure ==
# Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain the rice and set it aside.
# In a large pot, melt the butter over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and the garlic becomes fragrant.
# Stir in the drained rice and coat it well with the buttery mixture.
# Pour in the broth and add the bay leaf to the pot. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir well.
# Bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot with the lid and let the rice [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 15–20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is cooked and fluffy.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let the rice rest for a few minutes before fluffing it with a fork.
# [[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* For a richer taste, you can use chicken broth instead of vegetable broth.
* You can add some diced vegetables like [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]] or [[Cookbook:Pea|peas]] to the rice for extra flavor and color.
* Leftover rice can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat before serving.
* Liberian butter rice complements various proteins and vegetables, making it a versatile and tasty addition to your meals.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Eggplant Stew
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = Eggplant recipes
| cuisine = Liberian
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian eggplant stew''' is a delectable dish that highlights the unique flavors of eggplant in Liberian cuisine. This hearty stew is made with tender eggplant, savory [[Cookbook:meat|meat]] or [[Cookbook:fish|fish]], and a medley of aromatic spices. It is a popular and comforting meal in Liberia, often served with [[Cookbook:rice|rice]] or [[Cookbook:fufu|fufu]].

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:meat|meat]] ([[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], or [[Cookbook:Goat|goat]]), cut into pieces, or [[Cookbook:fish|fish]] ([[Cookbook:Tilapia|tilapia]] or [[Cookbook:Catfish|catfish]]), cleaned and gutted
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Chicken Broth|chicken broth]] or water
* 1 [[Cookbook:tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:bell pepper|bell pepper]], diced
* 1 [[Cookbook:Hot Pepper Sauce|hot pepper]], chopped (optional, for heat)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:pepper|pepper]]
* 2 large [[Cookbook:eggplant|eggplants]], peeled and diced
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* Large [[Cookbook: Stock Pot|pot]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onions and minced garlic to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onions are soft and translucent.
# If using meat, add the meat pieces to the pot and cook until they are browned on all sides.
# Pour in the chicken broth or water and bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]].
# Add the diced tomato, bell pepper, and chopped hot pepper (if using) to the pot. Stir well to combine with the other ingredients.
# Gently add the diced eggplant to the pot and stir to incorporate with the other ingredients.
# Season the stew with ground pepper and salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
# Let the stew simmer for about 20–25 minutes or until the eggplant is tender and cooked through.
# Stir occasionally during cooking to prevent sticking and to ensure even cooking.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let the stew rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* You can add other vegetables like [[Cookbook:carrot|carrots]], [[Cookbook:okra|okra]], or [[Cookbook:spinach|spinach]] to the stew for added nutrition and flavor.
* If using fish, be sure to remove any bones before adding it to the stew.
* This stew can be made with any type of meat or fish according to your preference.
* Liberian eggplant stew can be enjoyed as a standalone dish or served with [[Cookbook:rice|rice]], [[Cookbook:fufu|fufu]], or [[Cookbook:bread|bread]].
* Eggplant is a low-calorie vegetable and is a good source of fiber, vitamins, and minerals.

title: Cookbook:Lemon Pound Cake
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Cake recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==

=== Cake ===
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], softened, for greasing pan
* 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] for dusting pan
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Cake Flour|cake flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 16 tablespoons unsalted butter, softened
* 1¼ cups white [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] [[Cookbook:Zest|zest]] from 2 medium [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]]
* 2 teaspoons juice from same 2 lemons
* 4 large [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1½ teaspoons [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract

=== Lemon glaze (optional) ===
* ½ cup sugar
* ¼ cup juice from 1–2 medium lemons

== Procedure ==

=== Cake ===
# Adjust [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] rack to middle position and heat oven to 350 °F. 
# Grease a 9x5-inch Pyrex [[Cookbook:Loaf Pan|loaf pan]] with 1 tablespoon softened butter; dust with 1 tablespoon cake flour, tapping out excess. 
# In a medium bowl, [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] together flour, baking powder, and salt; set aside.
# In glass measuring cup or microwave-safe bowl, microwave butter, covered with [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]], in 30-second bursts until melted. Whisk melted butter thoroughly.
# In [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]], pulse sugar and lemon zest until combined. Add lemon juice, eggs, and vanilla; process until combined. With processor running, drizzle melted butter through feed tube. Transfer mixture to large bowl. 
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] flour mixture over batter in three steps, gently whisking after each addition.
# Pour batter into prepared pan and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] 15 minutes. 
# Reduce oven temperature to 325 °F and continue to bake until deep golden brown and a [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] inserted in center comes out clean (about 35 minutes), rotating pan halfway through baking time. 
# Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then turn cake onto [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|wire rack]], poke on top and sides with a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick or skewer]], and brush on lemon glaze (see below). Cool to room temperature (at least 1 hour).

=== Lemon glaze ===
# While cake is cooling, bring sugar and lemon juice to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] in small nonreactive [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], stirring occasionally to dissolve sugar.
# Reduce heat to low and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until thickened slightly, about 2 minutes.
# [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] glaze onto cake.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Once cooled, cake can be wrapped tightly in plastic wrap and stored at room temperature for up to 5 days.
* '''Lemon-Poppy seed Pound Cake:''' Follow the above recipe through step 2. Toss 1 tablespoon flour mixture with ⅔ cup poppy seeds in small bowl; set aside. Continue with recipe from step 3, folding poppy seed mixture into batter after flour is incorporated.

== References ==
{{refbegin}}
*Pelzel, Raquel.  January-February 2004.  "Simplifying Lemon Pound Cake."  ''Cook's Illustrated'', p. 24-25.
{{refend2}}

}}'''Lemon-lime soda''' is a carbonated beverage flavored similarly to lemon- and limeade. This recipe originates from Flavorlab.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-10-09 |title=Sprite |url=https://www.flavorlab.xyz/recipes/sprite |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=Flavor Lab |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Ingredients==
* 2 whole [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]], washed
* 4 whole [[Cookbook:Lime|limes]], washed
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 [[Cookbook:Liter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Sugar|white sugar]]
* 4 tsp (20 ml) lime [[Cookbook:Juice|juice]]
* [[Cookbook:Carbonated Water|Carbonated water]], as needed

==Procedure==
# Remove the zest from the lemons and limes in strips, leaving behind the bitter white pith.
# Combine the sugar and zest in a container, and let this sit in the fridge for 24 hours. The sugar will extract the liquid from the citrus peels and produce a syrupy liquid.
# [[Cookbook:Sieve|Strain]] the solids out of the peel and sugar mixture.
# Mix the peel and sugar mixture with lime juice. This should produce slightly under ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 ml) of [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]]. 
# To make the finished soda, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.
* You can make a Shirley Temple by mixing five crushed frozen cherries with the zest and sugar or by adding a volume of [[Cookbook:Grenadine|grenadine]] syrup for every volume of lemon-lime syrup when making the finished soda.

text:

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Peru|Cuisine of Peru]]

'''Lomo saltado''' is a dish of marinated steak, vegetables and fried potatoes, usually served over white [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]. It is one of the most popular recipes in Peru and is often found on the menu at many smaller restaurants at a very reasonable price.

==Ingredients==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] (900 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] tenderloin or other tender steak
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] red [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]] (e.g. Burgundy)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] crushed [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 2 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], cut in strips
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], seeds removed, [[Cookbook:Purée|puréed]] in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]]
* 5 [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]] peeled and cut into strips for [[Cookbook:Frying|frying]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Aji amarillo|yellow Peruvian Chili Pepper]] (aji), cut into thin strips
* 1 tablespoon of [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 2 tablespoons of [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]] for frying
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] 
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Culantro|Culantro]] or [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]]

==Procedure==
# Cut the meat into thin strips and [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] them in the wine for 1 hour.
# Use a [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] to cook garlic in oil over medium heat and add the meat. Reserve the juice.
# Add the tomato purée, salt and pepper. Cook for a few minutes.
# Add the soy sauce while stirring the meat in the wok.
# Add the onions, aji strips, cilantro and vinegar. Combine the juice from the meat.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the potatoes in a separate pan and add to the other ingredients.
# Serve the dish with white rice.
==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Instead of puréeing the tomatoes, you can cut them into [[Cookbook:Slicing|slices]].
* You may omit the wine and use a greater quantity of vinegar.
* Using a different kind of hot pepper changes the flavor of this dish completely.
* You may choose not to marinate the beef.

title: Cookbook:Limoncello
text:
{{recipesummary
| Category = Beverage recipes
| Servings = 45
| Time = 20–80 days
| Difficulty = 2
| Rating = 2
}}{{Recipe}}

[[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]] '''limoncello''' recipe.

==Ingredients==
*15 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] superfine [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Fifth|fifths]] (1.5 [[Cookbook:Liter|litres]] total) 100 proof [[Cookbook:Vodka|vodka]]
*5 cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]

==Procedure==
# Wash the lemons with a vegetable brush and hot water to remove any residue of pesticides or wax. Carefully [[Cookbook:Zest|zest]] the lemons with a [[Cookbook:Zester|zester]] or vegetable [[Cookbook:Peeler|peeler]] so there is no white pith on the peel.
# In a 1-gallon glass jar, combine half the vodka and the lemon zest. Cover the jar and let sit at room temperature for at least 10 days, and up to 40 days in a cool dark place.
# In a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], combine the sugar and water and cook until thickened (about 5–7 minutes). Let the [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]] cool before adding it to the limoncello mixture. Add the additional fifth of vodka. Allow to rest for another 10–40 days.
# After the rest period, strain and bottle, discarding the lemon zest. Keep in the freezer until ready to serve.

==Notes, tips and variations==
* Wondering what to do with the lemons after you've zested them? Try making [[Cookbook:Lemonade|lemonade]], [[Cookbook:Ginger beer|ginger beer]], or [[Cookbook:Sima|sima]].

title: Cookbook:Luciabullar (Scandinavian Saffron Buns)
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Bread recipes
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[File:2005 baking of saffron buns 04.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Holiday Recipes|Holiday recipes]]

'''Lussekatter''' or '''luciabullar''' are Scandinavian saffron buns served on [[w:St. Lucia Day|St. Lucia Day]] (13 December).

==Ingredients==

*2 packages (4½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]]) active dry [[Cookbook:yeast|yeast]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] lukewarm water
*½ tsp crushed (¼ tsp powdered) [[Cookbook:saffron|saffron]] threads
*¾ cup (180 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Half and Half|half and half]], lukewarm
*½ cup (120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], beaten
*¾ cup (180 g) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*4–5 cups sifted [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*[[Cookbook:Raisin|Raisins]] to decorate

==Procedure==
#Combine the yeast and warm water.
#Mix saffron into the warm half and half and let stand.
#Combine the yeast and saffron mixtures. Mix in the melted butter, eggs, sugar, and salt.
#Mix half of flour into the wet mixture and beat until well-blended.
#Mix in additional flour until [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] is smooth but not too firm. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] on floured surface for ten minutes.
#Place dough in buttered bowl and let rise about 1½ hours or until doubled in volume.
#Divide the dough into multiple pieces. Roll each piece into a 7 inch-long snake, and form into an 'S' shape with the ends curled in. Place a raisin in each curl.
#Place buns on buttered [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|sheet pan]], cover, and let rise 45 minutes. 
#[[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] with beaten egg and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] at 375–400°F (190–200°C) for 10–15 minutes until golden and cooked through.

title: Cookbook:Loukoumas (Greek Donuts with Honey) II
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Servings = 8
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[File:Loukoumades.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}

Callimachus called these "honey tokens" some time during the 3rd century B.C. Loukoumades were the 1st prizes awarded to winners of the ancient Olympics. Now they are the perfect Greek cafe dessert celebratory piece of decadent, or mid-morning snack. They’re especially good on cold wintry afternoons with a nice cup of coffee. Bon appetit!
==Ingredients==

=== Fritters ===
* 4 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] active dry [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] warm [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 scant teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|Vegetable oil]] for frying

=== Topping ===
* [[Cookbook:Honey|Honey]] (preferably thyme honey)
* [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|Cinnamon]]
* [[Cookbook:Walnut|Walnuts]], crushed
* [[Cookbook:Sesame Seed|Sesame seeds]]

==Procedure==

=== Fritters ===
# Combine the yeast and ½ cup warm water.
# Mix the flour with the salt and put it in a deep bowl.
# Add the yeast and and 1 cup warm water, and mix well until you make a uniform thin paste.
# Cover and leave in the shade for 1½–2 hours until it rises and forms bubbles under the surface.
# Heat several inches of oil in a deep [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]]. Add the batter by large spoonfuls to make fritters. Turn the balls as they puff-up, [[Cookbook:Frying|frying]] 3–5 minutes until golden brown all over. Do not crowd the pan.
# Remove with a strainer or ladle, and place on paper towels; keep warm.

=== Topping ===
#Drizzle loukoumas with honey.
#Sprinkle with cinnamon, walnuts, and/or sesame seeds to taste.

title: Cookbook:Long Island Roast Duckling
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Duck recipes|servings=3–4|time=1 hour to 90 minutes|difficulty=2
}}{{recipe}}| [[cookbook:Duck|Duck]] | [[cookbook:Poultry|Poultry]]
__NOTOC__
Long Island roast [[Cookbook:Duck|duckling]] is part of the regional cuisine of eastern Long Island, New York stemming from Long Island's thriving duck-farming industry which began in the late 19th century.<ref name="American duck farming">[http://www.foodreference.com/html/fducks.html Info on American duck farming on the Food Reference website]</ref> 

According to Alton Brown, host of the Food Network's ''Good Eats'', duck farming got its start on Long Island after an American businessman touring China in 1873 bought 25 white pekin ducks and shipped them to Long Island. Only nine survived the trip but those nine reproduced quickly and their descendants eventually found themselves on Long Island's numerous duck farms.<ref name= "What's Up, Duck (part one)">[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QSO_Ej2WwZU Part one of the ''Good Eats'' episode titled ''What's Up, Duck?'']</ref><ref>[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Frn-M8HnlP0 Part two of the ''Good Eats'' episode titled ''What's Up, Duck?'']</ref>

White pekins (also called Long Island pekins) now represent 95% of the ducks sold and consumed in the US<ref>[http://www.mapleleaffarms.com/46#q13 Info on white pekin ducks on the Maple Farms website]</ref> and are raised on farms in many parts of that country.<ref>[http://metzerfarms.com The Mertzer Farms home page]</ref><ref>[http://duckhavenfarm.com The Duck Haven Farm home page]</ref><ref>[http://www.roastgoose.com The Schlitz Foods home page]</ref>

According to Brown, many people shy away from cooking whole ducks because of their high fat content.<ref name="What's Up, Duck (part one)"/> Fortunately, there are cooking methods for removing the excess fat.<ref>[http://www.thecitycook.com/cooking/recipes/data/000103 Info on roasting duck on The City Cook website]</ref>

White pekin meat has a mild flavor and, if served skinless, is lower in fat and calories than skinless chicken breast.<ref>[http://www.foodreference.com/html/fducks.html Info on white pekins on the Food Reference website]</ref> Farmers slaughter these birds after six to eight weeks of growth when the meat is at its most tender.<ref name="American duck farming"/>

This recipe utilizes a vertical roasting method to drain the fat away from the duck.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 whole [[Cookbook:Duck|pekin duckling]] (3–6 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]], 1.5–3 [[Cookbook:Kg|kg]])
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* Butter-flavored [[Cookbook:Cooking Spray|nonstick spray]]

== Preparation ==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|450 °F]].  
# Rinse and wipe duckling, removing giblets.
# Set bird aside in an airy place to allow the skin to dry.
# Rub inside cavity with salt and pepper.
# Insert vertical oven roaster (used for "beer can chicken") into bird, and prop it upright.
# Coat bird on all sides with butter-flavored spray and sprinkle salt and pepper lightly over the skin.
# Place bird and vertical roaster into a large roasting pan (use a wire rack insert if you have one) and add ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] water to the bottom of the pan.  
# Leave bird in oven for 30 minutes, then reduce heat to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|325 °F]] until done. No need to prick skin or baste bird, as the fat slowly [[Cookbook:Rendering|renders]] off leaving a wonderful crispy skin. Keep the bottom of the roasting pan covered with water to prevent smoking.
# Pour off fat and save, reserving drippings and liquid from the roasting pan.

==Notes, tips, and variations== 
*Serve with brown [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]], [[cookbook:Rice Pilaf|rice pilaf]] or baked [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]]. Cherry sauce and wild rice are also traditional.
*Use the duck fat to cook sliced [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]] or to make [[cookbook:Duck Confit|duck confit]].
*The fat and liver can be cooked together to make a very tasty paté so don't throw any of it out.

title: Cookbook:Lobster Thermidor
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Seafood recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Lobster thermidor''' is a dish created by stuffing an empty lobster tail with sautéed lobster meat that is cooked with butter, a light wine (often sherry), and cream. The resulting sauce is stuffed into a lobster shell then topped with either a cheese, mushrooms or combination of vegetables before being placed under an open flame or broiled.  

The dish originated in Europe but was popularized in the US in the mid-20th century. Perhaps the most prominent reference to Lobster Thermidor is in the movie Citizen Kane;<ref>{{cite web |title=Citizen Kane |url=http://www.dailyscript.com/scripts/citizenkane.html}}</ref> while never shown, is it used as an example of early 20th century Northeastern haute cuisine.  

While present in older American cookbooks, the preparation is no longer widely-known. It is related to Lobster Newberg, another lobster tail recipe commonly presented in older Northeastern-themed cookbooks.
==Ingredients==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (225 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) cooked [[Cookbook:lobster|lobster]] meat, preferably from the tail; see notes
* 1 cleaned [[Cookbook:lobster|lobster]] tail shell
* 3 [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:margarine|margarine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) heavy [[Cookbook:cream|cream]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|egg yolks]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:cup|cup]] (120 ml) [[Cookbook:sherry|sherry]] or [[Cookbook:brandy|brandy]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:cup|cup]] (120 g) grated [[Cookbook:Gruyère Cheese|gruyere]] or [[Cookbook:mozzarella|mozzarella]] [[Cookbook:cheese|cheese]]
* [[Cookbook:salt|Salt]]
* Freshly-ground black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]

== Procedure ==

=== Filling ===
#In a serving bowl, mix together egg yolks and cream, then set aside for later use.
#In a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] large enough to accommodate everything, warm the butter over low heat until it melts.
#Add the cooked lobster meat and wine to the butter, then [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] over medium-high heat for about 2–3 minutes, or until the meat is warmed through and the wine has been mostly absorbed.
#Slowly add the cream and egg mixture, stirring all the time to ensure that the sauce is evenly mixed.
#When the sauce has thickened remove from heat.

=== Assembly ===
#Set [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|broil]] or prepare an open flame.
#Carefully stuff the empty lobster tail with the filling.
#Top the filling with the grated cheese, salt, and pepper.
#Place the filled shell underneath the open flame and [[Cookbook:Broiling|broil]] for 3–8 minutes, or until the cheese melts and turns a golden brown.
#Remove from the oven, and serve on a warmed plate with garnish and appropriate accompaniments.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Cooking and shelling a fresh lobster can be a time consuming process, so frozen or pre-shelled tail meat is often used as a substitute. If you would like to prepare your own lobster meat, refer to the recipe for [[Cookbook:Boiled Lobster|boiled lobster]].
* While the base preparation of Lobster Thermidor often remains the same, the type of wine or cheese used, or the way that the lobster is cooked differs.
* Some preparations include utilizing the broth generated from cooking the lobster with [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]], [[Cookbook:Tarragon|tarragon]], and [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]] as an additional ingredient to thicken the sauce of cream and sherry.

title: Cookbook:Lángos (Hungarian Fried Flatbread)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Fritter recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
[[File:Merry Christmas from Budapest! (42).jpg|thumb|Langos fryer  with its products in street kitchen in Hungary]]
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* Instant [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]] or [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Lard|Lard]] or [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola oil]]

== Procedure ==
# Combine the flour and yeast. Add the eggs, then mix the yoghurt to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Add the salt, and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] until the dough is pliant and not too sticky, adding more flour or yogurt as necessary. The correct texture is really a matter of trial-and-error. It's not unlike an egg pasta dough, but it's rather less stiff.
# Transfer the dough to an oiled bowl. Cover and let rise overnight in a cool location, like the refrigerator.
# Gently deflate the dough.
# When you're ready to cook, heat about 2 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] of lard in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|pan]]. The oil should be hot enough that when you put a very small piece of the dough into it, it drops to the bottom, and immediately rises up to the surface frying.
# Take a lump of the dough (roughly a bit bigger than a ping-pong ball, but rather smaller than a tennis-ball) and flatten it into a disk shape. Do this by hand rather than using a rolling pin—just keep pressing it between fingers and thumbs, and turning it round and round. Make the centre of the disk fairly thin, and the edge rather thicker. It should end up about 8 inches across if possible. Don't worry over-much about getting it too circular and even; the hand-made look is all part of their attraction.
# Carefully slide the disk of dough into the hot oil and let it [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for 30 seconds or so. It should start to puff up as it fries; if it doesn't, either the oil isn't hot enough, or the disk is too thick.
# Carefully turn the dough over, and fry for another 30 seconds or so. Turn it over and see if the underside is golden brown or not. If not, fry for a while longer until both sides are golden brown, with a 'puffed-up' surface. Adjust the frying times for subsequent ones accordingly.
# Remove from the hot oil and drain away any excess.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
[[File:Lángos, 13 December 2023.jpg|thumb|Lángos with every traditional topping: salty garlic sauce, sourcream and cheese]]
* Lángos are traditionally served with a pungent fresh garlic [[Cookbook:Dressing|dressing]]. This is made by mincing up several cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] and mixing them into a small amount of oil and water, which is left to infuse for a while. You just spread the garlic dressing over the hot bread and eat.
* You can also top lángos with [[Cookbook:Crème Fraiche|crème fraîche]], [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]], or thick yoghurt (as a substitute for something called tejföl that you can't get outside of Hungary), and grated [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]. Fried lardons or diced [[Cookbook:Pancetta|pancetta]] are a good topping too.
* Three or four of these will leave you feeling pretty full, but if you've really hungry you could also have some good continental [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]] (ideally Hungarian kolbász, naturally) to go with them.

title: Cookbook:Lolly Cake
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Confection recipes
| Difficulty = 2
| Image = [[File:Lolly cake (2792116118).jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of New Zealand|Cuisine of New Zealand]]

'''Lolly cake''' is a [[cookbook:Cuisine of New Zealand|New Zealand]] cake which features [[cookbook:candy|lollies]] in the ingredients and thus can be thought of as "candy cake". The traditional candy used is Fruit Puffs which are like firm, slightly chewy [[cookbook:marshmallow|marshmallow]]s and are obviously fruity. Malt biscuits and coconut are also used and other ingredients can be added or substituted.

==Ingredients==
* 250 g (1 packet) malt biscuits 
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[cookbook:cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)
* 120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (1.5 sticks) of [[cookbook:butter|butter]]
* 200 g (½ can or 7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[cookbook:condensed milk|condensed milk]]
* 180 g (1 packet) Fruit Puffs
* Shredded [[cookbook:coconut|coconut]]

==Procedure==
# Crush the biscuits. They don't need to be a fine dust—some pieces can be left partially-crushed to give the cake a nicer texture.
# Mix in cinnamon, if you want it.
# Warm the butter and condensed milk in the [[cookbook:Microwave Oven|microwave]] for 30 seconds until the butter is very soft. It's okay if the butter melts a bit.
# Cut the fruit puffs in half if you want or leave them whole.
# Mix the fruit puffs with the crushed biscuits, then add the butter and condensed milk. Mix well.
# Roll the mixture into a log shape, or roll small amounts into little balls.
# Roll the log or balls in the shredded coconut until completely covered.
# Place on a tray and cover with [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]] to keep moist. Chill for several hours in the fridge until hardened.
# Cut cake while still cold before it warms up again

== References/External Links ==

*[http://isaac.freeman.org.nz/a-natural-history-of-lolly-cake Isaac Freeman:A Natural History of Lolly Cake] Website about Lolly cake, with good pictures..

title: Cookbook:Lo Mein
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Stir fry recipes|servings=variable|time=15–25 minutes|difficulty=2|
}}

{{recipe}}

This '''lo mein''' recipe is very flexible. Add what ever ingredients you think will fit. A popular combination is pork with water chestnuts and asparagus. "Stir fry-style meats and vegetables" simply refers to ingredients cut in pieces that are slightly smaller than bite-size and perfect for pan frying.
== Ingredients ==
* 1 part stir fry meat (e.g. [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]], [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], [[Cookbook:Shrimp|shrimp]])
* 1 part stir fry vegetables (e.g. [[Cookbook:Water Chestnut|water chestnuts]], [[Cookbook:Asparagus|asparagus]], [[Cookbook:Broccoli|broccoli]], [[Cookbook:Squash|squash]], [[Cookbook:Bamboo Shoot|bamboo shoots]])
* 1 part cooked lo mein [[Cookbook:Noodle|noodles]]
* Enough [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]] to heavily coat all the ingredients
* Enough [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] to coat a skillet
* Salt to taste
* Pepper to taste

* Crushed/minced [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Bean Sprout|Bean sprouts]] (optional)

== Cookware ==
* Skillet large enough for desired amount of ingredients
* Pot
* Strainer
* Stirring utensil (e.g. tongs, wooden spoon)

== Procedure ==
# Cook noodles in a pot according to the package directions.
# Coat a skillet with olive oil and place on stove with medium to low heat. Add garlic if desired, but don't let it burn.
# Add meat and vegetables to skillet, season with salt and pepper, lightly coat with soy sauce, and cook everything until it's done (about 8–10 minutes).
# If using, add bean sprouts right before everything is finished cooking, and cook them until they turn mildly translucent.
# Strain noodles and add them to the [[cookbook:stir-fry|stir fry]].
# Coat with soy sauce and cook for roughly 1 minute in order to sear in the flavor.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Spaghetti noodles work well too. For a healthier option, try whole-grain spaghetti noodles.
* When adding the soy sauce, start out light. Taste and then add more. It's much easier to add ingredients than remove them.

[[Category:Recipes using meat]]
[[Category:Recipes using pasta and noodles]]
[[Category:Pan fried recipes]]

title: Cookbook:Lumpia (Fried Filipino Spring Rolls)
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Filipino recipes|servings=6–8|time=Active: 1 hour
24 hours start to finish|difficulty=3}} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the Philippines|Cuisine of the Philippines]] '''Lumpia''' are a variety of fried Filipino spring rolls, and they make a tasty dish. ==Ingredients== * 1½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] (680 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) ground [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] or [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] * ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Chop|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Water Chestnut|water chestnuts]] * ½ cup chopped [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] * 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] * ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]] * [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] and freshly ground [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]], to taste * 2 packages (about 40 ea.) small-to-medium size [[Cookbook:Egg Roll|egg roll]] wrappers ([[Cookbook:Wonton Wrapper|wonton wrappers]]) * 4 cups [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|cooking oil]] * [[Cookbook:Sweet and Sour|Sweet and sour sauce]] ==Procedure== # In a large bowl, combine meat, water chestnuts, onion, eggs, soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Mix well and set aside. # On a clean, dry surface, place one egg roll wrapper with one corner facing you (like a baseball diamond). # Place about 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] of the meat mixture in the center of the wrapper. # Dip your fingers in a glass of water and lightly wet the corner pointing away from you (second base). # Fold the corner closest to you (home base) over the mixture, then fold the side corners over that and roll away from your body. The wet corner should seal the roll. # Repeat the filling and shaping process with the remaining ingredients. # Place the rolls in large zip-close plastic bags and freeze overnight. # In a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], heat the oil to about 350°F (175°C) or until it begins to shimmer and the oil bubbles lightly when a wooden chopstick is inserted. # Using [[Cookbook:Tongs|tongs]], place each frozen lumpia roll in the hot oil and [[Cookbook:Fry|fry]] until brown, about 3 to 4 minutes. Use tongs to turn rolls to ensure even cooking. # Remove the rolls to a plate covered with [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]] to absorb excess oil. ==Notes, tips, and variations== * Serve with sweet and sour sauce. title: Cookbook:Light Fluffy Pancakes
text:
{{recipesummary | category = Pancake recipes | Yield = 8 ea. 4-inch pancakes | time = Prep: 10 minutes
Cooking: 5 minutes per skillet | difficulty = 2 }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Breakfast Recipes|Breakfast Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]] ==Ingredients== * 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] all-purpose bleached [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] * ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]] * ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]] * ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]] * ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] * 1 large [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted * 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]] * [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|Vegetable oil]] for brushing [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]] ==Procedure== # Heat a large non-stick [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] or [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]] over low heat while preparing ingredients. # Mix flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, and baking soda in medium bowl. # [[Cookbook:Microwave Oven|Microwave]] buttermilk and milk in a 2-cup Pyrex measuring cup until room temperature (20–30 seconds). # [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] in egg, butter, and vanilla. # Add wet ingredients to dry ingredients and whisk until just mixed. # Return batter to measuring cup, stirring in 1–2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Water|water]] if necessary to make a thick but pourable batter. # Increase heat to medium and generously [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]] skillet or griddle with oil. # When oil starts to spider, but before it starts to smoke, ladle in batter about ¼ cup at a time to make pancakes. Work in batches, if necessary, to avoid overcrowding. # When pancake bottoms are golden brown and tops start to bubble (2–3 minutes), flip pancakes. # Cook until pancakes are golden brown on remaining side. # Repeat, brushing skillet or griddle with oil between batches of pancakes. # Serve hot. == Notes, tips, and variations == * Use bleached flour to make a tender pancake. * If using salted butter, reduce salt to ¼ teaspoon. * Pancake batter should pour, not glug! On the other hand, runny batter makes thin, oddly-shaped pancakes that frequently collide on the griddle. Stir in a touch more flour into thin batter. For batter that's too thick, whisk in water a teaspoon at a time. * The temperature of the pan or griddle is important: too hot and the pancakes are dark and raw; too cool and they're blond and hard. For tender, golden brown pancakes, heat the pan or griddle on low while you make the batter. Then increase the heat to medium and generously brush the pan or griddle with oil. It's ready when the oil starts to shimmer and, in any skillet or griddle other than non-stick, sends out tendrils that resemble an octopus or spider. But if the pan starts to smoke, set it down off the burner until the smoking subsides and the oil cools a bit. * This recipe easily doubles for a crowd. title: Cookbook:London Fog
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Beverage recipes
| Difficulty = 1
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Beverages|Beverages]]

'''London fog''' (also known as Vanilla Tea Misto or an Earl Grey Tea Latte) is the name of a drink which originated in Vancouver, British Columbia, [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Canada|Canada]], although the creator remains unknown, among several claims. One such claim is from Buckwheat Cafe on 4th Avenue in Vancouver (now closed) when in December 1996 a regular customer, Mary Loria, who was pregnant and couldn't drink coffee asked for an alternative.  Another is from the Island Coffeehouse in Langley, Washington, a non-profit student run organization, where it was originally made with Peppermint Tea in 2006.  However, patrons of Starbucks in Calgary, Alberta have asked for this drink since the winter of 2004, coincidentally when Loria was visiting family.  It is common in Washington and Oregon, as well as in BC's lower mainland and throughout British Columbia and Alberta. Canadian Second Cup cafés also carry the drink.

The "London Fog" was recently the subject of an investigation on the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation's afternoon show ''Freestyle''.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 bag Earl Grey [[Cookbook:Tea Leaves|tea]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] water
* 16 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] [[Cookbook:milk|milk]] (2% or whole)
* 1 shot [[Cookbook:vanilla|vanilla]] [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]]

== Procedure ==
# Add the boiling water to a mug along with the tea bag. Let steep for 2–4 minutes to achieve optimum flavor—the result is an Earl Grey tea concentrate. 
# Heat up milk. Access to a steamer is preferred. Mix in vanilla syrup.
# Add hot milk to the tea as desired. Adjust components according to taste.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* '''Oregon Mist:''' Replace the Earl Grey tea with green tea and the vanilla syrup with [[Cookbook:Amaretto|amaretto]]; popularized by the Glenwood restaurants in Eugene, Oregon.
* '''Manchester Fog:''' Replace the milk with [[Cookbook:Soy Milk|soy milk]].
* '''Dublin Fog:''' Replace the Earl Grey tea with Irish breakfast tea.
* '''Bangalore Fog:''' Replace the Earl Grey tea with a [[Cookbook:Chai Tea|chai]] tea blend; created by Kavya Raman at Roosters Coffeehouse, Carleton University, Ottawa ON; also known as a Bombay Fog (coined in Concordia-Loyola's Second Cup, Montreal, QC).
* '''Atlantic City Fog:''' Replace the Earl Grey tea with with rose tea; created by Alexis V. Juneau at MCB Quantico, Quantico, Virginia.
* '''Winter Fog:''' Reduce the vanilla syrup and add clover [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] to taste.
* '''Maui Fog:''' Replace the vanilla syrup with [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] syrup.
* '''Tokyo Fog:''' Replace the Earl Grey tea with [[Cookbook:Matcha|matcha green tea]].
* '''Cape Town Fog:''' Replace the Earl Grey tea with rooibos tea
* '''Nanaimo Mist:''' Replace the vanilla syrup with [[Cookbook:Almond|almond]] syrup; accredited to Ravenna.
* '''Oxford Haze:''' Replace the Earl Grey tea with English breakfast tea and the vanilla syrup with [[Cookbook:Hazelnut|hazelnut]] syrup.
* '''Victoria Fog:''' Replace the Earl Grey tea with [[Cookbook:Lavender|lavender]]-scented tea.
* '''Montreal Fog:''' Replace the Earl Grey tea with yerba mate, and add hazelnut syrup.
* '''London Smog:''' Add a shot of [[Cookbook:Coffee|espresso]].
* '''Mexican Fog:''' Replace the vanilla syrup with [[Cookbook:Agave Syrup|agave syrup]].
* '''Halifax Fog:''' Replace the vanilla syrup with Nova Scotian [[Cookbook:Maple Syrup|maple syrup]].
* '''Savannah Fog:''' Replace the vanilla syrup with lavender syrup.
* '''Seattle Fog:''' soy misto (½ water, ½ soy, steamed) with 2 pumps of vanilla syrup and one pump of hazelnut syrup, in 2 bags of Earl Grey Tea.
* '''Durban Fog:''' A cross between a Cape Town Fog and a Bangalore Fog; basically the same as a London Fog, but replacing Earl Grey with Rooibos Tea and adding a pinch of tea masala.
* '''Fog on the Tyne:''' Variation on the London Fog; start with a cup of hot milk, add a heaped spoonful of sugar, drop in an Earl Grey tea bag, and let it diffuse directly into the milk for 30–60 seconds.

title: Cookbook:Liver Kebabs
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Meat recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Liver kebabs''' taste very good and are ideal for feeding young children liver as long as you don't tell them beforehand what it is. Served with fresh bread and [[Cookbook:Moroccan Salad|Moroccan Salad]], the kebabs make a nice meal.

In Morocco every home has a shallow round clay pot that is filled with charcoal and used to grill meat and, in many homes, to cook the tagines on. Meat is put onto skewers and then held in a metal griller and cooked over the charcoal. As most Moroccan homes have an outdoor room (patio) everyone just sits round and eats as the meat comes off the grill. No need to wait for good weather to get the barbecue out!

* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Sunflower Oil|sunflower]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]

==Procedure==
#Cut the liver into small cubes about 1 cm square, and put them in a container.

#Mix this all together and leave to marinate for 30 minutes or more.

#[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] together the sugar and shortening.

text:
{{Recipe summary

}}

{{recipe}}

==Ingredients==

*1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]]
*2 large [[Cookbook:Onions|onions]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] thin
*[[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|Oil]] or [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] for frying
*Fresh or frozen green vegetables, such as [[Cookbook:Pea|peas]], [[Cookbook:Kale|kale]], [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]], [[Cookbook:Broccoli|broccoli]], etc.
*[[Cookbook:Flour|Flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* Large knob of butter
* A splash of [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]], [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]], [[Cookbook:Crème Fraiche|crème fraîche]], or similar
* about 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Lamb|lamb]] or ox [[Cookbook:Liver|liver]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* Henderson's relish, [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]], or similar (optional)

==Procedure==

#Wash (and optionally peel) the potatoes and put in a pan of boiling water.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] onions gently in a large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] with some of the oil.
# While the onions are frying, prepare the green vegetables.
# Prepare a plate or wide bowl, covering it in flour mixed with a bit of salt and pepper. This is for dusting the liver prior to frying.
# Once the potatoes are cooked, drain and then mash them, adding butter and cream or milk until you have the desired consistency. Put a lid on the pan to keep warm.
# Once the onions are soft, remove them from the pan with a slotted spoon, squeezing the oil or butter back into the frying pan as you remove them. Put them in a bowl on one side.
# Turn the heat of your frying pan up as high as possible and add a bit more oil or butter if necessary.
# Arrange the liver, flour and frying pan in a straight line.
# Start the process of dusting the slices of liver with flour on both sides and adding them to the hot pan. This needs to be done as quickly as possible and can be quite messy. Do not over-crowd the pan—if you find the liver takes up more surface-space than is available then leave the remains on one side and fry in a second batch.
# Cook the liver quickly, for only about a minute on each side so the slices are still pink within. Turn them over a couple of times. Quite a bit of the flour and blood will stick to the bottom of the pan. This is ok—don't scrape it off as it will be used for the gravy in a moment.
#Once the liver is done to your satisfaction remove it from the pan and put directly onto warmed plates. Have someone else serve out the mash and vegetables while you finish the gravy. The trick is to try and not let everything else get cold while you are doing this.
#Leaving the pan on a high heat, put the onions back in, add a good splash of Hendersons, and stir vigorously while adding boiling water, dissolving the juices stuck to the bottom of the pan. The gravy should thicken from the flour already stuck to the bottom of the pan. If it doesn't get thick enough you can add a bit more flour or cornflour (mixed with a little cold water in a small cup to avoid lumps). 
#Once the gravy is hot and thickened, spoon generously over the plates.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* When making the gravy, you can re-use the hot water from the vegetables. This can be a smooth maneuver, draining it into the gravy as you pass the pan over to be served onto plates.

title: Cookbook:Locrio (Dominican Chicken and Rice)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Rice recipes
| Difficulty = 4
| Image = [[File:Locrio de Pollo (Dominicano).jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}
[[Category:Recipes using chicken]]
A '''locrio''' is a common Dominican dish similar to [[Cookbook:Paella|paella]]. Like paella, there are many variations. The main point is to have a little tomato sauce/paste for coloring, and some caramelized sugar. In that way it is similar to the Trinidadian pilau. Like paella, the rice at the bottom should be toasted or browned, but not burnt. This browned rice is called "concon". You're not considered a good cook until you can do this.

== Ingredients ==
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]] for frying 
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] (1.8 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut in pieces
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]] (pitted) or [[Cookbook:Caper|capers]]
* 2 tbsp oil, for when rice is almost done
* ½ cup finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]]
* ½ cup finely diced [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 4 cups [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 5¼ cups chicken [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]] or water
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] or to taste
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]] (optional)
* 1 tsp ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]

== Procedure ==

=== Stovetop method ===
#Heat the ¼ cup oil in a pot over high heat.
#Add the sugar to the pot. Let it melt and [[Cookbook:Caramelization|caramelize]], turning light brown. Pay close attention and don't let the sugar burn. Do not use plastic utensils to stir the sugar, since it will be at around 350°F (175°C).
#Add the meat to the caramel and let it brown on all sides. Remove and reserve the meat.
#Add the garlic, onions, and celery to the pot. [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]].
#Add rice and cooked meat to pot with the vegetables. [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] together chicken stock and tomato paste until smooth, then stir it into the rice mixture. Stir in the salt, pepper, thyme, and olives.
#Check the seasoning. If the salt level is good, add an extra ½ tsp of salt. This is because the rice will absorb some of the salt, and it will come out a bit flat in the end unless you add extra salt.
#Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over high heat. Let it boil, stirring occasionally, until the water is absorbed. The high heat is needed to bring the rice temperature up so that it cooks. If you lower the flame at this point, the rice might not cook all the way.
#Cover, lower the heat, and let it cook for 15 minutes.
#Uncover, sprinkle 2 Tbsp oil on top, and stir so that the uncooked rice on top goes to the bottom. Cook for another 5 minutes.
#If rice still not cooked, give it another stir and cook for another 5 minutes. Sometimes you may need more time; see notes below.
#Turn heat on high for a couple of minutes to brown and toast the rice on bottom. Sometimes it does this by itself during the main cooking so you don't have to do this. Experience will tell.
#Serve.

=== Oven method ===
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (125°C).
#Proceed with the recipe as above, using an oven-proof pot, until the rice absorbs all the liquid. Once this happens, cover the pot, put it in the oven, and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for 30 minutes. 
#Add 2 tbsp oil, and stir so the uncooked rice is on the bottom and the bottom rice is on the top. Bake for another 20 minutes.
#Stir. If it is still not fully cooked, bake another 20 minutes.
#Serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*If the rice doesn't cook but all the water was absorbed, you can separate the rice from the meat, put it in a bowl, and give it 5 minutes on high in the [[Cookbook:Microwave|microwave]]. Often there wasn't enough heat to cook the rice. On some stoves, once covered (as mentioned above), you may have to cook 20 minutes, add oil, stir, and cook another 20–40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
*It is also helpful to put a sheet or two of [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminium foil]] over the pot before putting the lid on. That helps seal the lid and keep the heat/steam from escaping, and the rice often comes out better. 
*Dominicans tend to cook the rice on the dry side—the rice will be cooked through, but not too watery. The ratio should be 4 cups rice to 5½ cups liquid (some locrio recipes ask for 7–8 cups of liquid, which makes things mushy). If you have tomato sauce instead of tomato paste, you can use that also, as long as the ratios are the same (e.g. 1 cup tomato sauce to 4½ cups water/stock; which makes a total of 5½ cups liquid). If you halve the recipe, the ratio rice to liquid will be 2 cups rice to 2¾ cups liquid.
*Some people deep fry the meat separately, remove the excess oil, and then caramelize the sugar.
*The ingredients of the sofrito vary, and can be made in advance. Some add [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]], [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]], [[Cookbook:Culantro|culantro]], and other aromatics to it.
*Other vegetables such as 1 cup of cubed auyama squash are sometimes added with the rice.
*You can also substitute guineafowl, [[Cookbook:Rabbit|rabbit]], Dominican [[Cookbook:Salami|salami]], [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] chops, or other meat for the chicken. Almost any meat can be used, including cubed [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]] or spam, arrenque (smoked dried herring, pre-soaked in warm water to remove some salt, but cut the amount of salt you use), canned sardines, Vienna sausages, shellfish (mariscos) and if in desperation, ground beef, meatballs, hot dogs, etc. can also be used. You can use 2 lbs of chicken gizzards also, but gizzards need to be boiled (or pressure cooked) until tender first. 
*Some people use Sazón Completo for the seasoning. Although it is not authentic, you can also add 1 tsp ajinomoto (味の素), which is similar.
*You can take the skin off the chicken before frying it.
*Instead of chicken stock, some people throw in a stock cube.

title: Cookbook:Long Island Iced Tea
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Beverage recipes
| Difficulty = 1
}}

{{Recipe}}| [[Cookbook:tea|Tea]] 

A '''Long Island iced tea''' is a mixed cocktail originating in the [[Wikipedia:Prohibition|prohibition era]] and made popular in New York speakeasies. Despite its name, the drink does not contain any tea whatsoever.

== Ingredients ==
* ¼ part [[Cookbook:Vodka|vodka]]
* ¼ part white [[Cookbook:Rum|rum]]
* ¼ part [[Cookbook:Gin|gin]]
* ¼ part [[Cookbook:Tequila|tequila]] or [[Cookbook:Triple Sec|triple sec]]
* 1 part sweet and sour mix OR [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]/[[Cookbook:Lime|lime]] juice to taste
* 1 splash [[Cookbook:Cola|cola]] or [[Cookbook:Coffee Liqueur|coffee liqueur]]
* Lemon, [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] for garnish

== Procedure ==

=== Shaken method ===
# Shake all the ingredients except the cola with ice in a cocktail shaker.
# [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] into a highball glass.
# Float the cola on the top and serve with a lemon slice.

=== Stirred method ===
# Fill a highball glass until it's almost full with ice.
# Add vodka, gin, rum, and tequila.
# Add sweet and sour mix, leaving some room on top.
# Splash in the cola and enjoy.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Don't forget—it has to look like an iced tea, so don't add too much cola.
* To make a '''Long Beach Tea''', use [[Cookbook:Cranberry|cranberry]] juice instead of cola.
