title: Cookbook:Long Island Roast Duckling with Citrus
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Duck recipes
| Servings = 3–4
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

This recipe uses a conventional [[Cookbook:Roasting|roasting]] method based on the one featured on The City Cook website.<ref>[http://www.thecitycook.com/cooking/recipes/data/000103 Roast duck recipe on the City Cook website]</ref>

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (4–5 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]], 1.8–3.6 [[Cookbook:Kg|kg]]) whole [[Cookbook:Duck|pekin duckling]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]], cut into quarters
* 1 [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]], cut into quarters or eighths
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

== Preparation ==
# Defrost the duck in the fridge if it's frozen.
# Remove the giblets and any packages from the body cavity.
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|375 °F]] and place an oven rack in the center of the oven.
# Rinse the duck and pat it dry both inside and out with [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]].
# Pierce the skin every half inch with prongs, pushing the prongs through the skin and into the fat but not into the meat. The fat will escape through these holes as the duck cooks.
# Rub plenty of salt and freshly ground pepper on the skin. Then, place 2 pieces of lemon and 2–4 pieces of orange inside the duck's cavity.
# Tie the duck's legs together with a piece of butcher's twine. This will keep the citrus inside the cavity.
# Place the duck breast side up on a rack that has been placed on a roasting pan. It's important to use a roasting pan that has some depth so the fat drips into the pan and not the oven.
# Push a meat [[Cookbook:Thermometer|thermometer]] into one of the thighs.
# Place the bird on the center rack of the oven. It will cook in 1–1½ hours depending on its size.
# Remove the duck every 20 minutes from the oven and drain the excess fat. Rotate the duck each time you return it to the oven to help it crisp evenly. You'll know it's done when the skin is golden brown and crispy. Also, the meat thermometer should read no lower than 165 °F.
# Remove the bird from the oven. Pour out the liquid from the cavity and discard.
# Allow the duck to rest for ten minutes before carving.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 large [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breasts, cut into cubes
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

title: Cookbook:Liberian Potato Greens
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Liberian recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

This is an easy and delicious dish popularly cooked in West Africa.

== Ingredients ==

*3 large bunches of sweet potato greens (see notes)
*[[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
*2 big [[Cookbook:Onions|onions]], neatly [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] meat, cut into medium cubes
*Seasoned [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] to taste
*[[Cookbook:Onion Powder|Onion powder]] to taste
*Chicken [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|bouillon cubes]], crushed
*Ground red or black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] to taste

== Procedure ==

# Wash the potato greens very well, and remove the leaves from the stems. [[Cookbook:Chopping|Chop]] the leaves into small pieces and set aside.
# Heat a few tablespoons of oil in a large pot. Add the onions and meat, and cook until almost done. Remove from the pot and set aside.
# Add the potato greens, and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for about 15 minutes or until tender. Stir frequently to prevent burning.
# Add enough water to cover the greens, and season to taste with salt, onion powder, bouillon cubes, and ground pepper.
# Cook over medium heat until all the water is gone, stirring frequently.
# Remove from the heat and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Do not eat '''white potato''' greens—they are toxic. Sweet potato greens, however, are safe. You can get potato greens from the market or from local farmers.
* If desired, add a pinch of baking soda to the greens when cooking to keep their green color.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Palm Oil Stew
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = African recipes
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian palm oil stew''' is a delicious and hearty dish from Liberia. Made with a rich combination of palm oil, vegetables, and protein, this stew is a staple in Liberian cuisine and is often served with rice or fufu.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook: Pepper|green bell pepper]], [[Cookbook:Knife Skills|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook: Pepper|red bell pepper]], diced
* 1 Scotch bonnet [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile pepper]], finely chopped (optional, for spiciness)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut into pieces
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:Broth|chicken broth]]
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]], cut into steaks or fillets
* ½ pound [[Cookbook:Okra|okra]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]], diced
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Ground black pepper]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* Large [[Cookbook: Stock Pot|pot]]
* [[Cookbook: Wooden Spoon|Wooden spoon]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sauté|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and fragrant.
# Stir in the diced green and red bell peppers and chopped Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Cook for a few minutes until the peppers start to soften.
# Add the chicken pieces to the pot and cook until they are lightly browned on all sides.
# Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Cover the pot and let the chicken cook for about 20–25 minutes, or until it is fully cooked and tender.
# Once the chicken is cooked, add the fish steaks or fillets to the pot and let them simmer in the stew for an additional 5–10 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
# Stir in the sliced okra and diced eggplant. Let the stew simmer for another 5–7 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
# Season the stew with salt and ground black pepper to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let the stew rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Palm oil gives the stew its distinctive flavor and vibrant red color. It is a traditional ingredient in Liberian cuisine and can be found in specialty African grocery stores.
* For a spicier version, you can add more Scotch bonnet pepper or a pinch of [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|cayenne pepper]] to the stew.
* This stew is traditionally served with rice or [[Cookbook:Fufu|fufu]], a starchy side dish made from cassava or other root vegetables.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Pepper Soup
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = African recipes
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian pepper soup''' is a flavorful and spicy soup from Liberia. It is a popular dish that is often enjoyed as a warming and comforting meal, especially during cold weather or when feeling under the weather.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], grated
* 2 Scotch bonnet [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]], finely chopped
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut into pieces
* 4–5 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] chicken [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* 1 pound [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]], cut into steaks or fillets
* 1 [[Cookbook:Plantain|plantain]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], sliced
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Ground black pepper]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* Large pot
* Wooden spoon

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and fragrant.
# Stir in the chopped Scotch bonnet peppers and bay leaf. Cook for a few minutes to release the flavors.
# Add the chicken pieces to the pot and cook until they are lightly browned on all sides.
# Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Cover the pot and let the chicken cook for about 20–25 minutes, or until it is fully cooked and tender.
# Once the chicken is cooked, add the fish steaks or fillets to the pot and let them simmer in the soup for an additional 5–10 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
# Stir in the sliced plantain and carrot. Let the soup simmer for another 5–7 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
# Season the soup with salt and ground black pepper to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference and desired level of spiciness.
# Remove the pot from the heat and let the soup rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Liberian pepper soup is traditionally served with rice, [[Cookbook:Swallow|fufu]], or other starchy side dishes.
* For a milder version, you can reduce the amount of Scotch bonnet peppers used or remove the seeds before chopping them.
* You can also add other vegetables such as bell peppers, spinach, or cabbage to the soup for added flavor and nutrition.

== Nutrition ==
* This soup is a good source of protein from the chicken and fish, as well as vitamins and minerals from the vegetables and spices.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Fufu
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = Swallow recipes
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian fufu''' is a staple food in Liberia and many other West African countries. It is made from starchy vegetables like cassava, yams, or plantains, which are boiled, pounded, and formed into a smooth, dough-like consistency. Fufu is typically served with various soups and stews, making it a versatile and satisfying dish.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] [[Cookbook:Cassava|cassava]], [[Cookbook:Yam|yams]], or [[Cookbook:Plantain|plantains]]
* Water

== Equipment ==
* Large pot
* Potato [[Cookbook:Masher|masher]] or [[Cookbook:Mortar and Pestle|pestle and mortar]]

== Procedure ==
# Peel and cut the cassava, yams, or plantains into chunks, and place them in a large pot.
# Add enough water to cover the vegetables, and bring the pot to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over high heat.
# Reduce the heat to medium and let the vegetables [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until they are tender and easily pierced with a fork.
# Drain the water from the cooked vegetables, and transfer them to a large bowl.
# Use a potato masher, or mortar and pestle to pound the vegetables into a smooth, thick paste. You can also use a stand [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]] or [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]] for this step.
# Continue pounding and kneading the mixture until it forms a smooth and stretchy dough-like consistency. This process may take some time and effort, but it is essential for achieving the right texture.
# Once the fufu has reached the desired consistency, shape it into small balls or serve it as a large mound on a serving platter.
# Serve with various soups and stews. It can be used as a utensil to scoop up the soup or stew.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* To enhance the flavor, you can add a pinch of salt or other seasonings to the cooked vegetables before pounding.
* Some people prefer their fufu to be softer, while others prefer it to be firmer. Adjust the amount of pounding and kneading to achieve your desired texture.
* Leftover fufu can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. To reheat, steam it or place it in a [[Cookbook:Microwave|microwave]] for a few minutes until warmed through.
* Fufu is naturally gluten-free and can be enjoyed by those with gluten sensitivities.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Fried Plantains with Beans
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = African recipes
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian fried plantains with beans''' is a popular and delicious dish in Liberia. It combines the sweet and savory flavors of [[Cookbook:Plantain|ripe plantains]] with the heartiness of cooked [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]]. This dish can be served as a main course or as a side dish, and it's perfect for any occasion.

== Ingredients ==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Plantain|ripe plantains]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]], for frying
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] cooked [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]] (black-eyed peas or kidney beans)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
* ½ teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Black pepper|black pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
== Equipment ==
* Large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]]
* Slotted spoon

== Procedure ==
# Peel the ripe plantains and cut them into diagonal slices, about ½ inch thick.
# In a large frying pan, heat vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the plantain slices in batches until they are golden brown and crispy on both sides. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the fried plantains to a plate lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil.
# In the same frying pan, [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the chopped onion and minced garlic until they become translucent and fragrant.
# Add the cooked beans to the pan and mix well with the onions and garlic.
# Season the beans with ground paprika, ground black pepper, and [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] to taste. Stir to coat the beans evenly with the spices.
# Cook the bean mixture for a few minutes until it is heated through.
# Serve the fried plantains alongside the seasoned beans and enjoy this delightful and flavorful Liberian dish.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Adjust the seasoning according to your taste preferences. You can add other spices like cayenne pepper or thyme for extra flavor.
* If you prefer a sweeter taste, you can sprinkle a little [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]] on the fried plantains before serving.
* This dish can be served as a main course with rice or as a side dish with grilled or fried fish or meat.
* Leftover fried plantains and beans can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat before serving.
* Beans are rich in protein, dietary fiber, and various nutrients such as iron and folate.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Fried Sweet Potato Puffs
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = Potato recipes
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian fried sweet potato puffs''' are delightful and flavorful snacks that make a perfect treat for any occasion. Made with mashed sweet potatoes, these puffs are seasoned with a blend of spices and herbs, giving them a unique taste that will keep you coming back for more. They are fried to golden perfection, creating a crispy exterior with a soft and creamy interior.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 large [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]], [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiled]] and mashed
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]], lightly beaten
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking powder|baking powder]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Black pepper|black pepper]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|ground cinnamon]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|ground nutmeg]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil,]] for frying

== Equipment ==
* Large pot or [[Cookbook:Deep Fryer|deep-fryer]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixing bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Potato Masher|Potato masher]] or fork
* Slotted spoon
* [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|Paper towels]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large mixing bowl, combine the mashed [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]] with the beaten [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]].
# In a separate bowl, whisk together the [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]], [[Cookbook:Baking powder|baking powder]], [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], [[Cookbook:Black pepper|black pepper]], [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|ground cinnamon]], [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|ground nutmeg]], and cloves.
# Gradually add the dry ingredients to the sweet potato mixture, stirring until well combined.
# Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or deep-fryer to 350°F (175°C).
# Using a spoon or cookie scoop, carefully drop spoonfuls of the sweet potato mixture into the hot oil.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the sweet potato puffs in batches for about 3–4 minutes or until they are golden brown and crispy.
# Remove the fried puffs from the oil using a slotted spoon, and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil.
# Serve warm as a snack or appetizer.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* You can adjust the seasoning according to your taste preferences. Add more spices or herbs for a bolder flavor.
* These sweet potato puffs can be served with your favorite dipping sauce, such as [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]] or aioli.
* Leftover sweet potato puffs can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat them in the oven or microwave before serving.
* Sweet potatoes are a good source of vitamins, minerals, and fiber.

title: Cookbook:Liberian Roasted Corn
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = Corn recipes
| difficulty = 1
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Liberian roasted corn''' is a simple and delicious street food that captures the essence of Liberia's culinary delights. This delightful treat is made by roasting fresh corn over an open flame until it develops a smoky and charred flavor. Liberians often enjoy roasted corn as a snack or side dish, especially during gatherings or festivals.

== Ingredients ==
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]] on the cob

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Grilling|Grill]] or open flame (charcoal grill, gas grill, or campfire)

== Procedure ==
# Preheat the grill or set up an open flame (charcoal grill, gas grill, or campfire).
# Remove the husks and silk from the fresh corn on the cob, leaving the base intact for easy handling.
# Place the corn on the grill or directly over the open flame.
# Rotating the corn occasionally to ensure even cooking and prevent burning, roast the corn for about 10–15 minutes or until the kernels are tender and have developed a slightly charred appearance.
# Once the corn is roasted to your desired level, remove it from the grill or flame.
# Serve hot and enjoy as a flavorful snack or side dish.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* For added flavor, you can [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]] the corn with [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or oil before roasting. Some Liberians also sprinkle [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chili powder]] or other spices on the roasted corn for extra kick.
* Liberian roasted corn is often served with a variety of toppings, such as salt, pepper, or grated [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]].
* This recipe can also be made with corn still in the husks. Simply soak the corn in water for about 30 minutes before roasting to prevent the husks from catching fire.
* Liberian roasted corn is best enjoyed immediately after roasting while it is still warm and full of flavor.

title: Cookbook:Lumanda (Zambian Okra Stew)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = Stew recipes
| cuisine = Zambian
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Lumanda''' is a flavorful Zambian okra [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]] that celebrates the unique taste and texture of okra. This vegetarian stew is made with fresh okra pods, tomatoes, onions, and a blend of aromatic spices. It is a delightful dish often enjoyed with nshima, a popular Zambian staple food.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pepper|hot pepper]], chopped (remove seeds for less heat)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Paprika|ground paprika]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cumin|ground cumin]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Turmeric|ground turmeric]]
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Coriander|ground coriander]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] fresh [[Cookbook:Okra|okra]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste

== Equipment ==
* Large pot
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* [[Cookbook:Wooden Spoon|Wooden spoon]] or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]

== Procedure ==
# In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
# Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, and chopped hot pepper to the pot. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onions are soft and translucent.
# Stir in the ground paprika, ground cumin, ground turmeric, and ground coriander. Cook for a minute or two to release the flavors of the spices.
# Add the sliced okra and diced tomato to the pot. Stir well to combine the vegetables with the spice mixture.
# Season the stew with salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
# Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let simmer for about 15–20 minutes, or until the okra is tender and cooked through.
# Stir occasionally during cooking to prevent sticking and to ensure even cooking of the okra and tomatoes.
# Once the stew is ready, remove the pot from the heat and let rest for a few minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* For a thicker stew, you can add a spoonful of cornmeal or cassava meal to the pot during cooking.
* Lumanda is traditionally served with [[Cookbook:Nsima|nshima]], a stiff maize porridge, but it can also be enjoyed with rice or bread.

title: Cookbook:Luwombo (Ugandan Steamed Meat and Vegetables)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = Ugandan recipes
| cuisine = Ugandan
| difficulty = 3
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Luwombo''', a quintessential Ugandan dish, showcases the rich flavors and vibrant culinary traditions of the country. This unique cooking method involves steaming meat, vegetables, and a delightful blend of local spices in banana leaves, infusing the dish with an unmistakably authentic aroma and taste.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] or [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], cut into chunks
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] red [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 tablespoon minced [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
*[[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|Cayenne pepper]]
* 2 tablespoons groundnut paste (or [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]])
* 1 tablespoon groundnut powder (or [[Cookbook:Peanut|peanut]] powder)
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|groundnut oil]]
* 1 cup diced [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potatoes]]
* 1 cup diced [[Cookbook:Cassava|cassava]]
* 1 cup diced [[Cookbook:Banana|green bananas]] (matooke)
* 1 cup diced [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]] 
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Ground Crayfish|ground crayfish]] (optional, for added flavor)
* 1 cup fresh or canned [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]]
* 1 cup homemade chicken or vegetable [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* Banana leaves, for wrapping

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* [[Cookbook: Knife|Knife]]
* Large [[Cookbook: Mixing Bowl|bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Steamer|Steamer]] or large pot with a steaming rack

== Procedure ==
# In a large bowl, [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] the meat chunks with minced garlic, minced ginger, groundnut paste, groundnut powder, ground crayfish (if using), salt, and cayenne pepper. Allow the meat to marinate for at least 30 minutes to absorb the flavorful blend.
# Heat palm oil or groundnut oil in a large pot or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated meat and cook until beautifully browned on all sides, releasing an enticing aroma.
# Stir in the diced onions and cook until they soften and become fragrant.
# Add the diced sweet potatoes, cassava, green bananas, and eggplant to the pot.
# Pour in the fresh coconut milk and homemade chicken or vegetable broth, ensuring all the ingredients are immersed in the rich and creamy goodness. Bring the mixture to a gentle [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]].
# Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot with a lid, and let the ingredients [[Cookbook:Steaming|steam]] for about 1–2 hours until the meat is tender.
# Meanwhile, prepare the banana leaves by briefly holding them over an open flame to soften and make them pliable for wrapping.
# Take a portion of the steamed mixture and place it in the center of a banana leaf, folding the leaf around the mixture to create a packet. Repeat with the remaining mixture and banana leaves.
# Once all the packets are prepared, return them to the steamer or large pot with a steaming rack.
# Steam the luwombo packets for an additional 30 minutes.
# Serve the luwombo packets on individual plates.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Luwombo is often enjoyed with steamed rice or matooke, a dish made from green bananas, to complete the authentic Ugandan dining experience.
* Luwombo offers a well-rounded nutritional profile, boasting proteins from the meat and an array of vitamins and minerals from the diverse vegetables used.

|

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixer#Stand mixer|Stand mixer]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|Cake pan]] or rimmed [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] at least 1 inch (2.5 cm) deep – quarter sheet size (9x13 inches, 33 x 23 cm)

== Procedure ==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|350 °F (175°C, gas mark 4—moderate)]].
# Put the butter in a large mixing bowl, and [[Cookbook:Beat|beat]] it with an electric mixer for about 30 seconds. Alternatively, beat it with a wooden spoon until soft.
# Beat in the sugar, cocoa, salt, cloves, and cinnamon, scraping the bowl as needed, until you have a smooth, dark mixture.
# Beat in the eggs.
# Stir in the flour and hazelnut flour. If the butter was cold when you started, this step may be difficult.
# Spread about three-quarters of the cookie dough in the baking pan, reserving the remaining quarter for the topping.
# Spread the fruit preserves evenly over the raw dough in the baking pan.
# Drop the remaining cookie dough by spoonfuls on top of the fruit preserves. If desired, these can be flattened using the back of a spoon, wet fingers, or the waxed paper wrappers from the butter.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the preheated oven for about 35 minutes, until a wooden toothpick comes out clean.
# Cool in the pan. Cut into 32 bars (4x8 grid).

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You can use gluten-free flour substitutes. Avoid high-gluten bread flours.
* You can replace up to half the sugar with a sugar substitute.
* You can substitute other kinds of nut flours/nut meal.
* If you halve the recipe, use one whole egg and one egg yolk. Bake in a 7x11-inch pan, an 8x8-inch square pan, or a 9-inch round pan.
* If desired, the bars can be decorated by sifting a small amount of [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|powdered sugar]] over the pan just before cutting them.
* Store at room temperature or in the refrigerator for a few days. Freeze for longer periods.

It is made with "mel de cana" which literally means "cane honey," otherwise known as molasses. ==Ingredients== {| class="wikitable" style="background: none;color:inherit;" !Ingredient Weight conversions from USDA National Nutrient Database. Original ingredient order preserved. Where they were provided, used metric measures for conversion. Separate gram and ounce weights are not equivalent, but are within about 2% difference. When making a batch, more accurate measure will be found by using one or the other, but not mixing them. "Ounces" are understood as measures of mass or weight, there are no volumetric "fluid ounces" currently used in this formula. Madeira wine type not specified, weight calculated from average bulk density figures provided by vinhomadeira.pt for type Meio Seco. !Count !Volume !Weight ![[Cookbook:Baker's Percentage|Baker's %]] |- |[[Cookbook:Dough|Bread dough]] from the baker's shop | | |9 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] (250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) |10% |- |[[Cookbook:Baking Soda|Baking soda]], dissolved in the wine | |5 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] |69 g |2.76% |- |[[Cookbook:Madeira|Madeira]] wine | |1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] |240 g |9.58% |- |[[Cookbook:Molasses|Molasses]] | |1.8 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] |92 ounces (2560 g) |102% |- |[[Cookbook:Pork|Pork]] fat | | |27 ounces (750 g) |30% |- |[[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]] | | |18 ounces (500 g) |20% |- |[[Cookbook:Flour|Flour]] | | |90 ounces (2500 g) |100% |- |White granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] | | |36 ounces (1000 g) |40% |- |Candied [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] peel, cut into cubes | | |1.8 ounces (50 g) |2% |- |''Erva-doce'' ([[Cookbook:Anise|anise]], ground and sifted) | | |0.9 ounce (25 g) |1% |- |[[Cookbook:Cinnamon|Cinnamon]] | | |1.8 ounces (50 g) |2% |- |Ground [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]] | | |0.9 ounce (25 g) |1% |- |[[Cookbook:Walnut|Walnuts]], cut into halves | | |18 ounces (500 g) |20% |- |Ground [[Cookbook:Almond|almond]]s | | |9 ounces (250 g) |10% |- |[[Cookbook:Orange|Oranges]], juiced and [[Cookbook:Zest|zested]] |4 [[Cookbook:Each|ea.]] | |392 g |15.68% |- |'''Total''' |'''n/a''' |'''n/a''' |'''9160 g''' |'''366%''' |} ==Procedure== #One day before making the cake, buy the bread-dough at the baker's shop, sprinkle a little bit of flour on the dough, put it in a towel and keep it in a warm place until the next day. #Dissolve the baking soda into the Madeira wine. #Warm the molasses in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], add the butter and pork fat, and stir until melted and combined. Let this mixture cool. #Sift flour into a bowl, and mix in the sugar. Make a well and put the bread dough into it. #Work the flour-sugar mixture into the bread dough. As soon as this is well-joined, start to incorporate the molasses-fat mixture little by little. #Add some of the candied lemon peel, as well as the Madeira wine, orange juice and orange zest, anise, cinnamon, and cloves. Incorporate and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] thoroughly until the dough doesn't stick to the bowl. #Cover the dough with a towel and put it in a warm spot. Keep it in a warm place for 3–4 days. #Grease the [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pans]]. This cake is traditionally made in wide, round, low pans. #Divide the dough into parts of 250–500 g or 750 g, depending on your baking pans. #Decorate the cake with half-walnuts, sliced almonds, and the rest of the candied lemon peel. #[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for about 50 minutes at 355 °F (180 °C). Let cool down before taking it out of the baking pan. ==Notes, tips, and variations== *In Madeira these honey cakes are made on 8 December, which is traditionally considered the day of Mary's Immaculate Conception, because tradition says this cake is only good for Christmas if it is made on this day. *It is a custom to make enough of this cake in order to have some during the whole year. Once cooled and thoroughly wrapped into vegetable paper it remains good until next Christmas without losing quality or taste. *Another tradition surrounding this cake is that it is not cut with knives, but by hand, and also eaten by hand, nothing more than a tradition but very respected among Madeira locals. *Fennel is often used instead of anise. Raisins are sometimes added. ==Conversion notes== {{reflist|group=note}} ==External Links== *{{cite web |url=http://www.vinhomadeira.pt/Meio-Seco-188.aspx#387/ |title=Types of Madeira Wine |language=English |accessdate=2014-12-08}} *{{cite web |url=http://receitas.eduguedes.com.br/bolo-de-mel-da-madeira/ |title=Bolo de mel da Madeira |language=Portuguese |accessdate=2014-12-08}} *{{cite web |url=http://receitasdadonaredonda.blogspot.com/search/label/Bolo%20de%20mel%20da%20Madeira |title=Bolo de mel da Madeira |language=Portuguese |accessdate=2014-12-08}} *{{cite web |url=http://www.iguaria.com/sobremesa/bolo/bolo-de-mel-da-madeira/ |title=Bolo de mel da Madeira |language=Portuguese |accessdate=2014-12-08}} [[Category:Recipes for cake|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Portuguese recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Christmas recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Recipes using molasses]] [[Category:Baking recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using walnut]] [[Category:Recipes with metric units]] [[Category:Recipes using almond]] [[Category:Recipes using butter]] [[Category:Recipes for dessert]] [[Category:Recipes using anise]] [[Category:Recipes using baking soda]] [[Category:Recipes using granulated sugar]] [[Category:Recipes using ground cinnamon]] [[Category:Recipes using orange]] [[Category:Recipes using lemon]] [[Category:Recipes using clove]] [[Category:Recipes for bread]] [[Category:Recipes using wheat flour]]

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Cake|Cake]]

'''Mandarin orange cake''' is a common low-fat cake recipe with unique variations. The cake is simple to make and does not require you to start from scratch. All the ingredients can be found at grocery stores in the United States.  

== Ingredients ==

=== Cake ===
*  1 box (15 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 430 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) yellow [[Cookbook:Cake Mix|cake mix]]
*  1 can (11 oz / 312 g) mandarin oranges
*  3 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]

=== Icing ===
*  1 box (5.1 oz / 144 g) '''instant''' vanilla pudding mix
*  1 can (20 oz / 567 g) crushed [[Cookbook:Pineapple|pineapple]]
*  1 container (12 oz / 340 g) CoolWhip or other [[Cookbook:Imitation Whipped Topping|whipped topping]]

== Procedure ==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (180°C). Grease the sides and bottom of [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake pans]] with shortening, and [[Cookbook:Dusting|dust]] with flour.
# Pour yellow cake mix into mixing bowl. Add eggs and the mandarin oranges plus their juice. Blend until moistened, then beat for approximately 2 minutes at medium speed.
# Pour batter evenly into prepared baking pans. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] approximately 30 minutes in the preheated oven or until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick]] inserted into the center comes out clean.
# Remove from oven and let the cakes cool completely.
# Scoop CoolWhip into a clean mixing bowl. Add the instant vanilla pudding mix. Drain all the pineapple juice from the can of crushed pineapples, and fold the pineapple into CoolWhip. Chill icing for about 30 minutes.
# After the cakes cool, frost each layer with your icing.

== Nutrition ==

* Each serving is approximately 275 calories with about 4–5 grams of fat.

title: Cookbook:Makizushi (Maki Roll)
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Sushi recipes
| Difficulty = 4
| Image = [[File:Makizushi2.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}

'''''Makizushi''''', also called '''rolled sushi''' or '''maki roll''', is a variety of [[Cookbook:Sushi|sushi]]. It is made by layering [[Cookbook:Nori|nori]], seasoned sushi rice, and fillings, before rolling up and slicing into individual pieces. The outer layer of the maki roll varies, having either nori or rice on the exterior—the latter is sometimes called an inside-out roll.

==Ingredients==

* Prepared [[Cookbook:Sushi/Sushi Rice|sushi rice]]
* Fillings, as desired (this may consist of either raw/smoked [[Cookbook:Salmon|salmon]], [[Cookbook:Tuna|tuna]], etc or perhaps [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]] or [[Cookbook:Avocado|avocado]])
* [[Cookbook:Nori|Nori]] sheets 
* [[Cookbook:Wasabi|Wasabi]] paste
* Water
* [[Cookbook:Sesame Seed|Sesame seeds]], if making inside-out rolls with rice on outside (optional)

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Sushi Roller|Sushi roller]] (''makisu'')
* [[Cookbook:Plastic wrap|Plastic wrap]], if making inside-out rolls

==Instructions==

#Place the roller on a cutting board. If making inside-out rolls with rice on the outside, wrap the roller in a double layer of [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]] to prevent rice from sticking to the roller.
#Place a sheet of nori shiny side-down on top of the roller.
#Dampen your hands before applying the rice. Grab the rice with one hand and put a fistful on the center of the nori. Spread the rice over the nori approximately 6 [[Cookbook:Mm|mm]] thick, leaving a 2 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] gap on the side parallel to the bamboo. As a general rule, if you can't see the nori through the rice, you have too much.
#If making an inside out roll, flip over the nori and rice quickly onto the sushi roller. The rice should now be on on the surface of the plastic wrap, with the nori facing you.
#Place the primary ingredients in a row in the middle. Slowly use the roller to push the nori against itself (rolling it away from you), using your thumbs and heels of hands for stability. Be careful when you reach the row of ingredients, making sure that it goes underneath the roll rather than just being pushed along.
#When you reach the end of the nori sheet, use the roller to compact the roll a little, making sure the rice sticking it together. When evening out a bumpy roll, don't squeeze too hard on the sides and don't flatten the roll from the top.
#To fix the ends of the roll, poke about ½ inch out from one side of mat and while gently holding it in place, press it with the heel of your hand a little.
#Remove the maki from the sushi roller, and put it on the cutting board below.
#Wet a sharp knife before slicing. Slice the rolls from the center outwards, into sections of 5, 6, or 8 (depending on the roll and your preference). Cutting from the center first ensures that all ingredients will shift towards the outside two pieces. For the rolls of 6 or 8, cut from the center, then put one roll behind the other, and cut each half in half.
#If making an inside-out roll, you may garnish the exterior rice with sesame seeds.
#Serve with soy sauce for dipping. You may also want chopsticks, pickled ginger, and wasabi if culture allows. Sashimi, miso soup, other sushi, or just general Japanese food is also often served alongside it. Green tea is considered the drink of choice to have with sushi.
== Notes and tips ==

* Dampening the hands before handling the rice will prevent clumping and the rice sticking to your hands. However, too much moisture may also make the rice less sticky, so don't go overboard.

==Variations==
Common maki rolls include:
* '''California roll:''' [[Cookbook:Avocado|avocado]], [[Cookbook:Crab|crab]] meat or imitation crab, [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]].

* '''Tuna roll:''' [[Cookbook:Tuna|Tuna]], wrapped in [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] and [[Cookbook:Nori|seaweed]]. This same combination is used to make plain rolls with any other type of fish.

* '''Spicy tuna roll:''' [[Cookbook:Tuna|Tuna]], spicy sauce (mixture of Japanese [[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayonnaise]] and [[Cookbook:Sriracha|sriracha]])

* '''Kamikaze roll:''' [[Cookbook:Tuna|Tuna]], [[Cookbook:Yellowtail|yellowtail]], spicy sauce

* '''Philadelphia roll:''' [[Cookbook:Salmon|Salmon]] (either raw or smoked), [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]]

* '''Cucumber roll:''' Sliced cucumber

* '''Egg roll:''' Sliced [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|egg yolk]].

title: Cookbook:Malvani Chicken Curry
text:
__NOTOC__{{recipesummary

}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Meat_Recipes|Meat recipes]]

'''Kombdi vade''' is a Malvani dish, which is quite popular in Maharashtra. The dish consists of the traditional Malvani [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] curry (including chicken pieces with bones), vade (also known as puri, which is a fluffy, fried bread of wheat and nachni flour), onion, lemon and solkadhi (a drink made from coconut milk).

==Ingredients==
*8 [[Cookbook:Green chilly|green chillies]], chopped
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] paste
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] paste
*800 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (1.8 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] / 8 ea.) medium-sized pieces of [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]]
*1 fresh [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]], flesh [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:chilli|chilli powder]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsps]] [[Cookbook:Garam Masala|garam masala]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsps]] Malvani Special Masala
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
*Finely-chopped [[Cookbook:Cilantro|coriander leaves]] for garnishing

==Procedure==
#Grind half of the green chillies to a paste and mix it well with the ginger and garlic pastes. 
#Make cuts on the chicken pieces, rub this mixture on to them well, and [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] for about an hour at least.
#Toast coconut shavings in a pan with a little hot oil until light brown. Cool and grind along with half the onions to a paste.
#Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the onions on medium level for about 2 minute(s) or until they are light brown in color.
#Add the remaining chopped green chillies and spice powders and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for a few seconds. Add the marinated chicken pieces and fry on medium level for about 3 minutes or until they are lightly browned.
#Add the paste and salt, then mix well. Add water according to the desired level of consistency and bring to a boil. Cover and cook on low level for about 25 minute(s) or until the chicken pieces are tender and fully cooked.
#[[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with finely-chopped coriander leaves. 

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* If it is difficult to obtain fresh coconut, it can be replaced by desiccated coconut shavings. For this recipe, there is no need to soak it in warm water. Roast it directly.

}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Beverages|Beverages]]

Traditional '''Madras filter coffee''' requires the use of specific fresh-roasted [[Cookbook:Coffee|coffee beans]] and [[Cookbook:Chicory|chicory roots]], which are not always available outside [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|India]]. This recipe uses Indian instant coffee that has chicory in it, which is available in some Indian stores and supermarkets. Nestle Bru instant coffee has 30% chicory added and in general has a near enough taste to authentic Madras filter coffee.

== Ingredients ==

* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* ½–2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] instant [[Cookbook:Coffee|coffee]] with chicory root
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* [[Cookbook:Sugar|Sugar]] (optional)

==Procedure==
# Bring the water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], and stir in the coffee. Ensure there are no lumps.
# Bring the milk to a boil.
# Add the coffee mixture to the milk, and sweeten with sugar to taste.
# While the coffee is still boiling hot, pour it into a mug or, preferably, a stainless steel tumbler. While pouring the coffee, slowly raise the saucepan so the coffee falls into the mug from a height of about 1–1½ ft. This will cause the coffee to froth like espresso.
# If desired, you can dip a teaspoon in the coffee and lightly spread a few drops of it over the froth in the mug.
# Serve piping hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Filter coffee in India is actually made in a closed steel container called a coffee filter.

title: Cookbook:Makki di Roti (Indian Cornmeal Flatbread)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Bread recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Pakistan|Cuisine of Pakistan]]

[[Cookbook:Roti|Roti]], in general, refers to an Indian [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] cooked on an iron griddle ([[Cookbook:Tava|tava]]). '''Makki di roti''' (lit. "roti made from corn") refers to a special roti where cornmeal is used instead of the usual [[Cookbook:Flour#Wheat Flour|wheat flour]]. It is a famous delicacy from the north-Indian state of Punjab, and is cooked in the winters and served with ''saron da saag'' (cooked mustard leaves) and [[Cookbook:Lassi|lassi]]. Makki roti is yellow when cooked and has less adhesive strength, which makes it difficult to handle. It is more difficult to cook than ordinary wheat roti.

==Ingredients==

*1 handful [[Cookbook:Cornmeal|cornmeal]]
*1 spoonful unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], softened
*1 cupful lukewarm [[Cookbook:Water|water]]

==Equipment==

*Flat iron [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]] ([[Cookbook:Tava|''tahva'']]), preheated
*Flat board (''chakla'')
*Wide, flat mixing tray (''praat'')
*Cooking fire on which the ''tahva'' will be heated

==Procedure==

# Heap the cornmeal in a ''praat'' (a wide flat mixing tray) so it forms a hill. Make a well, and pour in a small quantity of the lukewarm water.
# Start to mix the cornmeal and water into a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. The dough should remain moist but not become sticky. Add water in small quantities to retain a moist feel. The final dough should not be sticky (sprinkle some extra cornmeal if needed to help soak up excess moisture).
# Add the soft butter (''makhan'') at the end and give it a final [[Cookbook:Kneading|kneading]].
# Take a small hand-sized portion of the dough from the mixing tray and roll it into a small ball (''ladu'') between the two hands. Gradually start to flatten the ball between the palms of the two hands (wet the hands and fingers to help the dough to stretch). At the same time rotate the flattening dough so that the thinning of the roti is even. It may start to crack at the edges. Repair any cracks by pressing them at the rims. Wetting the fingers and the palm of the hand will help to spread and give the roti a circular shape. Aim for an evenly thinned roti.
# When the roti is about the size of a small plate (or a little larger then a spread-out hand) place it on the preheated tahva. Leave the roti to take in the heat (it takes a while for roti to get cooked). Some areas of the roti will change in colour as the water evaporates. Soon after, the roti will be able to be moved on the tahva. With a dry cloth, press the areas of the roti that look moist.
# It is a matter of judgement when the roti can be turned over and heated on the other side. When the roti have been well cooked they should not have any moist looking areas. Some areas will have burned slightly but this is normal.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* The roti can be heated on open flames of the cooker or on a ''tava''. This process of placing roti on open flames is called ''radhna''. It takes time to get the thick roti to be well cooked.
* The cooked roti is smeared with some [[Cookbook:Clarified Butter|clarified butter]] (''ghee''). This is called ''chopardna''. The roti is then put into a serving dish. Traditionally, the roti is served as it gets prepared and is eaten fresh. On occasions when it has to be stored before serving it is placed in a dry tray called ''chahba''.

title: Cookbook:Machacado con Huevo (Eggs with Shredded Beef)
text:
{{recipesummary
| Category = Mexican recipes
| Servings = 10
| Rating = 2
| Difficulty = 2
| Image = [[Image:Machacado con huevo.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Cuisine of Mexico]]

'''Machacado con huevo''' is a dish which consists of shredded dry [[cookbook:beef|beef]] that is [[Cookbook:Scrambled Eggs|scrambled]] with [[cookbook:egg|eggs]]. Its name means "shredded with eggs" in Spanish. The shredded dry beef, ''carne seca'', is said to have originated in the town of Ciénega de Flores, about an hour north of Monterrey, [[cookbook:cuisine of Mexico|Mexico]]. The early settlers in the area air-[[cookbook:curing|cured]] beef so that it would be preserved. This particular dish was made famous by Tía Lencha, a local woman who prepared it and eventually sold it in a restaurant. Today there is a commercially available Tia Lencha dried beef in most supermarkets in Mexico.

The basic machacado con huevo is made with eggs and dried beef. Chopped [[cookbook:tomato|tomato]]es, [[cookbook:onion|onion]]s and [[cookbook:jalapeño|jalapeño]]s or serrano [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chile pepper]]s can be added, or [[cookbook:Salsa|salsa]] can be cooked into it, to create another version.

Machacado con huevo often comes as a "[[cookbook:taco|taco]]" presentation.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[cookbook:butter|butter]] or [[cookbook:margarine|margarine]]
*6 large [[cookbook:egg|egg]]s, lightly beaten
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] shredded [[cookbook:beef|beef]] filling 
*10 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. 8-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] soft taco-size [[Cookbook:Flour Tortilla|flour tortilla]]s, warmed 
*1 can (16 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[Cookbook:Refried Beans|refried beans]], warmed 
*2 cups (8 ounces) shredded [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar]] or [[Cookbook:Monterey Jack Cheese|Monterey Jack Cheese]]
*[[cookbook:Salsa|Salsa]] for accompaniment

==Procedure==
#Heat butter in large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium-high heat. 
#Add eggs; cook, stirring frequently, for 2–3 minutes or until eggs just begin to set.
#Stir in shredded beef filling. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 2 to 3 minutes or until eggs are cooked and beef is heated through. 
#Serve eggs with tortillas, beans, cheese, and salsa.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Machacado con huevo can be served in a big bowl, and with some soft tortillas at hand can be prepared in your plate, can be served in the table as tacos, or can be eaten without using tortillas at all.
* Queso fundido con [[cookbook:chorizo|chorizo]] (melted cheese with chorizo) is also something that can be found at the table when eating machacado con huevo. It is usually served at the table in a pan, and added to the taco.

title: Cookbook:Malai Mixed Vegetable Curry
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Curry recipes|servings=10|time=30 minutes|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian Cuisine]]

'''Malai mixed vegetable''', is a creamy side dish for Indian bread.

==Ingredients==
* 3 green [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|capsicums]] (bell peppers)
* 1 each orange, yellow, and red capsicum
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Paneer|paneer]] cubes
* [[Cookbook:Cashew|Cashew nuts]]
* 4 large [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Pea|peas]]
* 3–4 [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|green chillies]] (depending on spice requirement), finely chopped
* Dried [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] and [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Garam Masala|Garam masala]]
* [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|Red chilli powder]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Turmeric|Turmeric]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] [[Cookbook:Cream|whipping cream]]
* 1 Tbsp [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]]
* [[Cookbook:Cilantro|Cilantro]] for garnishing

==Procedure==

# Cut the bell peppers into ½-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] pieces.
# [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] paneer until golden brown; set aside.
# Soak a handful of cashew nuts in warm water.
# Grind the tomatoes and the soaked cashew into a fine paste. Keep this paste aside.
# Sauté the chopped vegetables, green chillies, and dried parsley in the butter/oil until they are cooked. You could also microwave the vegetables for ~10 minutes without water, and then sauté them in butter for a minute.
# Add the tomato paste to the vegetables and cook for 5 minutes.
# Add the garam masala, red chilli powder, salt, and turmeric according to taste; [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 2 minutes.
# Add the whipping cream and the sour cream, and let it cook until the cream thickens.
# Add the paneer and mix well.
# [[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with cilantro and cashew nuts.
# Serve hot with [[Cookbook:Naan|naan]] or [[Cookbook:Roti|roti]].

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* You could choose other vegetables like [[Cookbook:Zucchini|zucchini]] or [[Cookbook:Broccoli|broccoli]] if you like.

title: Cookbook:Magic Brownies
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
| category = Recipes for dessert|
| yield = 9 brownies
| time = 3–4 hours
| difficulty = 3
}}
{{recipe|Brownies, Magic}}

A '''magic brownie''' is a brownie that has been infused with cannabis. Eating the brownie results in a cannabis high one to a few hours after consumption—as a result, care should be taken not to eat too many of them to avoid adverse effects<ref>https://dhss.alaska.gov/dph/director/pages/marijuana/edibles.aspx</ref><ref>https://patriotcare.org/use-medical-marijuana-edibles/</ref><ref>https://www.phidenverhealth.org/community-health-promotion/substance-misuse/marijuana-edible-facts</ref>.

{{warning|'''Warning:''' The possession and use of cannabis is forbidden in many countries. '''Please read the wikibooks [[Wikibooks:Risk disclaimer|risk disclaimer]] before attempting to follow this recipe.'''}}
== Ingredients ==
* {{convert|4|g|oz|abbr=on}} [[Cookbook:Cannabis|cannabis]], ground
* 60 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (½ stick/2.1 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] 
* 300 g (3½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]/11 oz) [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]] chips
* 180 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (¾ cup/160 g/5.6 oz) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] 
* 2 standard [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] 
* 5 ml (1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]]) [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] 
* Grated [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] [[Cookbook:Zest|zest]]
* 250 g (1¾ cups/8.8 oz) self-raising [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] 

== Procedure ==

# Melt the butter in a small [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and stir in the cannabis. Cook slowly over a low temperature for 2–3 hours. Do not allow to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] or exceed 200 °F (93°C).
# If desired, [[Cookbook:Straining|strain]] the butter to remove the cannabis solids.
# Melt the chocolate chips in the [[Cookbook:Microwave|microwave]] or over a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double boiler]]. Combine the melted chocolate and infused butter, stirring until smooth.
# Stir in the sugar, and allow the mixture to cool if needed.
# Stir in the eggs, vanilla, salt, and lemon zest until smooth.
# [[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] in the flour just until combined.
# Transfer the batter to a greased and/or [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment]]-lined [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|pan]]. 
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 360°F/180°C for about 20–25 minutes or until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick]] inserted in the center comes out without any batter on it.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Try using brown cane sugar instead of white sugar.
* Melt some chocolate and mix with a little sugar, vanilla, lemon, and a little more weed. Drizzle on the freshly cooked brownies for a little added flavour and high. This creates a nicer tasting brownie with more of a kick.
* Try adding a few crushed up biscuits before baking for a more varied taste.

text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Vegetable recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Madbucha''' or '''matbucha''' is a North African dish of stewed tomatoes and peppers. It can be used as a side dish with meats, as well as put on bread or white rice. There's more than one way to make it, and the following recipe is a family recipe. 

==Ingredients==
*[[Cookbook:Oil and fat|Oil]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]s, [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*2 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], chopped
*15 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]]
*10 [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]], cut into small pieces
*5 [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]], chopped small
*330 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] canned [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
*[[Cookbook:Cumin|Cumin]]
*[[Cookbook:Parsley|Parsley]]
*[[Cookbook:Oregano|Oregano]]

==Procedure==
#Take a pot that is big enough for all of the above ingredients, cover the bottom with oil, and put it on a flame.
#When the oil gets hot, add the onion and garlic. 
#When they start to fry, add the rest of the vegetables and salt.
#Mix it up a bit and cover the pot.
#Leave it to cook, mixing it every so often, until the level of the liquid is higher than the level of the vegetables.
#Drain off most (but not all) the liquid.
#Add the tomato paste and the spices.
#Mix, and let it cool.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* When chopping the peppers, you want them small but not so small that they disappear when cooked.
* The peppers can be any color, but red is traditional.

title: Cookbook:Ma'amoul (Arabian Filled Pastries)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Recipes for pastries
| Difficulty = 3
}}__NOTOC__
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Middle Eastern cuisines|Middle Eastern cuisine]]

'''Ma'amoul''' are [[Cookbook:Pastry|pastries]] filled with dates or nuts, and they are popular throughout the Arab world. They can be made in special ma'amoul moulds, and there are three shapes of mould. The flattish circular shape is used for date ma’amoul; the round domed shape for walnut ma’amoul; the long oval for pistachio ma’amoul. Some families do not use moulds, but have special crimping tweezers for making patterns on the top of the pastry. Alternatively, a fork may be used.

The Sephardi Jews of the Eastern Mediterranean refer to date ma'amoul as ''menenas''. These are often made in the form of date rolls rather than balls.

==Ingredients==

=== Pistachio filling ===
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) finely-[[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Pistachio|pistachios]]
* ¼ lb [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Rosewater|rose water]]

=== Walnut filling ===
* ½ lb (250 g) finely-chopped [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]]
* ¼ lb sugar
* 1 tbsp ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]

=== Date filling ===
* 1 lb (500 g) pitted [[Cookbook:Date|dates]], chopped
* ½ teacup [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* [[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]] (optional)

=== Pastries ===
* 1 lb (500 g) [[Cookbook:Flour|plain white flour]] (up to a quarter of the flour may be replaced with fine [[Cookbook:Semolina|semolina]])
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Sugar|white sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|Baking powder]] (optional)
* ½ lb (250 g) unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] (Normandy butter is best)
* 1–2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Rosewater|rose water]] or [[Cookbook:Orange#Oranges in Cooking|orange flower water]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Water|water]] or [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|Icing sugar]]

==Special equipment==

* Wooden ma'amoul moulds, oiled and dusted with flour

==Procedure==

=== Fillings ===
# Mix chopped [[Cookbook:Pistachio|pistachios]] with sugar and rose water.
# Mix chopped [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]] with sugar and [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]].
# Combine the chopped dates and water in a pot. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], squashing the mixture against the side of the pan with a wooden spoon until approximately uniform in consistency. Mix in the butter if using. Blend with an [[Cookbook:Food Processor|electric chopper]] if desired to make a smoother paste. Allow to cool.

=== Pastries ===
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] the flour into a mixing bowl. Mix with the white sugar, and a pinch of salt if desired. Some people add a very small quantity of baking powder.
# Work in the butter until the consistency is as uniform as possible; one way is to heat the butter in the microwave first until it is nearly melted, and then mix it with the flour into a sort of crumble. Cover and leave at room temperature for several hours to overnight.
# Break up the dough with your fingers, and add the rose water or orange flower water and 2 tbsp water or milk until it is malleable. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] the whole into a smooth ball.
# Take a walnut-sized ball of the dough, stick your thumb into it, and hollow out into a cup shape so that the walls are as thin as possible without breaking.
# Insert filling to about three-quarters full, and pinch the aperture closed. Pat gently into a ball, not letting the walls break.
# Decorate the ball on top with tweezers or the prongs of a fork. Alternatively, pat it into a wooden mould and flatten the exposed bottom surface, then bang the mould face down on the work surface to extract the moulded pastry.
# Repeat the assembly steps until all the dough and the filling is used. If at any stage the remaining dough shows signs of drying out, knead in a little more water or milk.
# Place the pastries on an ungreased [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] in a preheated [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] (180°C / 355°F; 160°C if a fan oven) for 20 minutes: they must not be allowed to become hard or brown. In fact they should look a little moist and underdone when removed from the oven: they will steam off and harden as they cool.
# Leave the pastries to cool, and [[Cookbook:Dusting|dust]] with icing sugar when cold. Keep in a sealed plastic box or biscuit tin.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Some people use ground [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]], with or without green food colouring, instead of pistachios for the filling.
* A variant served on very special occasions is known as ''karabij''. Make nut ma’amoul, using water rather than milk and no flower water, in the form of balls rather than in a mould, leaving them smooth without making any indentations. Arrange in a pyramid and serve with a special cream called ''naatiffe''. This is made by boiling water, lemon juice, sugar, orange flower water and soapwort root (''Saponaria officinalis'') into a syrup, and folding in stiffly beaten egg whites. Some books mention ''bois de Panama'' instead of soapwort, but apparently this is a fallacy<ref>http://www.anissas.com/natef-a-miraculous-transformation/</ref>.

title: Cookbook:Mango and Coconut Chutney (Am ki Chatni)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Chutney recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian cuisine]]

== Ingredients ==
* 2 almost-ripe [[Cookbook:Mango|mangoes]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] fresh or canned [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]] or [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]], chopped
* 1 Tbsp fresh ginger, scraped and finely chopped
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|cayenne pepper]]
* 2–3 Tbsp fresh [[Cookbook:Orange|orange juice]], or a mixture of orange and [[Cookbook:Lime |lime juice]]

== Preparation ==
# Place the mango on one side on a work surface and make a slit in the tip across its width with a sharp knife. Then hold the mango upright on its stem end, on the work surface, and carefully slice the flesh, with the skin attached, off one side of the stone, as close to it as possible. Then turn it the other way and cut off the flesh from the other side of the stone.
# Place each mango half, skin-side down, on the work surface, and cut lines through the flesh down to the skin in a lattice pattern so that you end up with a checker-board pattern with ½-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] squares.
# Grasp the mango half with both your hands, skin down and your two thumbs on the flesh and your four fingers of each hand underneath on the skin. Now, turn the skin inside out by pushing the skin inwards with your four fingers of each hand while pushing the two sides downward with your two thumbs. You will now have the skin of the mango with cubes of flesh attached which can be easily cut off with a sharp knife.
# Place the mango cubes in a small bowl.
# Add the coconut, cilantro, ginger, cayenne, orange/lime juice, and salt and mix gently with a tablespoon.
# Leave to [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] in the refrigerator for 1–2 hours before serving.

'''Macaroni pie''' is a side dish that goes well with stewed [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], callaloo or any stewed peas like pigeon peas or lentils. It can also be enjoyed on its own.

It has versions derived from Caribbean, Early American and Scottish origins.

==Ingredients==
*1 package (225 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]] / 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) dried [[Cookbook:Macaroni|macaroni]] pasta
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]s
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]
*1½ [[Cookbook:cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Condensed milk|evaporated milk]]

*1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], grated
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Pepper|white pepper]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] prepared yellow [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]
*1 pat of unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] macaroni in salted water until tender; drain.
#[[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] eggs until fluffy.

#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 175°C (350°F) until firm (about 30 minutes). A fork or metal [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] should come out dry when you press it all the way through the pie.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

title: Cookbook:Maltese Rabbit Stew (Stuffat tal-Fenek)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| servings = 4–6
| time = Prep: 1 hour</br>Cooking: 4 hours
}}

{{recipe}}
== Ingredients ==
* 1 large (about 2 [[Cookbook:kg|kg]]) whole [[Cookbook:rabbit|rabbit]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Sunflower Oil|sunflower oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:clove|clove]] [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]]
* 300 [[Cookbook:g|g]] white [[Cookbook:potatoes|potatoes]], peeled
* 1 small [[Cookbook:carrot|carrot]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 800 [[Cookbook:g|g]] canned [[Cookbook:Tomato|crushed tomatoes]] or canned '[[Cookbook:Pelati|Pelati]]'
* 200 [[Cookbook:ML|ml]] [[Cookbook:Red Wine|red wine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:bay leaf|Mediterranean bay leaves]]
* [[Cookbook:Tabasco Sauce|Tabasco]] sauce
* Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:pepper|black pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:salt|Salt]] to taste
* 100 [[Cookbook:g|g]] canned [[Cookbook:pea|peas]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Mixed Spice|mixed spice]]

== Procedure ==
#Cut up the rabbit at the joints. Cut the rib section into 3–4 pieces, and divide the legs at all the joints. Split the head of the rabbit in half. The whole animal should be cut into about 10–12 pieces so they are large and chunky, but small enough that they can be easily manipulated with large [[Cookbook:Utensil|spoon]]. Remove and keep internal organs apart.
#[[Cookbook:Mince|Mince]] the garlic. Heat the oil in a large [[Cookbook:frying pan|frying pan]]. Heat some of the garlic in the oil. Add some rabbit pieces and cook through.
#Remove cooked meat from the pan and place in a large container. Cook the rest of the meat in the same way in batches, adding some garlic with every batch. The meat should be well cooked but not very brown.
#Fry the internal organs whole in the same oil until well-cooked. Take some of the smaller pieces of meat without bone and add them to the organs. Keep these apart from the main meat.
#Cut the potatoes into large irregular chunks, slightly smaller than the pieces of meat.
#In a [[Cookbook:Stock pot|stock pot]], place the fried rabbit, the potatoes, the chopped carrot, the tomato pulp, wine, sugar and laurel leaves. Add salt, pepper, mixed spice and Tabasco carefully. Cover and [[Cookbook:simmer|simmer]] on a low flame for 4 hours. Stir occasionally during the first hour.
#Once done, add the peas, and cook until tender (about 10 minutes).

== Serving ==
A typical Maltese rabbit stew is served in a few different ways depending on the situation, family tradition and locality. One way is to simply serve a plate of stew with Maltese bread for dipping in the sauce. Sometimes the internal organs and some small bits of boneless meat are served without any garnish on a small plate with salt, pepper, and fresh sour-dough bread as a special treat for children as they wait for this time-consuming dish to be prepared. A full ''fenkata'', a Maltese word meaning 'rabbit-based dinner party' could be as follows:
# Start with Maltese galletti, Gbejniet, Zalzett, bigilla, and the internal organs of the rabbit as [[Cookbook:entrée|entrées]].
# For second plate serve [[Cookbook:Spaghetti|Spaghetti]] (typically slightly overcooked in Maltese cuisine) with a covering of sauce from the stew.
# Serve the rabbit meat and potatoes (with little sauce) as main course, always accompanied by bread, and a strong red wine.
# Serve Maltese style [[Cookbook:Trifle|Trifle]] or Traditional Maltese Ice Cream (also called Gelat tan-Nanna) for [[Cookbook:dessert|dessert]].
# Round off with [[Cookbook:peanut|peanuts]] in the shell and [[Bartending/Alcohol/Anise_liqueur#Anisette|Anisette]].

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* The best stew is slow cooked on the lowest flame for as long as possible. Using a higher flame you can reduce cooking time to 2 hours, but this is not a dish that should be rushed. If you have the time you can even cook it for 6 hours on a camping-type flame for an even richer taste.

title: Cookbook:Malawach (Flaky Flatbread)
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Flatbread recipes|servings=12|time=4–5 minutes|difficulty=3|image=[[File:Malawach.jpg|300px|Malawach]]}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Malawach''' is a layered, flaky [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] that is popularly eaten in Israel, and now made popular in other regions. It is typically brushed with oil or fat and cooked flat in a frying pan.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] white [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose wheat flour]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white granulated [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] dried [[cookbook:yeast|yeast]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[cookbook:salt|salt]]
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] lukewarm water (or such as is sufficient for kneading dough)
* [[cookbook:vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]] (sufficient for lining skillet)
* 200 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] melted [[cookbook:butter|butter]] or [[cookbook:margarine|margarine]]

== Procedure ==
# Mix together the flour, sugar, yeast, salt, and water, starting with only 2 cups of water. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] the dough well, adding additional water if necessary to make it soft and pliable.
# Cover and let dough rest until it doubles in size.
# Take up dough and begin to knead it by hand. Divide dough into 12 smaller portions and place upon oiled surface. Let dough rest until each portion rises and doubles in size, occasionally oiling the surface of dough.
# Grease a work surface with oil. Roll out each piece of dough with a [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]] to get very large, almost paper-thin, rounds of dough.
# [[Cookbook:Brushing|Brush]] each round liberally with melted butter. Fold the dough in half, from the top towards the bottom. Then, roll it up from the top towards the bottom as one would roll-up a sleeping bag, forming a rope. Coil the rope around itself into a spiral.
# Cover and allow the dough to rest until it rises and doubles in size.
# Roll each spiral out again into a thin round. Brush again with butter, then repeat the rolling and coiling process.
# Allow the dough to rest once more while covered until it rises.
# Heat a [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] with a little vegetable oil.
# Use your hands to flatten out the dough coils on a greased surface.
# Place flattened dough portions in skillet and cover with lid. [[Cookbook:Frying#Pan-frying|Fry]] the dough on a medium to low heat until the bottom turns an amber color. Flip over and fry on reverse side without the lid.
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Malawach is often served with a [[Cookbook:Hard Boiled Eggs|hard-boiled egg]], along with tomato [[cookbook:salsa|salsa]] that has been flavored with freshly-[[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[cookbook:coriander|coriander]].

Algerians are very fond of '''m'semen''', a [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] made from basic ingredients like flour, semolina, butter, and water. Some people also fill the pancakes with minced meat and vegetables before frying in oil until they become crisp and golden.

# On a lightly-floured surface, [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] the dough for 10 minutes or until it is smooth.
# Divide the dough into smaller pieces, and [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll]] each out into very thin rounds.
# [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] each dough round with oil.
# Fold the rounds into square envelope shapes, making 4 folds into the center.
# Cook each flatbread in a hot, lightly-greased [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] until browned.

== Ingredients ==

# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] together the [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] and baking powder in a bowl.
# Mix in the salt, lemon zest, sugar, and cloves.
# Rub in the [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] until the flour becomes coarse.
# Combine the vanilla and [[Cookbook:Water|water]], then mix this into the flour mixture to get a firm [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].

title: Cookbook:Mahshi (Egyptian Stuffed Vegetables)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Egyptian recipes
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[File:Mahshi.jpg|300px]]
}}{{Recipe}}

'''Mahshi''' is a delicious Egyptian dish that involves stuffing various vegetables with a flavorful mixture of rice, herbs, and spices. It is a versatile and satisfying dish that can be customized to individual tastes. Mahshi is typically served as a main course and is enjoyed by families and friends during festive occasions or gatherings.

== Ingredients ==
* Assorted vegetables for stuffing, such as [[Cookbook:zucchini|zucchini]], [[Cookbook:eggplant|eggplant]], [[Cookbook:bell pepper|bell pepper]], and [[Cookbook:tomato|tomato]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] medium-grain [[Cookbook:rice|rice]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:tomato|tomato paste]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:olive oil|olive oil]]
* ¼ cup fresh [[Cookbook:parsley|parsley]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* ¼ cup fresh [[Cookbook:mint|mint leaves]], finely chopped
* 2 cloves [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:cumin|cumin]]
* 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:coriander|coriander]]
* [[Cookbook:salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:black pepper|Black pepper]] to taste
* Water, as needed

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]] for cutting and hollowing out vegetables
* Spoon for scooping out vegetable seeds and flesh
* Mixing bowl
* [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|Baking dish]] or casserole dish
* [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|Aluminum foil]]
* [[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]]

== Procedure ==
# Prepare the vegetables for stuffing by carefully cutting off the tops and scooping out the seeds and flesh, creating hollow shells. Set aside the scooped-out vegetable flesh for later use.
# In a mixing bowl, combine the medium-grain rice, tomato paste, olive oil, finely chopped parsley, finely chopped mint leaves, minced garlic, ground cumin, ground coriander, salt, and black pepper. Mix well until all the ingredients are thoroughly combined.
# Fill each hollowed vegetable with the rice and herb mixture, packing it firmly and leaving some space at the top for the rice to expand while cooking.
# Arrange the stuffed vegetables in a baking dish or casserole dish, placing them closely together to support each other.
# Use the reserved vegetable flesh to fill any empty spaces between the stuffed vegetables. This helps to prevent them from shifting during cooking.
# Pour enough water into the baking dish to partially cover the stuffed vegetables. This will help create a moist cooking environment.
# Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil, ensuring it is tightly sealed to retain moisture.
# Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] the mahshi for about 60–75 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender and the rice filling is cooked through.
# Remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 10–15 minutes to allow the tops of the stuffed vegetables to slightly brown.
# Once cooked, remove the mahshi from the oven and let it cool slightly before serving.
