title: Cookbook:Raspberry Filled Pastry Strips (Alexandertorte)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Recipes for dessert
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Pastry|Pastry]] | [[Cookbook:European cuisines|Europe]]

'''Alexandertorte''' or '''Aleksander torte''' is a layered pastry filled with fruit preserves.

==Ingredients==

* ½ [[Cookbook:Lb|lb]] (225 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|unsalted butter]], chilled and cut into small pieces
* 3½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (840 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tbsp|tbsp]] (45 ml) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
* 1½ cups (360 ml / 12 [[Cookbook:Oz|oz]]) raspberry [[Cookbook:Jams and Jellies|preserves]]
* 2 tbsp (30 ml) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], softened
* 2 cups (480 ml) [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|confectioner's sugar]]
* ¼ cup (120 ml) [[Cookbook:Water|cold water]]
* 2 tsp (10 ml) [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]

==Procedure==

# In a large [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]], combine the chilled butter, 3 cups of the flour, and the sugar. With your fingertips, rub until the mixture resembles flakes of coarse meal. [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] in the egg and continue to mix until the pastry is smooth. Shape it into a ball, wrap it in wax paper, and refrigerate 1 hour, or until the dough is firm.
# With the back of a spoon, rub the preserves through a fine [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]] set over a 1-quart [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], then cook over moderate heat, stirring constantly, for 3–5 minutes, or until they thicken into a thin purée. Set aside off the heat.
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 250°F (120°C). 
# Cut the chilled pastry in half and shape each half into a rectangle. One half at a time, roll the pastry between two sheets of lightly floured wax paper into a rectangle approximately 10 inches wide and 15 inches long. 
# With a pastry [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]], coat each of 2 [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|cookie sheets]] with 1 tablespoon of butter and sprinkle them with flour, tipping the sheets from side to side to coat them evenly. Then invert the sheets and tap them against a hard surface to dislodge any excess flour. 
# Peel off the top sheets of wax paper and use the bottom ones to lift the 2 rectangles of pastry onto the 2 cookie sheets. Peel off the remaining sheets of wax paper. 
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] 40 minutes, or until the pastry begins to turn a pale gold. Watch carefully for any sign of burning and regulate the heat accordingly. Let cool.
# With a metal [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]], spread the raspberry purée evenly over one sheet of the pastry, covering it completely and smoothly. Slide the second sheet of pastry gently onto the first. 
# With a spoon, stir the confectioner's sugar, water and lemon juice together in a large mixing bowl to form a thin [[Cookbook:Icing|icing]]. Spread the icing over the top layer of pastry with the spatula, and set the cake aside to cool to room temperature. 
# With a small, sharp knife or pastry wheel, slice the Aleksander Torte into strips 1 inch wide and 2 inches long, cutting the ends on the diagonal.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Radish_Pie|Radish Pie]]

'''Radish pie''' is a savory [[Cookbook:Pie|pie]] suitable for a vegetarian diet.  Radishes, fresh goat cheese, and walnuts give the pie a unique taste, which is most flavorful when served cold.

==Ingredients==
*1–2 bunches red [[Cookbook:Radish|radish]]es
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (60 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], divided
*8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (227 g) [[Cookbook:Phyllo Dough|phyllo]] dough
*1 red [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] dry [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]] wine
*2 large [[Cookbook:egg|egg]]s
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|yolk]]
*¾ cup (177 ml) heavy [[Cookbook:cream|cream]]
*4 oz (113 g) fresh goat [[Cookbook:cheese|cheese]] 
*¾ cup (177 ml) broken [[Cookbook:walnuts|walnut]] pieces
*⅓ cup (80 ml) fresh Italian [[Cookbook:parsley|parsley]]

==Procedure==
[[File:RadishPieSlice250px.jpg|thumb|250x250px|Slice of radish pie]]
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (175°C).
#Wash the radishes well, remove and discard tops. Put radishes into a small [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]] and drizzle with olive oil. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for about an hour. Let them cool and then cut into small cubes.
#Use half the butter to grease a [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie pan]], and then line it with pieces of [[wikipedia:Phyllo|phyllo dough]], covering the pan evenly. Tuck any stray bits under to make a nice edge.
#Heat the remaining butter in a large pan and sauté the onion in it for about 5 minutes. Add the wine and diced radishes, then cook for another minute. Remove from heat and pour into the pastry shell.
#In a bowl, mix together the eggs and cream, and then pour over the vegetables in the pie crust. Crumble the goat cheese over the cream.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the pie in a preheated oven at aforementioned temperature for 20 minutes.
#Add the walnuts and bake for another 15–20 minutes.
#Remove the pie from the oven and top it with the chopped parsley.
#Let cool completely before serving.
==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Use fewer radishes for milder taste, or add more according to your own taste.
*The radishes can be baked the day before and then refrigerated until you make the pie.
*For a professional look, garnish each serving with a sprig of parsley.

'''Radish tart''' is a tasty and colorful [[Cookbook:Pie|pie]], best served hot from the oven. Fresh red radishes and yellow cheese give this pretty pie an interesting look and taste.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*½ cup cold [[Cookbook:butter|butter]]
*1 cup (4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) shredded Edam, Gouda, or Gruyere [[Cookbook:cheese|cheese]], divided ([[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|Cheddar]] is also acceptable)
*1 cup heavy [[Cookbook:cream|cream]], divided
*4 [[Cookbook:egg|egg]] yolks
*¼ tsp [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
*½–1 small bunch of red [[Cookbook:radish|radishes]]

==Procedure==
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 425°F (220°C).
#[[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] and measure flour into a bowl. Cut in the butter until the particles are coarse. Stir in half of the cheese. Pour in ¼ cup of the cream; [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|toss]] the mixture with a fork until all parts are moistened.
#Turn the dough into a 9-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] round [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie pan]]. With floured fingers, press the mixture into the bottom and sides of the pan, then prick the shell with a floured fork.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the pie shell for 10–12 minutes. The sides will slip down a little during baking. Cool on a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|wire rack]].
#Lower the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C).
#Sprinkle the remaining cheese evenly over the bottom of the cooled pie shell. [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] together the egg yolks, the ¾ cup cream, and the salt. Pour the egg mixture over the cheese. Place the radish slices evenly over the top of the pie.
#Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until set.
#Remove the pie from the oven, cut it into wedges, and serve it hot. 

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*If you really like the taste of radishes, use ½ cup or more. For a milder pie, use ¼ cup.
*The cheese crust has a pleasant crisp texture when eaten fresh out of the oven. Leftovers can be refrigerated and reheated later, but the texture will not be as good.
*A really sharp knife will aid in cutting the wedges without displacing the radishes.

title: Cookbook:Red Bean Paste
text:
__NOTOC__ {{recipesummary|category=Bean recipes|yield=500 ml|time=Soaking: 4 hours+
Boiling: 1½–2 hours
Making: 15 minutes|difficulty=3|image=[[File:Ogura Toast (Toast with Sweet Red Bean Paste) (6639292463).jpg|300px]] }} {{Recipe}}| [[:Category:Vegetable recipes|Vegetables]] | [[:Category:Bean recipes|Beans]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of China|Chinese Cuisine]] '''Red bean paste''' (in simplified Chinese: '''红豆沙''', in traditional Chinese: '''紅豆沙''', Pinyin: '''hóngdòushā''', meaning "red bean sand", due to its texture) is a sweet paste used for many things in Chinese, Japanese and Korean cuisine. It is made from mashed [[Cookbook:Azuki Bean|adzuki beans]] (known as red beans in Chinese), mixed with sugar. A range of texture from coarse and gritty to fine and smooth is possible. For a coarse paste, boil the beans for less time and mash by hand. For a fine paste, boil for longer and use a blender to mash the beans. ==Ingredients== *200 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] dried [[Cookbook:Azuki Bean|adzuki beans]] *Water as needed for soaking and boiling *150 ml [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] *75 ml [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable]] or [[Cookbook:Peanut Oil|peanut oil]] for frying ==Procedure== # Wash the beans, checking for and removing any that are damaged or diseased. Soak the beans in cold water for at least 4 hours or, preferably, overnight. This softens the beans slightly and reduces the cooking time greatly. # Drain the beans and rinse once soaked. # Place into a small [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] and cover with water. Bring to the [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. # Simmer the beans for 1½–2 hours, until soft and disintegrating slightly. Longer boiling will result in a smoother paste. Remember to top up the water occasionally so the beans don't boil dry and burn. # Drain away the water. # Depending on the desired texture, [[Cookbook:Mashing|mash]] the beans by hand (coarse) or in a blender (fine) until they are as you want. Note that the paste is very thick, so if using a blender, it is easier to do it a bit at a time. # Stir in the sugar. You should now have a thick but damp paste. # Preheat the oil in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] or wok, and fry the bean paste, using a spatula or spoon to stir, until the water has been driven off. The bean paste will now be quite dry, with a slightly grainy texture. # Cool, and store in an airtight container until needed. This paste will keep for at least a week in the fridge. ==Use== Red bean paste is used in many recipes: *As a filling for [[Cookbook:Baozi|baozi]] *As a filling for [[Cookbook:Daifuku|daifuku]] *As a filling for mooncakes *As an ingredient in red bean soup *As a filling for tangyuan, boiled glutinous rice balls *For zongzi, made of steamed or boiled rice and red bean paste *Spread on toast, much like peanut butter or jam == Notes, tips, and variations == * 75 ml sounds like a lot of oil, but it is required to drive out the water properly. title: Cookbook:Quorn Pitta
text:
__NOTOC__{{recipesummary|category=Sandwich recipes|servings=1|time=10 minutes|difficulty=1 | Image = [[Image:Quornpitta.JPG|300px]] }}{{recipe}} Dubbed the "VDP QE Quornpitta", this pitta is prepared with Quorn and is suitable for vegetarians. The contributing author noted the following anecdote:
''I first came up to the idea of the pitta as I found that chopped-up Quorn pieces available from supermarkets taste (after microwaving without additives) quite bad. After adding ketchup, it tasted way better, so I started thinking and experimenting and finally came up with blending tomato paste, vinegar, garlic and some red peppers (similar to a regular taco-mix). This sauce I made is however not made with sugar and not greasy (unlike ketchup). I added the whole in a pitta, as this is widely available (you may use other oven-baked breads too). As certain nutritionist organisations have their own version of pitta too to include in their diets, and as the ingredients used here are even better in quality.''
==Ingredients== [[Image:Quornpitta_requirements.jpg|thumb|310x310px|VDP QE Quorn pitta required materials]] === Sauce === * 1–1½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Red pepper flakes|red pepper flakes]] * 1 can (240 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]] (double concentrate) * 2 [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallots]] or 1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] * ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]] * 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] white [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] * 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (or to taste) * ½ teaspoon dried [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]] or several stalks of fresh oregano (or to taste) * 1 teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]] (or to taste) * 1 teaspoon of ground [[Cookbook:Black Cardamom|black cardamom]] === Assembly === * [[Cookbook:Pita|Pita bread]] * Quorn ==Procedure== #Combine the ingredients for the sauce, and make sure it's completely smooth. #[[Cookbook:Microwaving|Microwave]] the sauce for 2 minutes. Stir the sauce, make sure its not dried out (add some vinegar if too dry), and microwave for 2 minutes more. The sauce can be then set aside. #Microwave the Quorn for 1–2 minutes. Combine sauce and Quorn, and make sure it's smooth—that the whole should look like a paste rather than meat. Microwave again for 2 minutes. #Prepare the pitta as indicated or use as is. Put the Quorn mixture inside the pitta. #Serve. text:

__NOTOC__
{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Pasta|Pasta]]
==Ingredients==

=== Base ===
* 12 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (340 [[Cookbook:gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Pasta fresca all'uovo|pasta dough]] or 1 package of wonton wrappers
* Filling of choice (see below)

=== Fillings ===

* [[Cookbook:Ravioli/Cheese Filling|Cheese Filling]]
* [[Cookbook:Ravioli/Crab Meat Filling|Crab Meat Filling]]
* [[Cookbook:Ravioli/Fresh Herb and Cheese Filling|Fresh Herb and Cheese filling]]
* [[Cookbook:Ravioli/Meat Filling|Meat Filling]]
* [[Cookbook:Ravioli/Potato and Garlic Filling|Potato and Garlic Filling]]
* [[Cookbook:Ravioli/Smoked Salmon Filling|Smoked Salmon Filling]]
* [[Cookbook:Ravioli/Spinach and Ricotta Filling|Spinach and Ricotta Filling]]

==Procedure==

===Assembly===
[[Image:Ravioli-casalinghi-con-la-ricotta-2.jpg|thumb|Half-moon ravioli|308x308px]]

==== Method I ====
# Divide the pasta dough into 4 equal pieces.
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] one of these portions until it is about a 1/16-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (1.5 [[Cookbook:Mm|mm]]) thick rectangle.
# Roll out another the same size. Cover with a damp tea towel.
# Place about 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoonful]] of filling about every 2 inches (5 cm) across and down the rectangle of dough in a checker-board pattern.
# With a wet [[Cookbook:Brush|pastry brush]] or your index finger, paint lines down between the mounds of filling in a checker-board pattern.
#Carefully place the other sheet of pasta on top of the other one and press down around the mounds of filling firmly.
# With a sharp knife, pizza wheel or pastry cutter, cut the ravioli into individual squares.
# Crimp the edges with a fork. Besides being decorative, this ensures that they are well sealed.
# Process the other two portions of dough in the same way.

==== Method II ====
# Cut 3-inch (7.5 cm) diameter circles with a biscuit cutter, OR take one wonton wrapper.
# Place 1 tbsp of filling in the centre of a pasta circle or wonton wrapper, wet the edges, and cover with another circle. Alternatively, use half the amount of filling.
# Fold over one edge of the circle (or wonton wrapper) to the other edge to form a semi-circular shaped raviolo.
# Crimp the edges

===Cooking===
# Gently drop the ravioli into 1½–2 gallons (~8 liters) of gently [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] salted water. If boiling is too vigorous, the ravioli may break open.
# Stir gently with a heat-proof [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]] to prevent sticking. Contrary to the dictates of purists, you may add a little olive oil to the water if you wish.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] the ravioli for about 8 minutes or until tender but not soft.
# Off the heat, remove the ravioli gently with a [[Cookbook:Slotted Spoon|slotted spoon]] or a [[Cookbook:Spider|spider]].
# Drain in a [[Cookbook:Colander|colander]].
# Serve with tomato sauce, or with melted butter and Parmesan cheese.

title: Cookbook:Racuszki (Polish Pancakes)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Polish recipes|servings=3|time=15 minutes|difficulty=2|}}
{{recipe}}

'''Racuszki''' are [[Cookbook:Pancake|pancakes]] made from [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]] fried on a hot griddle or a pan. They are a traditional Polish dish, but they exist in several variations in many different local [[Cookbook:Cuisine|cuisine]]s, such as Danish [http://xphiles.typepad.com/table/2006/04/easter_ebleskiv.html|Ebleskivers]. Usually the form varies from small pancakes or something akin to donuts, and the filling can change as well (e.g. apple and cinnamon, raisins, etc.).

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] sour milk or cultured [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*1½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Eggs|eggs]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Kg|kg]] [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]] (optional), [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#In large bowl, [[Cookbook:Mix|mix]] the baking soda, salt, and flour together well.
#Add sour milk and eggs, and [[Cookbook:Mix|mix]] until smooth.
#Pour small ladlefuls of the mixture into a [[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] pan, one at a time OR dip slices of peeled apples in batter and put them in the pan.
#Cook until the edges are dry. Turn; cook until golden.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Serve with sugar, butter, maple syrup, melted chocolate, or jam. Sugar is traditional, and some people eat them without toppings.
* Racuszki do not store well.
* Use [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]] or cultured [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]] if you do not have sour milk, but do not replace it with normal milk.
* Cooking apples are preferred, if using.

text:
{{Recipe summary

| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Radish stew''' dates back to at least the 4th century when a recipe appeared in the Roman cookery book Cnecht. It is a simple and inexpensive dish, and is said to calm an upset stomach.

==Ingredients==
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] [[Cookbook:Radish|red radish]], cut in 1-inch strips, or about 5–6 [[Cookbook:Slicing|slices]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], cut in 1-inch chunks
* 4–6 [[Cookbook:green onion|green onion]]s, [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:flour|flour]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] dried leaf [[Cookbook:thyme|thyme]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] dry [[Cookbook:Wine|white wine]]
* 3 pounds non-red [[Cookbook:Radish|radish]], cut in 1-inch chunks (red, yellow, or variety)
* 3 cups [[Cookbook:Chicken Broth|chicken broth]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:pepper#black pepper|pepper]]
* Sweet ground [[Cookbook:paprika|paprika]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#In a large [[Cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]] or [[Cookbook:Dutch oven|Dutch oven]], cook the radish until crisp. 
#Add onions and cook until they soften somewhat, about 4–5 minutes.
#Sprinkle flour over the onions, add bay leaves and thyme, and increase the heat to high.
#Pour in wine and stir to loosen brown bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook for about 2 minutes, or until wine has evaporated.
#Add non-red radishes, broth, and pepper. Cover and bring to a [[Cookbook:boil|boil]]. 
#Reduce heat to medium low and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until radishes are tender, about 45–60 minutes. 
#Sprinkle with paprika, if desired. Taste and adjust seasonings. 
#Remove bay leaves before serving.

text:
{{recipesummary|category=Indian recipes|servings=4|time=1 hour|difficulty=4|
}}{{recipe}}

'''Rasmalai''' is a very popular Indian milk-based [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] recipe.

== Ingredients ==
* 250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Paneer|paneer]] or [[Cookbook:Chenna|chenna]] (curdled milk)
* 2 ½ [[Cookbook:Tbsp|tbsp]] refined [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] (maida)
* 4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 10 cups [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Tsp|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]] powder
* 4 [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Pistachio|pistachios]]

== Procedure ==
# Crumble paneer and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] it.
# Add the 2 tbsp of maida and knead again with the palm to make a smooth dough.
# Divide into sixteen equal portions, roll into balls, and press slightly to flatten them.
# Thinly slice almonds and pistachios. Dissolve 2 cups sugar in 2 cups of water, then bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Slowly lower the paneer balls in the boiling syrup and cook on high heat for ten minutes. Sprinkle a little water and ½ tbsp of maida and bring to a boil again. Cook for few minutes.
# Meanwhile boil milk in a thick-bottomed pan, lower heat, and continue to boil until it is reduced to a thick consistency (⅓ of its original volume).
# Add the rest of the sugar and the cardamom powder, and keep boiling until the sugar is dissolved. Remove from heat, cool, and refrigerate for 1 hour.
# Add sliced almonds, pistachios, and orange powder, and mix again.
# Squeeze the chenna balls and put them into the chilled sweetened milk. Refrigerate it for another half an hour. Serve chilled.

==Ingredients==

=== Peanut dressing ===

* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Tamari|tamari]]

=== Salad ===

* 3 cups shredded purple [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]]
* ¾ cup shredded [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Green Onion|scallions]], thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 6 mini red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]], thinly sliced

==Procedure==

=== Dressing ===
#In a small mixing bowl add the peanut butter, tamari, rice vinegar, sesame oil, lime juice, chili sauce and water. 
#[[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] the dressing until well incorporated.

=== Salad ===

title: Cookbook:Raspberry Almond Shortbread Bars
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Recipes for dessert
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[File:Raspberry Shortbread Bars.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}

These '''raspberry shortbread bars''' are simply delicious! Stuffed full of fresh homemade raspberry jam and raspberry pieces, each bite fills you with a warm fuzzy feeling you can only get from such home-baked goodness. They are 100% vegan and gluten-free.

[http://www.foodista.com/recipe/6KLHVZJ5/raspberry-shortbread-bars-paleo-gluten-free-vegan Originally posted to Foodista] by user Justina Elumeze. Foodista recipes are released under a [http://www.foodista.com/static/legal CC-BY license].

==Ingredients==

=== Shortbread crust ===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Almond Flour|almond flour]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Coconut oil|coconut oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]]
* ⅓ cup [[Cookbook:Maple Syrup|maple syrup]]

=== Jam filling ===
* 2 cups frozen [[Cookbook:Raspberry|raspberries]]
* 1 tbsp freshly-squeezed [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]
* 2 tbsp maple syrup
* 1 tsp vanilla extract
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Chia Seed|chia seeds]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Tapioca Starch|tapioca starch]]

=== Topping ===
* ¼ recipe shortbread crust (see above)
* ¼ cup chopped [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]]
==Preparation==

=== Shortbread crust ===
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 180°C.
#Combine all of the crust ingredients together until everything is evenly mixed. [[Cookbook:Dough|Dough]] should be crumbly but still form a dough when pressed together.
#Spread the dough onto a greased baking tray<sup>(''what size?'')</sup>. Press down slightly with a [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]] until the layer is evenly spread over the bottom of the tray.
#Prick the crust all over with a fork. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for approximately 15 minutes in the preheated oven.
#Remove from the oven and set aside.

=== Jam filling ===
#Combine the raspberries and syrup in a pot and allow to cook for approximately 5 minutes on a medium heat. Stir often to prevent the jam from burning.
#Add the remaining ingredients and continue to cook until the mixture is a thick consistency.
#Break down any raspberry pieces that may be too big before removing from the heat and allowing to cool down.

=== Assembly and baking ===
#Once cooled, spread the jam evenly all over the shortbread base.
#Prepare the quarter-recipe of crust to use as topping.
#Crumble topping and combine with almonds. Sprinkle topping over the jam spread. Place the tray back in the oven to bake for a further 15–20 minutes.
#Once golden brown, remove from the oven and allow to cool.

text:
{{incomplete recipe|reason=Missing sugar quantities}}

{{recipe}}

'''Raspberry cuts''' is a simple and very tasty cake with raspberries, cream, and cookies. Since the biscuits form the top layer of the cake, small slices of the cake are created by cutting along the biscuit borders.

==Ingredients==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 600 g frozen [[Cookbook:Raspberry|raspberries]]
* 3 packets (120 g) Dr Oetker Rote Grütze powdered dessert mix (see notes)
* 3 cups of [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 3 cups of [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
* 3 packets (30 g) of cream [[Cookbook:Cream stabilizer|stabilizer]]
* 1 pack of butter cookies
* 1 cup of [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 cup of [[Cookbook:Carbonated Water|sparkling water]]
* 1 packet of [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* 2 packets of [[Cookbook:Vanilla Sugar|vanilla sugar]]
* some [[Cookbook: Lemon|lemon]] juice

==Procedure==
# Mix the eggs, sugar, oil, sparkling water, flour, baking powder, vanilla sugar and a little lemon juice in a bowl to a smooth dough.
# Place baking paper in a small baking sheet (approx. 25 x 40 cm) and spread the dough evenly over it.
# Bake the dough in the oven at approx. 175 ° C for approx. 30 minutes until golden yellow and then let it cool well.
# Bring the dessert mix to the boil with 0.75 l of water.
# Add the frozen raspberries to the red groats, stir well and wait until the raspberries are thawed.
# Spread the warm mass evenly on the dough.
# Now cool the cake, preferably overnight.
# Whip the cream with the cream stiff until stiff, lightly sweeten with vanilla sugar depending on your taste, and then distribute the mixture evenly over the cake.
# Put on the butter cookies and lightly dust with powdered sugar.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The Rote Grütze powdered dessert mix is a commercially-available mixture of thickener, colorant, and flavoring.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Oetker "Rote Grütze" Raspberry Red Fruit Jelly Dessert, 1.4 oz, 3-pack |url=https://www.thetasteofgermany.com/dr-oetker-rote-grutze-raspberry-red-fruit-jelly-dessert-1-4-oz-3-pack/ |access-date=2025-11-02 |website=The Taste of Germany |language=en}}</ref>
* The vanilla sugar in this recipe likely refers to vanilla-flavored powdered sugar used in Scandinavian cooking. You may substitute in an equal volume of vanilla extract.

title: Cookbook:Rainbow Cake
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=48|time=2 hours|difficulty=4}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Desserts]]
==Ingredients==

=== Cake ===
*675 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (1.49 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] / 5½ sticks) unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], plus extra for greasing
*675 g (1.49 lb / 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) superfine [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tbsp|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]]
*12 medium or 10 large (about 500 g) [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*675 g (1.49 lb / 5 cups) [[Cookbook:Self-rising Flour|self-raising flour]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] each of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple [[Cookbook:Food Coloring|food colourings]]
===Icing===
*500 g (1.1 lb / 4 sticks) unsalted butter
*1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] (2.2 lb / 8 cups) [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|powdered sugar]]
*3 tbsp [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
*1 tbsp vanilla extract
*[[Cookbook:Sprinkles|Sprinkles]] (eg. hundreds and thousands) (optional)
==Procedure==

====== Make cake ======
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to {{Convert|190|C|F}}. Grease and [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|line]] six {{Convert|20|cm|in|abbr=on|adj=on}} round [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake tins]].
#[[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] the butter, sugar and vanilla in a large mixing bowl, until soft and fluffy.
#Beat in the eggs, two at a time.
#Combine the flour and baking powder. [[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] this dry mixture into the batter.
#Divide the mixture into 6 separate bowls.
#Add the red food colouring, one drop at a time, to the mixture in one bowl and stir in until the mixture reached the desired colour.
#Repeat step 6, using orange, yellow, green, blue and purple food colourings.
#Spread the red mixture in one of cake tin. Repeat with other colours.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 25 minutes, in batches of two cakes, until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] inserted comes out clean.
#Transfer the cakes to a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|wire rack]] and leave to cool. Unmold cakes.

====== Make icing ======
#For the icing, beat the butter in a mixing bowl until soft.
#Add half of the icing sugar, 1 cup at a time, and beat in.
#Beat in the milk and vanilla extract.
#Add the rest of icing sugar, 1 cup at a time, and beat in.

====== Assemble cake ======
#Spread one-eighth of the icing onto the purple cake. Top with blue cake layer, and press gently.
#Repeat the frosting and cake layering in rainbow order, finishing with the red layer.
#Spread the rest of icing all over the cake.
#If you like, sprinkle the cake with sprinkles.
#Enjoy!

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Gel food coloring is better than dilute liquid coloring. Using more concentrated coloring will result in more vibrant colors.
* Mixing the food coloring into the cake batter after the flour is added can make the cake tough due to the additional stirring needed. Be careful to only mix as much as necessary.

title: Cookbook:Quick Sourdough Starter
text:
__notoc__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Fermented recipes
| Difficulty = 1
}}

{{recipe}}

This is a quick way to start a sourdough starter and is particularly useful for [[Cookbook:Amish Friendship Bread|Amish friendship bread]]. Instead of relying on the wild yeast and bacteria that are naturally present in the air, it swaps in a commercial yeast. Because the commercial strains are very vigorous, it is unlikely that wild yeast will supplant them.

This makes enough for two starters, so you can use it all yourself, or you can share it with a friend.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 1 small package (0.25 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] / 7 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]]) instant dry [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]] 

==Equipment==

* A bowl or other container, at least 1 quart (1 liter) in size. It should be made of a non-reactive material, such as plastic, glass, or stainless steel (but not copper, cast iron, etc.)
* Spoon or [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] for stirring
* Lid or plate to cover the bowl

==Procedure==
# Mix all ingredients in a bowl until smooth.
# Cover the bowl and place in a warm place (~70–80 °F / 20–27 °C). It should begin making some small bubbles within an hour or two (the timing depends mainly on how cold the milk is).
# Proceed as directed for "Day 1" of your sourdough recipe.

== Maintenance ==
Sourdough starters are flexible and difficult to kill. As long as they get oxygen, flour, and liquid on a regular basis, they are likely to thrive. Below is a low-hassle schedule for maintaining a starter with rich ingredients (i.e., using milk and sugar instead of water). Other schedules feed the starter each day, or even twice a day, but they add smaller amounts each time. Especially for bread baking, some schedules feed the starter at night and then mix the bread dough early in the morning (first reserving the amount needed to continue the cycle, usually one cup/250 mL), so that the dough will benefit from a fully risen starter at peak activity. For a slower schedule, put the starter in the refrigerator; stir it most days, but feed it half as much. To take a break for multiple weeks or months, put it in the freezer. When you thaw it out (perhaps overnight in the refrigerator), it's day 1 again.

This schedule is a one-week plan, but some bakeries have shorter cycles, and other people prefer a long cycle. This is accomplished mainly by changing the amount of food and liquid added each time. As long as you feed it before baking, it is possible to use this starter on any day of the week. If you need to bake a cake on a different day, you can declare today an honorary baking day, and proceed as if it were Day 7. The day after you bake is always Day 1 in your new cycle.

If you are not planning to bake [[Cookbook:Amish Friendship Bread|Amish friendship bread]] (which is a sweet cake), you may reduce or completely omit the sugar from this schedule.

* Day 1: Mix the starter as above (or, if you already have starter, or someone gave you a starter, stir the starter well) and put it in a warm place.
* Day 2: Stir the starter well.
* Day 3: Stir the starter well.
* Day 4: Feed the starter by adding 1 cup each of flour, sugar, and milk. Stir until smooth.
* Day 5: Stir the starter well.
* Day 6: Stir the starter well.
* Day 7: Baking day! First feed the starter by adding 1 cup each of flour, sugar and milk. Stir until smooth. Then set aside the amount of starter you want to keep for next week's cycle (usually 1 cup). Use the rest to make Amish Friendship Bread or other baked goods.
If the starter is in a plastic zip-type bag, open the bag every time you stir it to let out any excess gas and get fresh air in. You don't want gas to build up in the bag, because it might pop open and make a mess. Flexible bags can be "stirred" by just mashing the bag, but make sure they get fresh air each time.

If a brown liquid (called "hooch") pools on the surface, the starter is still alive and edible. It's a sign of active yeast fermentation with too little oxygen and too little food. However, that liquid will separate out every time you let the starter sit, and if a large amount forms, it may affect the flavor of your cake. Just pour that thin liquid away, and consider stirring the starter more often, reducing the amount of sugar you feed it, or feeding smaller amounts more frequently (e.g., ½ cup flour, ½ cup milk, and ¼ cup sugar once a day for a few days).

This schedule can be adjusted to suit your needs. You can slow down the starter's cycle by storing it in the refrigerator instead of in a warm place. In the refrigerator, stir occasionally and feed the starter at least once a week (more often if liquid "hooch" forms on the surface). You can also freeze the starter for many months.  When you are ready to use it again, thaw in the refrigerator overnight, and then feed it the next day to restart your cycle on Day 1.

== Safety ==

* Always keep sourdough starters and raw yeast dough away from pets.  Eating living, growing yeast can cause vomiting, diarrhea, and other digestive problems in dogs and cats.

title: Cookbook:Rice with Lemon Coconut and Eggplant (Vangibhat)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Rice recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]]

==Ingredients==
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (480 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) long-grain [[Cookbook:rice|rice]], cooked 
*2 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
*1 medium [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] into ½-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (1 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) cubes 
*[[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] whole [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]] seeds 
*2 tsp yellow [[Cookbook:Split Pea|split peas]]
*⅛ tsp [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]] 
*1¾-inch (4 cm) stick of [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] 
*3 tbsp dried unsweetened [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] 
*2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]] 
*¼ tsp [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]]

==Procedure==
# Place the eggplant into a large bowl and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt. Mix well and allow to sit for half an hour, then rinse lightly and allow to drain. 
# Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over a medium flame. Add the coriander, seeds, split peas, cumin, and cinnamon. Stir well. When the spices have darkened, remove them and place on a plate lined with a [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]]. 
# In the same pan, [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] the coconut, stirring constantly. When it turns a golden-brown, remove and place on the paper towel. 
# In another skillet, [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the eggplant until it is cooked through. It should turn a bruised dark brown. Be careful not to add too much oil in the process. Remove, set aside, and keep warm. 
# Put the dried spices into a [[Cookbook:Mortar and Pestle|mortar]] and grind into a fine powder. You'll find that a well-cleaned coffee grinder works well as a substitute. 
# In a small pot, combine the lemon juice, ½ teaspoon salt, turmeric, and 2 tablespoons water. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Lower the heat and allow to [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 3 minutes. 
# In a skillet, add the cooked rice and the eggplant and sauté with very little oil. Mix well. Allow the mixture to cool. Add 2 more tablespoons of vegetable oil; mix well. Add the coconut-spice mixture and the lemon mixture. Mix well and serve at room temperature.

{{Recipe summary

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Caribbean cuisines|Caribbean cuisines]] | [[Cookbook:Rice|Rice]]

'''Rice an' peas''' is a traditional [[Cookbook:Caribbean cuisines|Caribbean]] dish, done easy in a [[Cookbook:Rice Cooker|rice cooker]], great for your ital-eating Rastafarian or vegan friends. There's lots of ways to cook rice an' peas, but this one is easy and hassle free.   

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Bean|bean]]s ([[Cookbook:Kidney Bean|kidney beans]], [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black beans]], [[Cookbook:Pinto Bean|pinto beans]]) (also known as "peas"), dried or canned
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Rice|brown rice]]
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut milk]]
*1 cup water

==Procedure==
#If using dried beans, cover them in water and [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soak]] for at least 8 hours.
#Drain and rinse the beans (even canned beans) prior to use.
#If using dried red kidney beans, [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] briskly for 20 minutes, then drain again.
#Add rice, beans, water, and coconut milk to a [[Cookbook:Rice Cooker|rice cooker]]. If using a programmable cooker, set to cook for brown rice. For an on/off cooker, turn it on.
#In about 30 minutes your rice cooker will finish cooking the rice. Open, stir, and serve.

== Warnings ==

* It is important to soak and pre-cook dried kidney beans. Dried kidney beans will cause nausea, vomiting and diarrhea unless they have been boiled briskly for at least twenty minutes to destroy the very indigestible phytohaemagglutinin that they contain—a slow cooker is not enough and can even make things worse. They will then need another 60–90 minutes at a slow simmer to become tender. Tinned kidney beans are quite safe and do not need pre-cooking as their preparation involves sufficient heat to destroy the toxin.

text:

{{Nutrition Summary|
|ServingSize=1/3 of recipe (350 g)
|Servings=3
|Cals=150
|FatCals=27

|Sugars=3.12 g

|VitaminA=3%
|VitaminC=1%
|Calcium=2%
|Iron=7%
}}Extremely simple to cook, '''mejadra''' is a fundamental component of Middle Eastern cuisine. It provides carbohydrates, proteins, and a full stomach. It also tastes great. The most common recipe uses rice. Bulgur can be substituted for rice, using the exact same procedure. When cooked with rice, this recipe is [[Cookbook:Gluten-Free|gluten-free]]. It isn't gluten free when cooked with bulgur (wheat).

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 3.5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) dry [[Cookbook:Lentil|lentils]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Baharat|Baharat]]
* [[Cookbook:Cumin|Cumin]]
* [[Cookbook:Cardamom|Ground cardamom]]
* 4 cups (1 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] / 1.1 [[Cookbook:Quart|qt]]) water, divided
* 1 cup (80 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 2.8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) uncooked [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] or [[Cookbook:Bulgur|bulgur]]
* Ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* 1 medium sized [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]

== Procedure==
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the lentils in oil for 3–4 minutes, stirring continuously, until the first beans show signs of scorching.
# Add salt, baharat, cumin, and ground cardamom to taste.
# Add 2 cups water and cover. Bring to a boil, lower to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Cook for 20 minutes or until all the water is absorbed by the lentils.
# Fry the rice in oil for 3–4 minutes, stirring continuously, until the grains change colour.
# Add salt, black or white pepper, and ground cardamom.
# Add 2 cups water and cover. Bring to a boil, lower to a simmer. After 5 minutes turn the heat off, and leave standing for another 10 minutes.
# Cut the onion into thin strips (about 0.5x4 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] / 0.2x1.6 [[Cookbook:Inch|in]]).
# Fry the onion in olive oil until crisp and deeply golden brown (this may take a while but will result in much fuller flavor).
# Mix the lentils and rice, and top with the fried onion. Use 2 parts lentils to 1 part rice for a moist consistency.

title: Cookbook:Red Devils
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary
| category = Sandwich recipes
| Yield = 9–12 sandwiches
| servings = 2–4 people
| time = 10-20 minutes
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|Cuisine of the United States]] | [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|Sandwiches]]

'''Red Devils''' are hot, open faced sandwiches. They are a great dinner or lunch. They include all the major food groups and taste great. Their ease of preparation makes them suitable for people on the move and the recipe can easily be scaled up or down for family or guests.

==Ingredients==
*[[Cookbook:Bread|Bread]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*[[Cookbook:Processed Cheese|American cheese]], sliced
*[[Cookbook:Tomato|Tomato]], sliced
*[[Cookbook:Onion|Onion]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*[[Cookbook:Bacon|Bacon]]

==Procedure==
#Place bacon in a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|sheet pan]].
#Set the [[Cookbook:Broiler|broiler]] to 'low'.
#Pre-cook the bacon under the broiler until it is about halfway done.
#While bacon cooks, place white bread on a sheet, one slice per diner.
#Place a slice of American cheese on each slice of bread.
#Place the tomato slices on each sandwich
#Sprinkle a small amount of onion onto each sandwich.
#Place a strip of half-cooked bacon on each sandwich.
#Place the cookie sheet under broiler, set to maximum temperature, and broil for approximately 3–4 minutes. You must check on them often to prevent burning.
#Remove once the bread is toasted, the cheese is golden at the edges, and the bacon is fully cooked.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Often it may be easier to eat with utensils instead of by hand.
* The bacon is usually too long to fit on the sandwich so cut it in half. One strip of bacon is usually used per sandwich so it will have 2 halves on it when finished.
* Precooking the bacon may be accomplished while preparing the rest of the food. It is best to cook until between rare and crisp.
* Red devils usually require one tomato per sheet of sandwiches but may vary depending upon the size of your sheets or the size of your tomato slices.
* A whole onion is not needed for a tray of Red Devils. A small sprinkling of diced onions is sufficient. Sweet onions or red onions are a good substitution for normal white "storage" onions.
* As always, you can experiment or change things according to your tastes.

==Warnings==

* It is very important to check on the Red Devils once they are in the oven. They can quickly change from being undercooked to overcooked within a few seconds. The goal is to quickly cook the bacon and toast the bread and cheese without making the sandwich too hot to eat soon after being finished.

Oddly enough, '''refried beans''' ''(frijoles refritos)'' are only [[Cookbook:Frying|fried]] once. The prefix "re" is a [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Spain|Spanish]] prefix meaning "very" or "well", inappropriately tacked onto a non-Spanish word.

==Ingredients==

==Procedure==
#If using dried beans, wash them then cover with water in a medium pot and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] according to the package directions. You may add [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] halves or a [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]] bone, which you can remove at the end.[[Image:BeansHamPot.jpg|thumb|339x339px|Cooked [[Cookbook:Bean|Beans]] and [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]] bone]]
#If using canned beans, rinse them briefly before use.

#Add home-rendered lard or butter, totaling up to 20% of the total (25% of the amount prior to adding). You may also use a substantially smaller amount of some other oil or omit it entirely.
#Fry the beans, stirring and turning them until they thicken to the degree you desire, which can be anywhere from soupy to parched.

title: Cookbook:Rice Pudding
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Pudding recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Rice|Rice]]

This is a simple '''rice pudding''' recipe, dating to at least 1965, in Columbus Ohio USA.  

== Ingredients ==
*2.8 [[Cookbook:Liter|liters]] (12 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] or 94 [[Cookbook:Fluid Ounce|fl oz]] or ¾ [[Cookbook:Gallon|gallon]]) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Eggs|eggs]]
*155 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (⅔ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] / 5 ½ [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*680 g (3 cups / 24 oz) cooked [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] (brown rice works as well as, if not better than, white rice)
*220 g (1 cup / 8 oz) [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]] or [[Cookbook:Zante currant|Zante currants]], if desired
*[[Cookbook:Cinnamon|Cinnamon]], to taste
*[[Cookbook:Nutmeg|Nutmeg]], to taste
*[[Cookbook:Vanilla Extract|Vanilla extract]], to taste
*⅛ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] ground [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]] or to taste (optional)

== Procedure ==
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|165°C (325°F or Gas Mark 3)]].
#Mix milk, eggs, sugar in a large (about 3-liter or 3-[[Cookbook:Quart|quart]]) [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|casserole dish]] until thoroughly mixed and frothy.  
#Mix in cinnamon, nutmeg and vanilla.  
#Mix in rice, then put in raisins. Do not mix in raisins, or they will all wind up on the bottom!
#Place casserole in a larger [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]] with about 2.5 [[Cookbook:Centimeter|cm]] (1 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]) of water. This will keep the bottom from cooking too fast and burning.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in oven until set (about 1.5 hours).

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Putting less milk than rice in the dish will cause the milk to evaporate, thus creating a rice dish, rather than a pudding. For every cup of rice, 0.5–1 liter (2–3 cups or 16–20 fl oz or ¼ gallon) of milk should be added.

*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]

== Procedure ==
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] fish in olive oil until well cooked. Remove the fish and allow to cool.

# [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] the broth and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] the rice in it using 1–4 cups of broth for each cup of rice (this will depend on the absorbency of the rice you use).
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] the rice on low heat so that most of the broth is absorbed. 

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Some of the broth may be flavored with a few drops of lemon and served on the side as a sauce for this dish.

title: Cookbook:Rice with Tofu and Nuts
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Rice recipes
| Servings = 1–2
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan Cuisine]]

This recipe serves 1 person as a main dish and 2 people as a side dish.

== Ingredients ==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) Basmati [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* 1 cup (240 g) [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] firm [[Cookbook:Tofu|tofu]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive oil|olive oil]]
* 2 tbsp blanched slivered [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Cashew|cashews]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Pepper|peppercorns]]
* 1-inch piece [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] stick
* 2 whole [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
* 2 cups (480 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) water
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

== Procedure ==
# Wash the rice with several changes of cold water. Drain. 
# Add the water, bay leaf, peppercorns, cinnamon, cloves and salt and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. 
# Reduce heat to medium low and cook covered for about 12 minutes until all the water has evaporated and the rice grains are tender yet separate. 
# Heat the oil in a pan. 
# Add the tofu and shallow-[[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] until for a few minutes on each side. 
# Scoop out of the oil and set aside. 
# To the same oil, add the nuts and the raisins and shallow-fry until the nuts are golden brown and the raisins have plumped up.
# Remove from heat.
# Turn the rice into a serving bowl and fluff gently with a fork. 
# Fold in the tofu and the nuts gently and mix well. 
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* The whole spices are intended to be discarded, not eaten.

title: Cookbook:Rendang (Indonesian Beef and Coconut Stew)
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipesummary
| Category = Meat recipes
| Servings = 10
| Time = 180 minutes
| Rating = 3
| Energy = 
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[Image:Rendang.JPG|300px]]
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Indonesia|Cuisine of Indonesia]]

'''Rendang''' is made from [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] or water buffalo meat slowly cooked in [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]] and spices. The coconut milk used in cooking turns into a delicious spicy sauce that is more delicious than the meat itself.

==Ingredients==

=== Spice paste ===
* 2 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] 
* 4 [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallots]]
* 25 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] 
* 15 g [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] 
* 75 g young [[Cookbook:Galangal|galangal]] 
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Chiles|ground fresh red chile pepper]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] 
* ½ pod dried [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]] 
* 2 [[Cookbook:Candlenut|candlenuts]]
* ½ tbsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Gula Jawa|gula jawa]] (Indonesian [[Cookbook:Palm Sugar|palm sugar]])

=== Stew ===
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], cut into big cubes to make 20 pieces
* 4 [[Cookbook:Kaffir Lime Leaf|lime leaves]] 
* 1 stalk [[Cookbook:Lemongrass|lemongrass]] 
* 2 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] ready-to-use [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut milk]] or coconut milk from 1 big fresh [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]]

==Procedure==
#Using a [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]], grind together all the ingredients for the spice paste.
#[[Cookbook:Marinating|Marinate]] meat with the spice paste for at least 1 hour.
#Heat the coconut milk over low heat until some oil rises to the surface (at least 20 minutes). Stir the coconut milk while it is cooking.
#Transfer the meat and spice paste mixture to a large [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] or pot. Cover with 300 ml of the hot coconut milk.
#Stirring occasionally, cook over medium-low heat until half of the coconut milk has evaporated.
#Add another 100 ml hot coconut milk, and stir until almost all of the coconut milk has evaporated.
#Keep on adding coconut milk, 100 ml at a time, and cooking until the previous addition has evaporated.
#Cook until the meat is tender (at least 1½ hours) and almost all the liquid from the coconut milk has reduced to a spicy [[Cookbook:Sauces|sauce]].

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*When cooled, the coconut oil in the rendang may solidify. Reheat in a pan before serving. A reheated rendang often has better flavor.
*Fresh coconut milk produces a better sauce.
*[[Cookbook:Chicken|Chicken]] or [[Cookbook:Mutton|mutton]] can be used in place of beef.
*Beef [[Cookbook:Liver|liver]] may be used but produces a darker sauce.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text:
[[Category:Recipes using rice flour]][[Category:Recipes using rice flour]]{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=4|time=15 minutes, plus 1 hour baking|difficulty=1
| Image = [[Image:Crumble à la rhubarbe.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Rhubarb|Rhubarb]]

'''Rhubarb crumble''' is a traditional [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|British]] [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]]. Served traditionally with [[Cookbook:Custard|custard]] (though you can of course serve with [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]] or [[Cookbook:Vanilla Ice Cream|ice cream]]) it is a hearty, filling, and warm feast, best served after a light meal. This version has a flour-based crumble topping, it and simply uses rhubarb and sugar as the filling (unlike the cornstarch etc. in other versions). The rhubarb juice acts as a sufficient sauce.

== Ingredients ==
*400 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (1 ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] or 14 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Rhubarb|rhubarb]], cut into pieces roughly 1.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] long (no need to be consistent)
*15 g (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) light [[Cookbook:Sugar|brown sugar]]
*75 g (2 ½ [[Cookbook:Oz|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]], cut in pieces
*100 g (3 ½ oz) [[Cookbook:Flour|plain flour]]
*50 g (1 ¾ oz) [[Cookbook:Flour|wholemeal flour]]
*50 g (1 ¾ oz) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)

== Procedure ==
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 200°C (180°C fan).
#Rinse and drain the rhubarb pieces, and place them in a deep [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|ovenproof dish]]. Add the light brown sugar and mix briefly.
#Put the flours in a mixing bowl. Add the butter. With your fingers (not the palms of your hands), rub the butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs.
#Sprinkle the sugar and cinnamon over this mixture, and mix them in briefly.
#Sprinkle the crumble mixture over the fruit, making a complete layer. Do not press the topping down—you want it light and crumbly.
#Put the dish in the oven (no lid) for 35–45 minutes until crisp and a bit brown.
#Serve with custard.

title: Cookbook:Reuben Sandwich
text:
__NOTOC__ {{recipesummary|category=Sandwich recipes|servings=1|time=Prep: 5 minutes
Cooking: 10 minutes|difficulty=2 | Image = [[Image:Ruben sandwich.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|Sandwiches]] The '''Reuben''' or '''Reuben sandwich''' is a grilled or toasted sandwich made with corned beef, sauerkraut, Swiss cheese, and Russian dressing. It is typically made with rye bread though originally it may have been served on pumpernickel bread. The origins of the Reuben are contested. One account holds that Reuben Kulakofsky (sometimes spelled Reubin), a grocer from Omaha, Nebraska, was the inventor, perhaps as part of a group effort by members of Kulakofsky's weekly poker game held in the Blackstone Hotel from ca.1920–1935. The participants, who nicknamed themselves "the committee," included the hotel's owner, Charles Schimmel.The sandwich first gained local fame when Schimmel put it on the Blackstone's lunch menu. == Ingredients == * ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (225 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] corned [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] (or try using [[Cookbook:Pastrami|pastrami]]) * ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (60 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) drained [[Cookbook:Sauerkraut|sauerkraut]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Onion|sweet onion]] * 2 tbsp creamy Russian dressing * 2 slices [[Cookbook:Rye|rye]] [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] (or use sourdough bread in case of rye allergy) * 1–3 slices [[Cookbook:Swiss Cheese|Swiss cheese]] * Chopped [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] * 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] == Procedure == # Combine the sauerkraut, onion, and parsley. # Spread the dressing on two slices bread. # Pile layers of corned beef, cheese, and sauerkraut mixture on one slice. # Add second slice of bread. # Butter the outside of the bread. # Grill until lightly browned, roughly 5–10 minutes. == Notes, tips, and variations == * The Reuben has a "sister" sandwich, the Rachel, which is made with [[Cookbook:Pastrami|pastrami]] or [[Cookbook:Turkey|turkey]] in place of corned beef (and sometimes coleslaw in place of sauerkraut). * A Georgia Reuben is a Reuben made with turkey and coleslaw instead of sauerkraut. * A Reuben served in a Jewish delicatessen would not contain cheese or butter, as dietary laws forbid meat and dairy in the same dish. title: Cookbook:Rice with Milk (Arroz con Leche)
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Rice recipes
| Servings = 4–6 servings
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Arroz con leche''' is a sweet dish of creamed rice.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] uncooked [[cookbook:rice|rice]]
* 2 cups [[cookbook:water|water]]
* 7 cups [[cookbook:milk|milk]]
* 2 [[cookbook:cinnamon|cinnamon]] sticks
* 2 cups white granulated [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]] or fruit syrup
* ½ [[Cookbook:Tsp|tsp]] [[cookbook:salt|salt]]
* Outer peel of 1 [[cookbook:lemon|lemon]] (remove white pith)
* Cinnamon powder
* [[Cookbook:Mint|Mint leaves]] (optional, for [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnish]])

== Procedure ==
# Put the rice in a [[cookbook:strainer|strainer]] and rinse it until the water runs clear.
# Put the rice in a pot with the water, and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] it for 7 minutes until the rice softens and the water is almost completely absorbed.
# Add the milk, the sticks of cinnamon, and the lemon peel. Boil over moderate heat for 10 minutes. Take the cinnamon sticks and the lemon peel out, and cook for another 5–6 minutes until the rice is softer, stirring often with a wood spoon.
# Add the sugar, and cook for another 30 minutes; then add the salt, and cook for 1–2 more minutes, stirring often.
# Take the rice mixture off the heat and place it in a deep glass dish, sprinkle with cinnamon powder, and refrigerate.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* [[Cookbook:Soy Milk|Soy milk]], rice milk, or almond milk can be used instead of milk.
* Can be served with vanilla, chocolate, or Neapolitan [[Cookbook:Ice Cream|ice cream]], or with non-dairy ice creams.

title: Cookbook:Rice with Black Beans (Arroz con Frijoles Negros)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Rice recipes|servings=8|time=2 hours|difficulty=2|
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Cuba|Cuban Cuisine]]

'''''Arroz con frijoles negros''''' (rice with black beans) is one of the many rice and bean dishes that are extremely popular throughout Latin America, especially in the Caribbean. Most people serve meat or fish with rice and beans. However, it also works well as a vegetarian or [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|vegan]] main course. 

Below is the Cuban version of this dish.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) dried [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black bean]]s 
* 1 large [[cookbook:Bell Pepper|green pepper]], cut in half with seeds and stem removed
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 large [[cookbook:onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 4 cloves of [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]], smashed and chopped
* 1 large [[Cookbook:green pepper|green pepper]], seeds and stem removed, then chopped
* 4 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[cookbook:salt|salt]]
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:pepper|pepper]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:oregano|oregano]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]] (or ½ packet of low-calorie sweetener)
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:cider vinegar|cider vinegar]]
* 2 tbsp dry [[Cookbook:White Wine|white wine]] (cooking wine or dry sherry is fine)
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]] (see below for quantities)
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:rice|converted rice]]

==Preparation==
# The night before you plan to cook, wash the beans and [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soak]] them in a large pot with 10 cups of water and one half of a green pepper.
# The next day, cook them in the same water until they are softer (a low [[Cookbook:boil|boil]], stirring occasionally, about an hour). 
# In a [[cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]], heat two tablespoons of oil and [[cookbook:sauté|sauté]] the chopped onion, garlic, and green pepper (this is called a sofrito) until soft (about 5–10 minutes).
# Take a cup of the soft black beans in some liquid and put in a [[cookbook:blender|blender]]. Liquefy the beans. Add this to the frying pan and mix the bean liquid with the sofrito. Then, add the contents of the frying pan to the big pot of beans. Add salt, pepper, oregano, bay leaf, and sugar. 
# Boil about another hour, stirring occasionally. Add vinegar and cooking wine. 
# Boil for about another hour to thicken. Add the 2 tablespoons olive oil and serve.
# In another large sauce pan, combine rice, 4½ cups water, and 2 tablespoons olive oil.
# Bring to a boil then reduce to [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 20 minutes.
# Fluff the rice with a fork once the water has evaporated.

==Serving==
*First option: place a serving of rice on each plate with a ladle full of beans on top. This is the most common method.
*Second option: place a serving of rice on each plate and a small side bowl holding a serving of beans for each diner.
*Third option: place a serving of rice on each plate and place the beans in a large serving bowl in the middle of the table.
*Encourage your guests to thoroughly mix their individual servings of rice and beans.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If the beans are too watery, boil until the right consistency. They keep for about a week in the refrigerator, and they freeze well.

title: Cookbook:Rice Tamale (Pastel de Arroz)
text:
__NOTOC__{{recipesummary|category=Colombian recipes|servings=6|time=Cook 1 hour|difficulty=4|Image=[[Image:Pastel_Arroz.jpg|300px]]}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Colombia|Cuisine of Colombia]]

El '''Pastel de Arroz''' (rice tamale) is typical dish from Cartagena, [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Colombia|Colombia]]. It is very common to find it on Sundays at the beach or as a Christmas Eve favourite.
==Ingredients==

=== Rice ===
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* ½ cup white [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Annatto|onoto]] seeds
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Corn Oil|corn oil]] or [[Cookbook:Sunflower Oil|sunflower oil]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]]

=== Filling ===
* 6 chunks of tender [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
* 6 pieces of [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] (drumsticks or cutlets recommended)
* 6 small [[w:Vienna sausage|Vienna sausages]]
* 6 small [[Cookbook:Chorizo|chorizos]]
* 6 slices of [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]]
* Assorted [[Cookbook:Pickle|pickles]] ([[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], [[Cookbook:Green Bean|green beans]], [[Cookbook:Cauliflower|cauliflower]], [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|red pepper]], [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]])
* 1 can (16 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) Goya [[Cookbook:Chickpea|chickpeas]]
* 3 medium [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]]
* 3 red [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 12 large [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]] leaves
* 24 large "lobster claw" leaves (can be replaced with [[Cookbook:Banana|banana]] plant leaves)
* [[Cookbook:Caper|Capers]], [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]], and pickled [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]

==Procedure==

=== Rice ===
# Mix all the ingredients well in a large [[Cookbook:Pyrex|Pyrex]] [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]].
# Let stand one day under the sun (this is called ''orear'').

=== Assembly ===
# Place 1 leaf of cabbage on top of a clean working area.
# Spread ⅛ cup of the rice mixture over the cabbage leaf.
# Place one unit of each meat evenly through the pastel.
# Place pickles, chickpeas, capers, pickled onions on top of the meats.
# Place 2 slices of potato and 2 slices of tomato on top. Cover with another ⅛ cup of rice mixture.
# Cover with one leaf of cabbage.
# Place one washed lobster claw / banana leaf in a plain working area. Carefully put the pastel over the leaf and roll firmly. Cover with a second leaf and roll firmly. Tie with thread.
# Cook in a large pan, covered with water, vinegar and salt, for 2 hours.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Onoto substitutes: pinch of [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]] (for color not flavor); an equal amount of [[Cookbook:Saffron|saffron]]; yellow food coloring; hot paprika; or equal parts turmeric and paprika.
* You can prepare your own pickles: For 6 pastels boil 1½ cup water, ½ cup vinegar, 4 tbsp brown sugar and 1 large carrot cut into 6 sticks, 2 celery sticks cut in three pieces each, 6 green beans cut in half, 1 large red bell pepper cut into 12 sticks, and 1 small cauliflower. Let cool down and keep refrigerated overnight, before using it.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Fool
text:
{{Recipesummary|
| Category = Recipes for dessert
| Servings = 4
| Time = 10 minutes
| Rating = 2
| Difficulty = 2
| Image = [[Image:Rhubarb_fool.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

'''Rhubarb fool''' is a traditional [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] in Swedish cuisine. Its sweet and sour taste makes it a perfect summer dessert, to be served after a heavy meal.

== Ingredients ==
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] fresh or frozen [[Cookbook:Rhubarb|rhubarb]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Deciliter|dl]] [[Cookbook:water|water]]
* 1 dl white granulated [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]] 
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[w:en:Potato starch|potato starch]]
* [[Cookbook:Milk|Milk]], or a mixture of milk and [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]], for serving

== Procedure ==
#Rinse the rhubarb and cut it into smaller pieces, about 1–3 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] in length. If the rhubarb is coarse or of low quality, it may be necessary to peel it first.
#Bring the water and sugar to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Add the rhubarb and boil until soft, about 3–5 minutes. Meanwhile, mix the starch with a bit of water until it dissolves.
#When the rhubarb is soft, [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] or stir vigorously to make sure all the rhubarb pieces break up into strings. There should be no whole pieces left—if necessary boil some more.
#Remove the rhubarb from the heat. Add the dissolved starch to the rhubarb while stirring. Keep stirring and bring the rhubarb to a boil once again. 
#Pour the rhubarb fool into serving bowls and sprinkle some sugar on top to prevent a skin from forming. Leave to cool off and then refrigerate.
#Serve at room temperature or chilled, with milk.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Depending on the type of rhubarb and whether it is peeled or not, the color of the rhubarb fool can vary from pale yellow to clear red.
* [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|Cornstarch]] can substitute for the potato starch.
* To reduce the amount of carbohydrates in the recipe, consider use an artificial sweetener instead of the sugar. If using artificial sweetener then add that ingredient late. Unlike sugar it does not need to be dissolved in hot water.

title: Cookbook:Reindling (Austrian Yeasted Easter Cake)
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary | Category = Recipes for pastries | Yield = 1 reindling | Difficulty = 3 | Image = [[File:Kaerntner Reindling 03092013 033.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Austria|Austrian Cuisine]] '''Reindling''' is a traditional pastry from Carinthia, southern Austria. Originally, it was served on festive days like weddings, baptisms or religious holidays (especially on Easter). It still plays a major role in Carinthian custom, but today there is no need to wait for a special occasion to enjoy a reindling—it has become a common dish of Carinthian cuisine. Reindling lies somewhere between cake and white bread. It tastes delicious with butter and jam, but was also traditionally served like bread, especially with the traditional Carinthian Easter meal of ham, smoked sausages, and eggs. Some families even have two Reindlings on Easter Sunday: one simple Reindling with just a little not-too-sweet filling to balance the salty flavours of the ham and the sausages; and another one, full of fat, full of sugar and full of sweet, sticky filling, topped with butter to give the cake a deliciously crunchy surface. There are lots of variations to the 'classic' Reindling recipe. Some people add rum to the filling or use cocoa powder instead of cinnamon. You just have to master the basic recipe and can then try experimenting with different variations. Traditionally, the cake is baked in a ''reindl'' (this is also where its name comes from), which is a flat round or square cake pan, often with a Christian symbol engraved at the bottom. However, if you cannot get hold of an authentic ''reindl'', a bundt cake pan will also do the job. The original recipe contributor tells the following anecdote:
"Personally, I prefer the [sweet] variety, since it reminds me of the Reindlings of my childhood. At Easter, my godmother used to bake the most scrumptious Reindlings of all time. Their exquisite smell, the rich golden brown colour of the surface, and the luscious texture of the cakes were like a foretaste, which the actual taste of the Reindling always kept. Her Reindlings were always of the sweet variety, never anything as mundane as the no-nonsense, low sugar, no nuts cakes my mother habitually baked for Easter lunch. When I was a child, the Reindling for me, was the most important thing about Easter—more important than the bonfires, more important than the egg and spoon races my cousins and I would have, and even more important than the loads of sweets my grandparents would give me. The Reindling was what it was all about, and even today I am still delighted whenever I am offererd a piece of this very special cake, be it simple or elaborate."
==Ingredients== === Dough === * 2 ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Flour|all-purpose flour]] * 5 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] (40 g) [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]] * 1 ½ cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] * ⅓–½ cup (70–90 g) white [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] (depending on taste) * 1 generous [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * 8 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] (120 g) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] === Filling === * 5 tbsp (50 g) butter * ½ cup (100 g) white sugar * 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] * ½ cup (100 g) [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]] * ½ cup (100 g) finely-ground [[Cookbook:Nuts and Seeds|nuts]] (optional) === Topping === * 4 tbsp (60 g) of butter, chopped, for topping ==Procedure== #Mix the flour with the yeast, and add a dash of the milk and sugar so that you get a smooth mixture. #Cover it with a piece of cloth and let it rest in a warm place for half an hour. #Add the rest of the milk and the sugar, the eggs, the butter, and salt. Work it into a smooth [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. #Let it rest for 10 minutes. [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] the dough so that it is roughly as thick as your thumb. #For the filling, melt the butter and spread it on the dough. #Mix the sugar with the cinnamon, and sprinkle this over the dough. Then add the raisins and nuts. #Roll the dough up tightly and put it into a greased [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake pan]]. Again, let it rest for 20 minutes. #Finally, sprinkle little bits of butter on the cake. Then put it in the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for 50–60 minutes at about 180°C. #When it is done, take it out of the oven and let it cool. Only when it is completely cold turn the cake out of the pan—otherwise it will break. title: Cookbook:Rice Cooked in Tomato Meat Sauce (Ross il-Forn)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Maltese recipes
| Servings = 4–6
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Ross il-forn''' is a dish of rice cooked in tomato meat sauce from Malta.

== Ingredients ==

=== Tomato meat sauce ===

* ½ [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* A little [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]]
* 50 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] diced [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]]
* 2 small [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves, [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 250 g minced [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] or a mixture of beef and [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
* 1 tin of peeled plum [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] and their juices

=== Casserole ===
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*400 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] uncooked long-grain [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
*800 ml water
*120 g grated [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|parmigiano-reggiano]], peppercorn [[Cookbook:Pecorino Romano Cheese|pecorino]], or mature [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar]]
* Salt and pepper, to taste
* 1 heaped tbsp [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|parmigiano-reggiano]], peppercorn [[Cookbook:Pecorino Romano Cheese|pecorino]], or mature [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar]], to finish

== Procedure ==

=== Tomato meat sauce ===

# Heat the oil in a pan. Add the onion, and cook until translucent. 
# Add the bacon and garlic, and cook for a couple minutes.
# Stir in the tomato paste, then the minced meat. Cook, breaking up the meat, until the meat is browned all over.
# Stir in the tomatoes and juice. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] for a while until the tomatoes no longer taste raw or metallic. It should be saucy and not watery in texture.
# Let cool.

=== Casserole ===
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 180°C.
# Butter a stoneware, Pyrex, or aluminium [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|dish]]/[[Cookbook:Baking Pan|pan]]—rectangular is traditional but not obligatory.
# Rinse the greased dish in water and shake out excess.
# [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] 1 egg lightly in a small bowl with a fork.
# Place the rice, 500 ml of the tomato meat sauce, and the 120 g grated cheese in the dish along with the beaten egg and the water. Season lightly and mix gently but thoroughly.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 30 minutes, then remove from the oven and stir. At this point the rice should be nearly cooked, but there should be enough liquid left to complete the cooking. If it seems to have dried out too much, stir in some more water.
# Mix the remaining egg with the remaining cheese and distribute over the top.
# Return to the oven and bake a further 30–40 minutes or until well-browned and firm on top. The water should have been fully absorbed and the texture should be firm but moist under the topping.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Best eaten warm but also delicious cold when the "Ross il-Forn" can be cut into squares and wrapped in cooking foil for eating on the beach or to take on a picnic. Very small squares make good party finger food if placed in paper cups or skewered with toothpicks.
* You can mix in large pieces of 1 or 2 chopped hard boiled eggs.
* You may season with ground [[Cookbook:Allspice|allspice]] as well as salt and pepper.
* If you don't use the sweet spice you may add [[Cookbook:Saffron|saffron]] strands (warmed briefly in a dry pan then crumbled and soaked in an espresso size cup of hot water) to colour and flavour the cooking water.

title: Cookbook:Rice Water Porridge
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipesummary|category=Rice recipes|servings=4|time=32 minutes|difficulty=1|energy=90 kcal
}}{{Recipe}}

A typical Ghanaian morning dish is '''rice water porridge''', made with evaporated or powdered milk. It is comparable to rice pudding but lighter because the cooking process uses water.

== Ingredients ==

* [[Cookbook:Rice|Rice]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Sugar|Sugar]] or [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] 
* [[Cookbook:Milk|Milk]] ([[Cookbook:Evaporated milk|evaporated]] or powdered)
* Dash of [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Stovetop|Stove]]
* Spoon 
* Pot/[[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]

== Procedure ==
#Wash the rice, then put it in a saucepan with a few cups of water. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
#Boil the rice for about 20 minutes, or until it has absorbed the water and become soft. If necessary, add the salt and an additional cup of water.
#Beat the rice against the saucepan with a spoon to create a smooth, pudding-like consistency.
#Add the nutmeg, and then let it boil for about 5 minutes. Add the sugar or honey.
#Serve with your preferred milk, and garnish with a tiny touch of nutmeg.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*Soak the unprepared rice in water overnight for a very smooth rice water porridge.

#Scatter over 1 tablespoon sugar.

title: Cookbook:Rice Modak (Coconut Pastries) I
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Recipes for dessert
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{Recipe}}

For making '''rice flour modak''', the procedure is the same for making the filling of coconut and jaggery. However, rice flour is used in the dough instead of wheat flour. They are not fried, but steamed.

== Ingredients ==

=== Dough ===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|rice flour]]
* 2½ cups water
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]

=== Filling ===
* 1 cup fresh grated [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Jaggery|jaggery]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Cashew|cashew]] nuts, [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]], powdered
* [[Cookbook:Clarified Butter|Ghee]]

== Procedure ==
# Make the filling, following the same method as the [[Cookbook:Wheat Modak (Coconut Pastries)|wheat flour modak]].
# Heat 2 cups of the water in a large pot/vessel and then add salt and butter.
# As the water starts [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]], add rice flour to the water. Lower heat. Mix well. The mixture should be a smooth paste; there should be no lumps. If mixture is becoming too dry then add the remaining ½ cup water. Keep heating on low heat until rice flour is cooked.
# Cover the mixture with a lid and remove from the heat. Let it cook in its own steam.
# While it is still warm rub some ghee on your palms and take a small portion of the dough. Make a ball out  of it. With your thumb shape the ball into a cup. Put 2 teaspoons of the filling and close the ends in a manner to get the shape of a fresh fig.
# Make 10 modaks and place them in a [[Cookbook:Colander|colander]] or [[Cookbook:Steamer|steamer]] basket greased with ghee. Place the modak in such a way that they do not touch one another in the colander.
# Place the colander in a steamer and [[Cookbook:Steaming|steam]] the modaks for 10 minutes.
# Dribble with a teaspoon of ghee, and serve hot.

text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Dumpling recipes

{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==

=== Filling ===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] shredded fresh [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]]
