title: Cookbook:Spinach Artichoke Dip
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Dip recipes
| Difficulty = 1
}}

{{recipe}}

Formal or informal, '''spinach artichoke dip''' is a great appetizer at any party. It is quick and easy taking very little time to prepare. The dip may be served with a variety or crackers, breads, or chips. 

==Ingredients==
* 16 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] (450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (180 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) heavy [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]] (use half milk, if desired) 
*⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (80 ml) grated [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]] 
*¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (60 ml) [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic powder]] 
* 16 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] (450 g) frozen cut leaf [[Cookbook:spinach|spinach]], thawed and well drained 
* 1 can quartered [[Cookbook:artichoke|artichoke hearts]], rinsed and well-drained
*⅔ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (160 ml) shredded [[Cookbook:Monterey Jack Cheese|Monterey Jack cheese]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] prepared (240 ml) [[Cookbook:salsa|salsa]] 
* Crackers or [[Cookbook:Tortilla Chip|tortilla chips]], for serving

==Procedure==
#In a [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]] fitted with a metal blade, process the cream cheese, cream, Parmesan cheese, and garlic powder until smooth and creamy. Add the spinach and process until thoroughly mixed. Add the artichokes and process just until coarsely chopped.
#Turn the mixture into a 3½-quart electric [[Cookbook:Slow Cooker|slow cooker]]; smooth the top.
#Cover and cook on the high heat setting for 1¼–1½ hours, until hot in the center. Sprinkle the top evenly with the Jack cheese and spoon the salsa in a ring around the inside edges of the slow cooker. Cover and continue heating on high 15 minutes longer, or until the cheese is melted. 
#Reduce the heat to the low setting and serve warm with crackers or tortilla chips for dipping. Refrigerate any leftovers.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*This dip is best served hot but may also be served chilled.
*If served in a bread bowl, pieces may be broken off and used as dipping tools for further enjoyment. 
*Other condiments that go great with this dip include sides of salsa, guacamole, or sour cream. 
*This is great appetizer for vegetarians, and vegan cream cheese may be substituted if need be.

'''Stargazy pie''' is a rich fish pie from Cornwall in the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|United Kingdom]]. 
== Ingredients ==
*As many fresh [[Cookbook:Fish|Herrings, Pilchards or Mackerel]] to fill your [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie dish]]
*Sufficient [[Cookbook:Pastry Dough|pastry]] to cover your dish

*Up to 6 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] or ½ [[Cookbook:Pint|pint]] (300 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) of [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]] or top-of-the-milk
*Fine [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|breadcrumbs]]
*Fat [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon rashers]] (green or smoked to your preference)
*2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Tarragon|tarragon]] [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
*[[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]]

== Procedure ==
#Scale, clean, and bone the fish, separating and retaining their heads.
#Season inside each with salt, pepper, and parsley. Roll neatly.
#Butter [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie dish]], and sprinkle a thick layer of breadcrumbs on.
#Lay in some of the fish, then alternate breadcrumbs and fish until dish is full. Cover with bacon rashers.

#Arrange fish heads on pastry, so as they are looking up (to the stars).
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in a hot [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]].
#Serve with a sprig of parsley in mouth of each fish.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Kidney Pudding
text:
{{recipesummary
| category = Meat recipes
| servings = 4
| time = 4.5 hours
| difficulty = 3
| Image = [[Image:SteakKidneyPudding.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Meat_Recipes|Meat recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]]

This recipe comes from [[w:Mrs Beeton|Mrs Beeton]]'s famous [[w:Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management|Book of Household Management]].

==Ingredients==
* 900 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) [[Cookbook:Beef|rump steak]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Kidney|kidneys]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Black pepper]]
* Suet-crust

==Procedure==
# Cut the steak into about 2.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] (1 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]) squares. Cut each kidney into 8 pieces. 
# Line the basin with crust, leaving a small piece of crust to overlap the edge.
# Then cover the bottom with a piece of the steak and a few pieces of kidney; season with salt and pepper, and then add another layer of steak, kidney and seasoning. Proceed in this manner until the basin is full, when pour in sufficient water to come within 5 cm (2 inch) of the top of the basin.
# Moisten the edges of the crust, cover the pudding over, press the two crusts together, so that the gravy does not escape, and turn up the overhanging pastry.
# Wring out a cloth in hot water, flour it and tie up the pudding; put it int boiling water and let it boil for at least 4 hours. If the water diminishes, always replenish with hot water from a jug, as the pudding should be kept covered all the time, and not allowed to stop boiling.
# When the cloth is removed, cut out a round piece in the top of the crust, to prevent the pudding bursting, and send it to table in the basin, either in an ornamental dish or with a napkin pinned round it. Serve quickly.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* To make the crust, combine 175 g (6 oz) [[Cookbook:Suet|suet]] per 450 g (1 lb) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]], and moisten with [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] to make a dough.

Tender, juicy, marinated steak rolled with Monterrey Jack cheese sauce in a corn tortilla, baked and topped with more cheese sauce and green chile sauce.

== Procedure ==
#Combine oil, lime, chipotles, adobo, salt, pepper, and cumin in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]]. Pour into a gallon size zip-top bag and add steak. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
#Heat a charcoal [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]], but use a chimney or else you will have a solvent flavored steak. Ditch the grate and place the steak right on the coals and cook 60 seconds per side for medium rare.

Roll and place seam side down on a [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment]]-lined [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|sheet pan]]. Repeat until all tortillas have been used up. While you're at it, eat any remaining steak.

title: Cookbook:Steak au Poivre (Pepper Steak)
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Meat recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Pepper steak''' is a dish where tender beef steaks are crusted with cracked peppercorns and then seared in a hot pan. A pan sauce can then be made of the meat drippings.
== Ingredients ==
* [[Cookbook:Salt#Types of salt|Kosher salt]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (24–32 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[Cookbook:Beef#Loin|beef tenderloin steaks]], 1 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] black [[Cookbook:Pepper|peppercorns]], cracked
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Cognac|cognac]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Cream|heavy cream]]
* ¼ cup unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], divided
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]

== Procedure ==
#Sprinkle steaks on both sides liberally with kosher salt. Press peppercorns into both sides of each steak. Let sit for 30 minutes or until room temperature.
#Melt 1 tbsp butter with oil in a large stainless steel [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium high heat. Add steaks and cook 5 minutes per side for medium rare, 6 for medium, and 7 for well done. Remove from pan and keep warm.
#Raise heat in pan to high. Turn off the heat, then [[Cookbook:Deglazing|deglaze]] pan with cognac. Carefully ignite with a firestick or kitchen lighter, then swirl the pan until flames die.
#Put heat to medium and whisk continuously to remove fond. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and cook until liquid has reduced by half.
#[[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] in cream. Bring to a boil and cook until liquid has reduced to ⅓ cup.
#Slowly whisk in butter, 1 tbsp at a time. Spoon sauce over steaks and serve warm.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Don't even think about using a nonstick pan. You can't build a pan sauce in a nonstick skillet.
* If you don't want to ignite the cognac, you do not have to. It just makes a performance that makes people stare at you with amazement.

== Warnings ==

* If you do choose to ignite, remember to keep a lid, in case things get out of hand, and a fire extinguisher, in case something bad happens and you need it.

This recipe is for a '''spicy beef brisket roast'''. It may be served with [[Cookbook:Potato|mashed potatoes]].

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] (2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]]) piece of [[Cookbook:Beef#Brisket|beef brisket]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] or coarsely-chopped [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]
* 1 cup thinly sliced stalk of [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves
* 1 tsp toasted, ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]] seeds
* ½ tsp cracked [[Cookbook:Pepper|black peppercorns]]

* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 cups of diced [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], fresh or canned
* ¼–½ cup [[Cookbook:Stock|beef stock]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vinegar|red wine vinegar]]

* 2 [[Cookbook:Bay leaf|bay leaves]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]], green or red, thinly sliced
* 1 medium or hot [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chile pepper]] (optional)
== Procedure ==

# Heat oil in large heavy pot, add brisket, and brown on all sides.
# Push meat to the side. Add onions and celery, and cook over medium heat until softened.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If using a larger piece of brisket, adjust other quantities accordingly.
* While cooking, do not add cold liquid to the meat, and make sure to pour not cold tomatoes on top of the meat. Otherwise, the meat can become hard.

title: Cookbook:Spinach and Ricotta Lasagna
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Pasta recipes|servings=12|time=3 hours and 15 minutes|difficulty=3}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|Cuisine of The United States]] | [[Cookbook:Italian-American_cuisine|Italian-American Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Pasta_Recipes|Pasta Recipes]]

[[Cookbook:Lasagne|'''Lasagna''']] is a well known baked Italian pasta dish.  This hearty, meatless recipe attempts to compose the tang of the tomato sauce with the creaminess of the ricotta and the sweetness of the spinach.

This recipe is the assembly of four different preparations into a baked dish and is presented here as such.  While it might seem long, complicated and overwhelming, this recipe is fairly simple and not very involved while the result is almost guaranteed to impress.

== Ingredients ==

=== Sauce ===

*2 cans (56 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) San Marzano or Roma [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
*1 head (about 12 cloves) [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], peeled
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]

=== Cheese mixture ===

*2 tubs (30 oz) [[Cookbook:Ricotta|ricotta]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]

=== Spinach ===

*3 packages (27 oz) frozen [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]]

=== Pasta and Assembly ===

* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] lasagna [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]] sheets
* ¾ lb shredded [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella]]

== Procedure ==

=== Sauce ===

# Put a thick-bottomed pot over medium-low heat. Add the oil and garlic, and stir until fragrant and blisters begin to form.
# Add the tomatoes, and reduce the heat to low.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] until it has a sauce consistency and has reduced to about ⅔ the original volume (about 1½ hours).
# Turn off the heat and remove the garlic cloves to mash them with a fork. Add the garlic purée to the sauce.
# Add salt to taste, cover, and let rest 30 minutes.

=== Cheese mixture ===

# Pour the ricotta cheese onto a [[Cookbook:Cheesecloth|cheesecloth]] or tea towel in a [[Cookbook:Strainer|strainer]], and let drain for 30 minutes.
# Combine the eggs and ricotta, and beat until creamy with a hand [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]].
# Cover and reserve, ensuring it is at room temperature during assembly.

=== Spinach ===

# Thaw, drain, and press the liquid out of frozen spinach.
# Reserve until ready to assemble.

=== Pasta ===

# Cook the pasta according to the manufacturer's directions, drain and place back into the pot with cold water.
# Lay the sheets on a clean, wet tea towel and roll the cloth until ready to use.

=== Assembly and cooking ===

# Ladle sauce at the bottom of a 9x13-inch [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|pan]] or [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|dish]] and layer lasagna sheets.
# Sparsely deposit spinach onto the noodles and apply cheese mixture with a rubber [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]].
# Add more sauce and repeat the previous step until the pan is almost full and covered with a layer of lasagna.
# Add sauce and cover with grated mozzarella.
# Put the pan onto a tray and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] at 350°F for approximately 30 minutes, or to an internal temperature of 150°F.
# Let rest for 15–20 minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* It is possible to prepare everything else while the sauce simmers.
* The stem-part of the tomatoes can be pinched out, to break the tomato apart without crushing it.
* Placing a wooden spoon transversely onto the pot before setting the lid on it allows evaporation and prevents splatter.
* The tomato sauce also works great on pizza.
* Using fresh spinach is not recommended.
* Laying the lasagna sheets in alternating directions (lengthwise, widthwise, lengthwise, etc.) increases structural strength.
* If presentation requires it, the lasagna can be [[Cookbook:Broiling|broiled]] for a few minutes at the end of baking.

text:

This '''steak and wine pie''' is a variation on the [[Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie|Steak and Ale Pie]] recipe, one with a richer and more fruity sauce and a more crumbly, stiffer crust.

== Ingredients ==
=== Pie dough ===
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]], cut into small cubes
* 5 tbsp [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 handful dry [[Cookbook:Italian Seasoning|Italian seasoning]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

=== Meat ===
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* ¼ cup red wine or [[Cookbook:Lemon juice|lemon juice]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* 1 lb [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] chuck rib
=== Filling ===
* ½ tbsp butter or margarine
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]
* [[Cookbook:Thyme|Thyme]] (fresh or dried) to taste
* [[Cookbook:Basil|Basil]] (preferably dried) to taste
* ½ stalk [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]], sliced ⅛ inch thick
* ⅓ whole [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], sliced ⅛ inch thick, then cut into semicircles
* ½ small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* ⅞ cup red [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
* 1 tbsp gravy granules
* 1 tbsp tomato [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] 
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

== Equipment ==
* 13-cm- or 5-inch-diameter pie plate or ceramic bowl
* [[Cookbook:Saucepan|Saucepan]]
* [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]]
* [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|Rolling pin]]
* Spoons, cutlery and [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]], as needed
* [[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]] or [[Cookbook:Toaster Oven|toaster oven]] (preferred)

== Procedure ==
===For the dough===
# Combine the flour, salt, and Italian seasoning in a shallow bowl, and mix to distribute well. Mix in the butter until solid, firm dough lumps form. If mixing by hand, pinch and clasp them together until a ball can be formed.
# Dust a work surface and the dough ball with a little flour to prevent sticking. Flatten dough with a rolling pin until it forms a thin disk large enough to be draped over the pie plate or bowl.
# Freeze the dough for 20 minutes, or for the duration of filling prep and cooking.
=== Filling ===
# Combine the oil, wine, and soy sauce to make a marinade. Submerge the beef in the marinade, and let this marinate in the fridge for 24 hours.
# Remove the meat from the marinade, and slice it ¼ inch thick.
# Heat the saucepan over high heat, then add the butter and let it melt. 
# Add the sliced beef to the saucepan. Sauté, stirring, until browned all over.
# Add bay leaf, thyme, basil, celery, onion, and carrot. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until onions and celery are soft.
# Scrape some of the fond off the pan bottom without taking it out, if possible. Stir in the wine, Worcestershire sauce, and gravy granules for 1 minute 
# Turn heat to low, stir in ketchup, and cover the pan. Cook until stew volume is reduced by a third to half and liquids are beginning to thicken.
# Season with salt and pepper to taste.
# Remove from the heat, and discard the bay leaf.

=== Assembly and final baking ===
# Pour filling into the pie plate or bowl.
# Cover with the pie crust disk and press around edges to seal. The dough falling apart is acceptable as long as it retains an amount of crunch or flakiness.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 445 °F (230 °C / Gas 8) for 10 to 15 minutes or until top crust turns medium brown. Handle with care.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The butter/margarine can be substituted by 2 tbsp olive oil mixed with 1 tbsp milk.
* The gravy granules can be substituted by 1 tsp beef bouillon mixed with 2 tsp hot water.
* If you want a bottom crust for the pie, double the dough quantities, and divide the dough in half before rolling out each portion. Grease the baking dish and line it with one of the dough disks before freezing and filling.
* You can also slice the steak before marinating it in order to facilitate the flavor permeation. You may not need to marinate for as long if you do so.

title: Cookbook:Spinach Mushroom Omelet
text:
{{Incomplete recipe|reason=missing paprika instruction}}__notoc__
{{recipesummary
| category = Breakfast recipes

| time = 20 minutes
| difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Breakfast Recipes|Breakfast Recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Omelet Recipes|Omelet Recipes]]

This '''spinach mushroom omelet''' is an American diner-style breakfast dish that provides a creamy mix of fresh vegetable taste and sharp cheddar.

== Ingredients ==
* 3 standard [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 pinch ground black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* 1 pinch ground [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]] (optional)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 heaping handful of fresh [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]]
* ⅔ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] baby bella [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]], thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Each|ea.]] large red [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* ½ cup shredded aged [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar cheese]]
* ¼ tsp [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Cooktop|Stovetop]]
* [[Cookbook:Skillet|Skillet]] (30 cm or 12 inch diameter)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]<nowiki/>[[Cookbook:Spatula|s]]
* [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]]
* [[Cookbook:Ramekin|Ramekin]] or other small bowl
== Procedure ==
# In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, salt, pepper, nutmeg and milk, until even and glossy.
# Heat the skillet over medium heat. Add half the butter, tilting the skillet in a circular motion to coat evenly.
# Add paprika, mushrooms, and onions, and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until lightly browned.
# Add spinach and toss for 30 seconds, or until slightly wilted, but still crunchy. Remove the vegetables from the heat and set aside.
# Add the remaining half of the oil or butter to the pan over medium heat, and coat evenly. Lower the heat.
# Pour the egg mixture into the skillet, swirling the pan to ensure an even, creamy layer of eggs. Heat until the eggs have begun to set, with some fluff on top.
# Top the egg layer with the vegetables, distributing the vegetables evenly. Sprinkle the cheese evenly on top.
# Gently push the edges of the omelet half a centimeter toward the center of the skillet with two spatulas, making sure not to break it. Turn the heat off.
# Use the spatulas to carefully lift/pull half the omelet off the skillet and fold it over the other half. Carefully move the entire omelet onto a plate and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you want to prevent the mushrooms from browning after you slice them, submerge them in a bowl of cool water until ready to cook them. Drain before adding to the pan.

This is a fragrant, long-grain variety of [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] often used in Indian recipes. Basmati can be cooked in the same way as other rice, in the ratio of two cups water to one cup rice. The recipe below helps to bring out the flavour of basmati.

* 400 [[Cookbook:gram|g]] white basmati [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]

title: Cookbook:Steamed Pork With Mustard Greens
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Chinese recipes|servings=4|time=1 hour|difficulty=3}}

{{recipe}}

'''Steamed pork with mustard greens''' (梅菜扣肉, pinyin: Méicàikòuròu) or '''mei cai kou rou''' is a Chinese dish from the Hakka people. It is very popular and tasty but contains a lot of saturated fat.

==Ingredients==
* About 10.5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] [[Cookbook:Mustard Greens|mustard greens]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:cornstarch|cornstarch]] combined with 1 tsp cold water
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 2 tsp light [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* 1 tsp rice [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]] or water
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] [[Cookbook:pork|pork]] tenderloin
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Black Bean Sauce|black bean and garlic sauce]]
* About 2 tbsp water
* Freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]

==Procedure==
# Wash greens and discard tough stems. 
# Bring a large pot of water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], add greens, and cook for 2 minutes. 
# Drain greens and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking. Drain again, then cut greens into long diagonal strips.
# In a medium bowl, combine cornstarch and water. Stir in sugar, soy sauce and rice wine. Cut pork into thin slices and add to the mixture. [[Cookbook:Marinating|Marinate]] about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
# Heat oil in a preheated [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] or large heavy [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium heat. Add black bean sauce and [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|stir-fry]] for 1 minute.
# Add pork and stir-fry for 2 minutes. 
# Add mustard greens and water. Mix well and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] gently about 4–5 minutes, until pork is cooked through and greens are tender.
# Season with pepper and serve.

==References==
* Hsiung, Deh-Ta. ''The Chinese Kitchen: A Book of Essential Ingredients with Over 200 Easy and Authentic Recipes''. New York: St. Martin's Griffin, 2002.

title: Cookbook:Sticky Date Pudding
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Recipes for dessert
| Servings = 12
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}

A '''sticky date pudding''' is a favorite Australian pudding, especially in Southern climates in the winter months. Your family and friends will love you forever if you make them the following recipe.

==Ingredients==
=== Sauce ===

* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (480 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1 cup (240 ml) water

=== Cake ===
*1 cup (240 ml) pitted [[Cookbook:Date|dates]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|bicarbonate of soda]]
*2 cups (480 ml) plain [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|bicarbonate of soda]]
*2 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*2 tsp [[Cookbook:Mixed Spice|mixed spice]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], at room temperature
*1½ cups (360 ml) [[Cookbook:Superfine Sugar|castor sugar]]
*1 cup (240 ml) [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
*2 tsp of [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] essence

=== Serving ===
*500 ml [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
 
==Equipment==
*[[Cookbook:Double Boiler|Double boiler]]
*Electric [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]] (a free standing one is better, as you need to beat the eggs for some time for best results)
*[[Cookbook:Sieve|Sieve]] or flour sifter
*Large [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake tin]], lined with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]] and well-greased

==Procedure==

=== Sauce ===
# Place brown sugar and water in top of double boiler.
# Over simmering heat, stir until all brown sugar is dissolved.
# Remove from the heat, and set aside to cool.

=== Cake ===
# [[Cookbook:Chopping|Chop]] dates roughly, place in [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and add sodium bicarbonate along with just enough water to cover everything.
# Bring to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 1 minute. It should froth up from the bicarb; when it does, remove from heat once foam reaches the top of the saucepan.
# Set aside to cool.
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 180°C.
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] flour, bicarbonate of soda, salt, and mixed spice together twice.
# Beat eggs lightly. Add castor sugar and [[Cookbook:Whipping|whip]] as for making a sponge; it should be really light and fluffy.
# [[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] in oil and vanilla essence, but don’t over-mix this as you’ll lose all the air in the egg mixture.
# Fold in the sifted flour, sodium bicarbonate, and salt. Then, fold in the cooled date mixture.
# Pour into prepared tin. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in oven at 180°C for about 80–90 minutes, not too high in the oven or the top will burn. Cooking time and temperature can be reduced slightly if a fan-forced oven is used
# Test cake with [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]], which should come out dry. Remove from oven, and leave pudding in the tin

=== Serving ===
# Use a skewer to create lots of holes throughout the hot pudding
# Pour approximately 1 cup of caramel mixture onto the hot pudding; this will soak into the holes of the pudding
#Slice into desired portions, and serve immediately with cream or ice cream.

'''Eton mess''' is a [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] of English origin consisting of a mixture of strawberries, pieces of meringue and cream, which is traditionally served at Eton College's annual prize-giving celebration picnic on the "Fourth of June" (actually celebrated on the last Wednesday in May).<ref>{{cite web|title=Glossary C–G|url=http://www.joyofbaking.com/other/glossaryCG.html|publisher=JoyofBaking.com|accessdate=[[w:10 July|10 July]] [[w:2007|2007]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dates of Halves|url=http://www.etoncollege.com/Eton.asp?state=load&di=171|publisher=[[w:Eton College|Eton College]]|accessdate=[[w:6 December|6 December]] [[w:2007|2007]]}} {{cite web|title=Eton Glossary|url=http://www.etoncollege.com/eton.asp?di=321#fourthofjune|publisher=[[w:Eton College|Eton College]]|accessdate=[[w:6 December|6 December]] [[w:2007|2007]]}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==
*4 medium-sized [[Cookbook:Meringue|meringues]]
*280 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1 ⅕ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] or 9 ½ [[Cookbook:Fluid Ounce|fl oz]]) [[Cookbook:Cream|double cream]]

*10 ml (1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla essence]]
*150 ml (⅗ cup or 5 fl oz) Greek [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yoghurt]]
*500 g (2 ⅕ cups or 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] 2 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Strawberry|strawberries]]

== Procedure ==
#Rinse the strawberries, remove the tops, and cut into halves.
#Break the meringues into pieces (not too small) and place into a bowl.
#Put the double cream, vanilla essence, and icing sugar into a bowl. [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] until reasonably stiff. 
#Combine the whipped cream, yoghurt, strawberries, and meringue, being careful not to mash the meringue into pieces that are too small.

title: Cookbook:Steamed Rice
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Rice recipes
| Difficulty = 2
| Image = [[File:Meshi_001.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Steamed rice''' is a simple dish, but some individuals have trouble cooking it. Common issues include adding too much rice or water, and not following the package directions. This recipe for steamed rice is fail-safe and does not require the use of a special rice cooker or microwave.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] or 8.5 fl oz) dry [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
*2 cups water
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (optional)

==Procedure==
# Wash the rice if desired.
#Place the rice in a deep [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] with lid. Add salt if using, and stir.
#Bring rice to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over high heat. Stir.
#Reduce heat to low and cover the pot. Cook on low for 12 minutes.
#Uncover rice and serve.

== Visual procedure ==
<gallery mode="packed">
File:Steamed Rice How to 01.jpg|1. Fill cup with desired amount of rice.
File:Steamed Rice How to 02.jpg|2. Pour rice into saucepan (mix optional salt in at this point).
File:Steamed Rice How to 03.jpg|3. Pour water into saucepan. Remember—twice as much water as rice.
File:Steamed Rice How to 04.jpg|4. Stir water so that floating rice sinks.
File:Steamed Rice How to 05.jpg|5. Place saucepan on stove and set temperature to "high". Do not cover.
File:Steamed Rice How to 06.jpg|6. Wait until water begins to boil.
File:Steamed Rice How to 07.jpg|7. Stir rice again.
File:Steamed Rice How to 08.jpg|8. Set temperature to lowest setting. Cover saucepan with lid.
File:Steamed Rice How to 09.jpg|9. After twelve minutes turn the element off and uncover. The rice is ready to eat.
</gallery>

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* This formula can be easily scaled up or down. The universal rule with cooking steamed rice is that the proportion of water should be double that of the rice. If you use one cup of rice you must use two cups of water. If you use two cups of rice you must use four cups of water.
* 1 cup dry rice is enough for three adults.

title: Cookbook:Strawberry Dumplings
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=4|yield=12 dumplings|time=30 minutes|time=2}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Austria|Austrian Cuisine]]

'''Strawberry dumplings''' ('''erdbeerknödel''') are a typically Austrian dish usually served as a main course, rather than as a dessert. This recipe is a tasteful, quick, and easy dish for, say, an evening with in-laws. Cooking strawberry dumplings is relatively easy, but of course it can only be perfected by practice. If you have grown tired of strawberry dumplings, just vary the filling and use other fruits of your choice. 

==Ingredients==
* 1/5 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (50 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 4/5 cups (200 g) [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|breadcrumbs]]
* 1/5 cup (50 g) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
* 2 cups (500 g) curd cheese (e.g. [[Cookbook:Quark|quark]], [[Cookbook:Pot Cheese|pot cheese]], or [[Cookbook:Farmer Cheese|farmer cheese]])
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ cup (125 g) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 12 ripe, medium-sized [[Cookbook:Strawberry|strawberries]], rinsed and trimmed
* [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|Icing sugar]]

==Procedure==

=== Breadcrumbs ===
# Melt the butter in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]].
# Add the breadcrumbs and the sugar and toast them until they gain a brown colour. Stir well, as the sugar makes the crumbs burn faster.

===Dough===
# Put the egg and the curd cheese into a large bowl.
# Add a pinch of salt.
# Stir until the mixture is smooth; the egg and the cheese should be blended well.
# Slowly add the flour, stirring until the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] sticks to one side of the bowl.
# Let the dough rest for about 5 minutes. If the dough is too moist, which sometimes happens due to the salt, add some more flour.

===Assembly===
# Cover your hands with flour, so that the dough won't stick to your fingers when forming the dumplings.
# Take a large tablespoon of dough and put it onto your palm.
# Add some flour and roll the dough slightly between your hands until you receive a small ball.
# Press the ball flat and put a strawberry into the middle. Cover the strawberry with dough, and pinch to seal.
# Sprinkle the dumpling and your hands with some more flour. Carefully roll the dumpling until you get a smooth, round ball.
# Put the dumplings on a floured plate. Leave enough space between them, as they will otherwise stick to one another.
===Cooking===
# Fill a large pot with about 3 liters of water and bring it to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Put the dumplings into the boiling water. Let them boil in the open pot for about 10 minutes. The dumplings are done, when they float as if they "danced".
# Take the dumplings out of the boiling water and roll them in the breadcrumbs until they are covered evenly. Since the crumbs are supposed to stick, the dumplings should still be moist on the surface.
# Serve the dumplings together with a little of the roasted crumbs, and sprinkle them with icing sugar
==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Always use fresh, ripe strawberries, as they taste much sweeter than the ones you can buy in the supermarket. Also consider picking strawberries yourself; this way you can choose the ripe and fresh ones and get the size you need for the dumplings. Moreover, you can try a few while picking. Use the spare strawberries for making jam.
* The breadcrumbs can be toasted without sugar, but in this case you will miss on the caramel flavor. You can also roast the breadcrumbs without butter.
* This recipe also works well with other fillings like [[Cookbook:Apricot|apricots]], [[Cookbook:Plum|plums]], or [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]]. In Austria the dumplings are also filled with "Mozartkugeln", which are little balls of chocolate, [[Cookbook:Nougat|nougat]], and [[Cookbook:Almond Paste|almond paste]]. If you use apricots or plums as a filling, you can add a pinch of [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] to the sugar before mixing it with the breadcrumbs. If you serve dumplings with a chocolate filling, garnish them with chocolate sauce and ground [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]].
* It is a good idea to serve the dumplings with [[Cookbook:Ice Cream|ice cream]] (preferably vanilla flavor), garnished with fresh berries and a [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]] leaf.
* Enjoying a glass of cold [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] together with the dumplings is especially refreshing in the summer months. In Austria it is also common to serve sweet dishes with a cup of coffee.
* Curd cheese dough only tastes well with sweet fillings. For savory dumplings, which are very popular in Austria, Germany and the Czech Republic, use potato dough and no breadcrumbs.

# Clean the large bowl and [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]] the inside with 1 tablespoon of the melted butter.
# Brush the top of the dough with another 2 tablespoons of the melted butter and place it in the bowl.

# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] the dough into a rectangle measuring 12 x 8 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] (30 x 20 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]), and brush it with the remaining melted butter.
# Fold two opposite sides of the rectangle towards the middle, overlapping them slightly. Press the joint gently to keep it in place.
# Taper the ends of the loaf slightly and push the sides gently together to form a mound in the middle. The loaf should be about 3½ inches (9 cm) wide and 14 inches (35 cm) long.
# Place the loaf on a floured [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] and brush it with any remaining melted butter. Leave it in a warm place for an hour or until it has doubled in size.
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 375°F (190°C)
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the stollen for 45 minutes, or until it is brown and crusty.
# Allow the stollen to cool and then [[Cookbook:Sifting|sift]] the icing sugar over the top.

title: Cookbook:Stovies
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Potato recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Stovies''' is a traditional Scottish dish originating mainly from the North Eastern counties of Angus and Aberdeenshire where even today the dish is still most commonly found and served. Recipes and ingredients vary widely between regions and even families, but the dish usually consists of potatoes and onions and some form of cold meat (especially sausages or leftover roast; mince or corned beef in the east). The potatoes are cooked by stewing with fat. A regional variation is to serve the stovies with oatcakes. 

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] (2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]]) [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]]
*50 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (2 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) beef drippings or [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*3 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], roughly [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*125–250 g (4–8 oz) cooked [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] or [[Cookbook:Lamb|lamb]] (leftovers from a roast dinner)
*2–3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] finely chopped [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], [[Cookbook:Chive|chives]], or [[Cookbook:Green Onion|spring onions]]
*[[Cookbook:Seasoning Salt|Seasoning salt]] (optional)
*Freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]] (optional)
*[[Cookbook:Allspice|Allspice]] or grated [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#Peel potatoes if they are "main crop", but leave the skins on new potatoes. [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] about 5 [[Cookbook:Mm|mm]] (¼-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]) thick. Or, slice roughly in different thickness so that the thin make a mush when cooked, while the others stay whole.
#Heat fat in a large heavy-base pot (one with a tight-fitting lid) and add the onions. Cook until lightly brown. Add the potatoes and stir well, coating all sides with the fat.
#Put the lid on and cook over a very low heat, shaking the pot once or twice to prevent sticking, until the potatoes are cooked.
#Add the meat, mix through, and turn up the heat to brown a little.
#Serve with brown sauce, parsley, and optional seasonings.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The same recipe can be adapted to use steak, beef or pork sausages instead of leftover meat. If making stovies this way, brown the sausages with the onions at the start.
* Recipes vary but mince is used most commonly, not only in the East but all over Scotland

==References==
* [http://www.dsl.ac.uk/dsl/getent4.php?plen=8753&startset=40575673&dtext=snd&query=STOVE "Stove"] in the Dictionary of the Scots Language

* [http://www.scotlandontv.tv/scotland_on_tv/video.html?vxSiteId=60fdd544-9c52-4e17-be7e-57a2a2d76992&vxChannel=Food%20Recipes&vxClipId=1380_SMG1132&vxBitrate=300 Head Chef] of Glasgow's Oran Mor Restaurant states that the dish can be created from any ingredients left in your fridge

{{recipe}} 

Herb-grilled steak brushed with olive oil and butter and cooked to perfect medium rare with roast potatoes and sautéed peppers rivals even the best steakhouse. 

== Ingredients ==

=== '''Steak''' ===
* 4 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (24–32 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[Cookbook:Beef|strip steaks]]
* 1 ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Rosemary|rosemary]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 tsp [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], finely chopped
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* Extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], divided

=== '''Potatoes''' ===
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] redskin [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], cut into 2-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] cubes but left unpeeled
* 1 tbsp salt
* 1 tbsp black pepper
* ¾ cup olive oil
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 ½ tsp dried rosemary
* 1 tbsp dried [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]

=== '''Peppers''' ===
* 4 assorted [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] into 3-inch strips
* 1 tbsp olive oil
* Salt
* Freshly-ground black pepper
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] red [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]

=== Other ===
* Few glasses red wine or [[Cookbook:Cognac|cognac]]
* Nice [[Cookbook:Salad|salad]] for an appetizer (hopefully with a homemade dressing)

== Procedure ==
#Set up a charcoal [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]] for direct and indirect heat.
#Heat a large pot of water to a rolling [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Add potatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
#Shock potatoes in a bowl of ice water, drain, and pat very dry with [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]].
#Place potatoes on a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|cooling rack]] and let dry for 2 hours.
#Combine remaining roast potatoes ingredients in a large stainless steel bowl. Add dry potatoes and [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|toss]] to coat.
#Place potatoes on a 13x9-inch [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]] and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] at 450°F for 25 minutes.
#Meanwhile, prepare the steaks: [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] steaks with extra-virgin olive oil. Sprinkle with salt and freshly ground black pepper and rub herbs into flesh.
#[[Cookbook:Grilling|Grill]] steaks, covered, over direct heat, for 1¼ minutes, then rotate 90° and cook for another 1¼ minutes. Flip and repeat 1 more time.
#Move steaks to indirect heat and cook, turning often, until internal temperature reaches 143°F for medium rare.
#Remove to serving platters and top each with 1 tablespoon of the butter. Keep warm in a 200°F oven.
#Meanwhile, heat a 10-inch straight-sided [[Cookbook:Sauté Pan|sauté pan]] over medium-high heat. Add oil and peppers to pan and cook, shaking the pan often, 8 minutes. Remove to serving platters.
#Place potatoes on serving platters. [[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with sprigs of rosemary, if desired. Serve.

title: Cookbook:Steamed Tuna Bao Buns
text:
{{Incomplete recipe}}__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Dumpling recipes
| Difficulty = 3
| Image = [[File:Steamed Buns (4650154698).jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Steamed tuna bao buns''' are a type of steamed dumpling from American-Asian cuisine. They are made with a simple yeast leavened dough and steamed until soft and fluffy. They can be eaten plain or stuffed with a variety of fillings. This recipe uses a tuna and pineapple filling.

== Ingredients ==

=== Dough ===
* [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|All-purpose flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|Rice flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Tapioca Starch|Tapioca starch]] (or [[Cookbook:Potato Starch|potato starch]])
* ½ packet dry active [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]]
* [[Cookbook:Milk|Milk]], warm (~100°F)
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* White granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* Lukewarm [[Cookbook: Water|water]] (~100°F)

=== Filling ===
* Canned [[Cookbook:Tuna|tuna]]
* Canned [[Cookbook:Pineapple|pineapple]] in juice, cut into small pieces
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] canned pineapple juice
* [[Cookbook:Barbecue Sauce|Barbecue sauce]] (your choice)
* Seasoning powder (hot [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]], [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]], [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]], ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], ground [[Cookbook:Star Anise|star anise]])
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Vegeta|Vegeta]] seasoning (optional, has [[Cookbook:MSG|MSG]])
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] spicy [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]
* Shelled whole [[Cookbook:Peanut|peanuts]]

== Procedure ==

=== Dough ===
# Add active dry yeast and honey to around 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] warm water and milk. If using instant yeast there is no need to bloom the yeast.
# Sift in a mix of all purpose flour, rice flour, tapioca starch. It should be mostly AP flour, but the exact mixture is not precise.
# Add a little salt and sugar. Begin to combine the dough with a oiled [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]], continue adding flour until it starts to come together.
# Begin [[Cookbook:Mixing|kneading]]—it will be sticky—and continue adding flour. Oil on hands will help.
# Add a little oil if it is needed (not more than 1 tbsp) and continue kneading until the dough is elastic.
# Place the dough in a covered food-safe plastic container large enough to accommodate the expanding dough.
# Allow dough to rise somewhere warm. Check on it in around 2 hours—once it doesn't bounce back when poked, it is ready for filling.

=== Filling ===
# Combine tuna, pineapples, peanuts, and seasoning powder, and mix until the tuna has a paste-like consistency. Pineapple pieces should be small.
# Add a little barbecue sauce; it should be moist but not too wet.
# Optionally add 1 tbsp pineapple juice, which will make it sweet.
# Add mustard according to taste.
# Let rest, uncovered, for around 2 hours

=== Assembly ===
# Take a piece of dough slightly larger than a golf ball and flatten in your hand. Don't make this too thin.
# Add filling and fold closed by pinching around the edges (google "folding bao" for help with this step). For plain bao they can be log-shaped.
# Add to [[Cookbook:Steamer|steamer]] with boiling water, and [[Cookbook:Steaming|steam]] 10–12 minutes.
# Serve hot.

title: Cookbook:Sticky Toffee Pudding (with dates)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=12|time=1 hour 10 minutes|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}}
{{nutritionsummary|1/12 of recipe (160 g)|12|715|461|51.2 g|34.6 g|33 mg|245 mg|58.2 g|3.2 g|44.5 g|5.4 g|4%|4%|10%|6%}}
'''Sticky toffee pudding (STP)''' is a rich, dense, gooey dessert originating from the United Kingdom that can now be found across the world. Often found on a [[wikipedia:Pub|pub]]'s menu, or in British or Commonwealth schools meals, this is a classic dessert that became popular in the 1970s.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.mcld.co.uk/recipes/#sticky-toffee-pudding |title= Sticky toffee pudding |author= Mcld (Wikibooks user) |date= 29 November 2008 |accessdate=19 July 2022}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==

=== Cake ===
* 1¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]/8.8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Self-rising Flour|self-raising flour]]
* ⅞ stick ({{convert|100|g|oz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) unsalted butter, room temperature
* 1 cup ({{convert|250|g|oz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) [[Cookbook:Superfine Sugar|caster sugar]]
* 2 large or 3 medium eggs
* 2½ cups ({{convert|250|g|oz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) [[Cookbook:Date|dates]] (without stones), finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1¼ cups ({{convert|300|ml|USoz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) water
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|bicarbonate of soda]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] essence

=== Toffee sauce ===
* 1⅔ cups ({{convert|400|ml|USoz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) [[Cookbook:Cream|whipping cream]]
* ⅔ cup ({{convert|120|g|oz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) dark, soft [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1 teaspoon vanilla essence
* 3 sticks ({{convert|375|g|oz|disp=s|abbr=on}}) unsalted butter

== Procedure ==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 180°C/360°F.
# [[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] together the butter, sugar and vanilla. You can do this by beating it in a bowl with a wooden spoon for about 5 minutes, taking care to break up the crystals and smooth the mixture out as much as possible. Or, do it using an electric [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]] if you prefer.
# Add the eggs one at a time, [[Cookbook:Beating|beating]] after you've added each egg.
# Fold in the flour.
# Bring the water to the [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and add the dates. Add the bicarb and immediately take the pan off the heat. Let it cool slightly, then add to the [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]].
# Pour the batter into a greased [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake tin]]—make sure you use one with enough room for the cake to rise.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the oven for 40 minutes, or until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] inserted into the cake comes out clean.
# Remove from the oven and set aside to cool a little while you make the sauce
# Mix the sauce ingredients in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Heat gently, stirring often to make sure that the mixture doesn't separate, until it is a smooth sauce—don't allow it to bubble.
# Divide the cake into portions and poke holes all over the top with a skewer or chopstick.
# Pour the sauce over the top of the cake, making sure it gets in the holes. Serve with cream, custard, or ice cream.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Finely chopping the dates helps make a really gooey cake, but some people prefer to chop the dates roughly so that they're more obvious in the finished pudding.

'''Sticky Toffee Pudding (STP)''' is a rich, dense, gooey [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] originating from the United Kingdom that can now be found across the world. Often found on a pub's menu, or in British or Commonwealth schools meals, this is a classic dessert that became popular in the 1970s. This recipe makes for a great STP, but without the dates!<ref>{{cite web |url= https://tamandlaura.blogspot.com/2007/03/how-english-can-you-get.html |title= How English can you get? |author= Tam & Laura |date= 11 March 2007 |accessdate=19 July 2022}}</ref> It was published by Tam and Laura under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 2.5 License, retrieved 2008-11-29 from http://tamandlaura.blogspot.com/2007/03/how-english-can-you-get.html. Laura has given permission for it to be reprinted here under the [[Wikibooks:Copyrights|wikibooks license]] (permission obtained 2008-12-18, by email, [[User:Mcld|mcld]]).

== Ingredients ==

=== Cake ===

* 1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] all-purpose [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* ¾ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
* ½ teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
* ¼ teaspoon freshly ground [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
* 1 cup packed dark [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* ¼ cup (½ stick) unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], room temperature
* 2 standard [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* 1 cup chopped toasted [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]]

=== Toffee sauce ===

* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Cream|whipping cream]]
* ⅔ cups white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* ¼ cup (½ stick) unsalted butter

== Procedure ==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350 °F.
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] dry ingredients together.
# [[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] butter, sugar, and eggs together.
# Combine wet and dry ingredients, mixing just until blended. Mix in walnuts.
# Pour batter into 8x8 buttered [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|pan]] and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] until [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] comes out clean, about 25 minutes.
# Meanwhile, make the toffee sauce:
#* Combine half the cream with sugar and butter in heavy large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]].
#* [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] over medium-high heat until mixture thickens slightly and is deep golden, stirring constantly, about 10 minutes.
#* Remove from heat; cool 5 minutes.
#* Gradually [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] in remainder of cream (mixture will bubble vigorously). Stir over low heat until mixture is smooth.
# Poke warm cake all over with a chopstick or the handle of a wooden spoon. Pour half of toffee sauce over, making sure it soaks into all parts of the cake. Let sit for at least 30 minutes.
# Serve warm, topped with remaining toffee sauce and creme fraiche or unsweetened whipped cream.

title: Cookbook:Stovetop Barley I
text:
__notoc__
{{recipe summary|Barley recipes|2|30-90 minutes
| Difficulty = 1
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Barley''' is a nutritious grain popular across the world. While it is most commonly used in cooking as an ingredient in stews or to add flavour to breads, barley can be prepared much as any other staple grain such as wheat berries or rice. This recipe is for the preparation of barley on the stove, much like how rice is prepared.

Barley at most stores is typically sold as either as a whole grain, known as hulled, pot, or scotch barley; or as a processed grain with the bran and hull removed, commonly called pearl barley. Pearl barley has a more mild flavour and cooks faster, but it lacks the fiber and nutrition of pot barley and has a higher glycemic index. Barley will yield roughly three times its dry volume when cooked. 

== Ingredients == 
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Barley|barley]]
*3 cups water
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (optional) 
*2 tsp [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|neutral cooking oil]] (optional, to reduce foaming)

== Procedure ==
#If desired, rinse barley under running water until water runs clear.
#Combine the barley, water, salt, and oil in a pot.
#Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], skimming off any foam that forms. 
#Reduce to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]], cover, and cook until all the water is absorbed by the barley. 
#Remove from heat, and fluff like rice.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*Some prefer a firmer barley, while others cook it longer for a softer mouthfeel. While pearl barley may eventually break down, pot barley is extremely difficult to overcook to the point of mushiness. Pearl barley cooks in 30 minutes, while pot barley will typically take around an hour.
*Barley may be soaked for up to several hours before cooking to soften the grains and reduce the cooking time by ⅓ to ½. This is particularly useful for pot barley.
*Barley foams more reliably than beans and should be watched until it has been boiling for several minutes
*Barley prepared in this fashion substitutes well for rice—and indeed, Korean and Japanese peasants would have historically eaten large quantities of barley relative to rice, just as most English peasants ate barley bread more often than wheat bread due to its lower cost.
*For a more flavorsome dish, barley can be cooked using the pilaf method.

title: Cookbook:Stovetop Barley II
text:
{{recipe summary
| Difficulty = 1|Barley recipes|2|30-90 minutes
}}{{Recipe}}

This method for cooking barley frees the cook from having to worry about the amount of water initially used, thereby removing the risk of grossly under-cooked barley that exists with the rice (absorption) method. It is useful when one wishes to leave the barley largely unattended (as the risk of scorching and sticking are all but non-existent), or when one cannot find the lid to one's pot.

== Ingredients ==
* [[Cookbook:Barley|Barley]]
* Water
* Salt (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Neutral cooking oil]] (optional, to reduce foaming)

== Procedure ==
# If desired, rinse barley under running water until water runs clear.
# Place the barley in a pot, and add enough water to cover the barley by several inches. Add salt and oil.
# Cover, and bring to a boil, skimming any foam that forms.
# Boil until barley grains have swelled to 3 times their original size and are a semiopaque white.
# Drain into a colander.

# Scoop out pulp, leaving a ¼ inch (0.75 cm) shell. [[Cookbook:Chopping|Chop]] the removed pulp.
# Heat olive oil in [[Cookbook:Sauté Pan|sauté pan]].
# [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] zucchini pulp, spinach, onions, and garlic for 5 minutes.
# Add mushrooms and sauté another 3 minutes.
# Remove from heat, add eggs, salt, and pepper, and mix well.
# Spoon filling into shells.
# Sprinkle with paprika.

This '''strawberry shortcut cake''' is one of those recipes from the 1970s with lots of already-processed ingredients. It's very moist because the syrupy strawberry mixture starts on top and soaks through as the cake bakes.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] mini [[Cookbook:Marshmallow|marshmallows]]
* 2 cups (20 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) frozen, sliced [[Cookbook:Strawberry|strawberries]] in syrup, completely thawed
* 1 pkg (3 oz) strawberry [[Cookbook:Jello|jello]] powder (known as ''jelly'' outside of North America)
* 2¼ cups [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1½ cups white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]

* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]

==Procedure==
#Generously grease the bottom of a 13x9-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake pan]]. 
#Sprinkle marshmallows evenly over bottom of pan.

title: Cookbook:Summer Rolls
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Vietnamese recipes|servings=4|time=15 minutes|difficulty=1|Image=[[Image:East-asian-food-spring-rolls-3.jpg|300px]]}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Vietnam|Cuisine of Vietnam]]

'''Summer Rolls''', or ''gỏi cuốn'' in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Vietnam|Vietnamese]], are wraps of various ingredients in rice wafers, and are often confused with [[Cookbook:Nem|nem]] or spring rolls (which, in turn, are often confused with [[Cookbook:Egg Roll|egg rolls]]).

==Ingredients==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Rice Wafer|rice wafers]] (rice paper, tapioca sheet)
* 4–8 [[Cookbook:Shrimp|prawns]]
* 50 g cooked [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] or [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] meat
* 50 g cooked rice [[Cookbook:Vermicelli|vermicelli]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] into fingers
* 4 leaves of leafy [[Cookbook:Lettuce|lettuce]] (e.g. romaine/cos, mignonette, etc.)
* 2 leaves of [[Cookbook:Nappa Cabbage|Chinese cabbage]], halved lengthways
* Fresh herbs, to taste (e.g. [[Cookbook:Cilantro|coriander]], [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]], [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]])
* Warm [[Cookbook:Water|water]]

==Procedure==
[[Image:East-asian-food-spring-rolls-1.jpg|thumb|Ingredients before rolling|308x308px]]
# Dip a rice wafer into the warm water and remove immediately when it is completely wet—it only needs to be in the water for a few seconds.
# Lay the rice wafer on a board or plate.
# Arrange a portion of the ingredients near the edge of the rice wafer in a neat pile, with the fingers of cucumber roughly parallel to the edge of the wafer.
# Fold the edge of the wafer over the pile of ingredients, and roll it over once.
# Fold the sides of the wafer inwards, to close of the ends of the roll you just made.
# Roll the wafer up the rest of the way, to enclose the roll completely.
# Set aside for 5 minutes to dry a little before eating. 
# The above process for each summer roll.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Summer rolls can easily be made vegetarian by omitting the prawns and meat, and adding more greens and vegetables like [[Cookbook:Bean Sprouts|bean sprouts]], [[Cookbook:Snow Pea|snow pea sprouts]], fingers of [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]].

title: Cookbook:Summer Pudding
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=4|time=1–2 hours|difficulty=2
| Image = [[File:Summer pudding.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

'''Summer pudding''' is a quintessentially British [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] made from wonderful fresh ingredients only available in the summer months. It is redolent of a private dinner at a smart country house, maybe somewhere in the Surrey hills near Shere, with the taste of an exquisite first course still lingering, a bottle of chilled champagne still half full, and the prospect of more enticing conversation to come as the evening turns into night. Once you make it once, you'll make it again and again!

== Ingredients ==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Punnet|punnet]] [[Cookbook:Strawberry|strawberries]], large ones halved
* 1 punnet [[Cookbook:Raspberry|raspberries]]
* ½ punnet [[Cookbook:Currant|blackcurrants]]
* ½ punnet [[Cookbook:Currant|redcurrants]]
* 1 loaf of white, pappy sort of [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] or [[Cookbook:Brioche|brioche]], crusts removed and sliced
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Caster sugar|caster sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Lime|lime]], finely [[Cookbook:Zest|zested]]
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]] leaves, finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 bottle of the best quality blackcurrant cordial you can find, in reserve

== Procedure ==

# Liberally butter the inside a pudding bowl about 5 inches in diameter. The bowl should preferably not be greater in diameter that the size of your pieces of sliced bread. If you are worried about getting the whole thing out of the bowl in one piece, line the bowl first with some [[Cookbook:Plastic wrap|cling film]]. It's a fiddly job, but ensures you get a perfect shape at the end.
# Combine the blackcurrants, redcurrants, mint leaves, lime zest, sugar, and about 3 tbsp water. [[Cookbook:Poaching|Poach]] them for about 5 minutes on the lowest possible heat setting of your stove. Add the strawberries and poach for another minute.
# Turn the heat off and add the raspberries. Leave to cool.
# Using the prepared bowl as a guide, cut a circle out of the white bread the same diameter as the top of the bowl. Do the same with the bottom of the bowl.
# Using a sharp knife, slice the bread into squares or oblongs, roughly the same height as the bowl, which will be used to line the inside of the bowl. This does not have to be an exact science. In simple terms what we are trying to do is to line the bowl with the white bread.
# Lay the smaller circle of white bread on the bottom of the bowl. Put the oblongs of white bread up the side of the bowl, overlapping slightly, and pour the fruit mixture into the void right up to the top. The bread should become well soaked in the juice from the cooked fruit. Indeed if there is not enough juice to soak the bread so it turns very red, use the cordial as a top-up.
# Place the large circle, or disc, of bread on the top and press it down well.
# Top with a weight or something that fits into the top of the bowl so it squashes everything down tight, and place it in the fridge for at least 40 minutes.
# When you are ready to serve the pudding, carefully using a knife to release the bread mould from the side of the bowl, and invert the whole thing onto a plate. If things become a little fraught and wobbly at this point, don't panic—just sort of whack everything back into shape using a wooden spoon.
# Decorate your plate with some more summer fruit, maybe a couple of mint leaves, and an artistic dollop of fresh [[Cookbook:Whipped Cream|whipped cream]] or [[Cookbook:Crème Fraiche|crème fraîche]], then serve with a flourish.

==Procedure==

=== Roasting ===

# Cut off the top of the squash and dig out the soft insides and seeds. Throw away the insides and seeds.
# Coat the squash, inside and out, with a thin layer of olive oil. Salt and pepper the inside.
# Place in a 350°F [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] and [[Cookbook:Roasting|roast]] until a fork easily pierces the flesh (about 30–45 minutes).
# While the squash is roasting, prepare the stuffing (below).

=== Stuffing ===

# Heat almond oil in a large pot. Add the slivered almonds, some red pepper flakes, and a little salt, and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the almonds until lightly browned and fragrant.
# Add the onion and continue to sauté until translucent, at which point you should add the garlic and red bell pepper and sauté for 1–2 more minutes.
# Mix in the rice pilaf mix, coating the mixture with the almond oil. Stir this around until the rice is hot and lightly toasted (3–5 minutes, or less).
# Add 2½ cups water or broth and bring it to an open [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Cover the pan and turn down the heat to let it [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until the rice is cooked (about 30–45 minutes).
# Salt and pepper to taste.
# When the rice is done, pour it into the roasted squash. Grate the cheese on top. [[Cookbook:Broiling|Broil]] a few minutes until the cheese is bubbly and toasty.

title: Cookbook:Stuffed Duck Breast with Cabbage and Dumplings
text:
__NOTOC__{{recipesummary|category=Dinner recipes|servings=4–6|time=Prep: 1 hour</br>Cooking: 2½ hrs|difficulty=3
| Image = [[File:Duck with side dishes.JPG|300px]]
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Austria|Austrian Cuisine]]

Almost every Austrian family has its own Christmas tradition. Christmas Eve differs from family to family; however, many cannot imagine Christmas without the delicious aroma of a succulent roast duck floating in the air. In general, Austrians are always really fond of eating duck.

Roasting a duck is a rather time-consuming activity that can turn the most silent time of the year into a quite stressful one for the cook as expectations in a culinary delicacy are always very high. Given that Christmas should be a happy feast for everybody—also for those preparing the meal—it is always helpful to invite family members or guests to come to the kitchen and help you prepare dinner. It is also recommended to start early enough and to consider that dishes prepared in advance will reduce stress later. 

This recipe serves a roast duck along with bread dumplings, also known as [[cookbook:serviettenknödel|serviettenknödel]]n, and a green cabbage salad. 

== Ingredients ==

=== Cabbage salad ===

* 1 head of green [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]], shredded
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1½ cups white [[Cookbook:Wine vinegar|wine vinegar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

=== Duck ===
*1 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (about 2.5 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) whole fresh [[Cookbook:Duck|duck]], at room temperature
*Salt
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
*50 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Marjoram|marjoram]] or other herbs
*4–5 [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]], peeled

=== Bread dumplings ===

* 4 stale white [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] rolls, cut into small cubes
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 5 g melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* Salt
* Ground [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
* [[Cookbook:Parsley|Parsley]]

== Procedure ==

=== Cabbage salad ===

# Put the shredded cabbage and the minced onion into a large bowl.
# Combine vinegar, salt, and sugar in a separate bowl and pour the mixture over the cabbage.
# Cover the salad, and refrigerate it for several hours before serving.

[[image:Duck_with_apples.jpg|thumb|300x300px|Seasoned, uncooked duck and apples]]

=== Duck ===

# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 200°C. If not already done, disembowel the duck, remove the clumps of fat from the tail, and rinse the whole bird carefully.
# Grease the bird with butter all over, and season it generously inside and out with salt, pepper, and marjoram.
# Stuff the duck with the peeled apples and make sure to close it appropriately. This will give a wonderful taste to the finished dish.
# Put the duck breast-side up into a roasting pan that is deep enough to hold the [[Cookbook:Rendering|rendered]] fat, and [[Cookbook:Roasting|roast]] it at 200°C for around 15 minutes.
# Take out the duck, [[Cookbook:Basting|baste]] it, turn it breast-side down, and roast for another 15 minutes. Continue to do so every 15 minutes. It takes roughly an hour to roast 1 kg; thus, you may prepare yourself to leave the duck in the oven for about 2½ hours.
# About 20 minutes before the end of the roasting process, put some more butter on the duck in order to obtain a crispy skin. The duck is ready to be served when its skin is richly browned and crisp.
# Turn off the oven and let the duck rest for another 10 minutes.

[[image:Ingredients_for_bread_dumplings.jpg|thumb|300x300px|Soaked breadcrumbs and eggs]]

=== Bread dumplings ===
[[image:Bread_dumpling_dough.jpg|thumb|300x300px|Dumpling mixture before wrapping in a towel]]

# Put the bread cubes into a large bowl and pour milk over them; use more or less milk depending on how dry the bread is.
# Melt the butter in a pan, and mix it with the eggs and the remaining ingredients in a bowl. Add to the bread mixture.
# Use your hands to squeeze the bread mixture through your fingers until it is smooth and sticky. If the dough is too loose, add 1–2 tablespoons of flour to firm it up.
# Bring a large pot of salted water to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and form small portions of the dough into balls.
# Drop the dumplings carefully into the water and let them [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 30 minutes until they are light, firm, and well risen. Remove them with a large spoon. Alternatively, form the dough into a roll, wrap it into a wet dishtowel, and firmly tie up both ends. Then, put it into the pot and let it simmer for about 30 minutes.

=== Serving ===

# Remove the apples from the duck, then carve it as desired. Put the dark brown gravy into an extra cup for serving.
# If you have cooked the dumpling mixture using the towel method, remove the large dumpling from the dishtowel, cut it into generous slices, and arrange them nicely on a plate. Otherwise, transfer the drained cooked dumplings to a dish.
# Serve the duck and dumplings hot, accompanied by the cabbage salad and a fruity red wine.

== References ==

* Mostar, Katinka: ''Das Große Katinka Mostar Kochbuch'', Suedwest Verlag: Muenchen 1978.
* Müller, Anna; Walser, Holger: ''Mein erstes Kochbuch'', Vorarlberger Verlagsanstalt Ges.m.b.H: Dornbirn 1970.

title: Cookbook:Stroopwafels
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Cookie recipes|servings=12|time=About 2 hours|difficulty=3
| Image = [[File:Gaufre biscuit.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Waffle|Waffle]] | [[Cookbook:Snack|Snack]]

'''Stroopwafels''' are a kind of [[Cookbook:Cookie|cookie]], originating in The Netherlands. They are typically a morning or evening snack eaten with tea or coffee. They are slightly chewy in texture and made with different fillings and flavors. The following recipe has been adapted from the Diana Dessert recipe [http://dianasdesserts.com/index.cfm/fuseaction/recipes.recipeListing/filter/dianas/recipeID/694/Recipe.cfm].

==Ingredients==
===Waffles===
*1 package (¼ [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounce]]) active dry [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] warm water 
*4 cups [[Cookbook:Flour|all-purpose flour]]
*1 cup unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*½ cup [[Cookbook:White Sugar|white sugar]]
*2 large [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]

===Filling===
*1½ cups packed [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
*1 cup unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 tsp ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*6 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] dark [[Cookbook:Corn Syrup|corn syrup]]
*½ cup finely-ground [[Cookbook:Hazelnut|hazelnuts]], optional

==Procedure==

=== Waffles ===
#Preheat a Pizzelle iron.
#Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.
#Add the butter to the flour, then mix in the sugar, cinnamon, eggs, and yeast mixture.
#Mix well and set aside to rise for 30–60 minutes.
#Roll dough into 12 small balls, squeeze each ball into the preheated pizzelle iron, and cook for about 30 seconds.

===Filling===
#In a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], cook the brown sugar, butter, cinnamon, and dark corn syrup until it reaches the [[Cookbook:Cooking Sugar|soft ball stage]] (234–240°F or 112–115°C).
#Stir in ground hazelnuts at this point, if using.

===Assembly===
#Cut each waffle into two thin layers and sandwich them with some filling.
#Repeat this process until all the filling and waffles are used.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* If using hazelnuts, remove skin, if possible. Grind hazelnuts in a [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]] until they are ground to a fine powder.
* Try eating your stroopwafel by resting it over a warm cup of coffee or tea. The steam will warm these up just right.
* Collect any remains of the waffles and let them cool. They can be served as "crumbs" and are usually also sold as such.

title: Cookbook:Stuffed Grape Leaves
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Appetizer recipes|yield=20 +|time=1 hour|difficulty=2|image=[[File:Sarma.jpg|300px|Grape leaves]]}}{{Recipe}}

'''Grape leaves (stuffed)''', (Arabic: ورق دوالي); (Hebrew: עלי גפן ממולאים), are an appetizer popular in Middle Eastern countries, including Turkey and Persia, where it is usually eaten with stuffed [[cookbook:rice|rice]] that has been seasoned with a multitude of spices.

== Ingredients ==
* Batch of thin, freshly-picked [[Cookbook:Grape Leaf|grape leaves]] (choose only the thinnest leaves)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] uncooked [[cookbook:rice|rice]], rinsed
* [[cookbook:turmeric|Turmeric]]
* [[cookbook:pepper|Black pepper]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] salt
* Dried [[Cookbook:Mint|mint leaves]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[cookbook:raisin|raisins]]
* Fresh [[cookbook:dill|dill]], finely chopped
* [[cookbook:parsley|Parsley]]
* [[cookbook:green onion|Green onions]] (scallions)
* [[cookbook:oil|Cooking oil]]
* 2 [[cookbook:lemon|lemon]]

== Procedure ==
# Soak leaves in [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] hot water to soften, about 15 minutes.
# Combine the rice, turmeric, pepper, salt, mint, raisins, dill, parsley and green onions.
# Place some of the rice mixture on a leaf, close to one end. Fold the three smaller ends of the leaf over the filling, then roll up the remainder like a sleeping bag or mat. Repeat with remaining rice and leaves.
# Place stuffed leaves in pot with a little water, oil, and lemon juice—the liquid should just barely cover the stuffed leaves.
# Cover pot with lid. First bring to a boil, then lower heat.
# Cook over low heat until the rice is cooked.
# Place sliced lemon on top of stuffed grape leaves for added flavour, and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Arabs have a practice to place the fatty tail of a sheep on top of the grape leaves while cooking, so that the melted fat is absorbed in the rice and leaves; in this manner it imparts its good flavour.

title: Cookbook:Super Foamy Milkshake
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Beverage recipes
| Difficulty = 1
}}

{{Recipe}}

The ''Super Foamy'' is a highly viscous milkshake with a smooth, airy texture. It is low-fat and, for a shake, high-fiber. Best of it all, due to its thickness it's easy to eat one's fill on a single portion. With the prototype recipe provided here, variations can be made by adding different flavors such as vanilla, banana or strawberry.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (2 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]]) locust bean gum powder
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] (10 grams) inulin powder 
* 2 tablespoons (10 grams) sweet [[Cookbook:Whey|whey]] powder 
* 200 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] [[Cookbook:Milk|skimmed milk]]

== Procedure ==
# Mix the locust bean gum powder, inulin powder, and sweet whey powder together.
# Add the resulting powder to the skimmed milk.
# Using an [[Cookbook:Mixer|electric mixer]], whip for 2 minutes until the product has turned to a fine foam. While whipping, move the whisks up and down so that air gets whipped into the shake.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Add the syrup or flavor of your desire.
* Any sources of fat must be excluded for the foam to build up. Therefore, the milk must be very low fat. When using [[Cookbook:Cocoa Powder|cocoa powder]] for creating a chocolate milkshake, do not use the mixer to spread the flavor—use a spoon instead, as the fat in the powder could cause the foam to collapse.
* [[Cookbook:Sweeteners|Artificial sugar substitutes]] are best for giving the shake a sweet taste.
* One serving equals approximately 700 ml in volume and 104 kcal in energy.
* The locust bean gum acts as the [[Cookbook:Thickener|thickening agent]], and the inulin gives the shake a smooth, "mouthful" texture.
* The sweet whey powder (along with the milk) acts as the component producing the foam. ''[[Cookbook:Whey|Whey drink powders]]'' are readily available on the market. They contain around 95% sweet whey powder with flavor and sweeteners added. They can be used to substitute the pure sweet whey powder. You can also use a fresh [[Cookbook:Egg White|egg white]] from a medium sized egg.

title: Cookbook:Sudanese Ful Medames
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Bean recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Ful medames''' is a traditional Sudanese dish made from cooked fava beans, commonly enjoyed for breakfast or as a light meal. It is a nutritious and filling dish, packed with protein and fiber. The beans are typically seasoned with olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and a blend of spices, resulting in a flavorful and satisfying culinary experience.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] dried [[Cookbook:Fava Bean|fava beans]]
* 4 cups water (for soaking)
* 4 cups water (for cooking)
* 4 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* ¼ cup extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* Juice of 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* ½ teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* Optional toppings: [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], chopped [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Hard Cooked Eggs|hard-boiled eggs]], [[Cookbook:Feta Cheese|feta cheese]]

== Equipment ==

* Large pot
* [[Cookbook:Colander|Colander]] or [[Cookbook:Sieve|strainer]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* Wooden spoon or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
* Serving dish

== Procedure ==

# Rinse the dried fava beans under cold water and then place them in a large pot. Add 4 cups of water to the pot and let the beans soak overnight, or for at least 8 hours. This helps soften the beans and reduce the cooking time.
# Drain the soaked fava beans and rinse them under cold water. Return the beans to the pot and add 4 cups of fresh water. Bring the water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and let the beans [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 1–1½ hours, or until they become tender. Stir occasionally and skim off any foam that forms on the surface.
# Once the beans are tender, drain them using a colander or strainer and transfer them to a mixing bowl. Add minced garlic, extra-virgin olive oil, lemon juice, ground cumin, ground coriander, and salt to the bowl. Mix everything together, ensuring that the beans are coated evenly with the seasoning.
# For a smoother consistency, you can use a fork or a potato masher to lightly mash some of the beans. This step is optional and can be adjusted according to your preference.
# Transfer the seasoned ful medames to a serving dish. Ful medames can be enjoyed warm or at room temperature. You can serve it with a variety of optional toppings such as chopped parsley, diced tomatoes, chopped onions, hard-boiled eggs, or crumbled feta cheese. It is commonly served with bread or as a side dish alongside other Sudanese specialties.

title: Cookbook:Superkanja (Gambian Okra Stew)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{Recipe summary
| Servings = 1
| Time = 1 hour 30 minutes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Superkanja''' is a highly nutritious and flavorful [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]] that brings together an array of leafy greens, including spinach, collards, okra, and sweet potato leaves. This dish has different variations throughout West Africa, such as the Ghanaian kontomire. Recognized as Gambia's super soup, this delectable bowl of goodness can be savored in various countries. Its name originates from the fusion of the Portuguese word for soup (sopa) and a West African term for okra (kanja), which lends the dish its unique texture.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] lean [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], cut into chunks
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] smoked [[Cookbook:Catfish|catfish]] or any fish of your choice
* 2 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* Pepper
* 2 lbs [[Cookbook:Okra|okra]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] into small cubes
* [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|Palm oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

== Equipment ==

* Pot
* [[Cookbook:Cooktop|Stovetop]]
* Cooking spoon

== Preparation ==

# Bring a pot of water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and add the meat and fish. Let them boil for 15 minutes, then remove the fish from the pot.
# To the pot, add salt, onions, pepper, and diced okra. Mix all the ingredients well.
# Cook the mixture over medium heat for 15 minutes, then incorporate the palm oil.
# Reduce the heat to low and let it [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
# Afterward, return the fish to the pot and continue simmering for 6–10 minutes on low heat.
# Serve the superkanja stew with white rice or fufu.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You can also include [[Cookbook:Crab|crabs]] and [[Cookbook:Shrimp|shrimp]] to enhance the dish.
