title: Cookbook:Zitumbuwa (Malawian Banana Pancakes)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipe summary
| category = Breakfast recipes
| cuisine = Malawian
| difficulty = 2
}}
{{Recipe}}

'''Zitumbuwa''' are Malawian banana [[Cookbook:Pancake|pancakes]] that are loved by both kids and adults. These fluffy and flavorful pancakes make for a delicious breakfast or snack option.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 ripe [[Cookbook:Banana|bananas]], [[Cookbook:Mashing|mashed]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] all-purpose [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Vanilla Extract|vanilla extract]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* Whisk or [[Cookbook:Fork|fork]]
* [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|Frying pan]] or [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]]
* [[Cookbook:Spatula|Spatula]]

== Procedure ==
# In a mixing bowl, combine the mashed bananas, all-purpose flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Mix well.
# In a separate bowl, whisk together the milk, egg, and vanilla extract.
# Gradually pour the wet ingredients into the banana-flour mixture, stirring until a smooth batter forms.
# Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan or griddle over medium heat.
# Pour a small amount of the pancake batter onto the hot pan, forming a circle.
# Cook the pancake for about 2 minutes or until bubbles form on the surface. Then, flip the pancake and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes on the other side until it is golden brown and cooked through.
# Repeat the process with the remaining batter, adding more oil to the pan as needed to prevent sticking.
# Serve warm, and enjoy them plain or with your favorite toppings, such as honey, syrup, or fresh fruit.
== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* For extra banana flavor, you can add a few slices of banana on top of each pancake before flipping.
* You can use whole wheat flour or a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour in this recipe.
* Zitumbuwa can be enjoyed with a variety of toppings, such as [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]] or chocolate spread.
* Zitumbuwa provide a delightful combination of natural sweetness from bananas and a soft, fluffy texture from the pancake batter.

title: Cookbook:Zacusca (Romanian Vegetable Spread)
text:
__NOTOC__
{{recipesummary|category=Appetizer recipes|servings=15|time=3 hr|difficulty=3
| image = [[image:Zacuscă bgiu.jpg|300px]]
}}
{{Distinguish|Zakuski}}
{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Appetizers|Appetizers]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Romania|Cuisine of Romania]] | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan Cuisine]]

'''Zacuscă''' is a vegetable spread popular in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Romania|Romania]]. It is usually eaten with [[Cookbook:bread|bread]]. Similar spreads are found in other countries in the Balkan region and bordering regions. Although traditionally prepared at home as a way to store vegetables for the winter, it is also commercially available.

==Ingredients==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] medium-large [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]] (any variety)
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] or [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]]
* 1 kg [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|red bell pepper]] of the gogoșar variety
* 1 kg [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]]
* 200 g [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato paste]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
* 700 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] [[Cookbook:Sunflower Oil|sunflower oil]]
* 20 dried [[Cookbook:Black pepper|black peppercorns]]
* 4–6 dried [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]
==Procedure==
# [[Cookbook:Roasting|Roast]] the eggplants and peppers until their skins are charred and easily removable by hand. Skin the vegetables. The pepper skins should come off easily in long strips. The eggplant skin might retain some of the flesh; some people like to take the back of the knife over the skin to remove that flesh and use it because it has a smokey flavor, but you can easily discard it if pressed for time.
# [[Cookbook:dice|Dice]] the eggplants and peppers in 1–2 cm cubes. The peppers will retain their shape, but the eggplant flesh is mushy so don't worry if your cubes aren't perfect shapes, they will disintegrate more when cooking and that is the goal.
# In a large nonstick [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]], [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the onions in the oil over medium until golden. 
# Add the peppers to the onions. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Make sure it doesn't stick to the bottom of the pan and burn.
# Stir in the eggplants, tomato paste, bay leaves, salt, and peppercorns. Simmer until the oil comes to the surface.
# [[Cookbook:Canning|Can]] the mixture in sterilized jars. Store in a cool place. If you don't want to can, zacusca can be stored in the fridge and consumed within a few days, like any stew. If that is the case, given the large quantity you just made, invite over a few friends and smear the spread on thin-to-medium slices of a [[Cookbook:Baguette|baguette]]. Bon appetite!

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* When adding the eggplant and remaining ingredients, you can also add mushrooms, boiled beans, zucchini, hot peppers, carrots, celery etc. This way you can have different spreads over winter with different flavor profiles.

title: Cookbook:Zimbabwean Chicken and Vegetable Soup
text:
__notoc__
{{Recipe summary
| Name = Zimbabwean Chicken and Vegetable Soup
| Category = Soup recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Zimbabwean chicken and vegetable soup''' is a delicious soup that combines a variety of vegetables with peanut [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] and a few red pepper flakes.

== Ingredients ==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]

* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] vegetable [[Cookbook:Broth and Stock|stock]], divided
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]]
* 2 cups canned diced [[Cookbook:Tomatoes with Cheese Stuffing|tomatoes]], with juices
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Chile Flakes|crushed red pepper flakes]], or more to taste
* 1 cup finely [[Cookbook:Chop|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]]
* 1 cup chopped [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potato]]
* 1 cup peeled and chopped [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]
* 1 cup peeled and chopped [[Cookbook:Turnip|turnip]]
* 1 cup chopped [[Cookbook:Okra|okra]]
* 1 cup chopped cooked [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], or to taste

== Equipment ==

* Soup pot
* Spoon
* Stovetop

== Procedure ==

# Heat the olive oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion, and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] for about 5 minutes until translucent.
# Stir ½ cup of the vegetable stock and the peanut butter into the onions until the mixture looks smooth.
# Stir in the remaining vegetable stock, diced tomatoes with their liquid, and crushed red pepper flakes; [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 30 minutes, stirring frequently.
# Stir in the cabbage, sweet potato, carrot, and turnip. Simmer, stirring, until the vegetables become soft (about 30 minutes). 
# Stir in the okra and chicken, and simmer for about 30 additional minutes.
